## Introduction
This document provides advanced guidance for operating, optimizing, and extending the Tab5 ESPHome-based HMI. It focuses on:
- Performance optimization strategies (memory management in PSRAM, CPU utilization reduction via push-only data flow, LVGL rendering optimizations for smooth animations).
- Debugging techniques (console overlay usage, log analysis, marker technique for tracing execution flow, common troubleshooting scenarios).
- Architectural decision rationale (ADR-backed explanations for non-obvious choices such as push-only data flow, single-page navigation, data packing strategies, offline resilience patterns).
- Advanced configuration options, extension points, migration guidance, expert usage patterns, profiling techniques, and contribution guidelines.

## Project Structure
The project is organized around a single entry point that composes modular packages:
- Entry point orchestrates boot sequence, entity substitutions, and package imports.
- Packages separate concerns: hardware, sensors, API logic, styles, globals, scripts, LVGL UI, IMU, and more.
- C++ layer centralizes LVGL updates, parsing, color mapping, gestures, and animation helpers.
- ADRs document key design decisions and their consequences.

```mermaid
graph TB
A["Entry Point<br/>tab5-ha-hmi.yaml"] --> B["Hardware<br/>tab5-hardware.yaml"]
A --> C["Sensors & Diagnostics"]
A --> D["API Logic<br/>tab5-api-logic.yaml"]
A --> E["Styles<br/>tab5-styles.yaml"]
A --> F["Globals<br/>tab5-globals.yaml"]
A --> G["Scripts<br/>tab5-scripts.yaml"]
A --> H["LVGL UI<br/>tab5-lvgl.yaml"]
A --> I["IMU<br/>tab5-imu.yaml"]
D --> J["C++ Layer<br/>tab5_custom.*"]
H --> J
```

## Core Components
- Push-only API services: Home Assistant calls ESPHome services to push payloads; firmware parses and updates LVGL atomically.
- Single-page LVGL dashboard with overlays and swipe pagination.
- Centralized C++ helpers for LVGL updates, parsing, animations, and state synchronization.
- Global variables for shared state across packages.
- Hardware configuration including display, touch, audio, Wi-Fi co-processor, and PSRAM usage.

Key responsibilities and interactions are defined in the architecture overview below.

## Architecture Overview
The system follows a push-only model where Home Assistant detects changes and pushes data to the device via ESPHome API services. The device never initiates network requests. Data flows one-way into the device, which parses payloads and updates LVGL widgets in a single pass.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome API"
participant CPP as "C++ Layer"
participant LV as "LVGL UI"
HA->>ESP : "service call tab5_maj_* (payload)"
ESP->>CPP : "lambda invokes parser/update"
CPP->>LV : "update labels/widgets once"
LV-->>HA : "screen reflects latest state"
```

- [architecture.md:191-207](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L191-L207)
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:41-78](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L41-L78)

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Push-only Data Flow and Parsing Pipeline
- Services receive payloads and delegate to C++ functions for parsing and UI updates.
- Bulk payloads use delimited strings to minimize network calls and reduce TCP socket pressure.
- LVGL updates are guarded against null pointers and incomplete initialization.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Service Received"]) --> Parse["Parse Delimited Payload"]
Parse --> UpdateSlots["Update Forecast/Sensor Slots"]
UpdateSlots --> RefreshTitle["Refresh Page Title / Central Card"]
RefreshTitle --> Guard{"Boot Complete & API Connected?"}
Guard --> |Yes| ApplyUI["Apply LVGL Updates"]
Guard --> |No| SkipUI["Skip UI Update"]
ApplyUI --> End(["Done"])
SkipUI --> End
```

### Single-Page Navigation and Swipe Handling
- Dashboard is a single LVGL page with overlays and layers; swipe gestures paginate forecast windows within a lower band.
- A dedicated button toggles between switches and forecast layers using crossfade animations.
- Game pages are isolated and skipped from swipe navigation.

```mermaid
classDiagram

+id : page_main
+on_gesture()
+widgets[]
}
class GestureHandler {
+handle_swipe_gesture(dir, y, ...)
}
class Layers {
+layer_forecast_daily
+layer_forecast_hourly
+layer_switches
}
LVGLPage --> GestureHandler : "delegates swipe"
LVGLPage --> Layers : "crossfade toggle"
```

### C++ Layer Responsibilities and Data Structures
- Centralized LVGL update functions guard against null pointers and uninitialized states.
- Color mapping functions translate temperatures and humidity to semantic colors.
- Animation helpers provide lightweight transitions for panels, popups, alerts, and icons.
- Data structures encapsulate weather slots, calendar cells, and alert UI bindings.

### Audio and Wake Word Integration
- Microphone and speaker configured via I2S with external ADC/DAC.
- Wake word detection integrated with media player lifecycle and voice assistant callbacks.
- Buffer durations tuned to mitigate streaming artifacts over Wi-Fi.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Mic as "Microphone"
participant MW as "micro_wake_word"
participant VA as "voice_assistant"
participant SP as "Speaker/Media Player"
Mic->>MW : "audio stream"
MW-->>VA : "wake word detected"
VA->>SP : "start TTS/announcement"
SP-->>VA : "idle when done"
VA->>MW : "re-arm wake word if enabled"
```

## Dependency Analysis
- YAML packages depend on global tokens and styles for consistent layout and theming.
- API logic depends on C++ layer for parsing and LVGL updates.
- LVGL UI delegates gesture handling and complex logic to C++.
- Hardware configuration sets up peripherals and influences performance (PSRAM, SDIO frequency, buffer sizes).

## Performance Considerations
- Memory Management in PSRAM:
  - Enable PSRAM for buffers and stack allocations where beneficial (e.g., microWakeWord task stack in PSRAM).
  - Use hex mode and appropriate speed settings to stabilize memory operations.
- CPU Utilization Reduction:
  - Push-only architecture eliminates polling cycles and reduces Wi-Fi radio wake-ups.
  - Batched payload parsing minimizes service calls and avoids repeated redraws.
- Rendering Optimizations:
  - Global style definitions reduce per-widget allocations in PSRAM.
  - Lightweight animations with reduced durations and amplitudes decrease repaint costs.
  - Avoid inline styles; reference IDs to reuse style objects.
- Network Stability:
  - Adjust TCP window size and yield during flash erase for stable OTA.
  - Pace push automations to avoid exhausting limited API connections.

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Console Overlay:
  - Access via the console button to view memory, network, system metrics, and management actions.
  - Not a log viewer; use ESPHome logs for payload/event traces.
- Log Analysis:
  - Monitor ESPHome logs for boot sequence issues, API connection state, and C++ log lines.
  - Close log sessions promptly to avoid holding API connections open.
- Marker Technique:
  - Insert debug markers in automation or code to observe real-time behavior without altering production logic permanently.
- Common Scenarios:
  - Black screen after software reboot due to GPIO expander settle time before display reset.
  - Stale data when push automations are gated behind a disabled helper flag.
  - STT/TTS broken due to entity ID collisions in dual-instance setups.
  - Touch not working because service calls are rejected in integration options.
  - Automation failure mid-stream due to schema validation errors; add continue-on-error guards.
  - API connections exhausted by leftover CLI processes.
  - Device reboots periodically when no API client connected; adjust reboot timeout.
  - Post-OTA black screen due to Wi-Fi co-processor link not coming up; requires full power cycle.

## Conclusion
The Tab5 HMI leverages a push-only architecture, single-page LVGL dashboard, and centralized C++ logic to deliver efficient, responsive, and maintainable user experiences. Performance is optimized through PSRAM usage, batched data processing, and lightweight animations. Debugging relies on the console overlay, structured logging, and targeted markers. ADRs capture the rationale behind key design choices, ensuring consistency and reducing future debates. Contributors should follow established workflows and guidelines to extend functionality safely.

## Appendices

### Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) Summary
- Push-only architecture, zero polling from the device.
- Single LVGL page with swipe navigation instead of multi-page tabs.
- Delimited-string payloads to reduce network overhead.
- No PNG alpha channel; pre-baked opaque backgrounds.
- Blocking boot delay before display reset sequence.
- Centralize LVGL logic in C++, not inline in sensor lambdas.
- Climate popup left un-factorized for clarity and stability.
- Single Home Assistant instance strategy.
- Shared modal shell header for consistent popups.

### Advanced Configuration Options
- PSRAM mode and speed for improved memory performance.
- TCP window size and yield during flash erase for stable OTA.
- Watchdog timeouts and safe mode parameters for robustness.
- I2C bus frequency and GPIO expander addresses for peripheral stability.
- Display and touchscreen calibration values for accurate touch input.
- Audio buffer durations and sample rates to balance quality and latency.
- API encryption keys and reboot timeouts for security and resilience.

### Extension Points for Custom Functionality
- Add new ESPHome API services in the API logic package and implement parsing/UI updates in C++.
- Extend LVGL UI by including additional component files and wiring gestures to C++ handlers.
- Introduce new global variables for shared state across packages.
- Create reusable scripts for multi-step actions to keep API logic clean.
- Implement custom game modules following the established pattern (isolated pages, lv_timer lifecycle, NVS persistence).

### Migration Guides for Version Upgrades
- When updating ESPHome components (e.g., official st7123 platform), remove obsolete external components and adjust references accordingly.
- If modifying include paths or package structure, run clean builds to avoid stale caches.
- Validate UI token changes across all components to prevent layout drift.
- Test push automations and API services after upgrades to ensure payload contracts remain compatible.
- Reboot devices fully after OTA if Wi-Fi co-processor fails to come up post-reboot.

**Section sources**

### Expert Usage Patterns and Profiling Techniques
- Use the console overlay to monitor SRAM/PSRAM usage, loop times, and network status in real time.
- Profile animations by adjusting durations and amplitudes to balance perceived smoothness and CPU load.
- Inspect LVGL widget trees and style references to eliminate redundant allocations.
- Leverage C++ helpers for atomic updates to avoid partial redraws and flicker.
- Employ markers in automations to trace silent failures and validate conditions under real contexts.

## Introduction
This document consolidates the key architectural decisions for the Tab5 system and explains why they were chosen, what alternatives were considered, and what trade-offs and consequences followed. It focuses on reliability, performance, and maintainability, and includes diagrams to illustrate patterns such as push-only data flow, single-page navigation, centralized LVGL logic, and shared modal chrome.

## Project Structure
The project organizes decisions under docs/decisions and implements them across ESPHome YAML configuration, LVGL UI definitions, and C++ logic:
- Decisions are captured as concise ADRs with Context/Decision/Consequences.
- The device firmware is defined in Tab5/*.yaml (LVGL pages, hardware, scripts, sensors).
- Central LVGL update logic lives in C++ (tab5_custom.cpp), keeping UI mutations out of YAML lambdas.
- Shared UI components live under Tab5/ui_components (e.g., modal_header.yaml, climate_popup.yaml).

```mermaid

end
```

## Core Components
- Push-only data path: Home Assistant automations detect state changes and push updates via ESPHome API services; the device never polls.
- Single-page dashboard: One main LVGL page hosts all home content; secondary interactions open fullscreen overlays/popups.
- Bulk data packing: Multi-valued datasets are serialized into delimited strings and parsed in a single pass in C++.
- Pre-baked backgrounds: PNG assets are baked against the background color at export time to avoid runtime alpha blending crashes.
- Boot delay for display reset: A blocking delay ensures the I2C GPIO expander is ready before toggling the display reset pin.
- Centralized LVGL logic: All non-trivial UI updates are implemented in C++ functions, not inline in YAML sensor lambdas.
- Climate popup design: Some buttons remain un-factored because each calls a distinct service with unique lambda logic.
- Single Home Assistant instance: Eliminates duplicate-entity and failover flag bugs by running one HA node.
- Shared modal shell: A single include produces consistent title bars and scrim across popups.

## Architecture Overview
The system uses a push-driven, single-page LVGL dashboard with centralized C++ logic and shared UI chrome.

## Detailed Component Analysis

### ADR-0001: Push-only architecture, zero polling from the device
- Context: Near-real-time state display without constant polling.
- Decision: Device is purely reactive; HA pushes updates via ESPHome API services.
- Trade-offs: Saves CPU/network when idle; risk of stale state if pushes miss; requires paired HA/device changes for new fields.
- Consequences: Zero polling cost; no built-in catch-up; mitigated by HA-side guards.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["State change in HA"]) --> Detect["Automation detects change"]
Detect --> Push["Push via ESPHome service"]
Push --> Device["Device receives event"]
Device --> Update["Update LVGL widgets"]
Update --> End(["Idle until next change"])
```

**Diagram sources**
- [0001-push-only-zero-polling.md:5-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-push-only-zero-polling.md#L5-L17)

**Section sources**
- [0001-push-only-zero-polling.md:5-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-push-only-zero-polling.md#L5-L17)

### ADR-0002: Single LVGL page + swipe navigation
- Context: Early multi-page tab bar did not match shipped firmware.
- Decision: One 1280×720 main page; overlays for details; swipe zones limited to specific regions; games use separate pages marked skip.
- Trade-offs: Maximizes dashboard real estate; less discoverable for deep features; requires disciplined gesture handling.
- Consequences: Consistent glanceable dashboard; game pages isolated; swipe behavior constrained to lower band.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Main["page_main"] --> |Tap card| Overlay["Overlay popup"]
Main --> |Swipe in lower band| Forecast["Cycle forecast windows"]
Main --> |Open Arcade| GamePage["Dedicated game page (skip)"]
GamePage --> |Quit| Main
```

**Diagram sources**
- [0002-single-page-swipe-navigation.md:5-29](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0002-single-page-swipe-navigation.md#L5-L29)
- [tab5-lvgl.yaml:17-36](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-lvgl.yaml#L17-L36)

**Section sources**
- [0002-single-page-swipe-navigation.md:5-29](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0002-single-page-swipe-navigation.md#L5-L29)
- [tab5-lvgl.yaml:17-36](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-lvgl.yaml#L17-L36)

### ADR-0003: Data packing with delimited strings
- Context: Multi-valued datasets would otherwise require many network calls.
- Decision: Serialize payloads into semicolon-delimited strings; parse in C++ in a single pass; update widgets atomically.
- Trade-offs: Reduces socket pressure; implicit contract between HA and C++; mismatch fails silently; fixed buffers prevent heap churn.
- Consequences: Fewer TCP connections; careful schema discipline required; robust parsing avoids memory issues.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
In["Delimited string payload"] --> Parse["Single-pass tokenizer"]
Parse --> Map["Map tokens to widget IDs"]
Map --> Apply["Apply LVGL updates"]
Apply --> Done["Atomic refresh complete"]
```

**Diagram sources**
- [0003-data-packing-delimited-strings.md:9-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-data-packing-delimited-strings.md#L9-L17)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:1-20](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L1-L20)

**Section sources**
- [0003-data-packing-delimited-strings.md:9-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-data-packing-delimited-strings.md#L9-L17)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:1-20](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L1-L20)

### ADR-0004: No alpha PNG — pre-baked backgrounds
- Context: Glassmorphism typically uses alpha compositing at render time.
- Decision: Bake opaque backgrounds into images at export; swap channels at export too.
- Trade-offs: Avoids firmware crash on MIPI-DSI alpha rendering; asset re-export needed for layout/color changes; encourages vector icons.
- Consequences: Stable rendering; reduced runtime work; asset pipeline becomes part of the design process.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Design["Design with transparency"] --> Bake["Bake against #23262E at export"]
Bake --> Ship["Ship opaque PNGs"]
Ship --> Render["LVGL renders without alpha"]
```

**Diagram sources**
- [0004-no-alpha-png-prebaked-backgrounds.md:5-16](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0004-no-alpha-png-prebaked-backgrounds.md#L5-L16)

**Section sources**
- [0004-no-alpha-png-prebaked-backgrounds.md:5-16](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0004-no-alpha-png-prebaked-backgrounds.md#L5-L16)

### ADR-0005: Boot delay for GPIO expander reset
- Context: Display reset pin routed through I2C GPIO expander; early toggles have no effect, causing black screens after software reboots.
- Decision: Insert a blocking delay before the display reset sequence during boot.
- Trade-offs: Adds ~1s to boot; prevents intermittent black screen; must not be removed without validation.
- Consequences: Reliable display initialization across reboots; documented as critical guard.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant FW as "Firmware"
participant EXP as "I2C GPIO Expander"
participant DISP as "Display"
FW->>FW : "on_boot priority 700"
FW->>FW : "delay(1000) [blocking]"
FW->>EXP : "Toggle reset_pin"
EXP-->>DISP : "Reset signal applied"
DISP-->>FW : "Initialized"
```

- [tab5-hardware.yaml:116-128](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L116-L128)

- [tab5-hardware.yaml:116-128](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L116-L128)

### ADR-0006: Centralize LVGL logic in C++
- Context: Inline LVGL calls in YAML lambdas are tempting but hard to maintain.
- Decision: Sensors/services read HA state and call named C++ functions; LVGL manipulation happens centrally.
- Trade-offs: Slightly more files to touch; improves grepability, testability, and consistency.
- Consequences: Clear separation of concerns; easier audits and refactors.

```mermaid
classDiagram
class YAML_Trigger {
+reads HA state
+calls C++ function
}
class CppLogic {
+update_*()
+lv_obj_* calls
}
YAML_Trigger --> CppLogic : "invokes"
```

- [0006-centralize-lvgl-logic-in-cpp.md:5-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0006-centralize-lvgl-logic-in-cpp.md#L5-L17)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:1-20](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L1-L20)

- [tab5_custom.cpp:1-20](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L1-L20)

### ADR-0007: Climate popup not fully factorized
- Context: climate_popup.yaml is large and repetitive, yet some buttons call different services with unique logic.
- Decision: Leave three buttons and temperature +/- as duplicated YAML rather than force a template that would parametrize service calls.
- Trade-offs: Slight duplication vs. over-engineering a template around actions.
- Consequences: Easier to keep button-specific behavior clear; future refactor could move to index-based dispatch in C++.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Grid["Climate grid buttons"] --> Shared["Templated buttons (HVAC modes, presets)"]
Grid --> Unique["Unique buttons (off, swing, quiet, +/-)"]
Unique --> Action["Distinct HA service + lambda"]
```

- [0007-climate-popup-not-factorized.md:5-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-climate-popup-not-factorized.md#L5-L17)
- [climate_popup.yaml:1-24](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_popup.yaml#L1-L24)

**Section sources**
- [0007-climate-popup-not-factorized.md:5-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0007-climate-popup-not-factorized.md#L5-L17)
- [climate_popup.yaml:1-24](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_popup.yaml#L1-L24)

### ADR-0008: Single Home Assistant instance
- Context: Dual-instance setup caused duplicate entities, broken integrations, and stuck active flags.
- Decision: Run one HA instance; disable the secondary at boot.
- Trade-offs: Removes apparent redundancy; eliminates a class of bugs.
- Consequences: Simpler operation; any future HA HA must explicitly handle entity-ID collisions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Primary["Primary HA"] --> Push["Pushes to device"]
Secondary["Secondary HA (disabled)"] -.->|Not started| Push
```

**Diagram sources**
- [0008-single-ha-instance.md:5-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0008-single-ha-instance.md#L5-L17)

**Section sources**
- [0008-single-ha-instance.md:5-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0008-single-ha-instance.md#L5-L17)

### ADR-0009: Shared modal shell header
- Context: Popups had inconsistent chrome, varying sizes, and multiple ways to draw titles.
- Decision: One include produces the entire title bar; one scrim; geometry tokens centralize sizes; no subtitles.
- Trade-offs: Enforces uniformity; reduces per-popup maintenance; requires adherence to token constraints.
- Consequences: Easier global styling; recovered usable height; automated checks enforce compliance.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Popup["Any popup"] --> Include["!include modal_header.yaml"]
Include --> Bar["Icon + Title + Close"]
Popup --> Scrim["!include modal_scrim.yaml"]
Bar --> Body["Body starts at y: ${modal_body_y}"]
```

**Diagram sources**
- [0009-modal-shell-header.md:13-20](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0009-modal-shell-header.md#L13-L20)

## Dependency Analysis
Key dependencies among decisions and implementation artifacts:
- Push-only (ADR-0001) drives how LVGL updates are triggered and how bulk payloads are handled (ADR-0003).
- Single-page navigation (ADR-0002) constrains where gestures and overlays live in LVGL.
- Centralized LVGL logic (ADR-0006) is the execution target for parsed payloads and gesture handlers.
- Hardware boot delay (ADR-0005) ensures reliable display init before LVGL runs.
- Modal shell (ADR-0009) standardizes overlay chrome used by popups like climate (ADR-0007).

```mermaid
graph LR
A1["ADR-0001 Push-only"] --> A3["ADR-0003 Delimited strings"]
A2["ADR-0002 Single page"] --> A6["ADR-0006 Centralize LVGL"]
A3 --> A6
A5["ADR-0005 Boot delay"] --> A2
A9["ADR-0009 Modal shell"] --> A7["ADR-0007 Climate popup"]
A8["ADR-0008 Single HA"] --> A1
```

## Performance Considerations
- Push-only minimizes radio wake-ups and CPU usage when idle.
- Delimited-string payloads reduce TCP connection pressure and avoid contention with audio streams.
- Pre-baked backgrounds eliminate costly or unstable runtime alpha blending.
- Centralized LVGL logic reduces scattered updates and simplifies profiling.
- Boot delay adds a predictable one-second cost to ensure reliable display init.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Black screen after software reboot: Ensure the blocking boot delay remains before display reset; removing it risks recurring black screens.
- Stale state on device: Verify HA-side automations fire reliably; consider adding guard automations and monitoring for missed pushes.
- Connection exhaustion: Prefer bulk payloads to avoid hitting the ESPHome native API connection cap.
- Modal drift or inconsistency: Use the shared modal header include and tokens; avoid inline scrics or custom offsets.

**Section sources**
- [0005-boot-delay-gpio-expander-reset.md:5-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0005-boot-delay-gpio-expander-reset.md#L5-L17)
- [0001-push-only-zero-polling.md:13-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-push-only-zero-polling.md#L13-L17)
- [0003-data-packing-delimited-strings.md:13-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0003-data-packing-delimited-strings.md#L13-L17)
- [0009-modal-shell-header.md:24-31](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0009-modal-shell-header.md#L24-L31)

## Conclusion
These decisions collectively produce a reliable, performant, and maintainable system:
- Push-only and bulk payloads minimize resource usage and network load.
- A single-page dashboard maximizes information density while keeping interactions intuitive.
- Centralized LVGL logic and shared modal chrome improve consistency and ease of maintenance.
- Hardware-level safeguards (boot delay) and simplified HA topology reduce failure modes.
Adhering to these patterns helps preserve system stability and clarity as the project evolves.

## Introduction
This document provides a systematic approach to diagnosing issues in the Tab5 system, with a focus on:
- Using the on-screen console overlay (MEMORY, NETWORK, SYSTEM, MANAGEMENT cards) for live diagnostics without a laptop
- Interpreting ESPHome logs and Home Assistant logs to pinpoint failures
- Applying the debug marker technique using [AI-DEBUG] tags to trace execution flow non-invasively
- Resolving common scenarios such as API connection problems, automation failures, network connectivity issues, and hardware initialization errors

The goal is to equip both human and AI agents with repeatable procedures that minimize guesswork and reduce debugging cycles.

## Project Structure
The debugging surface spans three layers:
- On-device UI: The System Console overlay exposes four glass cards with real-time metrics and management actions
- Device telemetry: ESPHome sensors and intervals feed data into the console via C++ helpers
- Host-side context: Home Assistant automations and services drive device updates; their logs are essential when the issue originates upstream

```mermaid
graph TB
A["User"] --> B["Console Overlay<br/>MEMORY / NETWORK / SYSTEM / MANAGEMENT"]
B --> C["ESPHome Sensors & Intervals<br/>WiFi, RSSI, Uptime, Temp, RAM"]
C --> D["C++ Console Helpers<br/>update_console_* functions"]
D --> E["LVGL Labels/Bars<br/>lbl_sys_*, bar_sys_*"]
F["Home Assistant"] -- "api: services" --> G["Device Services<br/>tab5_maj_*"]
F -- "Logs" --> H["HA Logs"]
I["ESPHome CLI"] -- "esphome logs" --> J["Live Device Logs"]
```

## Core Components
- On-screen console overlay: Four diagnostic cards plus management controls
  - MEMORY: SRAM/PSRAM usage, largest free block, flash info
  - NETWORK: SSID, IP, signal strength, HA connection status
  - SYSTEM: uptime, CPU temperature, loop time, volume slider
  - MANAGEMENT: screen re-push, automation reload, restart HA, reboot device (with confirm overlays)
- Diagnostics data pipeline: ESPHome sensors and intervals update LVGL widgets through C++ helper functions
- Debug markers: [AI-DEBUG] tags mark observation points in code and automations to accelerate future investigations

Key responsibilities:
- YAML defines UI widgets and actions; it does not perform calculations
- C++ functions read runtime state and paint labels/bars safely
- Intervals guard LVGL calls behind visibility checks to avoid unnecessary work

## Architecture Overview
The console overlay is a modal layer on the main dashboard. It is opened by a dedicated button and uses shared modal chrome. Data flows from ESPHome sensors into C++ helpers that update LVGL widgets. Management buttons call Home Assistant services or trigger device-level actions.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant LVGL as "LVGL Layer"
participant Diag as "Diagnostics Interval"
participant Cpp as "C++ Helpers"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
User->>LVGL : Open Console Overlay
LVGL-->>Diag : Visible flag set
Diag->>Cpp : update_console_diagnostics_ui(...)
Cpp-->>LVGL : Update labels/bars (SRAM, PSRAM, IP, SSID, loop time)
User->>LVGL : Click "MAJ Écran"
LVGL->>HA : input_boolean.turn_on (primary active)
LVGL->>HA : automation.trigger (push automation)
User->>LVGL : Click "Redémarrer HA"
LVGL->>HA : homeassistant.restart
User->>LVGL : Click "Reboot tablette"
LVGL->>LVGL : Trigger device reboot
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### On-Screen Console Overlay
- Purpose: Provide immediate, at-a-glance diagnostics and safe management actions directly on the device
- Cards:
  - MEMORY: Shows SRAM/PSRAM usage and fragmentation; useful for memory leaks or allocation pressure
  - NETWORK: Displays SSID, IP, RSSI, and HA connection status; helps isolate Wi-Fi vs API issues
  - SYSTEM: Shows uptime, CPU temperature, loop time, and volume; indicates performance bottlenecks or thermal throttling
  - MANAGEMENT: Re-push screen data, reload automations, restart HA, reboot device; includes confirmation overlays for destructive actions
- Interaction model:
  - Modal header with close action hides overlays
  - Destructive actions require explicit confirmation overlays
  - Volume control goes through a single script entry point to keep UI and HA consistent

Best practices:
- Use the console when you cannot connect a laptop; it is not a log viewer
- For payload/event tracing, use ESPHome logs instead
- Confirm destructive actions carefully; overlays prevent accidental HA/device restarts

**Section sources**
- [console_sys.yaml:1-390](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/console_sys.yaml#L1-L390)

### Diagnostics Data Pipeline
- Sources:
  - WiFi info (SSID, IP), WiFi signal (RSSI)
  - Uptime, internal core temperature
  - Debug sensors (free heap, loop time)
  - HA API status binary sensor
- Update cadence:
  - Periodic interval refreshes console UI only when visible
  - Sensor on_value handlers call C++ helpers to update specific labels
- Safety:
  - LVGL updates guarded by visibility check to avoid drawing when hidden
  - C++ helpers format values efficiently without heavy allocations

Performance considerations:
- Avoid string conversions in hot paths; use small buffers
- Keep interval work minimal; formatting happens in C++ helpers

**Section sources**
- [tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml:135-310](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml#L135-L310)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:1888-1967](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L1888-L1967)

### Debug Marker System ([AI-DEBUG])
- Purpose: Mark high-value observation points in code or automations to speed up future debugging sessions
- Usage:
  - Add [AI-DEBUG] comments near log lines, entities, or techniques proven to work
  - In Home Assistant, insert low-cost side effects (e.g., setting an input text) directly into the real automation to observe actual runtime context
- Benefits:
  - Reduces need to reconstruct failing contexts in isolated scripts
  - Captures exact template context, entity availability, and condition evaluation at trigger time
- Cleanup:
  - Remove or comment out temporary markers after confirming fixes

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:18-30](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L18-L30)
- [README.md:19-27](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/README.md#L19-L27)

## Performance Considerations
- Keep LVGL updates conditional on console visibility to avoid wasted work
- Prefer lightweight formatting in C++ helpers; avoid dynamic allocations in hot paths
- Use debounced scripts for frequent UI changes (e.g., volume slider) to limit service calls
- Close ESPHome log sessions promptly to avoid exhausting API connections

## Troubleshooting Guide

### Step-by-Step Diagnostic Procedures

#### 1) Start with the On-Screen Console
- Open the console overlay via the dedicated button
- Check NETWORK card:
  - If SSID/IP/RSSI are missing, investigate Wi-Fi configuration and antenna selection
  - If HA status shows offline, verify API connectivity and consider restarting HA
- Check SYSTEM card:
  - High loop time suggests UI or automation overload
  - Elevated CPU temperature may indicate thermal throttling
- Check MEMORY card:
  - Low free blocks or high fragmentation can cause crashes or freezes
- Use MANAGEMENT card:
  - “MAJ Écran” re-arms push flags and triggers a full refresh
  - “Recharger autos” reloads automations after YAML edits
  - “Redémarrer HA” and “Reboot tablette” require confirmation overlays

**Section sources**
- [console_sys.yaml:1-390](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/console_sys.yaml#L1-L390)
- [tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml:286-309](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml#L286-L309)

#### 2) Inspect Live ESPHome Logs
- Run `esphome logs` or use the ESPHome dashboard log view
- Look for boot sequence issues, API connection state changes, and any ESP_LOG* lines
- Close the session when done to avoid holding API connections open

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:9-16](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L9-L16)

#### 3) Inspect Home Assistant Logs
- Check automation trigger/condition evaluation results
- Look for template rendering errors and service call rejections
- Focus on steps immediately before the failure point

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:16-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L16-L17)

#### 4) Apply the Debug Marker Technique
- Insert a low-cost side effect (e.g., setting an input text) directly into the real automation at the suspected failure point
- Trigger the automation under real conditions and read back the value
- Remove or comment out the marker after confirming the fix

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:22-30](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L22-L30)

### Common Scenarios and Resolution Strategies

#### API Connection Issues
- Symptom: Device intermittently fails to accept new API connections
- Root cause: Leftover ESPHome CLI processes hold connections indefinitely
- Resolution: Close CLI sessions; kill orphaned local esphome processes if connections seem exhausted

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:73-80](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L73-L80)

#### Automation Failures
- Symptom: Weather/planning/climate data missing despite healthy Wi-Fi/API
- Root cause: Push automations gated by a shared boolean helper stuck off; guard automation disabled
- Resolution: Enable helper and guard automation; manually trigger push once; ensure guard automations stay enabled

- Symptom: Calendar/weather push silently breaks rest of automation
- Root cause: Passing raw datetime object to calendar service; validation failure aborts subsequent actions
- Resolution: Format datetime explicitly; add continue_on_error per push action; add is defined guards downstream

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:23-30](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L23-L30)
- [troubleshooting.md:53-60](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L53-L60)

#### Network Connectivity Problems
- Symptom: Black screen + device off the network after OTA; Wi-Fi co-processor never came up
- Root cause: Software reboot did not reset co-processor; hot retry loop starves firmware
- Resolution: Perform a full power cycle (power off and unplug USB-C for ~15 seconds); soft reboot is insufficient

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:93-110](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L93-L110)

#### Hardware Initialization Errors
- Symptom: Black screen after software reboot (not power cycle)
- Root cause: Display reset pin wired through GPIO expander needs settle time; toggling too early is ineffective
- Resolution: Blocking delay added before display reset sequence; do not remove without re-testing across multiple reboots

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:13-20](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L13-L20)

#### Touch Not Responding
- Symptom: Tapping screen does nothing; touch controller appears dead
- Root cause: Home Assistant rejecting service calls due to integration options
- Resolution: Enable “Allow service calls” in ESPHome integration options for the device

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:43-50](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L43-L50)

### Log Interpretation Guides

#### ESPHome Logs
- Boot sequence: Verify display reset timing and expander readiness
- API connections: Watch for connection limits and client drops
- Runtime warnings: Note repeated error loops that may starve other subsystems

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:9-16](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L9-L16)
- [troubleshooting.md:93-110](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L93-L110)

#### Home Assistant Logs
- Automation evaluation: Identify failed conditions or invalid payloads
- Template rendering: Catch type mismatches (e.g., raw datetime objects)
- Service calls: Detect rejected calls due to integration settings

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:16-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L16-L17)
- [troubleshooting.md:53-60](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L53-L60)

### Best Practices for Non-Intrusive Debugging
- Use the console overlay for quick checks without external tools
- Prefer markers in real automations over isolated reproduction scripts
- Keep debug markers temporary; remove them after fixes
- Guard LVGL updates behind visibility checks to avoid overhead
- Debounce frequent UI interactions to reduce service call load

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:18-30](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L18-L30)
- [tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml:286-309](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml#L286-L309)

## Conclusion
Effective debugging of the Tab5 system combines on-screen diagnostics, targeted log inspection, and disciplined use of debug markers. The console overlay provides immediate visibility into memory, network, system health, and management actions. ESPHome and Home Assistant logs reveal runtime behavior and upstream failures. By following the documented procedures and best practices, you can quickly isolate root causes and apply reliable fixes while minimizing disruption.

## Introduction
This document provides a comprehensive, practical guide to debugging the Tab5 system. It focuses on:
- The on-screen console overlay with MEMORY, NETWORK, SYSTEM, and MANAGEMENT cards
- The debug marker system using [AI-DEBUG] tags for non-intrusive tracing
- Log analysis techniques across ESPHome logs, Home Assistant logs, and device-specific patterns
- ESP32-P4 specific debugging tools, serial console access, and OTA debugging capabilities
- Practical examples for setting up debug markers, interpreting memory reports, and analyzing network issues
- Performance profiling techniques and common debugging workflows

## Project Structure
The debugging surface is composed of:
- An on-screen diagnostic overlay (LVGL UI) that displays live metrics and management actions
- A diagnostics sensor layer that periodically updates the overlay with memory, network, and system data
- Hardware configuration for logging, OTA, and ESP32-P4 specifics
- Documentation conventions for marking observation points in code

```mermaid
graph TB
subgraph "Device UI"
CONSOLE["Console Overlay<br/>MEMORY / NETWORK / SYSTEM / MANAGEMENT"]
end
subgraph "Diagnostics Layer"
SENSORS["Diagnostics Sensors<br/>WiFi / Uptime / Temp / Loop Time / Free Heap"]
INTERVALS["Intervals & Timers<br/>2s refresh loop"]
end
subgraph "Hardware & Runtime"
HW["ESP32-P4 Config<br/>Logger / PSRAM / OTA / Safe Mode"]
LOGS["Serial Logger<br/>USB_SERIAL_JTAG @ 115200"]
end
subgraph "Host"
HA["Home Assistant<br/>Logs & Services"]
SERIAL["Serial Console<br/>esphome logs / USB"]
end
CONSOLE --> INTERVALS
INTERVALS --> SENSORS
SENSORS --> HW
HW --> LOGS
LOGS --> SERIAL
CONSOLE --> HA
```

## Core Components
- On-screen console overlay: A modal LVGL screen with four glass cards showing live diagnostics and management controls.
- Diagnostics sensors: Periodic updates of WiFi status, IP/SSID, RSSI, uptime, CPU temperature, loop time, and heap usage.
- Logging and OTA: Serial logger via USB JTAG at 115200 baud; OTA with safe mode and post-update reboot.
- Debug markers: [AI-DEBUG] comments to mark useful observation points without changing runtime behavior.

Key responsibilities:
- UI: Render and update labels/bars for MEMORY, NETWORK, SYSTEM, and MANAGEMENT sections.
- Data: Poll or receive values from ESPHome sensors and push them to the UI.
- Control: Expose management actions (screen refresh, automation reload, HA restart, device reboot) with confirm overlays.

**Section sources**
- [console_sys.yaml:59-390](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/console_sys.yaml#L59-L390)

- [tab5-hardware.yaml:37-99](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L37-L99)

## Architecture Overview
The console overlay is updated by a 2-second interval that calls into C++ helpers to read heap stats, loop time, and WiFi info, then writes to LVGL widgets. Management actions call Home Assistant services through the ESPHome integration.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant UI as "Console Overlay (LVGL)"
participant INT as "Interval 2s"
participant DIAG as "Diagnostics Sensors"
participant CPP as "C++ Helpers"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
UI->>INT : Open console layer
INT->>DIAG : Read WiFi/IP/SSID, RSSI, Uptime, Temp, Loop Time, Free Heap
DIAG-->>CPP : Values + flags
CPP->>UI : Update labels/bars (MEMORY/NETWORK/SYSTEM)
UI->>HA : Management actions (reload automations, restart HA, reboot)
HA-->>UI : Service results / state changes
```

- [tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml:286-309](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml#L286-L309)
- [console_sys.yaml:200-390](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/console_sys.yaml#L200-L390)

## Detailed Component Analysis

### On-Screen Console Overlay
- Access: Open via the console button on the main UI (not by swipe).
- Cards:
  - MEMORY: SRAM/PSRAM usage bars, largest free block, flash size.
  - NETWORK: SSID, IP address, signal strength, Home Assistant connection status.
  - SYSTEM: Uptime, CPU temperature, loop time, volume slider.
  - MANAGEMENT: Screen refresh (re-push), reload automations, restart Home Assistant, reboot device — destructive actions behind confirmation overlays.
- Behavior:
  - Non-scrollable modal to avoid accidental scrolling.
  - Destructive actions use dedicated overlays with cancel/confirm buttons.
  - Volume slider uses a single script entry point to keep UI and HA consistent.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Open Console"]) --> Memory["MEMORY Card<br/>SRAM/PSRAM/Frag/Flash"]
Start --> Network["NETWORK Card<br/>SSID/IP/RSSI/HA Status"]
Start --> System["SYSTEM Card<br/>Uptime/Temperature/Loop/Volume"]
Start --> Manage["MANAGEMENT Card<br/>Refresh/Reload/Restart/Reboot"]
Manage --> Confirm{"Destructive Action?"}
Confirm --> |Yes| Overlay["Show Confirmation Overlay"]
Confirm --> |No| Execute["Execute Action"]
Overlay --> ConfirmAction{"Confirm?"}
ConfirmAction --> |Yes| Execute
ConfirmAction --> |No| Cancel["Cancel"]
```

### Diagnostics Data Pipeline
- Sources:
  - WiFi info (IP/SSID), WiFi signal (RSSI), internal temperature, uptime, debug free heap and loop time.
- Refresh:
  - Every 2 seconds, if the console layer is visible, update UI elements via C++ helpers.
- UI mapping:
  - Labels and bars are bound to IDs filled by the diagnostics layer.
  - Color coding indicates health (e.g., HA connection green/red).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
T0["Every 2s"] --> Check["Console Visible?"]
Check --> |No| End["Skip Update"]
Check --> |Yes| Read["Read Sensors<br/>WiFi/IP/SSID/RSSI/Uptime/Temp/Heap/Loop"]
Read --> Update["Update LVGL Widgets<br/>Labels/Bars/Colors"]
Update --> End
```

### Debug Marker System ([AI-DEBUG])
- Purpose: Mark valuable observation points in code for future debugging sessions without altering runtime behavior.
- Usage: Add a comment tag [AI-DEBUG] near a log line, entity, or technique that proved useful during investigation.
- Benefits: Saves time for subsequent debugging passes (human or AI) by reusing known vantage points.

Practical guidance:
- Place markers near key transitions or decision points.
- Keep markers minimal and non-invasive.
- Remove or comment out temporary markers after confirming fixes.

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:18-30](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L18-L30)
- [AGENTS.md:19-26](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/AGENTS.md#L19-L26)

### Logging and Serial Console
- Logger configuration:
  - Level INFO by default; DEBUG level can be enabled when needed.
  - Baud rate 115200 over USB_SERIAL_JTAG.
- Live logs:
  - Use ESPHome logs to observe boot sequence, API connections, and any ESP_LOG* lines.
  - Close log sessions promptly to avoid holding an API connection open.
- Serial access:
  - Connect via USB to capture boot messages and runtime logs.
  - Be aware that opening/closing the serial port can reset the chip on this hardware.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-hardware.yaml:37-83](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L37-L83)
- [debugging.md:9-16](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L9-L16)
- [troubleshooting.md:107-110](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L107-L110)

### OTA Debugging and Safe Mode
- OTA:
  - Platform configured with password protection and automatic reboot after successful update.
- Safe mode:
  - Configured to recover from repeated boot failures.
- Post-OTA behavior:
  - Device reboots automatically after OTA completion.
  - If issues occur, verify co-processor link and perform full power cycle if necessary.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-hardware.yaml:88-99](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L88-L99)
- [troubleshooting.md:189-203](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L189-L203)

### ESP32-P4 Specific Notes
- Board and framework:
  - ESP32-P4 EVBoard with ESP-IDF framework.
  - PSRAM enabled for large buffers and reduced SRAM pressure.
- Co-processor Wi-Fi:
  - Wi-Fi provided by ESP32-C6 over SDIO; ensure link comes up after software reboots.
- Display reset timing:
  - A blocking delay before display reset is required due to I2C GPIO expander settle time.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-hardware.yaml:9-36](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L9-L36)

## Performance Considerations
- Monitor loop time: High loop times indicate UI or task bottlenecks.
- Watch memory usage: Track SRAM/PSRAM percentages and largest free block to detect fragmentation or leaks.
- Avoid excessive logging: Keep logger level at INFO unless investigating; DEBUG adds overhead.
- Minimize UI updates: The console only updates when visible to reduce unnecessary work.
- Audio buffer tuning: Speaker buffer duration affects audio smoothness; adjust only with understanding of trade-offs.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide

### Black screen after software reboot
- Symptom: After OTA or software reboot, display remains black while other subsystems appear healthy.
- Root cause: Display reset pin routed through I2C GPIO expander needs settle time; toggling too early has no effect.
- Fix: Ensure a blocking delay precedes display reset initialization.

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:13-21](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L13-L21)
- [tab5-hardware.yaml:37-83](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L37-L83)
- [tab5-ha-hmi.yaml:66-88](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/tab5-ha-hmi.yaml#L66-L88)

### Wi-Fi co-processor not coming up after OTA
- Symptom: Device appears offline despite ping responses; logs show repeated failed Wi-Fi setup.
- Root cause: ESP32-C6 co-processor link not restored after software reboot; hot loop starves firmware including LVGL.
- Resolution: Perform a full power cycle (power off and unplug USB-C for ~15 seconds).

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:189-203](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L189-L203)

### Serial log session causing unexpected reboot
- Symptom: Unexpected reboot at the end of an esphome logs session.
- Cause: Opening/closing the USB serial port can reset the chip.
- Mitigation: Use device entities and Home Assistant logs once back online.

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:107-110](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L107-L110)

### Diagnosing silent automation failures
- Approach: Insert a debug marker directly into the real automation to observe execution with actual context.
- Technique: Use a low-cost side effect (e.g., input text update) at the suspected step, trigger the automation, and inspect the value.

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:22-30](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L22-L30)

## Practical Examples

### Setting up debug markers
- Identify a critical path or decision point in your code or automation.
- Add a [AI-DEBUG] comment near a log line or observable state change.
- Trigger the scenario and capture logs or states to validate behavior.
- Remove or comment out temporary markers after confirming the fix.

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:18-30](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L18-L30)
- [AGENTS.md:19-26](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/AGENTS.md#L19-L26)

### Interpreting memory usage reports
- Open the console overlay and check the MEMORY card:
  - SRAM percentage and KB used; color indicates severity.
  - PSRAM percentage and MB used; helps assess offloading effectiveness.
  - Largest free block in KB; low values suggest fragmentation.
  - Flash size confirms available storage.
- Correlate spikes with UI interactions or heavy tasks.

**Section sources**
- [console_sys.yaml:59-111](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/console_sys.yaml#L59-L111)
- [tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml:286-309](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml#L286-L309)

### Analyzing network connectivity issues
- Check the NETWORK card:
  - SSID and IP address confirm Wi-Fi association and DHCP.
  - Signal strength (RSSI) indicates link quality.
  - Home Assistant status shows API connectivity.
- Cross-check with ESPHome logs for Wi-Fi events and errors.
- If co-processor link is down, follow the full power cycle procedure.

**Section sources**
- [console_sys.yaml:112-136](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/console_sys.yaml#L112-L136)
- [tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml:119-167](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml#L119-L167)
- [troubleshooting.md:189-203](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L189-L203)

### Using the serial console and OTA debugging
- Connect via USB and run ESPHome logs to capture boot and runtime messages.
- Enable DEBUG logger level temporarily for deeper insight.
- After OTA, allow auto-reboot; if issues persist, verify co-processor link and consider full power cycle.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-hardware.yaml:37-99](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L37-L99)
- [debugging.md:9-16](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L9-L16)

### Performance profiling workflow
- Observe loop time on the SYSTEM card; high values indicate bottlenecks.
- Monitor memory usage trends under load; watch for fragmentation.
- Reduce logging verbosity to baseline (INFO) for normal operation.
- Validate UI responsiveness after changes; use the console overlay to quickly assess impact.

**Section sources**
- [console_sys.yaml:137-187](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/console_sys.yaml#L137-L187)
- [tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml:135-198](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml#L135-L198)

## Conclusion
The Tab5 system provides a robust set of debugging tools:
- An on-screen console overlay for immediate visibility into memory, network, system health, and management actions.
- A structured debug marker convention to preserve insights across sessions.
- Comprehensive logging and OTA support tailored to the ESP32-P4 platform.
- Practical workflows for diagnosing common issues such as black screens, Wi-Fi co-processor problems, and silent automation failures.

Use these techniques together to efficiently locate, analyze, and resolve issues with minimal disruption to production environments.

## Core Components
- Display and Touch: MIPI DSI display with ST7123 touchscreen; reset pin routed through I2C GPIO expander requiring boot delay before reset sequence.
- Audio Pipeline: ES7210 ADC microphone, ES8388 DAC speaker, media player with announcement pipeline; wake-word detection via microWakeWord.
- API Services: ESPHome services receive payloads from Home Assistant automations and update LVGL UI via C++ handlers.
- Health Monitoring: Home Assistant health package watches push gating boolean, unexpected reboots, and API connectivity.

Key responsibilities:
- tab5-hardware.yaml: hardware init, audio, wake word, voice assistant callbacks
- tab5-api-logic.yaml: service definitions, payload parsing, UI updates, reboot timeout guard
- HomeAssistant_Config README: push architecture, pacing, service naming
- tab5_health.yaml: alerts for primary instance inactive, unexpected reboots, API offline

## Architecture Overview
Push-only architecture: Home Assistant detects state changes and pushes data to the device via native ESPHome service calls. The device never polls. Data is serialized into delimited strings and parsed on-device to update LVGL UI efficiently.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome Device"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
participant HW as "Hardware (Display/Audio)"
HA->>ESP : "esphome.<device>_tab5_maj_*" with payload
ESP->>ESP : "parse_and_update_*" lambdas
ESP->>UI : "Update labels/widgets"
Note over HA,UI : "Traffic pacing delays prevent collisions with I2S audio"
HW-->>ESP : "Boot sequence ensures stable display/audio"
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Display and Touch Initialization
- Reset pin routed through PI4IOE5V6408 expander requires a blocking delay before toggling to ensure reliable reset after software reboots.
- Touchscreen uses ST7123 with interrupt pin and calibration; backlight control resumes/pauses LVGL.

Common symptoms and fixes:
- Black screen after software reboot: add blocking delay before display reset sequence.
- Touch not responding: enable "Allow service calls" in ESPHome integration options flow.

**Section sources**
- [docs/troubleshooting.md:13-20](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L13-L20)
- [docs/troubleshooting.md:43-50](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L43-L50)
- [Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml:116-142](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L116-L142)
- [Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml:151-167](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L151-L167)

### Audio Hardware and Voice Assistant
- Microphone capture at 16 kHz/16-bit mono via ES7210; gain staged in analog stage to avoid clipping.
- Speaker playback via ES8388 DAC; announcement pipeline format set to FLAC at 24 kHz mono.
- Wake-word detection runs locally; voice assistant callbacks update UI states.

Common symptoms and fixes:
- Poor STT/TTS quality: adjust mic gain, avoid digital gain factor, keep noise suppression at 0 unless noisy room.
- Playback gaps: maintain buffer_duration at 500ms to absorb network hiccups during streaming.
- Pipeline state confusion: use icon color feedback to identify listening, processing, speaking, error states.

**Section sources**
- [docs/voice_assistant.md:43-83](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/voice_assistant.md#L43-L83)

### API Services and Push Logic
- Services defined in tab5-api-logic.yaml handle weather, climate, alerts, calendar, and voice responses.
- Reboot timeout configured to prevent zombie devices while avoiding frequent reboots during HA outages.

Common symptoms and fixes:
- Weather/planning missing despite online status: check push gating boolean and guard automation.
- Calendar/weather push breaks rest of automation: format datetime explicitly and add continue_on_error guards.

### Home Assistant Health Monitoring
- Health package monitors primary instance active flag, unexpected reboots, and API connectivity.
- Alerts notify when push pipeline degrades silently due to push-only design.

Common symptoms and fixes:
- Primary instance inactive: re-enable input_boolean.is_primary_active and guard automation.
- Unexpected reboots: check power supply and ESPHome logs for crashes or brownouts.
- API disconnected: verify Wi-Fi, power, and device availability; reconnect if needed.

### IMU and Game Controls
- IMU provides tilt input for games and tap-to-wake functionality.
- Games are fullscreen LVGL pages with local persistence and zero network dependency.

Common symptoms and fixes:
- Game controls unresponsive: verify IMU polling and tap-to-wake settings.
- Orientation issues in portrait games: ensure correct axis mapping and nudge behavior.

## Dependency Analysis
The system relies on tight coupling between Home Assistant automations and ESPHome services:
- Automations serialize data and call specific services
- Services parse payloads and update LVGL UI
- Hardware components must be properly initialized to avoid silent failures

```mermaid
graph LR
HA_Auto["Home Assistant Automations"] --> |Service Calls| ESP_Services["ESPHome Services"]
ESP_Services --> |Parse & Update| LVGL_UI["LVGL UI"]
LVGL_UI --> |User Interaction| ESP_Services
ESP_Services --> |Hardware Control| HW_Init["Hardware Init"]
HW_Init --> |State Feedback| ESP_Services
```

## Performance Considerations
- Traffic pacing: delays between push blocks prevent TCP buffer saturation during I2S audio streaming
- Buffer management: speaker buffer duration prevents audible gaps during network hiccups
- CPU usage: wake-word detection consumes 5-8% CPU; remaining resources handle LVGL and networking
- Boot optimization: blocking delays are necessary for hardware stability despite adding boot time

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide

### API Connection Failures
**Symptoms:**
- Device shows healthy Wi-Fi but no data updates
- Service calls rejected by Home Assistant
- API connections exhausted

**Diagnostic Checklist:**
1. Verify `input_boolean.is_primary_active` is ON
2. Check ESPHome integration options for "Allow service calls"
3. Monitor `binary_sensor.m5stack_tab5_home_assistant_hmi_ha_api_status`
4. Close orphaned `esphome logs` CLI sessions
5. Test service endpoints using Home Assistant Developer Tools

**Resolution Procedures:**
- Enable push gating boolean and guard automation
- Configure ESPHome integration to allow service calls
- Kill stuck CLI processes holding API connections
- Use traffic pacing delays to prevent buffer overflow

**Section sources**
- [docs/troubleshooting.md:23-31](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L23-L31)
- [docs/troubleshooting.md:73-81](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L73-L81)
- [HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_health.yaml:43-82](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_health.yaml#L43-L82)
- [HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_health.yaml:137-176](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_health.yaml#L137-L176)

### Automation Failures
**Symptoms:**
- Calendar/weather data not updating
- Template sensor errors
- Service call validation failures

**Diagnostic Checklist:**
1. Check datetime formatting in templates (`strftime` instead of raw `now()`)
2. Verify entity IDs match your installation
3. Add `continue_on_error: true` to individual actions
4. Use debug markers in real automations for validation

**Resolution Procedures:**
- Format datetime explicitly: `"{{ now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') }}"`
- Replace placeholder entity IDs with actual values
- Insert debug markers directly in production automations
- Validate template rendering in Home Assistant Developer Tools

**Section sources**
- [docs/troubleshooting.md:53-61](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L53-L61)
- [docs/debugging.md:22-31](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L22-L31)
- [HomeAssistant_Config/README.md:118-135](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/README.md#L118-L135)

### Hardware Initialization Problems
**Symptoms:**
- Black screen after software reboot
- Touch controller appears dead
- Audio pop or distortion
- WiFi co-processor not coming up after OTA

**Diagnostic Checklist:**
1. Verify display reset sequence includes blocking delay
2. Check I2C expander communication
3. Test touch controller interrupts and calibration
4. Monitor audio boot sequence timing
5. Use serial console to check WiFi co-processor status

**Resolution Procedures:**
- Ensure blocking delay before display reset in boot sequence
- Power cycle device completely after OTA failures
- Adjust microphone gain staging to analog stage
- Verify amplifier enable timing relative to I2S clock stability

**Section sources**
- [docs/troubleshooting.md:13-20](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L13-L20)
- [docs/troubleshooting.md:93-111](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L93-L111)
- [docs/voice_assistant.md:63-83](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/voice_assistant.md#L63-L83)
- [Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml:116-142](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L116-L142)

### WiFi Connectivity Issues
**Symptoms:**
- Device connects to WiFi but cannot reach Home Assistant
- Fallback AP activates repeatedly
- DHCP lease confusion with other devices

**Diagnostic Checklist:**
1. Check WiFi signal strength and SSID/IP in console overlay
2. Verify ESP32-C6 co-processor link status
3. Monitor for "ESP-Hosted link not yet up" errors
4. Confirm proper power cycling after OTA updates

**Resolution Procedures:**
- Perform full power cycle (unplug USB-C for ~15 seconds)
- Check WiFi co-processor initialization logs
- Verify network configuration and DHCP settings
- Use console overlay to monitor real-time WiFi status

**Section sources**
- [docs/troubleshooting.md:93-111](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L93-L111)
- [docs/debugging.md:9-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L9-L17)

### Home Assistant Integration Failures
**Symptoms:**
- Entities not appearing in Home Assistant
- Service calls failing with authentication errors
- Duplicate entity IDs causing conflicts

**Diagnostic Checklist:**
1. Verify device name matches service call patterns
2. Check for duplicate entity IDs from remote integrations
3. Confirm encryption key configuration
4. Test API connectivity using esphome CLI

**Resolution Procedures:**
- Disable mirroring integrations causing ID collisions
- Update device name consistently across all configurations
- Verify API encryption key matches between HA and device
- Use unique entity IDs in custom integrations

**Section sources**
- [docs/troubleshooting.md:33-40](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L33-L40)

- [HomeAssistant_Config/README.md:151-157](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/README.md#L151-L157)

### Voice Assistant Setup Problems
**Symptoms:**
- Wake word not detected
- STT/TTS pipeline broken
- Audio playback issues
- Pipeline state confusion

**Diagnostic Checklist:**
1. Verify wake-word model loading and activation
2. Check microphone gain staging and noise suppression
3. Monitor voice assistant callback states
4. Test audio pipeline with announcement pipeline format

**Resolution Procedures:**
- Set microphone gain in analog stage (ES7210) rather than digital
- Keep noise suppression level at 0 for optimal Whisper transcription
- Verify announcement pipeline format matches TTS engine capabilities
- Use visual feedback icons to diagnose pipeline state transitions

**Section sources**
- [docs/voice_assistant.md:23-40](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/voice_assistant.md#L23-L40)

- [docs/voice_assistant.md:85-112](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/voice_assistant.md#L85-L112)
- [Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml:290-484](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L290-L484)

### Game Loading Errors
**Symptoms:**
- Games not launching from selector
- Controls unresponsive
- Orientation issues in portrait games
- Memory allocation failures

**Diagnostic Checklist:**
1. Verify game page declarations with skip flags
2. Check IMU calibration and tap-to-wake settings
3. Monitor PSRAM usage and memory allocation
4. Test touch input and gesture recognition

**Resolution Procedures:**
- Ensure game pages are declared with `skip: true` for swipe navigation
- Calibrate IMU for proper tilt sensing in motion-based games
- Optimize memory usage for complex game assets
- Verify touch coordinate mapping for different screen orientations

**Section sources**
- [README.md:116-148](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/README.md#L116-L148)

## Conclusion
This troubleshooting guide consolidates known issues and their solutions across the Tab5 system's major subsystems. By following the diagnostic checklists and resolution procedures outlined here, users can systematically identify and resolve common problems related to API connectivity, automation failures, hardware initialization, and voice assistant setup. The push-only architecture requires careful attention to Home Assistant-side configuration and monitoring, while hardware initialization demands precise timing and sequencing to ensure reliable operation.

## Introduction
This document provides expert-level usage patterns for advanced Tab5 configuration and customization. It focuses on complex entity mapping strategies, custom service handlers, and advanced automation integrations. It also documents extension points for adding custom UI components, integrating new sensors, and implementing custom game modules. Advanced configuration patterns such as conditional entity loading, dynamic component generation, and performance-tuned layouts are covered. Examples include sophisticated automations, custom template sensors, and integration patterns with external systems. Finally, it addresses scaling considerations for large deployments, security hardening techniques, monitoring strategies for production environments, and guidance for contributing custom features while maintaining compatibility across versions.

## Project Structure
The project is organized around a single ESPHome entry point that includes modular packages: hardware, styles, globals, scripts, LVGL layout, API logic, diagnostics, domotique sensors, IMU, HA controls, and alarm. The LVGL layout declares pages and widgets, while the API layer defines services that transform payloads into UI updates via C++ helpers. Home Assistant automations push data to these services using compact payloads.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant"] --> |API services| ESP["ESPHome (Tab5)"]
ESP --> |LVGL updates| UI["LVGL UI"]
subgraph "ESPHome Packages"
HMI["Entry: tab5-ha-hmi.yaml"]
API["API Logic: tab5-api-logic.yaml"]
LVGL["Layout: tab5-lvgl.yaml"]
G["Globals: tab5-globals.yaml"]
S["Scripts: tab5-scripts.yaml"]
C["C++ Helpers: tab5_custom.h/.cpp"]
end
HMI --> API
HMI --> LVGL
HMI --> G
HMI --> S
API --> C
S --> C
LVGL --> C
```

## Core Components
- Entry point and boot orchestration: loads substitutions, initializes hardware, waits for HA API, sets up global contexts, and starts background tasks like calendar prefetch and central rotator.
- LVGL layout: declarative UI with pages, widgets, gestures, and included components; supports swipe pagination and crossfade transitions between forecast and switches layers.
- API logic: service handlers receive payloads, parse them, and call C++ functions to update UI elements safely.
- Globals: shared state variables for page index, climate settings, alerts, volume, assistant popup state, calendar view, and more.
- Scripts: reusable sequences for debounced interactions, voice pipeline control, central panel rotation, dismiss flows, light/climate popups, and game open/close.
- C++ helpers: robust LVGL update functions, color mapping, gesture handling, animation utilities, and centralized semantic colors.

Key responsibilities and extension points:
- Add new UI components by including YAML fragments under LVGL pages or modals and wiring them through scripts or API lambdas.
- Integrate new sensors by exposing entities in user entities and pushing updates via API services or direct sensor bindings.
- Implement custom game modules by creating a dedicated LVGL page, a C++ namespace with open/close/is_open/on_imu, and scripts to launch it from the arcade selector.

## Architecture Overview
The system follows a push-only architecture: Home Assistant detects changes and calls ESPHome API services with compact payloads. The firmware parses and applies updates to LVGL in one pass, minimizing network overhead and ensuring consistent UI state.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome API"
participant CPP as "C++ Helpers"
participant LV as "LVGL UI"
HA->>ESP : "esphome.tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk(payload)"
ESP->>CPP : "parse_and_update_jours_bulk(payload)"
CPP-->>LV : "refresh_daily_forecast(...)"
Note over HA,LV : "Payloads are compact strings parsed once; UI updates are batched."
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Complex Entity Mapping Strategies
- Use substitutions to map Home Assistant entity IDs into ESPHome configuration via a local file. Copy the example and replace placeholders with your entities. This keeps per-home configuration isolated and version-safe.
- For bulk weather and calendar data, build compact payloads in Home Assistant templates and push them via API services. The firmware tokenizes these payloads efficiently and updates multiple UI slots atomically.
- Centralize semantic colors and UI constants in C++ to avoid scattered hex literals and ensure consistency across UI updates.

Practical tips:
- Keep payload formats stable; any change requires synchronized updates in both HA templates and firmware parsers.
- Guard all LVGL updates with boot and connection checks to prevent crashes during HA restarts.
- Prefer bulk pushes over many small calls to reduce TCP socket pressure and improve responsiveness.

**Section sources**
- [user_entities.example.yaml:1-75](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/user_entities.example.yaml#L1-L75)
- [automations_examples.yaml.example:88-145](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L88-L145)

### Custom Service Handlers
- Define new API services in the API logic package to accept payloads and invoke C++ handlers. Each handler should validate inputs, parse payloads, and call LVGL update functions.
- Use lambdas for logic that does not fit cleanly in YAML, such as state machine transitions or conditional UI updates.
- Maintain a clear contract between HA automations and firmware services; renaming either side breaks silent pushes.

Example pattern:
- HA automation builds a string payload and calls a service.
- Firmware lambda parses the payload and calls a C++ function to refresh UI slots.
- UI updates are guarded and batched to minimize repaints.

### Advanced Automation Integrations
- Push-only model: Automations detect state changes and call ESPHome services. Avoid polling from the device.
- Pacing: Insert delays between service blocks and within loops to prevent TCP stack saturation alongside I2S audio streams.
- Template sensors: Preprocess complex data in Home Assistant to keep firmware simple and within memory constraints.

Sophisticated examples:
- Weather and calendar bulk updates with compact payloads.
- Short-path alert/info updates triggered by lightweight events without re-running full weather/calendar scans.
- Rich assistant responses with Markdown text and optional images pushed to the assistant popup.

Guidelines:
- Declare widgets declaratively; move behavior to scripts or C++.
- Reuse existing styles and animations to maintain visual coherence.
- Ensure new components integrate with the central panel rotator if they belong there.

### Integrating New Sensors
- Expose sensors as entities in the user entities file and reference them in automations or scripts.
- For high-frequency or internal sensors, mark them internal to avoid flooding the recorder.
- Push derived values via API services when necessary to keep firmware minimal.

Best practices:
- Keep sensor names stable; use unique IDs.
- Validate states before pushing to avoid NaN or invalid values in the UI.
- Use debounces for interactive controls to reduce network chatter.

### Implementing Custom Game Modules
- Create a dedicated LVGL page with minimal containers; build visuals in C++.
- Implement a namespace with open/close/is_open/on_imu methods and preallocate LVGL objects to avoid heap churn.
- Add scripts to launch the game from the arcade selector and close all games before opening a new one.
- Persist state via NVS and ensure zero HA/network dependency for offline play.

Notes:
- Games run on separate pages marked skip to avoid swipe navigation interference.
- One exception allows orientation switching for specific games; document and guard such changes carefully.

### Advanced Configuration Patterns
- Conditional entity loading: Gate UI updates behind boot_complete and api.connected flags to prevent crashes during HA restarts.
- Dynamic component generation: Build payloads in Home Assistant templates and render them on-device via C++ tokenizers and LVGL updates.
- Performance-tuned layouts: Use global styles, preallocated LVGL pools, and short animations to reduce repaints and CPU load.

Operational tips:
- Keep animations short and amplitudes modest to balance perceived smoothness with rendering cost.
- Batch UI updates after parsing bulk payloads to avoid intermediate redraws.
- Use idle timeouts to return to the main dashboard automatically.

- Maintain consistent dismiss IDs across pushes so users can dismiss banners reliably.

Examples:
- Minute-based rain phrase updates with short payloads.

### Scaling Considerations for Large Deployments
- Reduce payload sizes and increase batching to minimize network overhead.
- Pace pushes to avoid TCP stack saturation, especially when audio streams are active.
- Monitor device health via diagnostics and console overlays; log connectivity issues at boot.

Recommendations:
- Use internal sensors where possible to avoid recorder bloat.
- Centralize style definitions to reduce PSRAM allocations.
- Keep automations idempotent and resilient with continue_on_error and safe defaults.

### Security Hardening Techniques
- Encrypt API traffic using a secret key configured in the API encryption block.
- Restrict access to sensitive services and automate only necessary endpoints.
- Validate all payloads server-side and device-side to prevent malformed data from affecting UI or logic.

Operational notes:
- Rotate secrets regularly and store them securely.
- Audit service contracts and payload formats to avoid regressions.
- Log errors and connectivity issues for faster triage.

- Use the system console overlay to inspect uptime, RSSI, core temperature, and HA connectivity.
- Emit periodic heartbeat events to confirm device availability.
- Track dismiss states and alert visibility to ensure users see critical information.

Practices:
- Refresh console status on overlay open to show current metrics immediately.
- Alert on long periods without API connections to detect zombie states.
- Use global flags to gate UI updates until boot and API are ready.
