```mermaid
C["Ring Overlay<br/>alarm_ring_overlay.yaml"] --> B
D["ESPHome Layer<br/>tab5-alarm.yaml"] --> A
D --> C
D --> B
E["Globals & Persistence<br/>tab5-globals.yaml"] --> D
```

## Core Components
- Alarm settings popup:
  - Enable/disable toggle with icon and label.
  - Fixed time adjustment with hour/minute up/down buttons.
  - Day-of-week chips for fixed-time mode.
  - Mode buttons: Fixed, Workdays, Before opening.
  - Configuration sliders/buttons: lead time, earliest/latest bounds, minimum rest after closing.
  - Next alarm preview panel with “rest day” toggle.
  - Melody selector with previous/next and volume slider; crescendo toggle.
  - Repetition (snooze), max ring duration, appointment reminder lead time.
  - TTS announcement toggle and appointment announcement toggle.
  - Action bar with test, stop, and close.
- Ring overlay:
  - Full-screen overlay with large clock, title, detail text, stop and snooze buttons.
  - Backdrop scrim acts as a tap-to-stop surface.
- Alarm engine:
  - Computes next ring time, handles snooze/dismiss, formats labels, renders UI.
  - Provides melody names, RTTTL scores, and gain/crescendo behavior.
  - Manages upcoming appointments and announcements.

## Architecture Overview
The system uses a unidirectional data flow from ESPHome entities to the C++ engine, then back to LVGL widgets via a render function. All user gestures call ESPHome scripts which update entities and trigger refresh/render.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant U as "User"
participant UI as "Popup/Ring UI"
participant HA as "ESPHome Scripts<br/>tab5-alarm.yaml"
participant ENG as "Alarm Engine<br/>alarm_clock.cpp/.h"
participant G as "Globals<br/>tab5-globals.yaml"
U->>UI : Tap enable/day/mode/slider
UI->>HA : Execute script (e.g., shift_time, toggle_day)
HA->>G : Update globals (mask, skip floor, etc.)
HA->>ENG : g_alarm_cfg updated via refresh
HA->>ENG : alarm_invalidate()
HA->>UI : tab5_alarm_sync_ui -> alarm_render_settings()
Note over UI,ENG : UI reflects current config and computed next alarm
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Alarm Settings Popup Layout
- Enable/disable toggle:
  - Large button toggles the alarm enabled switch and updates icon/label.
  - Triggers refresh to recompute next alarm and status icon.
- Fixed time adjustment:
  - Hour and minute up/down buttons adjust the configured time by 60 minutes or 5 minutes respectively.
  - Uses modulo arithmetic to wrap around midnight safely.
- Day chips:
  - Seven chips for Monday through Sunday; only affect fixed-time mode.
  - Visual highlight indicates active days; inactive days are dimmed.
- Mode buttons:
  - Three modes: Fixed, Workdays, Before opening.
  - Each mode changes how the next alarm is computed and what hints are shown.
- Configuration sliders:
  - Lead time before opening (minutes).
  - Earliest/latest bounds (time pickers).
  - Minimum rest hours after closing (hours).
  - Rest mode toggle: silence vs fixed-time on rest days.
- Next alarm preview:
  - Shows next scheduled time and contextual detail (date, work hours, rest).
  - Includes a toggle to ring on rest days using fixed time.
- Melody and volume:
  - Previous/next cycle through built-in melodies.
  - Volume slider sets alarm-specific volume independently of system volume.
  - Crescendo toggle enables progressive volume increase during ringing.
- Repetition and reminders:
  - Snooze interval and maximum ring duration.
  - Appointment reminder lead time and next appointment indicator.
  - TTS announcement toggle and appointment announcement toggle.
- Action bar:
  - Test alarm triggers the full ring lifecycle without scheduling.
  - Stop halts ringing immediately.
  - Close hides the popup.

**Section sources**
- [alarm_popup.yaml:47-709](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/alarm_popup.yaml#L47-L709)

### Real-Time Preview System
- Next alarm label and detail:
  - Computed by the engine considering mode, calendar, bounds, rest, and snooze.
  - Displays friendly text like “Today HH:MM”, “Tomorrow HH:MM”, or weekday + time.
  - Detail includes date and work schedule context or rest indication.
- Status icon:
  - Shows armed/disarmed state and color-coded readiness (green if next ring is calculable, amber otherwise).

### Melody Selection and Volume Control
- Melody cycling:
  - Buttons cycle through predefined melodies; preview plays the selected melody at current alarm volume.
  - Playback temporarily stops microphone capture to avoid I2S bus conflicts.
- Volume:
  - Slider sets alarm volume percentage; applied to RTTTL gain or media player volume depending on source.
  - Independent from system volume; restored after preview/ring to avoid side effects.
- Crescendo:
  - Progressive volume ramp per cycle until reaching base volume.

### TTS Notification Preferences
- TTS toggle:
  - When enabled, spoken announcements accompany alarm events.
  - Controlled via entity and reflected in UI label/state.
- Appointment announcements:
  - Toggle to announce upcoming appointments with screen and speech outputs.
  - Lead time configurable; next appointment displayed in UI.

### Integration with ESPHome Entities (Two-Way Data Binding)
- Entities:
  - Switches for enable, rest mode, crescendo, TTS, appointment announcements.
  - Datetime entities for fixed time, earliest/latest bounds.
  - Number entities for lead time, rest hours, snooze, max ring, volume, appointment lead.
  - Select entities for mode, melody, and day presets.
  - Text sensor for custom media URL.
- Binding:
  - Every entity change calls a refresh script that copies values into the C++ struct and invalidates cache.
  - Refresh also publishes preset day selections and updates diagnostic sensors.
  - UI sync builds a pointer map to LVGL widgets and calls the render function to repaint everything consistently.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-alarm.yaml:55-345](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-alarm.yaml#L55-L345)

### Rendering System
- Render function:
  - Takes a UI structure with widget pointers and current configuration/values.
  - Updates labels, toggles, highlights, and sliders to reflect the current state.
  - Generates next alarm labels and detail strings from the engine.
- Ring overlay rendering:
  - Shows current time, title, detail, and snooze button label with remaining duration.
  - Refreshed each cycle to keep snooze info accurate.

### Responsive Design Patterns
- Absolute positioning with consistent margins:
  - Two-column layout with fixed widths ensures stable alignment regardless of state changes.
- Consistent styling:
  - Glass cards, modal header, and uniform button styles provide visual coherence.
- Accessibility:
  - Large targets for critical actions (enable toggle, stop/snooze).
  - Clear labels and icons; high contrast for important information.
- State-only visual changes:
  - Active states modify borders and colors without shifting layout, preventing reflow.

## Performance Considerations
- Cached next ring computation:
  - Next alarm timestamp is cached and recalculated only on configuration changes or once per minute for safety.
- Minimal tick overhead:
  - One-second tick performs simple comparisons; heavy calculations are avoided.
- I2S bus management:
  - Microphone and speaker share a single bus; careful start/stop sequencing prevents silent playback or blocking states.
- Efficient UI updates:
  - Render function rebuilds pointer maps on demand and avoids static references to prevent null pointers early in boot.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Alarm does not ring:
  - Ensure the alarm is enabled and at least one day is selected for fixed-time mode, or calendar data is available for workday/opening modes.
  - Verify earliest/latest bounds do not exclude the desired time.
  - Check that the skip floor has not advanced past the intended time due to recent dismissals.
- No sound during preview or ring:
  - If microphone wake word is active, it may block the speaker bus; the system stops microphone capture before playing audio.
  - Confirm alarm volume is above minimum and crescendo is not masking low initial volumes.
- Unexpected repeated ringing:
  - Max ring duration will auto-stop long rings; verify snooze intervals and counts.
- Appointment announcements not appearing:
  - Ensure appointment list is pushed and lead time is set appropriately; check TTS and appointment announcement toggles.

**Section sources**
- [alarm_clock.cpp:155-247](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/alarm_clock.cpp#L155-L247)

## Conclusion
The alarm UI combines a clear, responsive settings popup with a robust ring overlay, backed by a precise C++ engine and seamless ESPHome entity binding. Users can configure alarms for various schedules, enjoy customizable sounds and notifications, and rely on reliable timing even without Home Assistant connectivity. The architecture ensures consistency between UI and engine state, with efficient caching and careful resource management for optimal performance.

## Introduction
This document is a comprehensive API reference for the ESPHome-based Tab5 HMI. It documents:
- All exposed ESPHome API services (tab5_maj_*) used by Home Assistant to push updates to the device UI
- Home Assistant-facing entities for volume control, current screen management, and screen navigation
- Event bus integration patterns and custom events
- Global variables, configuration parameters, and extension points
- Data schemas for weather payloads, climate states, light configurations, and game states
- Authentication, error handling, rate limiting considerations, and version compatibility notes
- Concrete examples of service calls, event handling, and integration patterns for extending the system

The system follows a push-only paradigm: Home Assistant detects changes and calls ESPHome API services; the firmware parses payloads and updates LVGL in one pass without polling.

**Section sources**
- [architecture.md:11-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L11-L17)
- [architecture.md:191-221](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L191-L221)

## Project Structure
The root entry point includes all packages and defines boot behavior. The key packages relevant to this API reference are:
- tab5_api_logic: ESPHome API service handlers that receive payloads and update UI via C++ lambdas
- tab5_ha_controls: Entities exposed to Home Assistant for remote observation/control of the screen
- tab5_globals: Shared global state variables accessed across packages
- tab5_scripts: Reusable scripts for complex actions (debounce, popups, calendar, assistant)
- tab5_lvgl: UI layout and pages (including swipe gestures and central card)
- user_entities: Substitutions mapping HA entity IDs into the firmware

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant"] --> API["ESPHome API Services<br/>tab5_maj_*"]

Logic --> Scripts["Scripts & Lambdas<br/>(tab5-scripts.yaml)"]
Scripts --> Globals["Globals<br/>(tab5-globals.yaml)"]
Scripts --> LVGL["LVGL UI<br/>(tab5-lvgl.yaml)"]
HA --> Controls["HA-facing Entities<br/>(tab5-ha-controls.yaml)"]
Controls --> Scripts
```

## Core Components
- ESPHome API services: Defined under api.services with names starting with tab5_maj_*. Each service receives typed variables or a string payload and executes lambdas to parse data and update LVGL widgets via C++ functions.
- HA-facing entities: Numbers, text sensors, selects, buttons defined in tab5-ha-controls.yaml expose volume, current screen name, and navigation controls to Home Assistant dashboards.
- Global state: tab5-globals.yaml holds shared variables such as active_page, clim modes, system_volume, has_alerts, and panel indices.
- Scripts: tab5-scripts.yaml provides reusable sequences for debouncing, opening/closing popups, calendar rendering, assistant responses, and central rotator logic.

Key responsibilities:
- API services parse payloads and call C++ helpers to update UI safely (null-guarded).
- Scripts encapsulate multi-step actions and debounce interactions to avoid flooding HA.
- Globals provide a single source of truth for cross-component state.

**Section sources**

## Architecture Overview
The system uses a push-only architecture where Home Assistant triggers automations that call ESPHome API services. The firmware processes payloads and updates LVGL directly. Boot sequence initializes hardware, media player, and waits for API connection before emitting a connected event.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome API"
participant LOGIC as "API Logic Handlers"
participant SCRIPTS as "Scripts/Lambdas"
participant LVGL as "LVGL UI"
HA->>ESP : Call service tab5_maj_* with payload
ESP->>LOGIC : Route to handler (lambda)
LOGIC->>SCRIPTS : Execute script if needed
SCRIPTS->>LVGL : Update labels/widgets
LVGL-->>HA : UI reflects latest state
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### ESPHome API Services (tab5_maj_*)
All services are defined under api.services in tab5-api-logic.yaml. They accept variables or a string payload and execute lambdas to parse and update UI.

Service catalog:
- tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk
  - Variables: payload (string)
  - Behavior: Parses hourly forecast bulk data and refreshes hourly forecast UI and page title
- tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk
  - Variables: payload (string)
  - Behavior: Parses daily forecast bulk data, refreshes daily forecast UI, invalidates alarm planning, updates planning banner
- tab5_maj_volet_etat
  - Variables: etat_physique (string)
  - Behavior: Updates shutter state UI and toggles wake word model based on movement
- tab5_maj_clim
  - Variables: target, current, mode, preset, fan, swing (strings)
  - Behavior: Updates climate popup targets, current temp, modes, and triggers recoloring script
- tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france
  - Variables: payload (string)
  - Behavior: Parses Météo-France vigilance data and updates alert slots with appropriate colors
- tab5_maj_probabilites
  - Variables: uv, gel, neige (strings)
  - Behavior: Updates rain prediction icon and humidity-based coloring
- tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle
  - Variables: condition, temperature, humidite (strings)
  - Behavior: Updates current weather display and humidity color
- tab5_maj_pluie_1h
  - Variables: index_5mn, intensite (strings)
  - Behavior: Updates 1-hour rain visualization bars and sets has_rain flag
- tab5_maj_info_texte
  - Variables: texte, couleur, meteo_id (strings)
  - Behavior: Updates central info panel text and dismiss tracking
- tab5_maj_reponse_vocale
  - Variables: texte (string)
  - Behavior: Shows vocal response in central panel for 8 seconds
- tab5_assist_reponse
  - Variables: texte, image_url (string)
  - Behavior: Displays rich assistant response with optional image and opens assistant popup
- tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk
  - Variables: payload (string)
  - Behavior: Parses Home Assistant alerts and updates up to 4 alert slots
- tab5_maj_planning
  - Variables: ligne1, ligne2 (strings)
  - Behavior: Updates planning banner (legacy compatibility)
- tab5_maj_rdv_prochains
  - Variables: payload (string)
  - Behavior: Stores upcoming appointments and updates next appointment sensor
- tab5_maj_calendrier_mois
  - Variables: annee, mois, codes, heures, details (strings)
  - Behavior: Stores monthly calendar data and renders if popup is open
- tab5_maj_calendrier_jour
  - Variables: date, payload (string)
  - Behavior: Renders day detail for calendar popup if visible and matching date

Payload formats:
- Bulk forecasts use semicolon-delimited strings with structured fields per time slot
- Météo-France alerts use pipe-delimited fields for multiple weather conditions
- Calendar data uses hex codes for day types, time ranges, and detailed descriptions

Expected responses:
- Services do not return values; they trigger UI updates through LVGL widget modifications
- Some services trigger side effects like alarm invalidation or wake word model toggling

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:39-529](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L39-L529)

### Home Assistant-Facing Entities
The following entities are exposed to Home Assistant for remote control and monitoring:

Volume Control:
- number.tab5_volume_pct
  - Type: Template number (0-100%)
  - Read: Returns system_volume * 100
  - Write: Calls tab5_volume_apply script with normalized volume
  - Behavior: Debounces volume changes and syncs UI widgets

Current Screen Management:
- text_sensor.tab5_screen_name
  - Type: Template text sensor
  - Read: Reports currently displayed screen (home, games, popups, console)
  - Priority: Checks overlay layers first, then dashboard panels

Screen Navigation:
- select.tab5_goto_screen
  - Type: Template select with predefined options
  - Options: Home, Voice Assistant, Calendar, Alarm, Climate, Plants, TV Remote, System Console
  - Behavior: Closes games if needed, navigates to target screen, resets activity timer

Calendar Refresh:
- button.tab5_reload_calendar
  - Type: Template button
  - Action: Prefetches current and next month calendar data

### Event Bus Integration
Custom events:
- esphome.tab5_connected
  - Emitted when device successfully connects to Home Assistant API during boot
  - Used by health monitoring automations to detect connectivity

Event flow:
- Device boots and waits for API connection
- Once connected, emits esphome.tab5_connected event
- Health monitoring can subscribe to this event for status tracking

### Global Variables and Configuration
Key globals used across components:
- active_page: Current main page index
- clim_target_temp, clim_hvac_mode, clim_preset_mode, clim_fan_mode, clim_swing_mode: Climate control state
- system_volume, system_muted: Audio control state
- has_alerts, has_rain, has_info: Central panel content flags
- ha_alert_id_0..3, has_ha_alert_0..3: Individual alert tracking
- forecast_page_index: Weather forecast page selection
- assist_popup_open, assist_text_size: Voice assistant popup state
- cal_view_year, cal_view_month, cal_detail_date: Calendar popup state
- alarm-related globals: ringing state, scheduling, and skip logic

Configuration parameters:
- Entity substitutions from user_entities.yaml map HA entities into firmware
- API encryption key configured via secrets
- Reboot timeout set to prevent zombie devices

### Data Schemas

Weather Payloads:
- Hourly forecast: Semicolon-delimited string with time, temperature, probability, and icon data
- Daily forecast: Semicolon-delimited string with day name, condition, min/max temperatures, and work hours
- Météo-France alerts: Pipe-delimited string with 11 fields covering wind, flood, storms, rain, snow, cold, waves, heat, avalanches

Climate States:
- target: Target temperature as string (parsed to float)
- current: Current temperature as string (parsed to float)  
- mode: HVAC mode (cool, heat, dry, fan_only, off)
- preset: Preset mode (eco, away, boost, none)
- fan: Fan mode (auto, low, quiet, etc.)
- swing: Swing mode (off, vertical, horizontal, both, windnice)

Light Configurations:
- Brightness: 0-255 integer value from HA light entity
- State: on/off boolean
- Entity ID: Mapped from user_entities.yaml substitutions

Game States:
- Game-specific state managed within isolated namespaces (Marble, Arkanoid, Pinball, Lode, Go, Trivia, Draughts, Chess)
- Each game maintains its own NVS persistence and LVGL state
- No direct API exposure for game state management

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:41-529](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L41-L529)
- [user_entities.example.yaml:18-75](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/user_entities.example.yaml#L18-L75)

### Authentication Methods
- ESPHome API encryption using key from !secret api_encryption_key
- Connection authentication handled by ESPHome framework
- No additional application-level authentication implemented

### Error Handling Patterns
- Null checks before LVGL operations to prevent crashes during boot or disconnection
- Graceful degradation when HA is unavailable (device remains functional offline)
- Health monitoring automations detect and alert on various failure scenarios
- Service handlers include defensive programming with early returns for null pointers

### Rate Limiting Considerations
- Volume changes debounced at 150ms to prevent flooding HA
- Light brightness changes debounced at 200ms  
- Climate temperature changes debounced at 250ms
- Push automation pacing: 1 second between service blocks, 150ms between items in loops
- Prevents TCP stack exhaustion when combined with I2S audio streaming

### Version Compatibility Notes
- Minimum ESPHome version: 2026.7.0 required for official ST7123 driver and audio features
- Backward compatibility maintained for legacy services like tab5_maj_planning
- Entity ID mappings externalized to user_entities.yaml for easy adaptation

## Performance Considerations
- Push-only architecture eliminates polling overhead
- Bulk payload processing reduces network calls and UI redraws
- LVGL animations optimized with shorter durations and reduced amplitudes
- Memory-efficient style definitions using global references instead of per-widget allocations
- Adaptive IMU polling reduces CPU usage when no tilt-controlled games are active
- Pre-allocated LVGL pools in games eliminate heap allocation during gameplay

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and solutions:
- Device appears frozen: Check if push automations are disabled (is_primary_active)
- API connection failures: Monitor esphome.tab5_connected event and health notifications
- Volume inconsistencies: Ensure tab5_volume_apply script is used consistently across all volume controls
- Calendar not updating: Verify SNTP time synchronization and calendar prefetch scripts
- Games not closing properly: Use tab5_games_close_all script before opening new games

Health monitoring automations provide:
- Primary instance inactive detection (5+ minutes)
- Unexpected reboot detection via uptime monitoring
- API disconnection alerts (2+ minutes)

- [tab5_health.yaml:43-176](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_health.yaml#L43-L176)

## Conclusion
The Tab5 HMI implements a robust push-only architecture with well-defined API services, comprehensive Home Assistant integration, and careful attention to performance and reliability. The modular design allows for easy extension while maintaining stability through defensive programming and health monitoring.

Key strengths:
- Clear separation between API layer, business logic, and UI presentation
- Comprehensive error handling and graceful degradation
- Efficient resource usage through bulk processing and optimized animations
- Extensible architecture supporting custom functionality through scripts and C++ extensions

```yaml
service: esphome.tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk
```

```yaml
service: esphome.tab5_maj_clim

  fan: "auto"
```

```yaml
target:
  entity_id: select.tab5_goto_screen
data:
  option: "Calendrier"
```

- UI components: Add new LVGL components following the declarative pattern

- Health monitoring: Add new automations in HomeAssistant_Config/packages for custom health checks

## Introduction
This document provides comprehensive configuration documentation for the Tab5 system. It covers global variables, user entity mappings, WiFi credentials, and system settings. For each parameter group, it explains validation rules, defaults, acceptable ranges, environment-specific configuration, secrets management, security considerations, runtime behavior (including hot-reload and restart requirements), and performance tuning options. Examples are provided as references to existing YAML files with correct syntax and indentation.

## Project Structure
The Tab5 ESPHome project is composed of a root entry file that includes modular packages:
- Root entrypoint composes substitutions, includes custom C++ modules, defines boot sequence, and loads packages.
- Packages encapsulate concerns: globals, hardware, LVGL UI, API services, scripts, sensors, styles, alarm logic, IMU, and HA controls.

## Core Components
This section summarizes the main configuration areas and their roles:
- Global variables: shared state across components (page index, climate modes, alerts, volume).

- API logic: Home Assistant services that update UI and internal state.
- Scripts: reusable sequences for complex actions (volume debounce, calendar rendering, alarm flows).
- Sensors: diagnostics (WiFi, uptime, core temp, SNTP) and home automation entities (lights, climate, plants).
- Alarm: wake-up schedule, melody, TTS announcements, snooze, and ring control.
- User entities: mapping from Tab5 to Home Assistant entity IDs.

## Architecture Overview
Configuration drives runtime behavior through a layered flow:
- Boot sequence initializes hardware, LVGL, and scripts; sets up time sync and pre-fetches data.
- Globals hold mutable state used by UI and scripts.
- API services receive payloads from Home Assistant and update globals/UI via C++ helpers.
- Scripts orchestrate complex interactions (e.g., calendar rendering, alarm ring loop).
- Sensors push updates into UI or trigger events.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Boot as "Boot (tab5-ha-hmi)"
participant HW as "Hardware (tab5-hardware)"
participant LV as "LVGL (tab5-lvgl)"
participant API as "API Services (tab5-api-logic)"
participant S as "Scripts (tab5-scripts)"
participant G as "Globals (tab5-globals)"
Boot->>HW : Initialize display/audio/PSRAM
Boot->>LV : Resume LVGL, turn on backlight
Boot->>S : Run initial scripts (alarm refresh, rotator)
API-->>G : Update globals via services
S-->>LV : Render UI using globals
S-->>API : Call HA services when needed
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Global Variables (Shared State)
Global variables define shared state between UI, scripts, and services. They include page indices, climate modes, alert flags, volume state, assistant popup state, calendar view state, and alarm-related flags.

Key parameters and behaviors:
- active_page: current page index (int, default 0).
- clim_target_temp: target temperature (float, default 20.0).
- volet_target_open / volet_en_mouvement: shutter target and movement flags (bool).
- va_stop_armed: voice assistant stop flag (bool).
- clim_hvac_mode / clim_preset_mode / clim_fan_mode / clim_swing_mode: HVAC state strings.
- has_alerts / has_rain / has_info: central panel content flags (bool).
- ha_alert_id_0..3: per-slot alert identifiers (string).
- system_volume / system_muted: volume level and mute state (float, bool).
- assist_popup_open / assist_text_size: assistant popup visibility and text size (bool, int).
- cal_view_year / cal_view_month / cal_detail_date: calendar navigation state (int, string).
- alarm_ringing / alarm_ring_cycle / alarm_ring_started / alarm_days_mask / alarm_skip_before: alarm runtime state and schedule mask (bool, int, uint32_t, uint8_t).

Validation and persistence:
- Types enforce value constraints at the ESPHome level (int, float, bool, std::string, uint32_t, uint8_t).
- restore_value toggles persistence across reboots for selected globals (e.g., conversation_mode, assist_text_size, alarm_days_mask, alarm_skip_before).

Runtime impact:
- UI reads these globals to render status, panels, and popups.
- Scripts update globals during interactions (e.g., volume changes, alert dismissals).
- API services write globals based on payloads (e.g., climate modes, alerts).

Hot-reload vs restart:
- Changing globals via services or scripts takes effect immediately without restart.
- Some structural changes (e.g., adding new globals) require recompilation and OTA.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-globals.yaml:12-236](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-globals.yaml#L12-L236)

### User Entity Mappings
User entity mappings connect Tab5 to Home Assistant entities. The example file lists placeholders for device trackers, media players, lights, climate, sensors, and plant metrics.

Parameters and usage:
- entity_tracker_pc / entity_tracker_tv: presence/status entities.
- entity_light_chambre / entity_light_salon / entity_light_bureau: light entities.
- entity_climate_salon: climate entity for temperature control.
- entity_tab5_pipeline_select: assistant pipeline selector.
- entity_primary_active / entity_push_automation: flags controlling push automations.
- Temperature/humidity sensors for rooms and plants.
- Plant moisture sensors (up to 5) and detailed metrics (EC, lux, temp, battery).

Validation and defaults:
- Values are substituted into ESPHome config via substitutions; must be valid Home Assistant entity IDs.
- Defaults are not enforced by ESPHome; incorrect IDs will cause missing states or errors.

Environment-specific configuration:
- Copy user_entities.example.yaml to user_entities.yaml and fill in your environment’s entity IDs.
- This file is gitignored alongside secrets.yaml to avoid committing sensitive mappings.

Security considerations:
- Keep user_entities.yaml out of version control.
- Ensure entity IDs do not expose internal topology beyond what is necessary.

Hot-reload vs restart:
- Updating entity IDs requires recompilation and OTA deployment.

Example reference:
- See the example mapping structure and comments for guidance.

**Section sources**
- [user_entities.example.yaml:1-75](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/user_entities.example.yaml#L1-L75)

### WiFi Credentials and Network Settings
WiFi configuration is centralized in the diagnostics sensors package and uses secrets for SSID/passwords. An AP fallback is configured for recovery.

Parameters:
- wifi.ssid / wifi.password: loaded from secrets.
- wifi.power_save_mode: set to NONE for consistent performance.
- wifi.ap.ssid / wifi.ap.password: fallback AP credentials from secrets.

Validation and ranges:
- SSID/password must match your network; invalid values prevent connection.
- AP password should be strong and unique for recovery access.

Environment-specific configuration:
- Store credentials in secrets.yaml and reference them via !secret.
- AP credentials are separate from primary network credentials.

Security considerations:
- Never commit secrets.yaml.
- Use strong passwords for AP and restrict physical access to the device.

Performance considerations:
- power_save_mode: NONE avoids sleep-induced latency.
- Ensure stable Wi-Fi; weak signals can degrade OTA and API connectivity.

Hot-reload vs restart:
- Changing Wi-Fi credentials requires reboot to reconnect.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml:16-31](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml#L16-L31)

### System Settings and Hardware Configuration
Core system settings include board, framework options, logger, PSRAM, OTA, safe mode, I2C, display, touch, audio, and media player.

Key parameters:
- esp32.board: esp32-p4-evboard; flash_size: 16MB; framework: esp-idf with advanced options (TCP window, yield during erase, CPU frequency).
- esp32_hosted: variant esp32c6 with SDIO pins and PSRAM usage.
- logger.level: INFO; baud_rate: 115200; hardware_uart: USB_SERIAL_JTAG; tx_buffer_size: 2048.
- psram.mode: hex; speed: 200MHz.
- ota.platform: esphome; password from secrets; on_end triggers restart button.
- safe_mode.num_attempts: 10; boot_is_good_after: 30s.
- i2c bus: sda/scl pins, frequency 400kHz; PI4IOE5V6408 expanders.
- display: mipi_dsi with ST7123 model, reset via expander, pixel mode RGB 16-bit.
- touchscreen: st7123 with interrupt/reset pins and calibration bounds.
- output/light: backlight PWM and monochromatic light with LVGL resume/pause hooks.
- i2s_audio/microphone/audio_adc/audio_dac/speaker: microphone and speaker setup with sample rates, bit depth, and buffer duration.
- media_player: speaker-based player with announcement pipeline format FLAC, sample rate 24000 Hz, mono.

Validation and ranges:
- Pins and frequencies must match hardware; incorrect values can cause crashes or non-functional peripherals.
- Audio buffer_duration and timeout affect playback stability; defaults tuned for streaming robustness.

Environment-specific configuration:
- Display model and pins are fixed for this hardware revision.
- Audio gain moved to analog stage (mic_gain) for better SNR; digital gain kept minimal.

Security considerations:
- OTA password stored in secrets.yaml.
- verify_ssl disabled for online_image fetching; consider enabling if serving images over HTTPS with trusted certs.

Performance considerations:
- PSRAM enabled for large buffers and image decoding.
- TCP window increased for stable OTA transfers.
- Logger buffer sized to reduce dropped logs under load.

Hot-reload vs restart:
- Most hardware changes require rebuild and OTA.
- Media player format/sample rate changes may require restart to apply cleanly.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-hardware.yaml:9-522](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L9-L522)

### LVGL UI Configuration and Tokens
LVGL configuration defines pages, widgets, gestures, modal geometry, fonts, colors, and style definitions.

Key parameters:
- lvgl.pages: main page with gesture handling and widget tree; additional game pages with skip flag to bypass swipe navigation.
- lvgl.rotation: 270 degrees; color_depth: 16; buffer_size: 100%.
- tab5-ui-tokens: modal dimensions, header height, body offsets, calendar grid offset, assistant response Y position.
- tab5-styles: color palette, fonts (Roboto, Roboto Mono, Material Design Icons, weather icons, chess pieces), LVGL style definitions (glassmorphism cards, buttons, modals).

Validation and ranges:
- Modal tokens must remain consistent; changing modal_card_w/h affects all popups.
- Font glyph sets are trimmed to required characters to save flash.
- Style definitions use named colors; avoid hardcoding hex values in UI code.

Environment-specific configuration:
- Fonts and icons are embedded; ensure glyphs cover required locales.
- Game pages are isolated and toggle rotation only during gameplay.

Performance considerations:
- Buffer size 100% reduces redraw artifacts but increases RAM usage.
- Rotation support enabled via explicit rotation key to allow runtime changes for games.

Hot-reload vs restart:
- Widget changes and style updates require rebuild and OTA.
- Runtime rotation changes occur during gameplay via LVGL component handle.

### API Services and Data Flow
API services define the contract between Home Assistant and Tab5. Each service receives a payload and updates UI/state via C++ helpers.

Services and parameters:
- tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk: hourly forecast bulk update (payload string).
- tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk: daily forecast bulk update (payload string); also invalidates alarm planning cache.
- tab5_maj_volet_etat: shutter state update (etat_physique string); enables/disables wake word “Stop” model during movement.
- tab5_maj_clim: climate update (target/current/mode/preset/fan/swing strings); recolors UI based on modes.
- tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france: weather alert parsing (payload string with pipe-delimited fields); updates central panel and date color.
- tab5_maj_probabilites: UV/frost/snow probabilities (uv/gel/neige strings); updates rain icon color.
- tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle: current weather (condition/temperature/humidite strings); updates humidity-based icon color.
- tab5_maj_pluie_1h: 1-hour rain intensity bars (index_5mn/intensite strings); updates bar heights and has_rain flag.
- tab5_maj_info_texte: info panel text (texte/couleur/meteo_id strings); supports local dismissal tracking.
- tab5_maj_reponse_vocale: vocal response text (texte string); shows central panel response.
- tab5_assist_reponse: rich assistant response (texte/image_url strings); opens assistant popup and optionally downloads image.
- tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk: Home Assistant alerts bulk update (payload string); maps to per-slot UI and dismissal state.
- tab5_maj_planning: legacy planning banner (ligne1/ligne2 strings); now derived locally after daily forecast updates.
- tab5_maj_rdv_prochains: upcoming appointments (payload string); stores list and schedules announcements.
- tab5_maj_calendrier_mois: monthly calendar data (annee/mois/codes/heures/details strings); caches and renders month if visible.
- tab5_maj_calendrier_jour: day detail (date/payload string); renders details if popup matches current date.

Validation and ranges:
- Payload formats are strict; mismatches can truncate or misparse data.
- String lengths are bounded (e.g., 1024 bytes for weather alerts) to prevent overflow.

Runtime behavior:
- Services update globals and call C++ functions to refresh UI elements.
- Some services trigger side effects (e.g., invalidating alarm planning, enabling wake word models).

Hot-reload vs restart:
- Service definitions take effect after OTA deployment.
- Payload contracts must remain compatible; changes require updating both HA automations and firmware.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:11-529](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L11-L529)

### Scripts and Reusable Actions
Scripts encapsulate complex sequences such as closing games, opening specific games, managing voice assistant interruptions, debouncing volume/brightness/climate controls, rotating central panels, and rendering calendars.

Key scripts:
- tab5_games_close_all: closes any open game overlay to prevent timers running concurrently.
- tab5_marble_open / arkanoid_open / lode_open / go_open / trivia_open / chess_open / draughts_open / pinball_open: open respective games with injected LVGL pointers and fonts.
- tab5_arcade_open: opens arcade selector after closing all games.
- tab5_volet_end_movement / tab5_volet_stop_voice_feedback: end shutter movement and provide voice feedback.
- tab5_vocal_arm_stop / disarm_stop / interrupt / interrupt_and_listen: manage voice assistant interruption and listening state.
- tab5_assist_toggle: click-to-converse behavior.
- tab5_debounce_volume_set / tab5_debounce_light_brightness / tab5_debounce_clim_temp: debounce user inputs to reduce network calls.
- tab5_volume_apply: central volume application with clamping, UI sync, and device push debouncing.
- tab5_clim_recolor: centralized climate UI recoloring based on modes and presets.
- tab5_central_rotator_auto: auto-advance central panel every 8 seconds when idle.
- tab5_show_vocal_response: pause rotator, show response, then resume.
- tab5_calendar_open / tab5_cal_render / tab5_cal_prev / tab5_cal_next: calendar navigation and rendering with caching and prefetching.

Validation and ranges:
- Parameters are typed (float, int, string) and clamped where applicable (e.g., volume 0–1).
- Debounce delays balance responsiveness and network efficiency.

Runtime behavior:
- Scripts interact with globals, LVGL, media player, and Home Assistant services.
- Calendar rendering uses stale-while-revalidate caching to open instantly and refresh in background.

Hot-reload vs restart:
- Script changes require OTA deployment.
- Runtime state changes (e.g., volume, calendar view) take effect immediately.

**Section sources**

### Sensors and Diagnostics
Diagnostics sensors expose system health and network status. Home automation sensors map to UI updates.

Key parameters:
- wifi_info: IP address and SSID sensors.
- uptime, wifi_signal, internal_temperature: periodic updates with interval-based UI refresh.
- debug.free / debug.loop_time: memory and loop timing diagnostics.
- sntp.time: time synchronization with timezone Europe/Paris; on_time_sync updates clock UI immediately.
- homeassistant entities: PC/TV status, light states and brightness, phone battery, room temperatures/humidity, plant moisture and metrics.

Validation and ranges:
- Sensor intervals balance freshness and resource usage (e.g., 60s for uptime/RSSI/temp).
- Home Assistant entity IDs must exist; missing entities result in no updates.

Runtime behavior:
- on_value handlers call C++ helpers to update UI labels and colors.
- Reconnection to HA triggers calendar prefetch for instant popup availability.

Hot-reload vs restart:
- Adding new sensors requires rebuild and OTA.
- Interval changes take effect after deployment.

### Alarm and Wake-Up Configuration
Alarm configuration exposes settings to Home Assistant and manages ring logic, melodies, TTS announcements, and appointment reminders.

Key parameters:
- tab5_alarm_enabled: enable/disable alarm (switch).
- tab5_alarm_time: scheduled time (datetime.time).
- tab5_alarm_early / tab5_alarm_late: earliest/latest allowed times (datetime.time).
- tab5_alarm_lead: lead time before opening (number, min 0–240, step 5).
- tab5_alarm_rest_hours: minimum rest after closing (number, min 0–14, step 1).
- tab5_alarm_snooze_min: snooze interval (number, min 1–30, step 1).
- tab5_alarm_max_ring: maximum ring duration (number, min 1–60, step 1).
- tab5_alarm_volume: ring volume percentage (number, min 10–100, step 5).
- tab5_rdv_lead: appointment announcement lead time (number, min 0–120, step 5).
- tab5_alarm_mode: fixed time/workdays/opening mode (select).
- tab5_alarm_melody: melody selection (select).
- tab5_alarm_days: day presets including custom mask (select).
- tab5_alarm_media_url: optional custom ringtone URL (text).

Validation and ranges:
- Min/max/step constraints enforced by ESPHome number/select types.
- Time boundaries are corrected internally if inconsistent (latest < earliest).

Runtime behavior:
- All changes trigger tab5_alarm_refresh to update internal config and UI.
- Ring loop manages I2S bus sharing with microphone, ensuring audible rings even when wake word is active.
- Appointment list stored locally; announcements triggered independently of HA availability.

Hot-reload vs restart:
- Setting changes take effect immediately via scripts.
- Structural changes (new entities) require OTA.

## Performance Considerations
- PSRAM usage: Enabled for SDIO buffers and image decoding; improves stability and frees internal SRAM.
- TCP window: Increased to 16KB for stable OTA transfers.
- Logger buffer: Sized to 2048 bytes to reduce dropped logs under load.
- Audio buffering: Speaker buffer duration set to 500ms to mitigate streaming hiccups; sample rate aligned with TTS engines.
- Debounce: Volume, brightness, and climate controls debounce to reduce network traffic and improve UX.
- Calendar caching: Stale-while-revalidate pattern ensures instant popup opens with background refresh.
- I2S bus mutex: Microphone and speaker share a single bus; alarm ring loop explicitly manages bus access to avoid silence.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common configuration issues and resolutions:
- Black screen after software reboot:
  - Cause: Display reset pin via I2C expander needs stabilization time.
  - Fix: Blocking delay in boot sequence (priority 700) ensures expander stabilizes before display init.
  - Reference: Boot sequence and logger comments explain the critical delay requirement.

- OTA instability:
  - Cause: Small TCP window or CPU yielding during flash erase.
  - Fix: Advanced SDK options increase TCP window and enable yield during erase; ensure stable Wi-Fi.

- Audio glitches during TTS:
  - Cause: Streaming over WiFi co-processor causes hiccups; insufficient buffer leads to micro-stutters.
  - Fix: Increase speaker buffer duration; align sample rate with TTS engine; avoid excessive noise suppression.

- Wake word conflicts with alarm ring:
  - Cause: Shared I2S bus; microphone capture blocks speaker.
  - Fix: Alarm ring loop stops microphone before playing ring; ensures audible rings even with wake word active.

- Missing Home Assistant entities:
  - Cause: Incorrect or missing entity IDs in user_entities.yaml.
  - Fix: Verify entity IDs in Home Assistant; ensure substitutions are correctly loaded.

- Calendar popup slow to open:
  - Cause: No cached data for current month.
  - Fix: Pre-fetch on boot and on HA reconnection; cache eviction keeps only adjacent months.

- Volume drift between UI and device:
  - Cause: Multiple sliders writing volume independently.
  - Fix: Centralized tab5_volume_apply script clamps values, syncs UI, and debounces device pushes.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-ha-hmi.yaml:66-116](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/tab5-ha-hmi.yaml#L66-L116)

## Conclusion
The Tab5 configuration is modular and well-structured, separating concerns into globals, hardware, UI, API, scripts, sensors, and alarm logic. Parameters are validated through ESPHome types and ranges, with defaults chosen for stability and usability. Secrets and user entities are externalized for security and environment adaptability. Runtime behavior is driven by scripts and API services that update globals and UI, with careful attention to performance and reliability. Troubleshooting guidance addresses known pitfalls such as display initialization, OTA stability, audio streaming, and wake word conflicts.

## Introduction
This document catalogs all global variables defined for the Tab5 system, explains their purpose, data types, default values, and restore behavior. It also documents naming conventions, categorizes variables by functional area (UI state, climate control, weather alerts, alarm system, voice assistant), shows how they are accessed and modified across the codebase, discusses memory implications, and provides troubleshooting guidance for persistence and state synchronization issues.

## Project Structure
Global state is centralized in a single ESPHome globals section and consumed by UI scripts, API logic, alarm logic, and Home Assistant controls. The main entrypoint includes packages and initializes boot-time state that depends on these globals.

## Core Components
The Tab5 system defines a cohesive set of global variables to coordinate UI state, device control, and cross-package communication. They are declared in one place and referenced from multiple modules to ensure consistency.

Key categories and representative variables:
- UI state: active_page, forecast_page_index, current_central_panel, show_switches, assist_popup_open, assist_text_size, conversation_mode, is_showing_vocal_response, is_showing_temp_planning
- Climate control: clim_target_temp, clim_hvac_mode, clim_preset_mode, clim_fan_mode, clim_swing_mode
- Weather alerts: has_alerts, has_rain, has_info, has_ha_alert_0..3, ha_alert_id_0..3, temp_dismiss_alert_id, info_meteo_dismiss_id, tab5_dismissed_local, global_neige, global_humidite
- Alarm system: alarm_ringing, alarm_ring_scheduled, alarm_ring_cycle, alarm_ring_started, alarm_days_mask, alarm_skip_before, alarm_rdv_speech, alarm_rdv_screen, alarm_ring_sub
- Voice assistant: va_stop_armed, assist_popup_open, assist_text_size, conversation_mode, is_showing_vocal_response
- System and media: system_volume, system_muted, volume_push_ts, boot_complete, plan_ligne_1, plan_ligne_2, plan_cycle_counter, current_light_entity, temp_planning_text

Naming conventions:
- snake_case identifiers with clear semantic prefixes:
  - clim_* for climate-related settings
  - volet_* for shutter/blind state
  - has_* flags for presence of alerts or conditions
  - ha_alert_* for Home Assistant alert slots
  - alarm_* for alarm engine state
  - assist_* for voice assistant UI/state
  - system_* for device/system settings
  - forecast_* for forecast page navigation
  - plan_* for planning banner text and counters

Restore behavior:
- restore_value: true means the variable survives reboots and is restored from NVS; false means it resets to initial_value at boot.
- Examples:
  - conversation_mode: restore_value: true (user preference persists)
  - active_page: restore_value: false (transient UI page)
  - assist_text_size: restore_value: true (user preference)
  - alarm_days_mask: restore_value: true (alarm configuration)
  - Most transient runtime flags (e.g., alarm_ringing, assist_popup_open) have restore_value: false.

Memory implications:
- int, float, bool, uint8_t, uint32_t: small footprint, suitable for frequently updated state.
- std::string: dynamic heap allocation; used for IDs, messages, and temporary buffers. Prefer short-lived strings for transient payloads (e.g., temp_dismiss_alert_id).
- Frequent writes to std::string can cause fragmentation; keep them minimal and reuse where possible.
- Persisted globals (restore_value: true) consume NVS space; limit the number and size of persistent strings.

When to use restore_value: true vs false:
- Use true for user preferences and configuration that should survive reboot (conversation_mode, assist_text_size, alarm_days_mask, alarm_skip_before).
- Use false for transient runtime flags that must reset on boot (active_page, assist_popup_open, alarm_ringing, boot_complete, volume_push_ts).

Examples of access and modification patterns:
- UI scripts read/write globals to reflect and drive LVGL state (e.g., forecast_page_index, current_central_panel).
- API logic updates globals based on Home Assistant pushes (e.g., clim_target_temp, clim modes, alert flags).
- Alarm scripts toggle alarm-specific globals during ring cycles and snooze.
- HA controls expose system_volume and mirror changes back to the device.

## Architecture Overview
The global variables act as the shared contract between UI, automation, and hardware layers. Boot sequence initializes critical globals and ensures consistent state before rendering.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Boot as "Boot (tab5-ha-hmi.yaml)"
participant Globals as "Globals (tab5-globals.yaml)"
participant Scripts as "Scripts (tab5-scripts.yaml)"
participant API as "API Logic (tab5-api-logic.yaml)"
participant Alarm as "Alarm (tab5-alarm.yaml)"
participant HA as "HA Controls (tab5-ha-controls.yaml)"
Boot->>Globals : Initialize globals (initial_value)
Boot->>Boot : Set boot_complete = true
Boot->>Alarm : Restore skip floor from NVS
Boot->>Scripts : Start rotator/auto behaviors
HA-->>Globals : Read system_volume, forecast_page_index
API-->>Globals : Update clim_target_temp, modes, alert flags
Scripts-->>Globals : Update UI state (forecast_page_index, panels)
Alarm-->>Globals : Toggle alarm_ringing, alarm_ring_cycle
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### UI State Globals
- active_page: Tracks the top-level page index. Default 0. Not restored. Used when switching pages via LVGL.
- forecast_page_index: Current forecast subpage (hourly/daily). Default 2. Not restored. Updated by swipe gestures and auto-rotator.
- current_central_panel: Index of central panel within forecast page 2. Default 0. Not restored. Updated by rotation and dismiss actions.
- show_switches: Boolean flag to show HA switches panel. Default false. Not restored.
- assist_popup_open: Boolean indicating if voice assistant popup is open. Default false. Not restored.
- assist_text_size: Font size preference for assistant popup. Default 1. Restored.
- conversation_mode: Boolean toggling discussion mode. Default false. Restored.
- is_showing_vocal_response: Boolean while vocal response overlay is displayed. Default false. Not restored.
- is_showing_temp_planning: Boolean while temporary planning banner is shown. Default false. Not restored.

Access and modification examples:
- Swipe gesture updates forecast_page_index and triggers UI refresh.
- Rotator script advances current_central_panel and syncs UI context.
- Assistant popup sets assist_popup_open and adjusts assist_text_size.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["User swipe"]) --> CheckPage{"forecast_page_index == 2?"}
CheckPage --> |Yes| Advance["Advance central panel"]
CheckPage --> |No| UpdateForecast["Update hourly/daily view"]
Advance --> SyncUI["Sync central panel UI"]
UpdateForecast --> RefreshTitle["Refresh page title"]
SyncUI --> End(["Done"])
RefreshTitle --> End
```

### Climate Control Globals
- clim_target_temp: Target temperature (float). Default 20.0. Restored implicitly via entity state but not explicitly flagged here.
- clim_hvac_mode: HVAC mode string (off/cool/heat/dry/fan_only). Default "off".
- clim_preset_mode: Preset string (none/eco/away/boost). Default "none".
- clim_fan_mode: Fan mode string (auto/low/quiet/Silence). Default "auto".
- clim_swing_mode: Swing mode string (stop/vertical/horizontal/both/windnice/on/3d). Default "stop".

Access and modification examples:
- UI buttons increment/decrement clim_target_temp optimistically and debounce to send climate.set_temperature.
- HA push service tab5_maj_clim updates clim_target_temp and modes, then triggers recolor script.

```mermaid
HA-->>API : Push new state
API->>Globals : Set clim_target_temp, clim_hvac_mode, clim_preset_mode, clim_fan_mode, clim_swing_mode
API->>Script : Execute recolor
```

### Alarm System Globals
- alarm_ringing: True while alarm is actively ringing. Default false. Not restored.
- alarm_ring_scheduled: True only for scheduled alarms (not test). Default false. Not restored.
- alarm_ring_cycle: Cycle counter for crescendo volume. Default 0. Not restored.
- alarm_ring_started: Timestamp of ring start for max duration guard. Default 0. Not restored.
- alarm_days_mask: Bitmask of enabled days (bit 0 = Monday). Default 0x1F. Restored.
- alarm_skip_before: NVS mirror to prevent re-ringing shortly after stop. Default 0. Restored.
- alarm_rdv_speech, alarm_rdv_screen, alarm_ring_sub: Temporary strings for speech/screen payloads and next detail. Defaults empty. Not restored.

Access and modification examples:
- Ring start sets alarm_ringing, clears microphone, opens overlay, starts loop.
- Loop increments cycle, updates gain, refreshes overlay, waits for silence, repeats until stop/snooze/max.
- Refresh script restores skip floor from NVS and recalculates next alarm time.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Alarm as "Alarm Script"
participant Globals as "Globals"
participant Speaker as "Speaker/Media"
participant Micro as "Microphone"
Alarm->>Globals : Set alarm_ringing = true
Alarm->>Micro : Stop capture
Alarm->>Speaker : Prepare rtttl/media
loop Until stop/snooze/max
Alarm->>Globals : Increment alarm_ring_cycle
Alarm->>Speaker : Play melody with gain
Alarm->>Micro : Stop capture before play
Alarm->>Globals : Refresh overlay state
end
Alarm->>Globals : Clear alarm_ringing
```

- UI scripts and API logic both read/write shared globals; ensure updates are idempotent and ordered (e.g., API updates precede UI recolor).
- Alarm loop reads globals and modifies UI overlays; ensure no direct LVGL calls in alarm core logic.

External dependencies:
- Home Assistant services push data into globals via API logic.
- LVGL components depend on globals for state synchronization.

## Performance Considerations
- Minimize std::string allocations: Use temporary buffers for parsing and pass references to UI functions. Reuse globals like temp_dismiss_alert_id for short-lived payloads.
- Debounce frequent writes: Volume and climate targets use delays to reduce network and device load.
- Avoid redundant updates: Centralized recolor and sync functions prevent repeated UI mutations.
- NVS usage: Limit restore_value: true to essential preferences to conserve storage and reduce write wear.
- Interrupt handling: Ensure microphone and speaker bus coordination to avoid blocking and silent failures.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Persistence problems:
  - If a preference resets unexpectedly, verify restore_value: true is set (e.g., conversation_mode, assist_text_size, alarm_days_mask).
  - For transient flags (e.g., active_page, assist_popup_open), expect reset to initial_value on boot.
- State synchronization:
  - Volume drift: Ensure volume_push_ts is set on push and interval sync respects the 2-second guard to avoid overwriting ongoing gestures.
  - Climate target mismatch: Confirm optimistic UI updates and debounce script execute; check HA push via tab5_maj_clim to reconcile.
  - Alert dismissal: Verify temp_dismiss_alert_id is cleared after HA service call; ensure tab5_dismissed_local is updated.
- Alarm behavior:
  - Re-ringing after stop: Check alarm_skip_before restoration and alarm_invalidate calls; ensure skip floor is set before first calculation.
  - Silent ring: Confirm microphone is stopped before playing rtttl/media; verify I2S bus availability.
- Voice assistant:
  - Popup not closing: Ensure is_showing_vocal_response is cleared after display duration; confirm rotator restart.
  - Stop command ignored: Verify va_stop_armed is armed during pipeline and micro_wake_word.stop is called appropriately.

## Introduction
This document explains the system-level settings and configuration parameters that control Tab5 behavior across network, display, audio, and performance tuning. It covers parameter validation rules, acceptable ranges, default values, runtime vs restart-required changes, and practical scenarios such as optimizing for different screen sizes, adjusting refresh rates, and configuring power management. It also provides guidance on monitoring system performance and debugging configuration issues.

## Project Structure
The Tab5 system is configured through a set of ESPHome YAML packages plus UI tokens and styles:
- Hardware and platform configuration (ESP32-P4, PSRAM, I2C/I2S, display, touch, audio, OTA, safe mode)
- LVGL UI layout and pages
- Global state variables shared across components
- API services to update UI from Home Assistant
- Reusable scripts for complex actions
- Style definitions and UI geometry tokens
- Sensors and diagnostics (WiFi, antenna selection, uptime, CPU temp, loop time)
- HA-facing controls (volume entity, screen name, navigation select)

## Core Components
- Platform and hardware: ESP32-P4 with ESP-IDF framework, PSRAM, I2C bus, MIPI DSI display, ST7123 touchscreen, I2S microphone and speaker, ES7210 ADC, ES8388 DAC.
- Network and OTA: WiFi credentials via secrets, optional AP fallback, secure API encryption key, OTA password, reboot timeout when HA API disconnects.
- Display and UI: LVGL with 16-bit color depth, full buffer, rotation 270°, style tokens, modal geometry substitutions.
- Audio pipeline: Microphone at 16 kHz, speaker at 48 kHz stereo, preferred media format FLAC 24 kHz mono for announcements, noise suppression and auto gain for voice assistant.
- Diagnostics and sensors: Uptime, WiFi RSSI, core temperature, free heap, loop time; WiFi antenna selection switch; SNTP time source.
- Runtime controls: Volume exposure to HA, current screen detection, remote navigation to screens.

## Architecture Overview
The system integrates hardware, UI, and network layers through ESPHome components and LVGL. Configuration flows from YAML into component initialization, while runtime updates flow via API services and scripts to keep the UI synchronized with Home Assistant state.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant API as "ESPHome API"
participant SVC as "Services (tab5-api-logic)"
participant SCR as "Scripts (tab5-scripts)"
participant LV as "LVGL UI"
participant HW as "Hardware (display/audio)"
HA->>API : Call service tab5_maj_*
API->>SVC : Execute lambda handlers
SVC->>SCR : Invoke reusable scripts
SCR->>LV : Update widgets/pages
LV->>HW : Render frames (buffered, never update_interval)
Note over LV,HW : LVGL drives redraws; display uses MIPI DSI
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Network Settings
- WiFi credentials are provided via secrets and can be changed without code.
- Power save mode is disabled for consistent throughput.
- Optional AP fallback is available for recovery.
- Antenna selection is exposed as a template select to toggle internal/external antenna via GPIO expander.
- API encryption key is required for secure communication; changing it requires reconfiguration of clients.
- Reboot timeout prevents zombie states when no API client is connected; default is set to avoid frequent reboots during HA downtime.

Validation and defaults:
- WiFi SSID/password must be present in secrets; otherwise connection fails.
- Antenna options are restricted to “Internal” or “External”.
- API encryption key must match between device and clients.
- Reboot timeout is configurable; default balances stability and recovery.

Runtime vs restart:
- WiFi SSID/password changes require restart to apply.
- Antenna selection applies immediately via GPIO.
- API encryption key change requires restart to reload config.
- Reboot timeout applies immediately if modified in config and reloaded.

Monitoring:
- WiFi status, IP, SSID, RSSI are exposed as sensors and updated periodically.
- HA API status binary sensor indicates connectivity.

### Display Preferences
- Display model is MIPI DSI with 1280x720 resolution, 16-bit pixel mode, RGB color order.
- Touchscreen uses ST7123 with interrupt-driven polling and calibration bounds matching display dimensions.
- Backlight is PWM-controlled with restore-on default and smooth transitions; LVGL pause/resume tied to backlight state.
- LVGL rotation is 270° (landscape dashboard), color depth 16-bit, full buffer size, little-endian byte order.
- Modal geometry tokens define popup sizes and offsets for consistent UI layout.

Validation and defaults:
- Dimensions must match hardware; calibration bounds should align with actual screen coordinates.
- Rotation must remain 270° unless explicitly overridden by game logic; enabling rotation support requires this key present.
- Buffer size set to 100% ensures smooth rendering but consumes more memory.

Runtime vs restart:
- Backlight level changes apply immediately.
- Rotation changes at runtime are supported for specific games; global rotation remains 270°.
- Modal geometry tokens are compile-time substitutions; changes require rebuild/reload.

Optimization scenarios:
- For smoother animations, ensure buffer_size is sufficient; current setting uses full buffer.
- Reduce animation durations/amplitudes in UIAnim constants to lower frame cost if needed.

### Audio Configuration
- Microphone: ES7210 ADC with 16-bit, 16 kHz sample rate; mic gain set to 30 dB to move amplification to analog stage for better SNR.
- Speaker: I2S audio with ES8388 DAC, 16-bit, 48 kHz stereo; ring buffer duration increased to reduce gaps during streaming.
- Media player preferred format: FLAC, 24 kHz mono for announcements to preserve quality and reduce network overhead.
- Voice assistant: Noise suppression level set to 0 to avoid degrading speech recognition; auto gain set to 15 dBFS.

Validation and defaults:
- Mic gain values are constrained to discrete steps; 30 dB is within allowed range.
- Sample rates must be within I2S limits (16–48 kHz); current settings comply.
- Preferred format and sample rate affect transcoding path; FLAC chosen for balance of quality and bandwidth.

Runtime vs restart:
- Mic gain and sample rates are compile-time; changes require rebuild.
- Media player preferred format applies on next stream setup; may need restart to fully apply.
- Noise suppression and auto gain are applied by HA pipeline; changes take effect on next session.

Performance considerations:
- Larger ring buffer reduces audible gaps but increases latency; current 500 ms balances responsiveness and continuity.
- Avoid excessive noise suppression to maintain transcription accuracy.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-hardware.yaml:170-221](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-hardware.yaml#L170-L221)

### Performance Tuning Options
- Framework SDK options: TCP window size increased for stable OTA; yield during flash erase enabled to prevent CPU freeze; CPU frequency set to 360 MHz; WDT timeout adjusted for long boots.
- PSRAM: Hex mode at 200 MHz for larger buffers and reduced SRAM pressure.
- Logger: Level INFO with USB serial UART; TX buffer sized for reliable logging.
- Safe mode: Limits boot attempts and defines good-boot threshold to recover from crashes.
- LVGL: Full buffer, never update interval (frame-driven), optimized animation timings.

Validation and defaults:
- SDK options must be compatible with ESP-IDF version; changes require rebuild.
- PSRAM speed must be supported by hardware; 200 MHz is validated.
- Logger baud rate and buffer size should match host capabilities.

Runtime vs restart:
- Most framework and SDK options require rebuild and restart.
- Logger level can be changed at runtime but affects performance and log volume.
- Safe mode thresholds apply after reload.

Monitoring:
- Free heap and loop time sensors help identify bottlenecks.
- Uptime and core temperature indicate thermal and stability conditions.

### Runtime Configuration Changes vs Restart-Required Settings
- Immediate runtime changes:
  - Backlight level, mute/unmute, volume slider, antenna selection, logger level (with caution).
  - Screen navigation via HA entities; popup open/close via scripts.
- Restart-required changes:
  - WiFi SSID/password, API encryption key, framework SDK options, PSRAM configuration, display model/dimensions, audio sample rates and ADC/DAC settings.
- Partial reload effects:
  - Media player preferred format may require new stream setup; some pipeline parameters apply on next session.

### Examples: System Configuration Scenarios
- Optimizing for different screen sizes:
  - Adjust modal geometry tokens (modal_card_w/h, modal_body_y) to fit alternative layouts; ensure all popups recalc offsets accordingly.
  - Keep LVGL rotation at 270° for dashboard; override only within game contexts where necessary.
- Adjusting refresh rates:
  - LVGL uses frame-driven rendering; adjust animation durations in UIAnim constants to reduce repaint load if perceived lag occurs.
  - Touchscreen update interval is set to 100 ms; lowering further may increase CPU usage without perceptible benefit.
- Configuring power management:
  - Disable WiFi power save for consistent throughput; consider reducing logger verbosity to save CPU.
  - Use safe mode thresholds to auto-recover from hangs; monitor core temperature and free heap to avoid thermal throttling.

## Dependency Analysis
Key dependencies and coupling:
- LVGL UI depends on style tokens and geometry substitutions; changes propagate across all popups.
- API services depend on globals to reflect state; scripts centralize complex actions to avoid duplication.
- Audio pipeline depends on I2S bus mutex; microphone and speaker share resources, requiring careful sequencing.
- Diagnostics sensors feed UI console; visibility checks prevent unnecessary LVGL calls.

Potential circular dependencies:
- None detected; UI updates are driven by services/scripts rather than direct cross-component loops.

External integrations:
- Home Assistant API for state synchronization and service invocation.
- SNTP for time synchronization independent of HA.

## Performance Considerations
- Logging: Keep logger level at INFO for production; DEBUG adds code size and runtime overhead.
- Animation timing: Shorter durations and smaller offsets reduce repaint cost; current UIAnim values are tuned for responsiveness.
- Buffer sizing: Full LVGL buffer ensures smoothness but consumes PSRAM; verify available memory under load.
- Audio buffering: Larger ring buffer reduces gaps but increases latency; current 500 ms is a balanced default.
- Network: Increased TCP window improves OTA stability; ensure WiFi signal strength is adequate.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and remedies:
- Black screen after software reboot: Ensure real delay before display reset pin toggles; rely on boot sequence delays and avoid removing protective delays.
- Audio glitches during streaming: Increase ring buffer duration; prefer FLAC format to reduce network jitter; avoid aggressive noise suppression.
- Frequent reboots due to HA downtime: Adjust reboot timeout to balance recovery and stability; monitor API status sensor.
- Volume desync between device and HA: Use centralized script to apply volume; debounce sliders and sync via intervals.

Monitoring tips:
- Watch free heap and loop time to detect memory leaks or CPU saturation.
- Check core temperature to avoid thermal throttling.
- Verify WiFi RSSI and SSID to ensure connectivity.

**Section sources**

Tab5’s system settings are carefully tuned for reliability, performance, and user experience. Network, display, audio, and performance parameters are defined in modular YAML files, with clear validation rules and sensible defaults. Runtime changes enable flexible operation, while restart-required settings ensure stability. Monitoring and troubleshooting guidance help maintain optimal behavior in diverse environments.

## Introduction
This document explains how to customize the Tab5 interface for your Home Assistant installation using user entity mappings. It covers:
- The YAML structure for defining custom entities, including lights, climate devices, sensors, switches, and system controls.
- How substitutions are loaded at build time and propagated into the ESPHome configuration.
- How the boot sequence integrates with Home Assistant and uses these mapped entities.
- Security guidance for sensitive data such as Wi-Fi credentials and API keys.
- Troubleshooting steps for entity resolution errors and connection issues.

The goal is to help you adapt the Tab5 dashboard to your specific Home Assistant environment without modifying core firmware files.

## Project Structure
At a high level:
- The main entry point includes your per-installation entity mappings via ESPHome substitutions.
- A public example file shows all supported mapping keys.
- Your production mapping file is gitignored and holds your real Home Assistant entity IDs.
- The boot sequence initializes hardware, waits for Home Assistant API connectivity, and starts background tasks that rely on these mappings.

```mermaid
graph TB
A["Entry Point<br/>tab5-ha-hmi.yaml"] --> B["Substitutions Include<br/>!include Tab5/user_entities.yaml"]
B --> C["User Entities File<br/>Tab5/user_entities.yaml"]
A --> D["Packages<br/>UI, Hardware, Scripts, etc."]
A --> E["Boot Sequence<br/>on_boot handlers"]
E --> F["Wait for HA API<br/>api.connected()"]
E --> G["Start Background Tasks<br/>scripts, globals, LVGL"]
```

## Core Components
- User entity mappings file: defines substitution keys and their corresponding Home Assistant entity IDs.
- Entry point: loads substitutions and composes the full ESPHome configuration from packages.
- Boot sequence: initializes display/audio, connects to Home Assistant, and triggers scripts that use the mapped entities.

Key responsibilities:
- Mapping file: one key per UI feature or sensor group; values are actual Home Assistant entity IDs.
- Entry point: centralizes inclusion of the mapping file and orchestrates boot behavior.
- Packages: consume the substitution keys throughout UI components and scripts.

## Architecture Overview
The Tab5 uses a push-only architecture. Home Assistant pushes updates to the device via ESPHome services. The device never polls for state. Your entity mappings define which Home Assistant entities drive each part of the UI.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome Device"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
participant BOOT as "Boot Sequence"
BOOT->>ESP : Initialize hardware (display, audio)
BOOT->>ESP : Wait for api.connected()
ESP-->>BOOT : Connected or timeout
BOOT->>HA : Publish event esphome.tab5_connected
BOOT->>ESP : Start scripts and set globals
HA-->>ESP : Push updates via tab5_maj_* services
ESP->>UI : Update widgets based on payloads
```

- [tab5-ha-hmi.yaml:66-162](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/tab5-ha-hmi.yaml#L66-L162)

## Detailed Component Analysis

### User Entity Mappings: YAML Structure
The mappings file is a simple key-value list where each key represents a UI feature or sensor group, and each value is a Home Assistant entity ID. The example file documents all supported keys and categories.

Supported categories include:
- Trackers and remotes: PC/TV presence and TV remote control.
- Lights: bedroom, living room, office lighting.
- Climate: thermostat or HVAC entity.
- Voice assistant pipeline selection.
- System console flags and automations: primary active flag and screen refresh automation.
- Temperature and humidity sensors: room-level readings.
- Plant sensors: up to five soil moisture sensors and detailed metrics (conductivity, illuminance, temperature, battery).
- Weather layout sizing tokens: cell width, height, and Y offset for weather cards.

Important notes:
- Copy the example file to create your local mapping file before editing.
- Only edit the local mapping file; it is gitignored to avoid committing secrets or private entity IDs.
- After changing mappings, recompile and deploy OTA so the new substitutions are baked into the firmware.

Common examples by category:
- Lights: map three light entities for different rooms.
- Climate: map a single climate entity for the living room.
- Sensors: map temperature and humidity sensors per room and a plant area sensor.
- Switches: map a switch used as a tracker or system control.
- Selects: map the voice assistant pipeline selector.

**Section sources**
- [user_entities.example.yaml:13-75](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/user_entities.example.yaml#L13-L75)

### Substitution Flow During Build and Boot
- The entry point includes your mappings file as ESPHome substitutions.
- All packages reference these substitution keys instead of hard-coded entity IDs.
- On boot, the device initializes hardware, waits for Home Assistant API connectivity, and runs scripts that depend on the mapped entities.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["ESPHome Compile"]) --> LoadMap["Load substitutions<br/>from user_entities.yaml"]
LoadMap --> Compose["Compose full config<br/>from packages"]
Compose --> Flash["Flash firmware"]
Flash --> BootSeq["Run on_boot handlers"]
BootSeq --> Connect{"api.connected?"}
Connect -- Yes --> Events["Publish connected event"]
Connect -- No --> LogWarn["Log warning about HA unreachable"]
Events --> Scripts["Execute scripts and set globals"]
Scripts --> UIReady["UI ready with mapped entities"]
```

### Security Considerations for Sensitive Data
- Keep sensitive data out of version control. Use separate files for secrets and per-installation mappings.
- Secrets file contains Wi-Fi credentials, API encryption key, and OTA password.
- The mappings file contains your Home Assistant entity IDs and should be treated as local-only configuration.
- Generate a valid API encryption key using the provided method in the installation guide.
- Do not commit either the secrets file or the mappings file.

Recommended practices:
- Store secrets at the repository root as documented.
- Create the mappings file by copying the example and editing only your local copy.
- Regenerate the API encryption key if you suspect compromise.
- Restrict access to the secrets file on your development machine and CI environments.

## Performance Considerations
- The device uses a push-only model; Home Assistant detects changes and pushes updates to the Tab5. This avoids polling and keeps CPU usage low when nothing changes.
- Payloads are packed efficiently on the Home Assistant side and parsed once on the device.
- The boot sequence includes deliberate delays to ensure hardware stability and avoid display artifacts.
- Avoid frequent reboots; the device remains functional offline with last known state until Home Assistant reconnects.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide

### Entity Resolution Errors
Symptoms:
- UI elements do not update or show missing data despite the device being online.
- Certain features (weather, planning, climate) fail while others work.

Likely causes:
- Incorrect or unavailable Home Assistant entity IDs in the mappings file.
- Push automations gated by a shared condition flag that is off.
- Duplicate entity IDs from mirroring another Home Assistant instance.

Actions:
- Verify each entity ID in your mappings file against Home Assistant’s entity registry.
- Ensure any shared condition flags controlling pushes are enabled.
- If running dual Home Assistant instances, disable entity mirroring that could cause ID collisions.
- Recompile and deploy OTA after updating mappings.

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:23-39](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L23-L39)
- [installation.md:34-65](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/installation.md#L34-L65)

### Connection Issues
Symptoms:
- Device appears online but does not receive updates.
- Repeated reboots when Home Assistant is unreachable.
- Black screen after software reboot or OTA.

Likely causes:
- Home Assistant API disconnected or blocked.
- ESPHome API connection limits exceeded by lingering CLI sessions.
- Display reset timing issue requiring a delay before initializing the screen.
- Wi-Fi co-processor link failure after OTA requiring a full power cycle.

Actions:
- Check Home Assistant’s ESPHome integration status and enable service calls if needed.
- Close orphaned `esphome` CLI sessions to free API connections.
- Review the boot delay and display reset sequence; do not remove critical delays.
- Perform a full power cycle if the Wi-Fi co-processor fails to come up after OTA.
- Monitor the device’s diagnostics entities for uptime, Wi-Fi status, and API health.

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:43-50](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L43-L50)
- [troubleshooting.md:73-80](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L73-L80)
- [troubleshooting.md:83-89](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L83-L89)
- [troubleshooting.md:93-109](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L93-L109)
- [tab5-ha-hmi.yaml:66-162](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/tab5-ha-hmi.yaml#L66-L162)

### Debugging Tips
- Use the debugging guidance to insert markers directly in automations and observe real context rather than isolated reproductions.
- Prefer observing device behavior via Home Assistant diagnostic entities once back online.
- When investigating silent failures, add small, visible side effects in the exact automation path to confirm execution.

**Section sources**
- [debugging.md:51-64](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/debugging.md#L51-L64)

## Conclusion
User entity mappings provide a clean, per-installation way to adapt the Tab5 interface to your Home Assistant setup. By maintaining a dedicated mappings file and keeping secrets separate, you can customize lights, climate, sensors, switches, and system controls without touching core firmware. The boot sequence integrates tightly with Home Assistant, relying on stable connectivity and well-defined push updates. Follow the security recommendations and troubleshooting steps to keep your deployment reliable and secure.
