## Introduction
This document describes the alert and notification schemas used across the Tab5 system. It covers:
- Home Assistant alert payloads, dismissal tracking, and UI slot mapping
- Weather alerts from Meteo-France vigilance levels and hazard-specific notifications
- System diagnostics and network status indicators
- Alarm clock notification schema including scheduled events, reminder priorities, snooze behavior, and media fallbacks
- Examples of payload structures, queuing mechanisms, user interaction states, persistence, read/unread tracking, and batch processing for concurrent alerts

## Project Structure
Alerting spans both Home Assistant (configuration and automations) and the ESPHome firmware (services, parsing, and LVGL rendering). Key areas:
- Home Assistant packages define scripts, templates, and automations that push alerts to the device and manage dismissed state
- Firmware services parse incoming payloads and update UI slots with colors, icons, and visibility flags
- Diagnostics sensors expose hardware/network health and HA connectivity
- Alarm engine runs independently on-device with SNTP time and cached calendar data; Home Assistant augments it with calendar reminders and optional TTS briefings

## Architecture Overview
The system uses a push-only model:
- Home Assistant pushes alerts and reminders to the device via ESPHome services
- The firmware parses payloads and updates LVGL UI slots with appropriate colors/icons
- Dismissal is tracked in Home Assistant and reflected back to the device through events
- The alarm engine runs locally using SNTP time and cached calendar data; Home Assistant provides calendar reminders and optional TTS announcements

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant FW as "Firmware Services"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
participant ALM as "Alarm Engine"
HA->>FW : tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france(payload)
FW->>UI : Update date color + up to 4 hazard slots
HA->>FW : tab5_maj_ha_alerts_bulk(payload)
FW->>UI : Parse slots, set icons/colors, mark has_ha[i]
FW-->>HA : esphome.tab5_alert_dismiss(alert_id)
HA->>HA : Update input_text.tab5_alerts_dismissed
ALM->>ALM : alarm_due(now), schedule ring/snooze
ALM-->>HA : Optional TTS briefing via script
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Home Assistant Alerts: Payload, Dismissal, and Persistence
- Dismissed list:
  - Stored in an input_text entity as a pipe-delimited list of alert IDs
  - Supports special markers like “ha:unavailable” and “meteo:<level>”
  - Scripts append new IDs only if not already present and trigger a screen update automation
- Cleanup automation:
  - Runs daily at a fixed time to remove obsolete entries based on current states
  - Keeps “ha:unavailable” when there are unavailable entities
  - Keeps “meteo:<level>” while the level matches current sensor value
  - Keeps update entities while they remain “on”
  - Keeps original alert IDs while their source remains in problematic states
- Dismiss handling:
  - Firmware emits an event with the alert ID when a user taps to dismiss
  - Home Assistant automation receives the event and calls the dismiss script
- Batch processing:
  - Firmware accepts a semicolon-separated list of alerts, each with three fields separated by pipes
  - Up to four slots are supported; each slot can wrap content and stores its own ID for tracking

Example payload structure (conceptual):
- Single alert: “alert_id|title|icon_or_color”
- Multiple alerts: “alert_id|title|icon_or_color;alert_id|title|icon_or_color;…”

Read/unread tracking:
- Each slot stores an ID; the same ID prevents re-display after dismissal
- The Home Assistant side maintains a persistent dismissed list to survive restarts

User interaction states:
- Dismiss triggers a queued script that updates the persisted list and refreshes the UI
- Cleanup ensures stale entries do not block future alerts

- [tab5_alerts_yaml:8-85](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_alerts.yaml#L8-L85)

### Weather Alerts: Meteo-France Vigilance and Hazard-Specific Notifications
- Service payload format (pipe-delimited):
  - phrase_prochaine_pluie|globale|vent|inondation|orages|pluie_inondation|neige_verglas|grand_froid|vagues_submersion|canicule|avalanches
- Global vigilance levels:
  - “Jaune”, “Orange”, “Rouge” influence the date label color
- Hazard-specific levels:
  - Non-green values populate up to four visible slots with corresponding icons and colors
  - Green or empty values are ignored
- UI behavior:
  - Date color changes based on global level
  - Active hazards are shown with colored icons; inactive ones are hidden
  - A flag indicates whether any alerts are active

Example payload structure (conceptual):
- “Next rain phrase|Global Level|Wind Level|Flooding Level|Thunderstorms Level|Rain-Flooding Level|Snow-Ice Level|Extreme Cold Level|Waves/Submersion Level|Heatwave Level|Avalanche Level”

Processing flow:
- Firmware splits the payload into fields
- Applies global color to date label
- Filters out green/empty hazard levels
- Populates up to four slots with icons and severity-based colors

**Section sources**
- [tab5_api_logic_yaml:200-279](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L200-L279)

### System Alerts: Hardware Diagnostics and Network Status
- Diagnostics sensors:
  - WiFi SSID/IP, RSSI, internal temperature, uptime, free heap, loop time
  - HA API status binary sensor reflects native API connectivity
- UI integration:
  - Console layer updates labels and bars for memory, loop time, IP, SSID
  - HA connection status is shown with color-coded text
- Health automations:
  - Detect primary instance inactivity, unexpected reboots, and long API disconnections
  - Create persistent notifications and send mobile notifications with continue-on-error to avoid blocking other channels

Example indicators:
- “Connecté” vs “Hors ligne” for HA API status
- Color changes for WiFi icon based on connectivity
- Uptime drop detection triggers reboot alerts

### Alarm Clock Notification Schema: Scheduled Events, Reminders, Snooze, and Media
- Configuration entities exposed to Home Assistant:
  - Enable/disable, days mask, fixed time, earliest/latest bounds, lead time before opening, rest hours mode, snooze interval, max ring duration, volume, melody selection, TTS announcement toggle, calendar reminder toggle, custom media URL
- Alarm engine:
  - Computes next ring time using SNTP and cached calendar data
  - Supports modes: fixed time, workdays only, and before-opening derived time
  - Enforces minimum rest after previous day’s closing when configured
  - Snooze sets a future trigger and increments a counter
  - Dismiss clears snooze and advances skip floor to prevent immediate re-ring
- Reminder announcements:
  - Home Assistant pushes a compact payload of upcoming appointments with epoch timestamps and titles
  - Firmware stores up to eight entries, marks them announced once triggered, and avoids re-announcing on subsequent pushes
  - Announcements produce both screen text and speech output
- Ring behavior:
  - Uses local RTTTL melodies or an optional media URL served by Home Assistant
  - Implements crescendo gain progression and respects I2S bus constraints by temporarily stopping microphone capture during playback
  - Shows overlay UI with time, title, and snooze options

Payload contract for reminders:
- Format: “epoch|title~epoch|title~…”
- Epochs are UTC start times; titles are sanitized to avoid protocol separators
- Maximum eight entries; sorting and deduplication occur in Home Assistant before pushing

Snooze functionality:
- Configurable snooze interval
- Each snooze sets a future trigger and increments count
- Display shows repetition number and remaining minutes until next ring

Media fallback:
- If a custom media URL is configured and HA is reachable, play via media player
- Otherwise, fall back to local RTTTL melody

### Alert Queuing and Batch Processing
- Home Assistant scripts use queued mode to handle rapid dismissals without conflicts
- Firmware processes batched alerts in a single service call:
  - Splits by semicolons
  - Parses each alert into three parts
  - Updates up to four UI slots
  - Tracks per-slot IDs for dismissal
- Weather alerts are processed in a separate service with a dedicated payload format and limited to four active hazard slots

### User Interaction States and Persistence
- Dismissal:
  - User tap triggers firmware event with alert ID
  - Home Assistant appends ID to persisted list and triggers UI refresh
  - Daily cleanup removes obsolete entries
- Read/unread tracking:
  - Per-slot IDs ensure an alert is not re-shown after dismissal
  - Special markers persist across restarts and reflect current system state
- Batch processing:
  - Multiple alerts can be displayed simultaneously in up to four slots
  - Each slot maintains its own visibility and ID state

## Performance Considerations
- Push-only design minimizes polling; alerts are updated only when needed
- Dismissed list operations are queued to avoid race conditions
- Firmware limits payload size and slot count to prevent overflow and excessive UI updates
- Alarm engine caches next ring time and recalculates only on changes or periodic safety checks
- Weather alert processing filters non-active hazards early to reduce UI churn

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Alerts not appearing:
  - Verify Home Assistant pushed payload via the correct service
  - Check that dismissed list does not contain the alert ID
  - Ensure payload length is within firmware limits
- Dismissal not working:
  - Confirm firmware event is emitted and received by Home Assistant
  - Validate script execution and UI refresh trigger
- Weather alerts incorrect:
  - Check global vigilance level and hazard-specific levels in payload
  - Ensure non-green levels are correctly capitalized and not empty
- Alarm not ringing:
  - Verify SNTP time synchronization
  - Check calendar cache availability and mode settings
  - Confirm snooze or dismiss did not advance skip floor
- Health alerts:
  - Monitor HA API status and uptime trends
  - Investigate power or network issues if reboots are frequent

## Conclusion
The Tab5 alert and notification system combines robust Home Assistant automation with efficient firmware processing to deliver timely, actionable alerts. It supports:
- Persistent dismissal tracking and cleanup
- Meteo-France vigilance with hazard-specific visualization
- System diagnostics and network status feedback
- Reliable alarm scheduling with snooze and calendar reminders
- Batch processing and safe queuing for concurrent alerts

This design ensures resilience even when Home Assistant is unavailable, while providing rich interactivity and clear visual cues for users.

## Introduction
This document specifies the calendar event schemas used by the Tab5 planning system. It covers:
- Monthly calendar payload structure, including date codes (two hex characters per day), time slot definitions (HH:MM-HH:MM), and event details with type classifications.
- Daily detail schema for appointment types (travail, ferie, vacances, rdv, anniv, fete) with text descriptions and icon mappings.
- Event priority rules, conflict detection behavior, and notification triggers.
- Examples of complete monthly payloads, daily event listings, and recurring event patterns.
- Timezone handling, daylight saving adjustments, and synchronization considerations between Home Assistant and the device.

## Project Structure
The calendar feature spans Home Assistant scripts that aggregate events from multiple calendars and push compact payloads to the device, and ESPHome UI components that render a monthly grid and a daily detail popup. The API layer bridges both sides.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant<br/>scripts.tab5_calendrier_mois/jour"] --> API["ESPHome API<br/>tab5_maj_calendrier_mois/jour"]
API --> Store["Device State<br/>cal_store_month_data / globals"]
Store --> Render["LVGL Rendering<br/>cal_render_* functions"]
UI["Calendar UI<br/>calendar_popup + cal_day_cell"] --> Store
UI --> API
```

## Core Components
- Monthly payload producer: Home Assistant script aggregates events from four calendars and builds a compact month view payload.
- Daily detail producer: Home Assistant script builds a typed list of lines for a selected day.
- Device API handlers: ESPHome services receive payloads and update device state or render UI immediately if the relevant screen is active.
- UI components: A 7x6 monthly grid and a nested daily detail popup.

Key responsibilities:
- Encode each day as two hex digits representing a bitmask of categories.
- Encode work hours per day as HH:MM-HH:MM strings separated by pipe.
- Encode daily details as typed lines with sanitized text.

**Section sources**

## Architecture Overview
The flow begins when the device opens the calendar popup or navigates months. It calls Home Assistant scripts to fetch events from multiple calendars, then receives compact payloads via ESPHome services. The device stores month data and renders the grid; tapping a cell requests the daily detail payload and renders up to six lines.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Dev as "Tab5 Device"
participant HA as "Home Assistant Scripts"
participant Cal as "Calendars"
participant API as "ESPHome API"
participant LV as "LVGL UI"
Dev->>HA : "script.tab5_calendrier_mois(annee, mois)"
HA->>Cal : "calendar.get_events(start,end)"
Cal-->>HA : "events"
HA-->>Dev : "esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_mois(annee, mois, codes, heures, details)"
Dev->>API : "service tab5_maj_calendrier_mois"
API->>LV : "store month data + render if visible"
Dev->>HA : "script.tab5_calendrier_jour(date)"
HA->>Cal : "calendar.get_events(day)"
Cal-->>HA : "events"
HA-->>Dev : "esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_jour(date, payload)"
Dev->>API : "service tab5_maj_calendrier_jour"
API->>LV : "render daily detail popup"
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Monthly Payload Schema
- Purpose: Provide a compact representation of the entire month for the grid view.
- Fields:
  - annee: Year string.
  - mois: Month number string.
  - codes: 62 hex characters (2 per day for days 1..31). Each byte is a bitmask:
    - Bit 1 (value 1): Travail (workday)
    - Bit 2 (value 2): Ferie (holiday)
    - Bit 4 (value 4): Vacances scolaires (school vacation)
    - Bit 8 (value 8): RDV (appointment)
    - Bit 16 (value 16): Anniversaire (birthday)
  - heures: 31 fields separated by pipe “|”. Each field is either empty or a time range in HH:MM-HH:MM format representing work hours for that day.
  - details: Optional embedded daily details for the whole month (31 fields separated by tilde “~”), each field being “type|texte;...” where semicolon separates lines within a day. If omitted or empty, tapping a day falls back to fetching the daily detail via the day script.

Notes:
- Only future-or-today dates are considered for non-static categories (work, holidays, appointments, birthdays); static school vacations apply regardless of past/future.
- Text sanitization replaces reserved separators: “|” becomes “/”, “;” becomes “,”, “~” becomes “-”.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:9-14](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L9-L14)
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:137-221](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L137-L221)
- [tab5_api-logic.yaml:481-505](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L481-L505)

### Daily Detail Schema
- Purpose: Show detailed lines for a single day in the daily popup.
- Payload: A string of up to six lines separated by semicolon “;”. Each line has the form “type|texte”.
- Types:
  - travail: Work shift with start/end times included when available.
  - ferie: Recognized holiday (from a whitelist).
  - vacances: School vacation period (Zone A).
  - rdv: Appointment (family or other calendar).
  - anniv: Birthday.
  - fete: Civil celebration not on the recognized holiday list.
- Text sanitization: Same as monthly details; reserved characters are replaced before transmission.

Rendering:
- Up to six lines are displayed with icons and text.
- If no lines exist, a status message indicates no plans.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:223-341](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L223-L341)
- [tab5_api-logic.yaml:507-527](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L507-L527)

### UI Mapping and Icons
- Legend shows visual cues for today’s outline, work hours, holidays, school vacations, appointments, and birthdays.
- Dots indicate presence of appointments and birthdays on a day cell.
- Work hours appear under the day number; early shifts (< 09:00) may be highlighted differently in related logic.

Icon mapping:
- Icons are rendered via LVGL font glyphs; specific glyph codes are defined in UI components and referenced during rendering.

**Section sources**
- [calendar_popup.yaml:157-188](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/calendar_popup.yaml#L157-L188)
- [cal_day_cell.yaml:27-33](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/cal_day_cell.yaml#L27-L33)

### Event Priority and Conflict Handling
- Bitmask composition: Multiple flags can be set for a single day. For example, a day can simultaneously be a holiday and contain an appointment.
- Work hour extraction: When building monthly heures, only the first matching “Travail” event per day is used to avoid duplicates.
- Daily detail ordering: Holidays and vacations are listed first, followed by work shifts, then other appointments, birthdays, and civil celebrations.
- Deduplication: Work entries are deduplicated by exact start-end pair to prevent repeated lines.

Priority summary:
- Static categories (holidays, vacations) take precedence in listing order.
- Work shifts are prioritized for time ranges.
- Appointments and birthdays are appended after primary categories.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:143-193](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L143-L193)
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:265-341](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L265-L341)

### Notification Triggers and Alarm Integration
- Next-ring calculation uses calendar-derived work hours to compute wake-up times and enforce minimum rest after previous shifts.
- Upcoming appointments are pushed to the device and stored locally to ensure announcements even if Home Assistant disconnects momentarily.
- The alarm subsystem invalidates its schedule when calendar data changes to keep next ring accurate.

### Timezone Handling and Daylight Saving
- Local date calculations use SNTP-synchronized time and normalize around noon to avoid DST edge effects near midnight.
- Calendar queries use Home Assistant’s timezone-aware datetimes; events are matched by date portion, ensuring correct coverage across multi-day events.
- The device relies on local time for rendering and alarms, while Home Assistant provides normalized payloads.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:173-187](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L173-L187)
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:91-119](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L91-L119)

### Recurring Events
- Recurrence is handled by the underlying calendar providers (e.g., Google Calendar). The scripts match events by their effective start/end dates without interpreting recurrence rules directly.
- Multi-day events are covered by checking whether the target date falls within the event’s start-to-end range.

## Performance Considerations
- Monthly queries limit to current or future window to avoid unnecessary past events.
- Payloads are compact strings to minimize network overhead.
- Device-side caching avoids re-rendering unless the popup is open for the requested month.
- Deduplication prevents redundant lines in daily details.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Empty month grid: Ensure Home Assistant scripts return valid codes and heures; verify calendar entities are reachable and events exist.
- Stale month data: Reopen the calendar popup to trigger refresh; pre-fetching occurs at boot and reconnect.
- Missing daily details: If details are empty, tapping a day will call the day script; confirm the day script returns typed lines.
- Alarm mismatch after calendar updates: Calendar changes invalidate alarm schedules; wait for recalculation or trigger a refresh.

## Conclusion
The Tab5 calendar system uses compact, typed payloads to efficiently synchronize monthly and daily views between Home Assistant and the device. Bitmask-based date codes encode multiple event categories per day, while daily details provide rich context with standardized types. Prioritization and deduplication ensure clear presentation, and integration with the alarm system leverages calendar data for smart notifications. Timezone-aware processing and DST-safe date math maintain correctness across regions and seasonal changes.

## Introduction
This document specifies the climate control state schemas and behaviors for the Tab5 system, focusing on how Home Assistant climate entities are synchronized to the device display. It covers:
- The climate update payload structure (target temperature, current temperature, HVAC mode, preset modes, fan speeds, swing configurations)
- Temperature value range validation and debounced updates
- Mode transition rules and preset availability handling
- State synchronization between Home Assistant and LVGL UI elements
- Examples of complete/partial updates and error conditions
- Color coding for operational states
- Integration with arc thermostat UI components and popup controls

## Project Structure
The climate feature is composed of:
- UI components for compact card and full-screen popup
- A central API logic service that receives push updates from Home Assistant
- Scripts that debounce user interactions and recolor icons based on current state
- Global variables holding the authoritative state used by both UI and scripts

## Core Components
- Compact climate card: displays room temperatures and a glass overlay with target temperature and ± buttons. Tapping the target opens the popup.
- Full-screen climate popup: three glass cards for MODE, TEMPERATURE, OPTIONS. Includes an arc thermostat (16–30 °C), ± buttons, presets (eco/away, boost), quiet fan toggle, and swing options (swing/stop, windnice).
- API logic service: receives push updates from Home Assistant and sets global state and UI labels.
- Scripts: debounce temperature changes and apply consistent icon coloring based on current state.
- Globals: hold the authoritative climate state used across UI and scripts.

Key responsibilities:
- User input (card and popup) updates globals optimistically and triggers debounced commands to Home Assistant.
- Home Assistant pushes back authoritative state via the API service, which re-renders UI and colors.

## Architecture Overview
The system uses an optimistic UI pattern with debounced writes and authoritative push-back from Home Assistant.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant U as "User"
participant UI as "LVGL UI<br/>climate_card / climate_popup"
participant SC as "Scripts<br/>tab5_debounce_clim_temp / tab5_clim_recolor"
participant HA as "Home Assistant<br/>climate entity"
participant API as "API Logic<br/>tab5_maj_clim"
U->>UI : Tap ± or adjust arc
UI->>SC : Update clim_target_temp (optimistic)
UI->>SC : Execute tab5_debounce_clim_temp
SC->>HA : climate.set_temperature (after delay)
Note over SC,HA : Debounce groups rapid taps into one call
HA-->>API : Push state (target/current/mode/preset/fan/swing)
API->>SC : Set globals and call tab5_clim_recolor
SC->>UI : Recolor icons and update labels
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Climate Update Payload Schema
The push payload received by the Tab5 API service contains:
- target: string representing the target temperature (float)
- current: string representing the current room temperature (float)
- mode: string representing HVAC mode
- preset: string representing preset mode
- fan: string representing fan speed/mode
- swing: string representing airflow swing configuration

Behavior:
- The service parses strings to floats for temperatures and updates globals and UI labels accordingly.
- After setting globals, it executes the centralized recolor script to reflect the new state visually.

Validation and constraints:
- Target temperature is clamped to 16–30 °C at the UI level before sending.
- When the HVAC mode is off, set_temperature forces hvac_mode to cool to satisfy device constraints.

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:162-198](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L162-L198)

- [tab5-scripts.yaml:383-398](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L383-L398)

### Temperature Value Range Validation
- Arc thermostat min/max: 16–30 °C
- ± buttons clamp to 16–30 °C per step
- Step size: 0.5 °C
- Debounce: 250 ms; only one climate.set_temperature per gesture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["User adjusts target"]) --> ClampMin["Clamp to >= 16.0"]
ClampMin --> ClampMax["Clamp to <= 30.0"]
ClampMax --> UpdateGlobal["Set clim_target_temp"]
UpdateGlobal --> UpdateUI["update_clim_target_ui()"]

Send -- No --> UseCurrent["Use current hvac_mode"]

```

### Mode Transition Rules
- Supported HVAC modes: cool, heat, dry, fan_only, off
- Off mode:
  - UI button calls climate.turn_off
  - For temperature adjustments, if mode is off or empty, set_temperature forces hvac_mode to cool to comply with device behavior
- Mode selection:
  - Each mode button sets clim_hvac_mode optimistically, then calls tab5_clim_recolor, then sends climate.set_hvac_mode to Home Assistant

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant U as "User"
participant UI as "HVAC mode button"
participant SC as "Scripts"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
U->>UI : Select HVAC mode
UI->>SC : Set clim_hvac_mode (optimistic)
UI->>SC : Execute tab5_clim_recolor
SC->>HA : climate.set_hvac_mode(entity, hvac_mode)
HA-->>SC : Push state via tab5_maj_clim
SC->>UI : Recolor icons based on mode
```

### Preset Availability Checks
- Presets supported in UI: eco (mapped to away), boost
- Toggle behavior: tapping an active preset toggles it back to none
- Implementation:
  - Sets clim_preset_mode optimistically
  - Executes tab5_clim_recolor to highlight active preset
  - Calls climate.set_preset_mode with the computed value

Notes:
- If the underlying device does not support a preset, Home Assistant will reject or ignore the command; the push-back via tab5_maj_clim will restore correct UI state.

### Fan Speeds and Swing Configurations
- Fan modes:
  - Quiet toggle switches between quiet and auto
  - UI sets clim_fan_mode optimistically, then calls climate.set_fan_mode
- Swing modes:
  - Two options: swing (oscillation) and windnice (gentle breeze)
  - UI toggles clim_swing_mode and calls climate.set_swing_mode
- Coloring:
  - Active fan/swing states are highlighted using tab5_clim_recolor

```mermaid
SC->>UI : Recolor icons for fan/swing
```

### State Synchronization Mechanism
- Optimistic UI:
  - On user actions, globals are updated immediately and UI reflects changes instantly
  - Commands are sent to Home Assistant after debounce
- Authoritative sync:
  - Home Assistant pushes the real state via tab5_maj_clim
  - The service updates globals and triggers tab5_clim_recolor to ensure UI matches device state

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> Idle
Idle --> Optimistic : "User action"
Optimistic --> Pending : "Debounce timer starts"
Pending --> Sent : "Send to Home Assistant"
Sent --> Synced : "Receive push via tab5_maj_clim"
Synced --> Idle : "UI updated and colored"
```

  - Red when mode is heat

  - Highlight active mode; others dimmed

  - Boost highlighted when active
- Fan:
  - Quiet/low highlighted when active
- Swing:
  - Swing/vertical/horizontal/both/on/3d highlighted when active
  - Windnice highlighted when active

## Performance Considerations
- Debouncing temperature changes reduces network load and prevents redundant commands during rapid interactions
- Optimistic UI improves perceived responsiveness by updating labels immediately
- Centralized recolor script avoids duplicated logic and ensures consistent visuals

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Rapid taps not applying temperature:
  - Ensure debounce is functioning; verify that only one climate.set_temperature is sent per gesture
  - Check that clim_target_temp is being clamped to 16–30 °C
- Mode off preventing temperature changes:
  - Confirm that set_temperature forces hvac_mode to cool when mode is off
- UI not reflecting device state:
  - Verify that Home Assistant pushes state via tab5_maj_clim and that tab5_clim_recolor runs
- Incorrect preset highlighting:
  - Confirm preset mapping (eco maps to away) and that toggle logic returns to none when tapped again

**Section sources**
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:383-398](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L383-L398)
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:162-198](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L162-L198)

## Conclusion
The Tab5 climate system combines optimistic UI updates with debounced writes and authoritative push-back from Home Assistant to deliver responsive and accurate control. Temperature clamping, mode-specific behavior, and centralized recoloring ensure consistent user experience. The defined schemas and flows provide a robust foundation for integrating with various climate devices while maintaining clear separation between UI, logic, and external services.

## Introduction
This document specifies all data schemas used by the Tab5 system, focusing on:
- Weather payload formats (hourly forecasts, daily forecasts, Meteo-France alerts)
- Climate state structures (temperature, mode, preset, fan, swing)
- Light configuration schemas (brightness, color values, group memberships)
- Game state persistence formats stored in NVS memory
- Schema versioning strategies, backward compatibility considerations, and migration procedures
- Examples of valid payloads and common error conditions for each schema type

The goal is to provide a clear, authoritative reference for developers integrating with or extending Tab5’s data contracts.

## Project Structure
Key files defining or consuming these schemas:
- API contract and service handlers: tab5-api-logic.yaml
- Global runtime state variables: tab5-globals.yaml
- C++ types and parsing/rendering logic: tab5_custom.h, tab5_custom.cpp
- Home Assistant alert dismissal and cleanup: tab5_alerts.yaml
- Demo payload builders and examples: scenarios.py

## Core Components
- Weather hourly forecast bulk payload: parsed into HourForecastData and rendered via refresh_hourly_forecast.
- Weather daily forecast bulk payload: parsed into DayForecastData and rendered via refresh_daily_forecast.
- Meteo-France alert payload: pipe-delimited fields processed to update vigilance banners and alert slots.
- Climate state: target/current temperatures plus HVAC mode, preset, fan, swing; persisted in globals and reflected in UI.
- Light configuration: brightness (0–255), on/off state, selected light index; UI reflects brightness percentage and selection.
- Game state persistence: per-game NVS keys store settings and board positions; writes are throttled to reduce flash wear.

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Weather Hourly Forecast Payload
- Service: tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk
- Payload format: semicolon-separated records; each record uses pipe-delimited fields:
  - idx: integer 0–14
  - heure_texte: string "HH:MM"
  - condition: string (weather icon key)
  - temp: float temperature
  - pluvio: float precipitation amount
- Parsing: parse_and_update_heures_bulk stores into HourForecastData array and triggers refresh_hourly_forecast.
- Validation rules:
  - Total payload length must be ≤ 2048 bytes; otherwise rejected to avoid OOM.
  - Each record must have at least 5 fields; extra fields are ignored.
  - idx must be within 0–14; out-of-range entries are skipped.
- Example references:
  - Record construction and size checks: scenarios.py
  - Parser implementation: tab5_custom.cpp

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Receive heures bulk"]) --> CheckLen{"Length <= 2048?"}
CheckLen --> |No| Reject["Reject payload (too long)"]
CheckLen --> |Yes| Split["Split by ';'"]
Split --> ForEach["For each record"]
ForEach --> Parse["Split by '|' -> [idx, time, cond, temp, pluvio]"]
Parse --> Validate{"idx 0..14 and >=5 fields?"}
Validate --> |No| Skip["Skip record"]
Validate --> |Yes| Store["Store in HourForecastData[idx]"]
Store --> Next["Next record"]
Next --> End(["Done"])
```

**Diagram sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:339-382](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L339-L382)
- [scenarios.py:131-136](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/tools/demo/scenarios.py#L131-L136)

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:41-54](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L41-L54)
- [tab5_custom.h:27-35](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.h#L27-L35)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:339-382](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L339-L382)

### Weather Daily Forecast Payload
- Service: tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk
- Payload format: semicolon-separated records; each record uses pipe-delimited fields:
  - idx: integer 0–14
  - nom_jour: string day label
  - condition: string (weather icon key)
  - tmin: float minimum temperature
  - tmax: float maximum temperature
  - est_repos: "0"/"1"
  - est_dimanche: "0"/"1"
  - est_passe: "0"/"1"
  - heures_ouverture: string work hours range
- Parsing: parse_and_update_jours_bulk stores into DayForecastData array and triggers refresh_daily_forecast.
- Validation rules:
  - Total payload length must be ≤ 2048 bytes; otherwise rejected to avoid OOM.
  - Each record must have at least 9 fields; extra fields are ignored.
  - idx must be within 0–14; out-of-range entries are skipped.
- Example references:
  - Record construction and size checks: scenarios.py
  - Parser implementation: tab5_custom.cpp

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Receive jours bulk"]) --> CheckLen{"Length <= 2048?"}
CheckLen --> |No| Reject["Reject payload (too long)"]
CheckLen --> |Yes| Split["Split by ';'"]
Split --> ForEach["For each record"]
ForEach --> Parse["Split by '|' -> 9 fields"]
Parse --> Validate{"idx 0..14 and >=9 fields?"}
Validate --> |No| Skip["Skip record"]
Validate --> |Yes| Store["Store in DayForecastData[idx]"]
Store --> Next["Next record"]
Next --> End(["Done"])
```

### Meteo-France Alerts Payload
- Service: tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france
- Payload format: pipe-delimited fields (exactly 11):
  - phrase_pluie: string
  - globale: "Vert"/"Jaune"/"Orange"/"Rouge"
  - vent: level
  - inondation: level
  - orages: level
  - pluie_inondation: level
  - neige_verglas: level
  - grand_froid: level
  - vagues_submersion: level
  - canicule: level
  - avalanches: level
- Behavior:
  - Sets global has_alerts based on active levels.
  - Colors the date according to globale.
  - Populates up to 4 alert slots with icons and colors.
  - Updates rain phrase display.
- Validation rules:
  - Buffer size is 1024 bytes; payloads exceeding this are truncated safely.
  - Missing fields default to "Vert" except phrase_pluie which defaults to empty.
- Example references:
  - Field list and buffer size: scenarios.py
  - Handler implementation: tab5-api-logic.yaml

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant SVC as "ESPHome Service"
participant UI as "UI Update"
HA->>SVC : tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france(payload)
SVC->>SVC : split fields by '|'
SVC->>UI : update_rain_phrase_ui(phrase_pluie)
SVC->>UI : set date color by globale
SVC->>UI : populate up to 4 alert slots with icons/colors
SVC->>SVC : set has_alerts flag
```

### Climate State Structure
- Fields:
  - target: string representing target temperature
  - current: string representing current temperature
  - mode: string HVAC mode
  - preset: string preset mode
  - fan: string fan mode
  - swing: string swing mode
- Persistence:
  - Stored in globals clim_target_temp, clim_hvac_mode, clim_preset_mode, clim_fan_mode, clim_swing_mode.
- UI updates:
  - Values are converted/updated in the service handler and then re-colored via a centralized script.
- Validation rules:
  - Temperature strings are parsed as floats; invalid values will not update UI.
  - Mode/preset/fan/swing are treated as opaque strings; only known values produce expected UI states.

```mermaid

+string clim_swing_mode
}
ClimateState --> Globals : "updates"
```

### Light Configuration Schema
- Brightness:
  - Range 0–255; represented as percentage in UI.
  - NaN indicates off; UI sets arc to 0 and hides percentage when off.
- Color:
  - Not part of the core schema here; color presets are handled by UI components and scripts.
- Group membership:
  - Current light entity tracked in current_light_entity; popup shows one of three lights (index 0–2).
- UI synchronization:
  - sync_light_popup_brightness updates arc and percentage label.
  - show_light_popup_ui selects the active light and updates power icon and selection border.

```mermaid

CheckOn --> |Yes| ReadB["Read brightness (0..255)"]
ReadB --> Clamp["Clamp to 0..255"]
Clamp --> UpdateArc["Update arc and % label"]
SetZero --> End(["Done"])
UpdateArc --> End
```

### Game State Persistence (NVS)
- Storage model:
  - Per-game NVS keys store both settings and current position/board state.
  - Writes are throttled to minimize flash wear; changes are staged in RAM and flushed periodically or on force.
- Key elements:
  - Settings include game size, mode, human/AI parameters, handicap.
  - Position includes board state, move number, captures, side to move, ko state.
- Persistence functions:
  - persist_load() restores from NVS.
  - persist_save() writes to NVS with throttling.
  - stash_settings()/stash_position() stage changes in RAM before flush.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant UI as "Game UI"
participant RAM as "RAM staging"
participant NVS as "NVS storage"
UI->>RAM : stash_settings() / stash_position()
Note over RAM : g_dirty = true
loop Throttled flush
RAM->>NVS : persist_save() if (now - last) >= min_ms
end
UI->>NVS : persist_load() on boot
```

## Performance Considerations
- Bulk payloads are limited to 2048 bytes to prevent out-of-memory conditions during parsing.
- In-place tokenization with strtok_r avoids heap allocations in hot paths.
- NVS writes are throttled to reduce flash wear and improve responsiveness.
- UI updates are optimized to avoid redundant repaints (e.g., icon roll suppression when unchanged).

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Payload too long:
  - Heures/jours bulk payloads > 2048 bytes are rejected; split into smaller batches.
- Truncated alert payload:
  - Alert payload buffer is 1024 bytes; ensure payloads fit within this limit.
- Invalid climate values:
  - Non-numeric temperature strings will not update UI; validate inputs before sending.
- Light brightness NaN:
  - When light is off, brightness may be NaN; UI treats it as 0 and hides percentage.
- Dismissed alerts not clearing:
  - Ensure Home Assistant scripts update dismissed lists and trigger refresh automation.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:339-382](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L339-L382)
- [tab5_api_logic.yaml:200-278](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L200-L278)
- [tab5_alerts.yaml:120-172](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_alerts.yaml#L120-L172)

## Conclusion
Tab5’s data schemas are defined through a combination of ESPHome services, C++ parsers, and global state. Weather payloads use compact, delimited formats for efficient transmission and parsing. Climate and light states are synchronized between Home Assistant and the device UI via well-defined fields. Game state persistence leverages NVS with throttled writes to balance durability and performance. Adhering to payload size limits, field order, and validation rules ensures reliable operation across updates and integrations.

## Introduction
This document details the Arkanoid breakout-style game state schema and runtime behavior as implemented in the Tab5 project. It covers ball physics, paddle positioning, brick layouts, power-ups, level progression, scoring with combo multipliers, life management, high score persistence, collision detection states, power-up activation effects, level completion criteria, and serialization for pause/resume and crash recovery via NVS.

## Project Structure
The Arkanoid game is a self-contained LVGL page built at runtime from C++ code. The YAML declares only four containers (root, HUD, field, panel), while all gameplay objects (paddle, balls, bricks, power-ups, menus) are created and managed in C++. A dedicated timer drives the game loop at approximately 30 Hz.

```mermaid
graph TB
YAML["LVGL Page YAML<br/>4 containers"] --> CPP["Arkanoid C++ Module"]
CPP --> UI["LVGL Objects<br/>Paddle, Balls, Bricks, Power-ups, Menus"]
CPP --> IMU["IMU Input<br/>on_imu()"]
CPP --> TOUCH["Touch Buttons<br/>Left/Right"]
CPP --> TIMER["lv_timer tick_cb()<br/>~30 Hz"]
CPP --> NVS["NVS Persistence<br/>persist_save/load()"]
```

## Core Components
- Ball physics state: position, velocity, active flag, glued flag; speed normalization per frame; sub-stepped movement to reduce tunneling.
- Paddle positioning: center X, width, velocity (for IMU mode), clamped within field bounds; supports IMU acceleration + friction and direct button speed modes.
- Brick layout configurations: 8 predefined levels using a grid of brick types; includes normal, tough, indestructible, and bonus bricks.
- Power-up inventories: pool of up to 8 simultaneous items falling down; types include expand/shrink paddle, slow/fast ball, multi-ball, glue, extra life.
- Level progression: 8 levels with increasing difficulty via higher base ball speed and tougher brick counts; boss level concludes the run.
- Scoring system: points per brick type, combo multiplier windowed by time, lives starting at 3, high scores persisted locally.
- Collision detection: AABB vs circle for bricks, wall bounces, paddle reflection with angle based on hit position, floor loss handling.
- Serialization: NVS-backed save structure with magic versioning; loads on open, saves on key transitions and close.

## Architecture Overview
The game runs inside an LVGL full-screen page. On open, it builds UI once, sets up event handlers, and starts a timer that calls the main tick function each frame. Input comes from IMU or touch buttons; the tick updates physics, collisions, power-ups, and HUD. Menus overlay the playfield for hub, settings, pause, level clear, game over, and high scores.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant LVGL as "LVGL Timer"
participant Tick as "tick_cb()"
participant Physics as "Ball/Paddle Update"
participant Coll as "Collision Detection"
participant PU as "Power-Up Logic"
participant HUD as "HUD Update"
participant Save as "NVS Persist"
User->>LVGL : Open game
LVGL->>Tick : Start timer (~30 Hz)
loop Each Frame
Tick->>Physics : Move paddle/balls (substeps)
Physics->>Coll : Check walls/paddle/bricks
Coll-->>Physics : Reflect/Hit/Bonus spawn
Tick->>PU : Update falling items & pickup
Tick->>HUD : Refresh labels if changed
alt Level complete / Game over
Tick->>Save : persist_save()
Tick-->>LVGL : Show menu panels
end
end
User->>LVGL : Close game
LVGL->>Save : persist_save()
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Ball Physics State
- Position and velocity in pixels per second; normalized each frame to maintain constant speed.
- Glued state allows launching from paddle; launch angle randomized slightly upward.
- Sub-stepping reduces tunneling through thin bricks.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Frame Start"]) --> Normalize["Normalize ball speed"]
Normalize --> Substep{"For each substep"}
Substep --> MoveX["x += vx * SDT"]
MoveX --> MoveY["y += vy * SDT"]
MoveY --> Walls{"Wall bounce?"}
Walls --> |Yes| ReflectX["Reflect vx or vy"]
Walls --> |No| PaddleCheck{"Paddle collision?"}
ReflectX --> PaddleCheck
PaddleCheck --> |Yes| ReflectPaddle["Angle based on hit position"]
PaddleCheck --> |No| Bricks{"Brick collision?"}
ReflectPaddle --> Bricks
Bricks --> |Hit| HandleHit["Damage/Score/Bonus"]
Bricks --> |Miss| Floor{"Floor below?"}
HandleHit --> Floor
Floor --> |Yes| LoseBall["Lose ball / respawn or game over"]
Floor --> |No| End(["End Frame"])
LoseBall --> End
```

### Paddle Positioning and Control
- Center X tracked with optional velocity for IMU mode; width adjustable via power-ups.
- IMU input smoothed with deadzone and clamping; button mode uses direct speed.
- Clamped to field boundaries; visual update every frame.

```mermaid
flowchart TD

Mode --> |Buttons| Direct["Direct speed move"]
Accel --> ClampV["Clamp velocity"]
ClampV --> MovePad["Update x += vx * DT"]
Direct --> MovePad
MovePad --> Bound["Clamp within field"]
Bound --> Render["Set LVGL position"]
```

### Brick Layouts and Special Types
- Grid-based layouts define rows/columns of bricks; colors cycle per row for classic look.
- Types:
  - Normal: one-hit, row-colored.
  - Tough: multi-hit with color change on damage.
  - Indestructible: obstacle, no damage.
  - Bonus: drops power-ups when destroyed.
- Level progression increases difficulty via more tough/indestructible patterns and higher base ball speed.

```mermaid

BT_TOUGH
BT_INDESTRUCT
BT_BONUS
}

```

### Power-Up System
- Pool of up to 8 items; spawned at brick destruction positions with weighted probabilities.
- Effects:
  - Expand/Shrink: adjust paddle width within limits.
  - Slow/Fast: modify ball speed within bounds.
  - Multi: duplicate an active ball into additional slots (max 3).
  - Glue: next paddle hit glues ball until tap releases.
  - Life: add extra life (capped).
- Falling animation and pickup via paddle overlap; off-screen removal.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Brick as "Brick Destroyed"
participant Spawn as "spawn_powerup()"
participant PU as "PowerUp Object"
participant Player as "Paddle"
Brick->>Spawn : Create item at brick center
Spawn->>PU : Set type, color, position
loop Each Frame
PU->>PU : y += fall_speed * DT
PU->>Player : Overlap check
alt Pickup
Player->>PU : apply_powerup(type)
PU->>PU : Deactivate & hide
else Off-screen
PU->>PU : Deactivate & hide
end
end
```

### Level Progression and Completion Criteria
- Levels indexed 0..7; load_level initializes bricks, paddle, single ball, resets power-ups, and sets base speed scaled by level index.
- Completion occurs when destructible bricks count reaches zero; final level triggers game over with saved score; otherwise shows level clear screen to proceed.

```mermaid

Play --> Check{"Destructible bricks == 0?"}
Check --> |No| Continue["Continue playing"]
Check --> |Yes| Last{"Level == 7?"}
Last --> |Yes| GameOver["Show game over + save score"]
Last --> |No| Next["Show level clear -> next level"]
```

### Scoring, Combo, Lives, and High Scores
- Points awarded per brick type; combo multiplier increases within a time window and caps at a maximum.
- Lives start at three; losing last ball triggers death flash and either respawn or game over.
- High scores stored in NVS with top-10 list insertion and sorting; best score displayed in HUD.

### Collision Detection States
- Wall bounces reflect appropriate velocity component and clamp position.
- Paddle collision reflects based on relative hit position to control angle; optionally glues ball if active.
- Brick collision uses AABB vs circle; determines primary axis of penetration to flip velocity; handles tough brick HP changes and bonus spawns.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Entry["Ball step"] --> Walls{"Hit side walls or ceiling?"}
Walls --> |Yes| ReflectWalls["Reflect velocity + clamp pos"]
Walls --> |No| Paddle{"Hit paddle?"}
ReflectWalls --> Paddle
Paddle --> |Yes| ReflectPaddle["Compute angle + set vel"]
Paddle --> |No| Bricks{"Hit any brick?"}
ReflectPaddle --> Bricks
Bricks --> |Yes| Resolve["Resolve axis + damage/handle bonus"]
Bricks --> |No| Floor{"Below floor?"}
Resolve --> Floor
Floor --> |Yes| Lose["Lose ball logic"]
Floor --> |No| Next["Next step"]
```

### Game State Serialization and Crash Recovery
- NVS-backed save structure includes magic number, top scores, control mode, sensitivity, mute flag, and IMU calibration offsets.
- Load validates magic; invalid or missing data resets defaults.
- Save called at key moments: settings changes, level clear/game over, and on close; ensures progress and preferences survive restarts.


## Dependency Analysis
- LVGL integration: UI creation and object pooling; timers drive the game loop; events handle pause, field taps, and menu interactions.
- IMU input: raw acceleration values feed tilt smoothing and paddle control; calibration offsets applied per session.
- NVS persistence: ESPHome global preferences store settings and high scores; versioned by magic to prevent corruption.
- No external dependencies beyond LVGL and ESPHome components; audio SFX are stubs ready for future integration.

## Performance Considerations
- Fixed timestep ~30 Hz with sub-stepping improves collision accuracy without heavy CPU usage.
- Preallocated LVGL object pools avoid allocations during gameplay hot path.
- HUD label updates are cached to minimize text writes.
- IMU smoothing and deadzones reduce jitter and unnecessary paddle movements.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- If the game does not start: ensure LVGL containers exist and are passed to open(); verify timer creation.
- If paddle does not respond: check control mode and IMU calibration; confirm event callbacks for buttons.
- If balls tunnel through bricks: verify sub-step configuration and ball speed scaling; consider reducing speed or increasing sub-steps.
- If power-ups do not appear: confirm spawn conditions and pool availability; check overlap detection and off-screen cleanup.
- If high scores are not saved: ensure persist_save is called on game over/close; verify NVS preference key and magic validation.

## Conclusion
The Arkanoid implementation provides a robust breakout-style experience with well-defined state structures for balls, paddles, bricks, and power-ups. It features progressive difficulty across eight levels, a responsive collision system, combo-driven scoring, and persistent high scores. The design emphasizes performance and reliability through fixed timesteps, object pooling, and NVS-backed serialization for seamless pause/resume and crash recovery.

## Introduction
This document describes the chess game state schema implemented in the project, focusing on:
- Board position representation using FEN notation
- Move history with algebraic notation (SAN)
- Player rating calculations (local Elo)
- AI difficulty settings and time-sliced search
- NVS storage format for persistent sessions (position, turn, clocks, settings)
- Move validation state, check/checkmate detection flags, castling rights preservation
- Examples of serialization, move history compression, and rating updates
- State corruption recovery, game reset procedures, and compatibility across AI levels

The implementation is split between a UI/state machine layer (chess_game.*) and a pure engine layer (chess_ai.*). The UI builds LVGL widgets from a minimal YAML skeleton and delegates all chess logic to the engine.

## Project Structure
- UI shell: declares four containers (root, HUD, board, panel) in YAML; C++ constructs the rest at runtime.
- Engine: defines Position, Move, Undo, generation/make/unmake, evaluation, search, FEN/SAN, perft.
- Persistence: a compact, trivially copyable struct saved via ESPHome preferences (NVS).

```mermaid
graph TB
YAML["UI Containers (YAML)"] --> UI["Chess UI + State Machine<br/>chess_game.cpp/.h"]
UI --> ENGINE["Chess Engine<br/>chess_ai.cpp/.h"]
UI --> NVS["NVS Preferences<br/>ESPPreferences"]
ENGINE --> FEN["FEN I/O"]
ENGINE --> SAN["SAN/UCI Notation"]
ENGINE --> SEARCH["Negamax Search + Quiescence"]
```

## Core Components
- Position: mailbox 0x88 board array, side to move, castling rights, en passant square, halfmove clock, fullmove number, king squares.
- Move: from/to squares, promotion type, flags (capture, en passant, castle, double push, promotion).
- Undo: captures, castling rights before move, ep before move, halfmove before move.
- Save state: magic, local Elo, stats, mode, level, human side, clocks, current FEN, plies played, settings.

Key responsibilities:
- chess_game.*: UI rendering, state machine, persistence, timers, user interaction, move application, end-game checks, hints, AI orchestration.
- chess_ai.*: rules, move generation, make/unmake, evaluation, search, FEN/SAN, perft.

## Architecture Overview
The system separates concerns cleanly:
- UI/state machine handles events, menus, HUD, board drawing, and orchestrates AI steps via a timer.
- Engine exposes a pure API for moves, legality, evaluation, and search without UI dependencies.
- Persistence uses a compact struct that fits NVS constraints and supports resume after reboot.

```mermaid
loop lv_timer
UI->>Engine : search_step()
Engine-->>UI : best move when done
end
UI->>Engine : search_best()
UI->>Engine : make()
end

```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Board Representation and FEN
- Board uses a 128-entry mailbox layout where valid squares are a1..h8 mapped into indices with out-of-board checks via bitwise mask.
- FEN parsing sets board, side, castling rights, en passant, halfmove/fullmove counters.
- FEN serialization writes ranks from 8 to 1, compresses empty runs, and appends side, castling, en passant, halfmove, fullmove.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["set_fen(fen)"]) --> ParseBoard["Parse rank by rank<br/>place pieces, track kings"]
ParseBoard --> Side["Parse side to move"]
Side --> Castle["Parse castling rights"]
Castle --> EP["Parse en passant square"]
EP --> Clocks["Parse halfmove & fullmove"]
Clocks --> End(["Position ready"])
```

**Diagram sources**
- [chess_ai.cpp:248-303](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/chess_ai.cpp#L248-L303)
- [chess_ai.cpp:306-336](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/chess_ai.cpp#L306-L336)

**Section sources**
- [chess_ai.cpp:248-336](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/chess_ai.cpp#L248-L336)

### Move History and Algebraic Notation (SAN)
- Each applied move records:
  - SAN string (French-style: R/T/F/C letters, disambiguation, x, =Q/R/B/N, +/#, O-O/O-O-O)
  - Move number and side to move at the ply
  - Zobrist hash of the resulting position for repetition detection
- Move list display groups white/black pairs and scrolls to keep recent moves visible.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Apply["play_move(m)"] --> SAN["move_to_san(before, m, out)"]
SAN --> Record["Record num, side, hash"]
Record --> Make["make(p, m, u)"]
Make --> Update["Update last-from/to, clear selection"]
Update --> Draw["draw_all(), refresh_movelist(), update_hud()"]
Draw --> CheckEnd["check_game_end()"]
```

**Diagram sources**
- [chess_game.cpp:1187-1244](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/chess_game.cpp#L1187-L1244)
- [chess_ai.h:203-209](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/chess_ai.h#L203-L209)

**Section sources**
- [chess_game.cpp:839-874](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/chess_game.cpp#L839-L874)

- [chess_ai.h:203-209](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/chess_ai.h#L203-L209)

### Player Rating Calculations (Local Elo)
- After each game vs Tab, Elo is updated using expected score based on difference between player’s Elo and opponent’s level Elo.
- Bounds clamp Elo to a safe range; draws yield 0.5, wins 1.0, losses 0.0.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
EndGame["end_game(res, reason)"] --> Stats{"Mode vs Tab?"}
Stats --> |Yes| Update["update_elo(score)"]
Stats --> |No| Skip["Skip Elo update"]
Update --> Persist["persist_save()"]
```

### AI Difficulty Settings
- Five levels define max depth, quiescence depth, target CPU budget, random move window, and reference Elo.
- Search is time-sliced: search_start initializes parameters; search_step advances one slice (~18 ms) until complete or deadline reached.
- Best move is available once depth 1 completes; progress UI shows depth, nodes, and CPU usage.

```mermaid
}
```

### NVS Storage Format and Persistent Sessions
- ChessSave is trivially copyable and includes:
  - Magic number for versioning
  - Local Elo and statistics (games, longest plies, total time, wins/losses/draws per level)
  - Settings: level, mode, human side, clock option, gestures, rule50, show_eval, demo speed
  - Resume fields: validity flag, level/mode/human, remaining clocks, plies played, current FEN
- On load, defaults are restored if magic mismatch or invalid values; on close/end, current FEN and clocks are persisted.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Load["persist_load()"] --> Valid{"Magic OK?"}
Valid --> |No| Defaults["save_defaults()"]
Valid --> |Yes| Use["Use loaded save"]
Use --> Clamp["Clamp enums/ranges"]
Close["close()/end_game()"] --> Store["store_running_game()"]
Store --> Save["persist_save()"]
```

### Move Validation, Check/Checkmate Detection, Castling Rights
- Legal move generation filters pseudo-legal moves by ensuring the moving side’s king is not left in check.
- Check detection uses attacked() on the king’s square.
- Castling rights are preserved/updated via masks on move/unmove; en passant is set only when capturable.
- End conditions include checkmate, stalemate, insufficient material, 50-move rule (configurable), and triple repetition via Zobrist hashes.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Gen["gen_impl()"] --> Pseudo["Generate pseudo-legal moves"]
Pseudo --> Legal["gen_legal(): filter by make()+unmake()"]
Legal --> Check["in_check() via attacked()"]
Check --> End["check_game_end(): mate/stalemate/insufficient/50-rule/repetition"]
```

## Performance Considerations
- Hot paths avoid allocations and heavy operations; LVGL objects are preallocated and reused.
- Search is time-sliced to keep UI responsive; budgets vary by difficulty level.
- Zobrist hashing for repetition is computed fully but used sparingly (not in hot search path).
- Evaluation uses piece-square tables and lightweight heuristics.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- State corruption recovery: If NVS magic does not match, defaults are restored and game resets to initial state.
- Resume failures: If FEN cannot be parsed, resume flag is cleared and game starts fresh.
- Game reset procedures: New game initializes start position, clears history, resets clocks and UI caches.
- Compatibility with AI levels: Level clamping ensures valid index; search parameters adapt accordingly.

- [chess_game.cpp:249-260](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/chess_game.cpp#L249-L260)

## Conclusion
The chess implementation cleanly separates UI and engine logic while providing robust persistence and AI capabilities. FEN-based serialization enables reliable resume, move history is efficiently displayed, and Elo tracking offers long-term engagement. Time-sliced search ensures responsiveness across difficulty levels, and comprehensive end-game detection adheres to FIDE rules.

## Introduction
This document explains the draughts (checkers) game implementation with a focus on:
- Game state schema: board representation, move encoding, king promotion tracking, and capture sequences
- AI opponent state: search algorithms, evaluation functions, and difficulty scaling
- Rule enforcement: forced captures, multi-jump sequences, endgame detection, and draw rules
- Examples of serialization, move validation logic, and AI decision trees
- Persistence, draw detection, and tournament mode support

The implementation supports two variants:
- International 10×10 with flying kings and mandatory maximum capture
- English 8×8 with short-range kings and mandatory capture (any legal capture suffices)

## Project Structure
The draughts module is composed of:
- Engine and UI orchestration in draughts_game.{h,cpp}
- AI search and evaluation in draughts_ai.{h,cpp}
- LVGL page shell in ui_components/draughts_game.yaml

```mermaid

GAME_CPP --> AI_CPP
```

## Core Components
- Board and position state:
  - Fixed-size square array for up to 10×10; current size n stored in Pos
  - Side to move, variant, must_from for multi-jump continuation, no_progress counter for draws
- Move structure:
  - Encodes from/to, capture list, landing path, and promotion flag
- Engine helpers:
  - Move generation, application, material/full evaluation, terminal detection

Key types and constants are defined in the engine namespace and used by both UI and AI.

## Architecture Overview
High-level flow:
- UI builds LVGL layout from YAML and C++
- Game loop runs a timer that drives AI steps and UI updates
- Engine enforces rules and generates moves
- AI uses iterative deepening negamax with alpha-beta pruning and optional quiescence search

```mermaid

Game->>Eng : gen_moves(Pos)
Game->>Game : validate selection / highlights
alt Human move selected
Game->>Game : apply_player_move(Move)
Game->>Eng : apply_move(Pos, Move)
Game->>Game : refresh_legal(), sync_pieces()
Game->>Game : after_human_or_ai_move()
else AI turn
Game->>AI : begin(Pos, Level)
loop Timer tick
Game->>AI : step()
alt AI ready
Game->>Game : apply AI move
Game->>Game : after_human_or_ai_move()
end
end
end
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Game State Schema
- Board representation:
  - Flat array sq[100] with index r*n + c; current board size n (8 or 10)
  - Piece values encode color and type: man vs king for white/black
  - Helpers identify side, king/man status, dark squares
- Position state:
  - side: whose turn it is
  - must_from: 255 means free choice; otherwise a specific square to continue a capture sequence
  - variant: international 10×10 or english 8×8
  - no_progress: increments on non-capturing/non-promoting moves; triggers draw at threshold
- Move structure:
  - Captures stored as indices of captured pieces; applied at end of move
  - Path stores intermediate landings for guided multi-jumps
  - Promotion flag set when reaching promotion rank

```mermaid
classDiagram
class Pos {
+uint8_t sq[MAX_SQ]
+uint8_t n
+uint8_t side
+uint8_t must_from
+uint8_t variant
+uint8_t no_progress
}
class Move {
+uint8_t from
+uint8_t to
+uint8_t n_caps
+uint8_t caps[MAX_CAPS]
+uint8_t n_path
+uint8_t path[MAX_PATH]
+uint8_t promote
}
class Engine {
+gen_moves(Pos, Move*, int) int
+apply_move(Pos&, const Move&)
+eval_material(Pos) int
+eval_full(Pos) int
+is_terminal(Pos, int*) bool
}
Engine --> Pos : "reads/writes"
Engine --> Move : "generates/applies"
```

### Rule Enforcement
- Forced captures:
  - All captures are enumerated first; if any exist, only captures are allowed
  - International variant filters to maximum capture length; English variant accepts any legal capture
- Multi-jump sequences:
  - During recursion, captured pieces remain on board to block but are tracked in a capture list
  - After the full sequence, captured pieces are removed in apply_move
  - must_from constrains subsequent moves to the originating piece during a chain
- King movement:
  - International: flying kings can move any distance along diagonals
  - English: kings move one square diagonally
- Promotion:
  - Man promoted to king upon reaching the last rank; promotion flag recorded in Move
- Draw detection:
  - no_progress increments on non-capturing, non-promoting moves
  - Terminal condition triggers draw when no_progress reaches threshold

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Generate Moves"]) --> Caps["Enumerate all captures"]
Caps --> AnyCaps{"Any captures?"}
AnyCaps --> |Yes| IntlCheck{"Variant == International?"}
IntlCheck --> |Yes| MaxCap["Filter to max capture count"]
IntlCheck --> |No| KeepAll["Keep all legal captures"]
AnyCaps --> |No| Silents["Generate silent moves"]
MaxCap --> Return["Return moves"]
KeepAll --> Return
Silents --> Return
```

### AI Opponent State and Search
- Difficulty levels:
  - Beginner: weighted random selection favoring captures and promotions
  - Amateur/Solid/Expert: iterative deepening negamax with alpha-beta pruning
  - Expert adds quiescence search limited to captures
- Node budget per step:
  - Scales with level to keep each step under ~25 ms
- Evaluation:
  - Material scoring with piece values
  - Mobility bonus proportional to number of legal moves
  - Pawn advancement bias toward promotion
- Decision tree:
  - Root moves scored via negamax; best move updated iteratively across depths

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Game as "Game Loop"
participant AI as "Ai : : begin/step"
participant Negamax as "negamax()"
participant Eval as "eval_full/quiescence"
Game->>AI : begin(Pos, Level)
loop Timer ticks
Game->>AI : step()
AI->>Negamax : evaluate root moves with depth limit
Negamax->>Eval : eval_full(p) or quiescence(p)
Eval-->>Negamax : score
Negamax-->>AI : best score per move
alt Depth target reached
AI-->>Game : ready() = true, best()
else Continue deeper
AI-->>Game : thinking...
end
end
```

### Move Validation Logic
- Selection:
  - Only own pieces that have legal moves may be selected
  - Highlights show valid destinations including intermediate path squares for multi-jumps
- Destination:
  - Direct destination match or ambiguous intermediate landing resolved by unique final destination
- Legal move filtering:
  - If captures exist, only those are allowed; international variant enforces maximum capture length

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Sel["Select piece"] --> CheckLegal{"Has legal moves?"}
CheckLegal --> |No| Deselect["Deselect"]
CheckLegal --> |Yes| Highlight["Highlight destinations/path"]
Highlight --> TapDest{"Tap destination?"}
TapDest --> |Direct| Apply["Apply move"]
TapDest --> |Intermediate| Resolve{"Unique final dest?"}
Resolve --> |Yes| Apply
Resolve --> |No| Ambig["Ambiguous; reselect"]
Apply --> Refresh["Refresh legal moves"]
```

### Endgame Scenarios and Draw Detection
- Win conditions:
  - One side has zero pieces
  - No legal moves available for the side to move
- Draw condition:
  - no_progress reaches threshold without captures or promotions
- Game over handling:
  - Records result, shows game over menu, persists state

### Tournament Mode Support
- Modes:
  - Player vs AI, Player vs Player, AI vs AI
- Behavior:
  - In PvP, human input always accepted
  - In TvT, AI plays both sides automatically via timer-driven steps
- Statistics:
  - Stats are tracked only in Player vs AI mode

## Dependency Analysis
- Engine depends on:
  - Board indexing helpers, piece/side predicates
  - Move generation routines for men, kings (international/English), and captures
- AI depends on:
  - Engine move generation and application
  - Evaluation functions for material and mobility
- UI depends on:
  - Engine for move legality and state queries
  - AI for time-sliced search and best move retrieval

## Performance Considerations
- Time-sliced AI:
  - Each step consumes a bounded node budget to stay within UI responsiveness constraints
  - Iterative deepening improves move quality over time
- Move ordering:
  - Captures prioritized to improve alpha-beta pruning efficiency
- Quiescence search:
  - Limited to captures at expert level to avoid horizon effects
- UI optimization:
  - Preallocated widgets and minimal allocations in hot paths
  - Fade animations decoupled from core logic

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- No legal moves:
  - Indicates loss for side to move; check terminal detection and piece counts
- Stuck in multi-jump:
  - Ensure must_from is correctly reset after applying move
- Draw not triggering:
  - Verify no_progress increments only on non-capturing/non-promoting moves and threshold is reached
- AI not selecting moves:
  - Confirm AI state is THINKING and step budget allows completion; check truncation flag

- [draughts_game.cpp:432-447](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/draughts_game.cpp#L432-L447)

## Conclusion
The draughts implementation provides a robust engine supporting two rule sets, enforced mandatory captures, multi-jump sequences, and clear endgame/draw conditions. The AI offers scalable difficulty through iterative deepening negamax with alpha-beta pruning and optional quiescence search. Persistence enables resuming games and tracking statistics, while modes support player versus AI, player versus player, and AI versus AI scenarios.

## Introduction
This document describes the non-volatile storage (NVS) schemas used to persist game state across sessions for eight arcade games on the Tab5 platform. It covers:
- Chess: board position, move history, player ratings, and difficulty settings
- Go: board configuration, stone placement, capture counts, and AI opponent settings
- Marble: level data, score tracking, and power-up inventory
- Arkanoid: ball physics, paddle position, brick layout, and power-up status
- Pinball: flipper mechanics, ball trajectory, and scoring systems
- Lode Runner: level maps, player position, item collection, and enemy AI states
- Trivia: question sets, score tracking, and difficulty progression
- Draughts: board position, piece movement history, and AI opponent configuration

It also documents NVS storage optimization strategies, data migration procedures for schema updates, and corruption recovery mechanisms implemented across these games.

## Project Structure
Each game module exposes a header defining a trivially copyable save structure stored via ESPHome’s global preferences. The corresponding .cpp implements load/save helpers and guards against corrupted or outdated saves by validating a magic constant and resetting to defaults when necessary.

## Core Components
Across all games, the persistence layer follows a consistent pattern:
- A single struct per game holds settings, statistics, and current session state
- A magic number identifies the schema version; mismatch triggers reset to defaults
- A dedicated NVS key (pref key) isolates each game’s data
- Load validates magic and clamps values to safe ranges; Save writes and syncs

Key responsibilities:
- Settings: mode, difficulty, control scheme, UI options
- Statistics: wins/draws/losses, best scores, career totals
- Session state: board positions, clocks/timers, active flags, temporary buffers

## Architecture Overview
The NVS persistence architecture is uniform:
- Each game defines a save struct with a magic field at the start
- On open(), the game loads its preference using a unique key
- If load fails or magic mismatches, defaults are initialized
- During gameplay, saves are written at key moments (close, menu transitions, end-of-game)
- Some games defer writes to reduce flash wear (e.g., Go uses a dirty flag and time window)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant App as "Game Module"
participant Pref as "ESPHome Preferences"
App->>Pref : make_preference<T>(key)
App->>Pref : load(&save)
alt valid magic
App->>App : clamp/validate fields
else invalid/missing
App->>App : initialize defaults
end
Note over App : Gameplay modifies in-memory state
App->>Pref : save(&save) + sync()
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Chess
Schema highlights:
- Magic and persistent stats: local ELO, completed games, longest sequence, total playtime
- Per-level win/draw/loss counters
- Settings: AI level, game mode (vs AI, hotseat, demo), human side, clock options, gesture hints, rule toggles, evaluation display, demo speed
- Resume state: validity flag, level/mode/human mirror, remaining clock times, ply count, FEN string

Board and history:
- Board position is stored as a FEN string within the save
- Move history is maintained in memory during play and not persisted per move; only resume snapshot is saved

AI and difficulty:
- AI level index and mode determine difficulty and behavior
- Demo speed controls pacing for AI vs AI

### Go
Schema highlights:
- Magic and settings: board size index, mode, human color, AI level, handicap stones, confirmation toggle, coordinate display, shake hint, last-move marker, territory preview
- Statistics: W/D/L per size/level, total games, cumulative time
- Resume state: presence flag, board size, side to move, passes, ko square, move number, captures, full board array

Engine integration:
- Board encoding and rules live in the engine; the save stores the minimal runtime state needed to resume

### Marble
Schema highlights:
- Magic and meta-progression: souls currency, run count, wins, best time, deepest room reached
- Inventory and upgrades: bitmask of owned items, per-stat levels, two equipment slots, skin selection
- Difficulty and calibration: difficulty setting, god mode flag, IMU calibration offsets

Progression:
- Level data is defined in code; the save tracks progress through rooms and collected items rather than storing full level layouts

## Performance Considerations
- Use trivially copyable structs to avoid serialization overhead
- Validate and clamp loaded values to prevent out-of-bounds access
- Defer NVS writes where possible (e.g., Go uses a dirty flag and time window) to reduce flash wear
- Persist only essential session snapshots (FEN for chess, board arrays for Go and draughts) to minimize write size
- Keep settings and statistics separate from volatile runtime state to reduce frequency of writes

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Corrupted or outdated NVS:
  - Symptom: game resets to defaults on boot
  - Cause: magic mismatch or failed load
  - Resolution: ensure magic constants match current schema; if needed, clear NVS or allow default initialization
- Out-of-range values after partial writes:
  - Symptom: unexpected modes or indices
  - Resolution: validation/clamping on load prevents invalid states
- Excessive NVS writes:
  - Symptom: reduced flash lifespan
  - Resolution: batch or throttle writes (see Go’s deferred strategy)

**Section sources**
- [chess_game.cpp:230-267](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/chess_game.cpp#L230-L267)
- [go_game.cpp:1-200](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/go_game.cpp#L1-L200)

## Conclusion
All eight games implement a consistent, robust NVS persistence model:
- Compact, trivially copyable save structures with explicit magic numbers
- Clear separation between persistent settings/statistics and transient runtime state
- Defensive loading with defaults and clamping to handle corruption and schema evolution
- Optimized write patterns to preserve flash endurance while ensuring data durability

This approach ensures reliable cross-session continuity for each game while maintaining performance and safety on embedded hardware.

## Introduction
This document explains the Go game state schema and implementation within the project, focusing on:
- Board configuration for 9×9, 13×13, and 19×19 grids
- Stone placement patterns and capture counting
- Territory scoring (Chinese area scoring with komi)
- AI opponent state including search depth, handicap handling, and ko rule enforcement
- Game session persistence with move history, pass counters, and resignation flags
- Examples of board state serialization, capture resolution logic, and territory calculation methods
- Rule validation, illegal move detection, and state rollback capabilities for undo functionality

## Project Structure
The Go subsystem is split into three layers:
- Engine layer: pure rules, board state, captures, ko, scoring, and utilities
- AI layer: time-sliced search, candidate generation, evaluation, and decision making
- UI/Persistence layer: LVGL rendering, NVS persistence, menus, move history, undo stack, and game flow control

## Core Components
- Engine::Pos: core board state (grid size, side to move, passes, ko, move number, captured counts, board array)

- Go game state: NVS save/load structure, move history buffer, undo stack, UI state machine, geometry, and rendering caches

## Architecture Overview
The system follows a layered architecture:
- UI/Persistence orchestrates user input, menu flows, and NVS persistence; it delegates rules to the engine and decisions to the AI
- The AI generates candidates and uses time-sliced search to pick moves while respecting budgets and deadlines
- The engine provides deterministic, non-reentrant operations over a shared scratch space to avoid stack overflow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant UI as "Go Game (UI)"
participant AI as "Go AI"
participant Eng as "Go Engine"
User->>UI : Tap intersection or Pass
UI->>Eng : is_legal(Pos, sq)
alt Legal
UI->>Eng : play(Pos, sq)
Eng-->>UI : success/failure
UI->>AI : begin(root, level, seed, komi)
loop Time-sliced steps
UI->>AI : step(slice_ms)
AI-->>UI : best_sq() or PASS/RESIGN
end
UI->>Eng : play(Pos, best_sq)
UI->>UI : update history, undo stack, NVS deferred
else Illegal
UI->>User : show message
end
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Board Configuration and Grid Sizes
- Supported grid sizes: 9×9, 13×13, 19×19
- Pos.n stores current grid size; constants define MAX_N=19 and MAX_SQ=361
- Geometry recalculates gap, stone radius, plate position based on screen constraints

Key behaviors:
- pos_init enforces valid n and resets state
- Layout functions compute positions for grid lines, star points, coordinates, and stones

**Section sources**
- [go_engine.h:26-28](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/go_engine.h#L26-L28)
