### Stone Placement Patterns and Handicap
- place_handicap places standard handicap stones at star points for h∈[2..9]
- For handicap games, White starts first and ko/reset are initialized
- Effective komi is reduced to 0.5 when playing against Tab with handicap ≥2

**Section sources**
- [go_engine.cpp:367-395](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/go_engine.cpp#L367-L395)
- [go_game.cpp:268-272](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/go_game.cpp#L268-L272)

### Capture Counting Mechanisms
- chain_liberties computes liberties using module-level stacks and generation stamps to avoid memset overhead
- play applies captures by checking adjacent enemy groups; removes captured stones and updates counters
- Ko rule: if exactly one stone is captured and the placed stone has only one liberty and forms a single-stone group, ko is set to the captured square

Capture flow:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["play(sq)"]) --> CheckPass{"sq == PASS?"}
CheckPass --> |Yes| IncPasses["passes++, side flip, ko reset, move_no++"] --> End
CheckPass --> |No| Legal{"is_legal(sq)?"}
Legal --> |No| Fail["return false"] --> End
Legal --> |Yes| PlaceStone["place stone"]
PlaceStone --> Adjacent["for each neighbor"]
Adjacent --> Enemy{"enemy group?"}
Enemy --> |Yes| Libs{"libs == 0?"}
Libs --> |Yes| Remove["remove group, count captured"]
Libs --> |No| NextAdj["next neighbor"]
Enemy --> |No| NextAdj
Remove --> KoCheck{"captured==1 and libs==1 and group_size==1?"}
KoCheck --> |Yes| SetKo["ko = last_cap"]
KoCheck --> |No| ResetKo["ko = PASS"]
SetKo --> UpdateCounts["update captured_by_*"]
ResetKo --> UpdateCounts
UpdateCounts --> FlipSide["side flip, passes=0, move_no++"] --> End
```

### Territory Scoring Algorithms (Chinese Area)
- score_chinese builds a live board excluding marked dead stones, counts living stones per color, walks empty regions to assign territory or dame, then adds komi to White
- territory_map fills an output map with T_BLACK/T_WHITE/T_DAME for empty intersections based on region ownership

Scoring flow:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
S(["score_chinese(komi, dead)"]) --> BuildBoard["build_live_board(dead)"]
BuildBoard --> CountStones["count black/white stones"]
CountStones --> WalkRegions["walk_empty_regions()"]
WalkRegions --> AssignTerr["assign T_BLACK / T_WHITE / DAME"]
AssignTerr --> Totals["compute black_terr, white_terr, dame"]
Totals --> Final["black = stones + terr<br/>white = stones + terr + komi"]
```

### AI Opponent State
- Levels: Beginner (weighted random), Amateur (1-ply), Solid (2-ply alpha-beta), Expert (iterative deepening up to 3 plies depending on board size)
- Search is time-bounded via step(slice_ms) with deadlines and total budget per level
- Candidate generation filters tactical moves (captures, saves, atari, extensions) and avoids self-eye suicide unless capturing
- Static evaluation considers material, safety (liberties), and influence diffusion
- Resignation threshold and forced pass heuristics prevent endless games


### Game Session Persistence
- GoSave struct persists settings, statistics, and in-game state across reboots
- Deferred NVS writes reduce flash wear; flush occurs on menu transitions, game end, and close
- Position restoration validates saved fields and reconstructs Pos and configuration

Persistence flow:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant UI as "Go Game"
participant NVS as "ESPPreferences"

UI->>NVS : persist_save() (deferred)
Note over UI,NVS : g_dirty flag + time window
UI->>NVS : sync() on critical moments
UI->>NVS : persist_load() on startup
NVS-->>UI : GoSave (validated)
UI->>UI : restore_position() if has_game
```

### Move History and Undo Stack
- Move history buffer stores up to MV_MAX moves for display
- Undo stack supports up to UNDO_MAX undos, storing previous position snapshots and metadata
- After_move triggers history append and undo push; do_undo restores prior state

Undo capability:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
Mv["apply_move(sq)"] --> Hist["append to g_mv[]"]
Hist --> UndoPush["push snapshot to g_undo[]"]
UndoPush --> Render["render HUD/movelist"]
UndoReq["do_undo()"] --> Restore["restore from g_undo[n-1]"]
Restore --> Pop["g_undo_n--"]
Pop --> Render
```

### Rule Validation and Illegal Move Detection
- is_legal checks:
  - Square is empty
  - Not ko forbidden
  - Has direct liberty OR extends friendly group with other liberty OR captures adjacent enemy group in atari
- fast_legal in AI leverages precomputed chain tables for speed

Validation flow:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
VStart["is_legal(sq)"] --> Empty{"sq empty?"}
Empty --> |No| Illegal["return false"]
Empty --> |Yes| Ko{"sq == ko?"}
Ko --> |Yes| Illegal
Ko --> |No| NeighborLoop["check 4 neighbors"]
NeighborLoop --> DirectLib{"direct liberty?"}
DirectLib --> |Yes| Legal["return true"]
DirectLib --> |No| Friendly{"friendly with libs>=2?"}
Friendly --> |Yes| Legal
Friendly --> |No| Atari{"enemy libs==1?"}
Atari --> |Yes| Legal
Atari --> |No| Suicide["return false"]
```

## Performance Considerations
- Engine uses module-level scratch buffers and generation stamps to avoid repeated allocations and memset calls
- AI uses O(N) chain building per position and bounded candidate lists to keep per-node cost low
- Time-sliced search ensures UI responsiveness; budgets and deadlines prevent indefinite computation
- Deferred NVS writes minimize flash wear during long games

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Illegal move errors: verify square is empty, not ko, and satisfies liberty/capture conditions
- Infinite thinking: ensure AI step slice_ms > 0 and budget_ms configured; check deadlines and abort flags
- NVS corruption: magic mismatch triggers defaults; ensure consistent GoSave layout and bump magic on changes
- Undo failures: confirm undo stack capacity and that snapshots are pushed before applying moves

**Section sources**
- [go_engine.cpp:115-150](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/go_engine.cpp#L115-L150)

- [go_game.cpp:325-396](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/go_game.cpp#L325-L396)

## Conclusion
The Go subsystem implements a robust, efficient, and user-friendly game experience:
- Clear separation between rules, AI, and UI/persistence
- Deterministic engine with optimized memory usage
- Responsive AI with time-bounded search and sensible heuristics
- Robust persistence with safe recovery and deferred writes
- Comprehensive rule validation and undo support for reliable gameplay

## Introduction
This document explains the Lode Runner (Coureur d’Or) implementation’s game state schema, platformer mechanics, puzzle-solving systems, enemy AI, item interactions, and save system. It is based on the C++ module that drives a full-screen LVGL page with no modal chrome, using persistent storage for scores and progress.

## Project Structure
The game lives in a single C++ module with a minimal YAML shell:
- lode_game.h: Public API, persistent save layout, palette, UI handles, and enums.
- lode_game.cpp: All gameplay logic, rendering, menus, persistence, and tick loop.
- lode_game.yaml: Declares five empty containers (root, HUD, field, pad overlay, panel overlay). The C++ code builds all widgets at runtime.

```mermaid
graph TB
YAML["lode_game.yaml<br/>5 containers"] --> CPP["lode_game.cpp<br/>builds UI + game loop"]
H["lode_game.h<br/>API + Save layout"] --> CPP
CPP --> LVGL["LVGL objects<br/>(field, hud, pad, panel)"]
CPP --> NVS["NVS via esphome::global_preferences"]
```

## Core Components
- Grid and tiles: 30x16 grid of 42px tiles; tile types include brick, solid, ladder, bar, exit.
- Actors: Player and up to 4 guards with position, movement step, facing, state, carry flag, dig direction, and timers.
- Items: Gold pieces tracked per cell; collected by player or picked up/dropped by guards.
- Holes: Temporary holes created by digging; close after a duration, trapping guards or killing the player if inside.
- Exit: Becomes active when all gold is collected; reaching top row completes the level.
- Persistence: Top-10 scores, best score, unlocked levels, control mode, sensitivity, speed, assist mode, calibration offsets.

- [lode_game.cpp:49-103](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/lode_game.cpp#L49-L103)

## Architecture Overview
The game runs in an LVGL timer-driven loop. On open, it loads settings from NVS, builds UI once, then shows the hub. During play, each tick updates input, physics, AI, items, holes, and rendering. Menus are overlays built from the same pool of LVGL objects.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant UI as "LVGL Page"
participant Game as "Game Loop (tick_cb)"
participant Input as "Input (buttons/IMU)"
participant AI as "Guard AI"
participant Persist as "NVS"
User->>UI : Open Lode Runner
UI->>Game : open(ui)
Game->>Persist : persist_load()
Game->>UI : build_ui()
Game-->>User : Show Hub
loop Every TICK_MS
Game->>Input : update IMU/buttons
Game->>Game : player_step()
alt All gold collected
Game->>Game : open_exit()
end
Game->>AI : guard_step()
Game->>Game : update_holes()
Game->>UI : draw actors + HUD
end
User->>UI : Close
UI->>Game : close()
Game->>Persist : record_score(), persist_save()
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Level Map Representation and Serialization
- Levels are defined as arrays of strings with a fixed legend: space (empty), # (brick), @ (solid), H (ladder), - (bar), $ (gold), P (player start), G (guard start), S (exit).
- At load, maps are parsed into a 2D tile array, gold map, and actor placements. Objects are pooled and reused across levels.
- Example serialization: each level is a 16-row string array; the engine reads rows left-to-right, padding missing columns with spaces.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Load Level"]) --> Parse["Parse rows into g_tile[][], g_goldmap[][]"]
Parse --> PlaceActors["Place player and guards"]
PlaceActors --> BuildTiles["Build LVGL tile objects (pool)"]
BuildTiles --> PlaceGold["Spawn gold LVGL objects"]
PlaceGold --> CheckExit{"Any gold left?"}
CheckExit --> |No| OpenExit["open_exit()"]
CheckExit --> |Yes| Done(["Ready"])
```

### Player Position Tracking and Movement
- Player state includes current cell, movement vector, sub-pixel progress, facing direction, animation state, and timers.
- Movement model: discrete steps aligned to the grid; horizontal movement uses run speed, falling uses fall speed. Gravity applies when unsupported.
- Inputs: buttons, tilt (with dead zone and hysteresis), or mixed mode where buttons override tilt.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Enter(["Player Step"]) --> MoveCheck{"Moving?"}
MoveCheck --> |Yes| Advance["advance(speed)"]
Advance --> CellEnter{"Step complete?"}
CellEnter --> |No| End(["Return"])
CellEnter --> |Yes| Collect["Collect gold if any"]
Collect --> ExitCheck{"Exit active and at top?"}
ExitCheck --> |Yes| Clear["Level clear"]
ExitCheck --> |No| Gravity{"Supported?"}
MoveCheck --> |No| Gravity
Gravity --> |No| Fall["Set A_FALL, move down"]
Gravity --> |Yes| Idle["A_IDLE"]
Idle --> DigWant{"Dig requested?"}
DigWant --> |Yes| TryDig["try_dig()"]
DigWant --> |No| Input["Apply input direction"]
TryDig --> End
Input --> End
```

### Platformer Mechanics: Ladders, Bars, Holes, Wall Running
- Ladders: Climb up/down only on ladder cells; can descend off-ladder (drop) if supported below.
- Bars: Hang and move under bars; dropping off a bar falls.
- Holes: Created by digging bricks beneath the player; holes close after a duration, blinking near closure. Guards trapped in holes escape after a delay; players die if caught closing.
- Wall running: Not implemented; movement requires support or ladder/bar; lateral movement needs a passable neighbor and support at the current cell.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Support{"Supported?"}
Support --> |No| Fall["Fall until supported"]
Support --> |Yes| Ladder{"On ladder?"}
Ladder --> |Yes| UpDown["Move vertically on ladder"]
Ladder --> |No| Bar{"On bar?"}
Bar --> |Yes| MoveUnder["Move horizontally under bar"]
Bar --> |No| Walk["Walk if neighbor passable"]
Walk --> Dig{"Dig request?"}
Dig --> |Yes| CreateHole["Create hole under target brick"]
Dig --> |No| Idle["Idle"]
```

### Puzzle-Solving State: Key Collection, Door Unlocking, Traps
- Keys and doors: Not present in this implementation. The “key” equivalent is collecting all gold; once all gold is collected, the exit becomes active (ladder to top row).
- Trap mechanisms: Guard traps occur when guards fall into holes; they remain trapped briefly, then climb out. If a hole closes while a guard is inside, the guard is eliminated and gold may drop.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Player as "Player"
participant Gold as "Gold"
participant Exit as "Exit"
participant Guard as "Guard"
participant Hole as "Hole"
Player->>Gold : Collect last gold
Gold-->>Exit : open_exit()
Note over Exit : Exit visible; reach top row to clear level
Guard->>Hole : Fall into hole
Hole-->>Guard : Trap for TRAP_MS
Guard-->>Hole : Escape (climb out)
Note over Guard,Hole : If hole closes while occupied, guard dies and drops gold
```

### Enemy AI States and Pathfinding
- States: Idle, Falling, Digging (not used by guards), Trapped, Exiting hole, Gone (respawn timer).
- Pathfinding: Inverse BFS from the player computes distance to every reachable cell. Guards choose moves that reduce distance; if unreachable, they move horizontally toward the player to stay threatening.
- Respawn: After death, guards respawn near the top with constraints to avoid immediate overlap with the player.

```mermaid
classDiagram
class Actor {
+int8_t cx, cy
+int8_t mdx, mdy
+int16_t sub
+int8_t face
+uint8_t st
+bool carry
+int8_t digd
+uint32_t until
}
class GuardAI {
+rebuild_dist()
+guard_choose(a)
+guard_step(a, idx, now)
+guard_respawn(a)
}
Actor <|-- Guard : "inherits fields"
GuardAI --> Actor : "updates"
```

### Item Interaction Logic
- Gold collection: When the player enters a cell with gold, it is removed and score increases; when the last piece is collected, the exit opens.
- Guard interaction: Guards may pick up gold randomly and later drop it nearby or on the ground; dropped gold must be retrieved by the player.
- Dropping: When a guard dies or escapes a trap, any carried gold is dropped onto a valid adjacent or supported cell.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
EnterCell["Actor enters cell"] --> HasGold{"Gold present?"}
HasGold --> |Yes| PickUp["Pick up gold (if guard)"]
PickUp --> DropLater{"Drop condition?"}
DropLater --> |Yes| Drop["drop_gold(cx,cy)"]
DropLater --> |No| Continue["Continue AI"]
HasGold --> |No| Continue
Continue --> End(["Done"])
```

### Save Game Functionality and Recovery
- Persistent data: Scores (top 10), best score, unlocked levels, control mode, sensitivity, speed, assist mode, calibration offsets.
- Load: On open, loads NVS; if magic mismatch or corrupt, resets to defaults and unlocks first level.
- Save: Periodically saved on key transitions; also saved on close.
- Corruption recovery: Invalid magic triggers reset; bounds checks clamp values to safe ranges.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Open["open()"] --> Load["persist_load()"]
Load --> Valid{"Magic valid?"}
Valid --> |No| Reset["Reset to defaults"]
Valid --> |Yes| Apply["Apply speed & settings"]
Reset --> Apply
Apply --> Run["Run game"]
Run --> Save["persist_save() on events/close"]
```

## Dependency Analysis
- UI layer: LVGL objects created once and reused; pools for tiles, gold, and actors minimize allocations during gameplay.
- Input: Buttons and IMU feed into a unified direction decision; mixed mode prioritizes buttons.
- Physics: Tile queries determine support, ladder access, and fall behavior.
- AI: Distance field computed via BFS; guards follow gradient with fallback heuristics.
- Persistence: NVS stores structured save; magic ensures compatibility.

```mermaid
graph LR
Input["Buttons / IMU"] --> Player["player_step()"]
Player --> Physics["tile_at(), supported(), can_step()"]
Player --> Items["collect gold, open exit"]
AI["guard_step()"] --> Dist["rebuild_dist()"]
Items --> Exit["open_exit()"]
Physics --> Holes["update_holes()"]
Holes --> Player
Holes --> AI
```

## Performance Considerations
- Fixed tick rate: 40 Hz during play, slower in menus to conserve CPU.
- Object pooling: Tiles, gold, and actors are preallocated; positions/colors updated only when changed.
- AI cost: Distance field recomputed every 4 ticks to balance responsiveness and performance.
- Speed scaling: Pixel-per-tick speeds ensure consistent difficulty across speed settings.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Stuck inputs: Ensure button release is handled; pad_sync clears held directions when leaving play state.
- Unresponsive tilt: Calibrate flat orientation; adjust sensitivity; verify IMU data is not NaN.
- Holes closing too fast/slow: Adjusted by constants; do not modify without retesting timing.
- Save corruption: If NVS magic mismatches, defaults are applied; verify magic constant and structure changes.

## Conclusion
The Lode Runner implementation provides a compact, efficient platformer with robust state management, clear mechanics for climbing, digging, and exiting, and a simple but effective enemy AI. The save system ensures progression and scores persist across sessions with safe recovery paths.

## Introduction
This document describes the marble roguelite game state schema and systems implemented in the project. It covers level progression data, player character attributes, inventory management, power-up collections, procedural generation state (dungeon layouts, enemy placements, item distributions), save system with checkpoint mechanisms, score tracking, achievement progress, examples of serialization and state modifications, corruption handling, checkpoint recovery, and difficulty scaling algorithms.

## Project Structure
The marble game is implemented as a self-contained LVGL page with minimal YAML scaffolding and rich C++ logic:
- UI containers are declared in a YAML file; all gameplay content (HUD, menus, entities) is built at runtime in C++.
- The core game logic, state, persistence, physics, and rendering live in a single C++ module split across header and implementation files.

```mermaid
graph TB
YAML["UI Containers (YAML)"] --> OPEN["Marble::open()"]
OPEN --> BUILD_UI["Build UI once"]
OPEN --> PERSIST_LOAD["Load NVS save"]
OPEN --> HUB["Hub screen"]
HUB --> START_RUN["Start run"]
START_RUN --> LOAD_ROOM["Load room"]
LOAD_ROOM --> TICK["Game tick loop"]
TICK --> PHYSICS["Physics & collisions"]
TICK --> ENTITIES["Entity updates"]
TICK --> HUD["HUD update"]
PHYSICS --> DAMAGE["Damage & invulnerability"]
ENTITIES --> PICKUPS["Pickups & chests"]
PICKUPS --> INVENTORY["Inventory & items"]
INVENTORY --> SAVE["Persist save"]
```

## Core Components
- Persistent meta-save structure for inter-session data (souls, runs, wins, best time, owned items, deepest room, stats, equipment, skin, difficulty, god mode, calibration).
- Runtime state for a run (room index, life, shield, gold, runes, timing flags, difficulty settings, boons, magnet radius, etc.).
- Entity pool for walls, traps, hazards, pickups, enemies, and exits.
- Room definitions for 6 levels with static specs and goals.
- Boons (run-time power-ups) and items (meta-progression collectibles/equipment).
- Difficulty scaling that affects hazards, speed, gold yield, and invulnerability duration.
- Save/load via NVS with magic versioning to handle schema changes.

Key state fields and their roles:
- Meta-save: souls currency, runs/wins/best time counters, bit-mask of owned items, deepest room reached, per-stat levels, equipped items slots, cosmetic skin, difficulty setting, god mode flag, IMU calibration offsets.
- Run-time: current room, life and max life, shield status, collected gold this run, rune count, timestamps for run start/enter, active difficulty constants, effective ball radius, soul multiplier, loot chance, boon list and effects, magnet radius, revive token, visual feedback timers.

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.h:32-47](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.h#L32-L47)
- [marble_game.cpp:352-427](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L352-L427)

- [marble_game.cpp:102-234](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L102-L234)

## Architecture Overview
The game uses a fixed full-screen LVGL page with three main layers:
- Field: play area where the marble moves and collides.
- HUD: compact top band showing room name, lives, gold, goal text, and time.
- Panel: overlay for menus (hub, shop, stats, reward selection, pause, end screens).

Control flow:
- open(): initializes UI once, loads NVS save, shows hub, starts a timer-driven tick loop.
- tick(): processes IMU input, dash, zones, integration with substeps, collision resolution, entity movement, pickup logic, damage, portal checks, HUD updates.
- close(): saves any partial run progress, stops timer, navigates back.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant UI as "LVGL Page"
participant Game as "Marble : : open/close/tick"
participant Save as "NVS Persist"
participant Physics as "Physics & Collisions"
participant Entities as "Entities & Pickups"
participant HUD as "HUD Update"
UI->>Game : open(ui)
Game->>Save : persist_load()
Game->>UI : build_ui()
Game-->>UI : go_hub()
UI->>Game : start_run()
Game->>Game : load_room(0)
loop 30 Hz
Game->>Physics : integrate + resolve walls
Game->>Entities : move hazards/pickups
Game->>Game : check pickups/damage/exit
Game->>HUD : update labels if changed
end
UI->>Game : close()
Game->>Save : persist_save()
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Level Progression Data
- Six rooms define a linear progression from “Seuil” to “Trone”. Each room has a name, entry line, goal text, spawn position, static specs array, number of elements, required runes (for final room), and star difficulty rating.
- Room transitions occur when the exit is reachable (runes collected in final room) or after boss rooms grant rewards. After specific rooms, players choose a boon.

Examples:
- Room 6 requires collecting runes before the central portal opens.
- Boss rooms drop guaranteed items or souls if collection is complete.

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.cpp:102-234](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L102-L234)
- [marble_game.cpp:1856-1865](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L1856-L1865)

### Player Character Attributes
- Stats are persistent and upgradeable via the “Campfire” menu using souls. Costs scale with total level to encourage specialization.
- Stats affect:
  - Vitality: increases max life.
  - Resistance: extends invulnerability duration and grants a starting shield at level 3+.
  - Finesse: reduces effective ball radius (down to a minimum).
  - Agility: improves tilt response.
  - Momentum: increases maximum speed.
  - Discovery: boosts soul gain and chest loot chance.

Stat modification example:
- Buying a stat point decrements souls by the computed cost, increments the chosen stat, and persists immediately.

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.cpp:286-306](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L286-L306)
- [marble_game.cpp:977-1009](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L977-L1009)
- [marble_game.cpp:2147-2157](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L2147-L2157)

### Inventory Management
- Items are discovered through chests or boss rewards and stored as a bit mask in the meta-save.
- Two equipment slots allow equipping items simultaneously, cycling through owned items per slot.
- Shop allows buying items (if affordable) or selling owned items at half price; selling removes the item from equipment if equipped.

Examples:
- Opening a chest grants either an undiscovered item or extra souls based on discovery stat and loot chance.
- Equipping an item applies its effect at run start (e.g., extra life, speed boost, control improvement, shield each room, magnet, brake, revive, greed).

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.cpp:1828-1854](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L1828-L1854)

- [marble_game.cpp:1658-1675](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L1658-L1675)

### Power-Up Collections (Boons)
- Boons are selected after certain rooms and apply for the duration of the run. They modify control, health, soul gain, magnet range, braking, speed, provide a shield per room, highlight the portal, grant a one-time revive, or provide temporary invulnerability per room.
- Unique boons cannot be duplicated within a run.

Application example:
- Selecting a boon adds it to the active list and modifies relevant runtime variables (e.g., increasing max life, extending magnet radius, reducing friction).

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.cpp:241-258](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L241-L258)
- [marble_game.cpp:1118-1139](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L1118-L1139)
- [marble_game.cpp:1141-1169](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L1141-L1169)

### Procedural Generation State
- Dungeon layouts are defined statically per room using Spec arrays describing walls, traps, hazards, pickups, and exits.
- Enemy placement includes saws (oscillating bars), orbs (orbiting hazards), and hunters (chasing enemies). Their motion parameters (amplitude, period/speed) are seeded per run and adjusted by difficulty.
- Item distribution includes gold, shields, magnets, brakes, dashes, runes, and chests. Some pickups jitter slightly between runs while remaining reachable and not overlapping obstacles.

Generation details:
- Mobile entities use phase offsets derived from a per-run RNG seed.
- Difficulty scales hazard periods (faster oscillation/orbit) and hunter speeds.
- Pickup jitter ensures variety while preserving connectivity to original positions.

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.cpp:113-234](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L113-L234)
- [marble_game.cpp:1541-1594](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L1541-L1594)
- [marble_game.cpp:1996-2032](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L1996-L2032)

### Save System and Checkpoint Mechanisms
- Meta-save is persisted to NVS with a magic version field. On load, if the magic does not match the expected version, the save is reset to defaults.
- Checkpoints:
  - Hub and menus do not alter run progress except settings and cosmetics.
  - During a run, abandoning or closing preserves earned souls and deepest room reached (except in god mode).
  - End-of-run outcomes credit souls, update deepest room, increment wins, and record best victory time.

Checkpoint recovery:
- If the device restarts or the game closes mid-run, reopening restores the hub with updated meta-progress; no mid-run state is preserved beyond souls and deepest room.

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.cpp:508-524](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L508-L524)

- [marble_game.cpp:2341-2360](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L2341-L2360)

### Score Tracking and Achievement Progress
- Runs launched and victories are tracked in meta-save. Best victory time is recorded in milliseconds.
- Deepest room reached indicates progression through the dungeon.
- God mode runs are excluded from statistics and rankings.

**Section sources**

### Game State Corruption Handling
- Magic version mismatch triggers a full reset to default values, ensuring compatibility with newer schemas.
- Calibration offsets and other fields are safely initialized on reset.

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.cpp:508-524](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L508-L524)

### Checkpoint Recovery
- Abandoning a run credits souls and updates deepest room (excluding god mode).
- Closing the game performs the same partial credit and then navigates back to the previous page.

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.cpp:2341-2360](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L2341-L2360)

### Difficulty Scaling Algorithms
- Three difficulties adjust:
  - Starting life delta.
  - Hazard multiplier (affects saw/orb periods and hunter speed).
  - Speed multiplier (maximum marble speed).
  - Gold multiplier (souls earned at end of run).
  - Invulnerability duration after damage.
- These multipliers are applied during run initialization and influence entity behavior and rewards.

**Section sources**
- [marble_game.cpp:260-284](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/marble_game.cpp#L260-L284)

## Dependency Analysis
- UI layer depends on LVGL objects created once and reused; no allocations during gameplay loops.
- Game logic depends on NVS preferences for persistence and LVGL timer for frame pacing.
- Room definitions depend on static Spec arrays; entity rendering depends on style helpers and detail children.
- Physics depends on constants for gravity-to-acceleration conversion, friction, bounce, and substep integration.

## Performance Considerations
- Hot path avoids dynamic memory allocation and string conversions; labels are only rewritten when values change.
- Substep integration prevents tunneling at high speeds.
- Preallocated pools for entities and decorations minimize runtime overhead.
- HUD caching reduces unnecessary LVGL invalidations.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Save corruption: If the magic value mismatches, the game resets to defaults; ensure schema version bump when modifying save layout.
- Mid-run loss: Closing or abandoning preserves souls and deepest room; verify end_run and close handlers credit progress appropriately.
- Portal not opening: Ensure runes are collected and exit style updates reflect open state; check gate cache to avoid constant re-styling.
- Damage looping: Verify invulnerability timers and shield consumption; confirm pit falls reset position and velocity.

## Conclusion
The marble roguelite implements a robust state schema combining persistent meta-progression with dynamic run-time state. Level progression is structured around six carefully designed rooms with deterministic layouts and controlled randomness. Player attributes, inventory, and power-ups interact through clear scaling rules and difficulty modifiers. The save system ensures resilience against corruption and supports partial checkpoint recovery. Performance is optimized for embedded constraints with preallocated resources and efficient rendering updates.

## Introduction
This document describes the pinball game state schema and runtime behavior for the “Neon Apron” table implemented in the project. It covers flipper mechanics, ball trajectory and collision resolution, bumper and target interactions, scoring with combos and multipliers, table layout including ramps and rollovers, multiball sequences, special modes (Frenzy), and persistence via NVS. It also provides examples of physics state serialization, ball collision detection, mode transitions, mid-game save/recovery, and error handling around physics calculations.

## Project Structure
The pinball feature is composed of:
- A header defining persistent state structures and public API
- A large implementation file containing all game logic, physics, rendering, UI construction, and input handling
- A YAML page that declares four empty containers used by the C++ code to build the full table at runtime

```mermaid
graph TB
YAML["UI Page (pinball_game.yaml)<br/>Defines 4 containers"] --> CPP["Game Logic (pinball_game.cpp)<br/>Builds table, runs physics, renders"]
H["Header (pinball_game.h)<br/>Persistent structs + API"] --> CPP
CPP --> LVGL["LVGL Runtime<br/>Drawing & Timers"]
CPP --> NVS["NVS Preferences<br/>Persist Save/Load"]
```

## Core Components
- Persistent save schema: compact, trivially copyable structures for career stats, top scores, and settings
- Game state machine: hub, playing, paused, game over, scores, settings
- Physics subsystem: gravity, friction, sub-stepping, collisions against walls/arches/flippers/bumpers/slingshots/targets/rollovers
- Scoring system: base points, multiplier, Frenzy bonus, Multiball jackpot, skill shot, lane rollovers, drop targets, banks
- Modes: Frenzy (time-limited bumpers), Multiball (extra balls, multiplier), Skill Shot (targeted rollover)
- Input: touch zones for flippers and plunger; IMU-based nudge and tilt
- Rendering: static table geometry built once; dynamic actors updated per frame
- Persistence: load/save to NVS with magic versioning

## Architecture Overview
High-level flow:
- Open: set portrait orientation, build UI once, start timer, show hub
- Tick loop: handle inputs, update physics (sub-steps), resolve collisions, score events, render updates, HUD sync
- Close: persist career stats, stop timer, restore landscape orientation, navigate back

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "Player"
participant UI as "LVGL Timer"
participant Game as "Pinball : : tick_cb"
participant Phys as "Physics Step"
participant Render as "Render/HUD"
participant NVS as "NVS"
User->>UI : Start game
UI->>Game : open()
Game->>Game : screen_portrait(true)
Game->>Game : build_ui()
Game->>UI : lv_timer_create(tick_cb)
UI-->>Game : tick_cb() every TICK_MS
Game->>Phys : step_flippers(), collide_*(), add_score()
Phys-->>Game : state changes (modes, multiball, drain)
Game->>Render : render_flippers(), render_balls(), effects, hud_sync
alt End or Exit
Game->>NVS : persist_save()
Game->>UI : screen_portrait(false), navigate back
end
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Flipper Mechanics
- Two flippers with rest and active angles, angular speed, and a punch boost when pressed
- Collision uses segment distance and relative velocity at contact point, applying impulse based on flipper angular motion
- Flippers are disabled during TILT penalty window

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Flipper Update"]) --> SetTarget["Set target angle<br/>(rest or active if not tilted)"]
SetTarget --> MoveAngle["Advance angle toward target<br/>by FLIP_SPEED * dt"]
MoveAngle --> Collide["For each ball:<br/>point-segment distance to flipper"]
Collide --> Hit{"Collision?"}
Hit -- No --> NextBall["Next ball"]
Hit -- Yes --> Resolve["Penetration fix<br/>reflect relative velocity<br/>apply punch if pressed"]
Resolve --> NextBall
NextBall --> End(["Done"])
```

### Ball Trajectory and Collision Detection
- Gravity pulls ball down; friction reduces velocity each sub-step
- Sub-stepping (4 steps per tick) prevents tunneling through thin rails
- Collisions:
  - Walls/rails: capsule collision against segments with restitution
  - Arch: circular constraint above center line
  - Flippers: moving segment with angular velocity
  - Bumpers: circle-circle push and kick
  - Slingshots: segment collision with directional normal kick
  - Targets: horizontal bar collision; dropping target on hit
  - Rollovers: trigger zone without physical collision
- Speed capped to MAX_SPEED

```mermaid
flowchart TD
S(["physics_step(dt)"]) --> Integrate["Integrate gravity + move ball<br/>apply friction"]
Integrate --> Walls["Collide with walls/rails<br/>capsule vs segment"]
Walls --> Arch["Collide with arch<br/>circular constraint"]
Arch --> Flips["Collide with flippers<br/>moving segment"]
Flips --> Bumpers["Bumper hits<br/>push + kick"]
Bumpers --> Slings["Slingshot hits<br/>normal kick"]
Slings --> Targets["Drop targets<br/>score + bank check"]
Targets --> Roll["Rollover triggers<br/>skill shot / lanes"]
Roll --> Cap["Cap speed to MAX_SPEED"]
Cap --> Drain{"Drain or Plunger return?"}
Drain -- Drain --> BallDrained["ball_drained()"]
Drain -- Return --> Serve["Return to plunger zone"]
BallDrained --> E(["End step"])
Serve --> E
```

### Bumper Interactions
- Three bumpers arranged in triangle; on hit, ball is pushed away with fixed kick magnitude
- Flash effect briefly shown; score added; during Multiball, extra jackpot fraction scored
- Frenzy mode triples bumper score

### Scoring Targets and Banks
- Three drop targets; hitting one drops it visually and adds score
- When all three are down, bank completes: alternates between starting Frenzy and Multiball
- Lane rollovers under the arch provide small scores; lighting resets when all three turn off

### Table Layout and Ramp Configurations
- Fixed geometry constants define screen size, HUD height, field dimensions
- Arch defined as a perfect semi-circle constraint for smooth rolling
- Plunger lane boundaries and bottom floor ensure safe return to launch position
- Rails and guides drawn as polylines with tight bounding boxes to minimize redraw area

### Multiball Sequences and Special Modes
- Multiball: spawns an additional ball from plunger lane, sets multiplier to 2, tracks active multiball state; ends when only one ball remains
- Frenzy: time-limited mode that triples bumper scores; triggered by completing target banks
- Skill Shot: after launch, a random rollover is highlighted; hitting it within time grants a large bonus

### Scoring System: Combos, Jackpots, Progressive Multipliers
- Base scores for bumpers, slings, targets, lanes, skill shot, bank completion
- Global multiplier applies to all scoring; increased during Multiball
- Jackpot fraction scored during Multiball on bumper hits
- Bonus balls awarded at score thresholds
- Bank completions alternate between Frenzy and Multiball to ensure both rewards occur over a game

### Mode Transition Logic
- States: OFF, HUB, SCORES, SETTINGS, PLAYING, PAUSED, GAMEOVER
- Transitions driven by user actions and game events (drain, multiball end, bank complete)
- Pause toggles via HUD click; resume returns to PLAYING with same state

```mermaid
PLAYING --> GAMEOVER : all balls drained

GAMEOVER --> HUB : hub
```

### Physics State Serialization and Persistence
- Save structure includes career totals, best single-ball score, tilt count, multiball count, top 10 scores, and settings (nudge sensitivity, sound flag, screen flip, invert nudge, IMU calibration)
- Magic number ensures compatibility; invalid or missing saves reset to defaults
- Persist functions write immediately at key moments (end of game, exit, settings change)


### Mid-Game Saves and Recovery
- On pause or exit while playing, career stats are updated and saved before closing
- Resume from pause restores exact game state (no partial physics snapshot needed)
- If game is abandoned, current score is recorded in career totals and top scores list

### Error Handling Around Physics Calculations
- NaN guards on IMU inputs prevent corrupting nudge calculations
- Speed capping avoids runaway velocities
- One-way gate (plunger flap) prevents reverse entry into plunger lane
- Safe checks for active balls and states before mutations

## Performance Considerations
- Static table geometry built once; only dynamic elements redrawn
- Polylines use tight bounding boxes to minimize invalidation
- Sub-stepping improves collision accuracy without excessive cost
- HUD text updates are cached to avoid redundant writes
- Timer period adapts between menu and gameplay to reduce CPU usage when idle

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Screen stays rotated after abnormal exit: ensure all exits call close() to restore landscape rotation
- Balls stuck in plunger lane: verify return-to-plunger thresholds and that auto-launch timer fires
- Nudge feels reversed: adjust invert_nudge setting; recalibrate flat orientation
- TILT too sensitive: lower nudge sensitivity; ensure proper flat calibration
- Scores not updating: confirm multiplier and mode flags are correctly applied; check HUD cache invalidation

## Conclusion
The pinball implementation provides a robust, performant state machine with precise physics, clear scoring rules, and reliable persistence. The design separates static geometry from dynamic actors, uses conservative collision tolerances, and maintains responsive UI updates. Modes like Frenzy and Multiball create engaging progression, while careful error handling and persistence ensure stability across sessions.

## Introduction
This document explains the trivia quiz game state schema, focusing on question set management, answer tracking, scoring logic, and difficulty progression. It details category organization with topic-based question pools, randomization algorithms, and the scoring system including point multipliers, streak bonuses, and penalty mechanisms. It also covers question bank management, difficulty adjustment, session persistence for long-term play tracking, and performance analytics.

## Project Structure
The trivia game is implemented as a self-contained LVGL page with minimal YAML scaffolding and rich C++ logic:
- UI containers are declared in a YAML file; all gameplay UI is built at runtime in C++.
- The core game engine defines board topology, state machine, rendering, input handling, and persistence.
- A large static question bank is organized by category and difficulty.

```mermaid

TRIVIA_CPP --> STATE["Game State Machine"]
TRIVIA_CPP --> QUESTIONS["Question Bank (by Category/Difficulty)"]
TRIVIA_CPP --> PERSIST["NVS Persistence"]
TRIVIA_CPP --> RENDER["LVGL Rendering & Timers"]
```

## Core Components
- Board topology: 73 nodes forming a ring, spokes, and hub.
- Game state machine: menus, setup, rules, stats, settings, confirmation, play phases, category pick, question, reveal, pause, victory.
- Question bank: per-category arrays with difficulty tags and four choices.
- Persistence: NVS save/load structure includes settings, global stats, and current game state.
- Rendering: preallocated LVGL objects, caches to minimize redraws, adaptive tick rate.

Key data structures:
- TriviaStats: cumulative games played, correct/incorrect counts, per-category correct/incorrect, wedges won, best turns.
- TriviaTeamSave: team name, color index, wedge mask, position.
- TriviaSave: magic, stats, persistent settings, current game snapshot.
- Team: runtime team info (name, color, wedges, position).
- BoardCell: cell type and category.

## Architecture Overview
The trivia game uses an event-driven LVGL loop with a central timer that drives animations, timers, and state transitions. Input callbacks route user actions into state transitions. The question draw mechanism ensures no repeats until the bag is exhausted.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant UI as "LVGL Layer"
participant Tick as "tick() Timer"
participant State as "State Machine"
participant QBank as "Question Bank"
participant Persist as "NVS"
User->>UI : Tap Roll / IMU Shake
UI->>Tick : Event queued
Tick->>State : roll_dice()
State->>State : animate dice, compute reach
State->>State : PH_CHOOSE highlight reachable cells
User->>UI : Tap reachable cell
UI->>Tick : Cell selected
Tick->>State : start_move(dest), finish_move()
State->>QBank : prepare_question(cat or final)
State-->>UI : Show question card + timer
User->>UI : Choose answer or time out
UI->>Tick : answer(slot)
Tick->>State : update stats, decide wedge/final
State->>Persist : persist_save() on key milestones
State-->>UI : Reveal verdict, continue or next turn
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Board Topology and Movement
- The board has 42 ring nodes, 30 spoke nodes (6 categories × 5 steps), and 1 hub node.
- Neighbors are computed based on ring adjacency, spoke connections, and hub links.
- Reachability is computed via DFS without backtracking to exactly N steps from current position.
- Path reconstruction animates pawn movement along the chosen path.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Roll Dice"]) --> ComputeReach["Compute reachable nodes (DFS, no backtrack)"]
ComputeReach --> Choices{"Number of reachable?"}
Choices --> |0| SkipTurn["Skip turn message, next team"]
Choices --> |1| AutoMove["Auto move to only destination"]
Choices --> |>1| Highlight["Highlight reachable cells"]
Highlight --> Select["User selects destination"]
Select --> Animate["Animate hop-by-hop movement"]
Animate --> Resolve["Resolve cell type"]
Resolve --> Hub{"Hub?"}
Hub --> |Yes| FinalCheck{"All wedges?"}
FinalCheck --> |Yes| FinalCatPick["Final category pick"]
FinalCheck --> |No| CatPick["Category pick"]
Resolve --> HQorCat{"HQ or Category?"}
HQorCat --> |HQ| PrepareHQ["Prepare HQ question"]
HQorCat --> |Cat| PrepareCat["Prepare category question"]
Resolve --> RollCase{"Roll case?"}
RollCase --> |Yes| ReRoll["Re-roll immediately"]
```

### Question Set Management and Randomization
- Questions are stored per category with difficulty tags (easy/medium/hard).
- Each category has a shuffled bag (Fisher-Yates) to avoid repetition within a game.
- Difficulty masking filters questions based on current difficulty setting.
- If no question matches the mask, fallback returns any available question.

```mermaid

+const char* w1
+const char* w2
+const char* w3
}
class Bag {
+uint8_t[] indices
+uint8_t pos
+shuffle()
+draw(mask) TriviaQuestion
}
TriviaQuestion <.. Bag : "referenced by"
```

### Answer Validation Logic
- Correct slot is randomly assigned among four options using shuffle.
- On answer selection, correctness is compared against the stored correct slot.
- Time-out is handled by passing a sentinel slot value.
- Verdict display highlights correct and picked answers, shows feedback text.

```mermaid

State->>State : If HQ and not already owned -> award wedge
State-->>UI : Show reveal overlay with colors and feedback
```

### Scoring System, Multipliers, Streaks, Penalties
- Correct answers increment global and per-category counters; incorrect answers increment corresponding negative counters.
- Winning a wedge occurs only on HQ cells when the category wedge is not yet owned.
- Correct answers grant replay opportunity; incorrect answers pass turn to next team.
- Final question: correct answer wins the game immediately; incorrect answer ends the attempt and passes turn.
- There are no explicit point multipliers or streak bonuses in the code; scoring is binary per question with wedge ownership gating rewards.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Ans["Answer Selected"] --> Check{"Correct?"}
Check --> |Yes| IncOk["Increment q_ok, cat_ok[c], game_ok"]
IncOk --> HQ{"HQ cell and wedge missing?"}
HQ --> |Yes| AwardWedge["Award wedge, increment wedges_won"]
HQ --> |No| Replay["Replay allowed"]
Check --> |No| IncKo["Increment q_ko, cat_ko[c], game_ko"]
IncKo --> NextTeam["Next team"]
AwardWedge --> Replay
Replay --> Continue["Continue same team"]
NextTeam --> Continue
```

### Difficulty Progression and Adjustment
- Difficulty is a setting with three levels: easy, normal, expert.
- Difficulty masks select subsets of questions by difficulty tag.
- During setup and settings screens, players can change difficulty; it affects subsequent question draws.
- No dynamic difficulty adjustment algorithm is implemented beyond the static mask.

```mermaid

```

### Session Persistence and Long-Term Tracking
- NVS stores magic, stats, settings, and current game snapshot.
- On open, if a saved game exists, it resumes; otherwise, hub screen is shown.
- Persistent fields include team names/colors, positions, wedge masks, RNG seed, and counters.
- Stats include games played, total correct/incorrect, per-category correct/incorrect, wedges won, and best turns.

```mermaid
classDiagram
class TriviaStats {
+games_played
+q_ok
+q_ko
+cat_ok[6]
```

### Performance Analytics and Rendering Optimizations
- Adaptive tick rate: faster during animations, slower during static phases.
- Render caches prevent redundant LVGL style updates each frame.
- Minimal allocations in hot paths; labels updated only when values change.
- Message bar provides transient status updates.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Frame["tick()"] --> DetectAnim{"Animation active?"}
DetectAnim --> |Yes| FastTick["Set fast period (~33ms)"]
DetectAnim --> |No| SlowTick["Set slow period (~100ms)"]
FastTick --> Render["Render layers, HUD, dice, panel, board, question"]
SlowTick --> Render
Render --> Cache["Use signature caches to skip redraws"]
```

## Performance Considerations
- Avoid dynamic memory allocation in hot paths; reuse preallocated LVGL objects.
- Use signature-based caching to minimize style changes per frame.
- Adaptive timer reduces CPU usage during idle phases.
- Keep string operations minimal; use snprintf buffers and conditional label updates.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- If no moves are possible after rolling, the game will skip to the next team automatically.
- If the question bag runs out under strict difficulty filtering, the system falls back to any question in the category.
- NVS corruption is guarded by magic checks; defaults are restored if invalid.
- IMU shake triggers are debounced to prevent accidental re-rolls.

## Conclusion
The trivia game implements a robust state schema with clear separation between UI, game logic, and persistence. It supports multiple teams, category-based question pools, randomized draws without repetition, and a straightforward scoring model centered on wedge acquisition and final victory. While there are no explicit point multipliers or streak bonuses, replay opportunities act as immediate reinforcement for correct answers. The system is optimized for embedded constraints with careful rendering and minimal allocations, and it persists both settings and ongoing sessions for long-term play tracking.

## Introduction
This document describes the light configuration schemas and control architecture used by the Tab5 system to manage multiple light entities. It covers:
- Light entity state structures (brightness, color values, group membership)
- Multi-light control architecture for simultaneous management
- Color preset system with predefined colors and named white tones
- Brightness arc implementation with percentage display and shortcut buttons
- Examples of state updates, group operations, and color transitions
- Error handling for invalid inputs and network issues

The system integrates ESPHome UI components with Home Assistant services to provide a responsive, debounced user experience while keeping presentation logic centralized in C++.

## Project Structure
Light functionality spans several files:
- UI definitions for the light popup and color presets
- Sensors that mirror Home Assistant light states and brightness attributes
- Scripts that debounce interactions and open the light popup with synchronized state
- C++ helpers that update LVGL widgets safely and consistently
- Globals that track the currently selected light entity
- HA controls that expose screen state and navigation

```mermaid
graph TB
UI["UI: light_popup.yaml"] --> Script["Script: tab5_light_popup_show"]
UI --> Preset["Preset Button: light_color_preset_btn.yaml"]
Script --> Cpp["C++: show_light_popup_ui / sync_light_popup_brightness"]
Sensors["Sensors: tab5-sensors-domotique.yaml"] --> Cpp
Cpp --> HA["Home Assistant Services"]
Globals["Globals: current_light_entity"] --> Script
HA_Screen["HA Controls: tab5-ha-controls.yaml"] --> UI
```

## Core Components
- Light Popup UI: A modal with three cards — Lamp selector (Chambre/Salon/LEDs), Brightness (arc + % + shortcuts), and Colors (named whites + preset palette). All actions target the dynamic entity id(current_light_entity).
- Color Preset Buttons: Reusable template button that sends a light.turn_on with a named color.
- State Mirroring: ESPHome sensors subscribe to each light’s on/off state and brightness attribute, updating the UI via C++ helpers.
- Debounce Scripts: The brightness arc triggers a debounced script that calls light.turn_on once the interaction settles.
- C++ Helpers: Centralized functions to update icons, arcs, and labels safely, including guards for closed popups and active drags.
- Globals: current_light_entity tracks which light is being edited in the popup.
- HA Controls: Expose the current screen name, including “Lights” when the light popup is visible.

## Architecture Overview
The multi-light control architecture uses a shared popup that dynamically targets one light at a time via a global variable. When opened, it reads the current on/off state and brightness from ESPHome sensors and renders them into LVGL widgets. User interactions either call Home Assistant services directly (toggle, turn off all) or go through debounced scripts (brightness arc). Real-time updates flow back from Home Assistant to ESPHome sensors, which push changes to the UI via C++ helpers.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant U as "User"
participant UI as "Popup UI"
participant S as "ESPHome Script"
participant H as "Home Assistant"
participant L as "Light Entity"
U->>UI : Open light popup
UI->>S : Execute tab5_light_popup_show(light_idx)
S->>H : Read light states & brightness
H-->>S : is_on[], brightness[]
S->>UI : show_light_popup_ui(...)
Note over UI : Title, selection highlight, power icon, arc synced
U->>UI : Drag brightness arc
UI->>S : Execute tab5_debounce_light_brightness
S->>H : light.turn_on(entity_id=current_light_entity, brightness=arc_value)
H-->>L : Apply brightness
L-->>H : New brightness attribute
H-->>UI : Sensor update -> sync_light_popup_brightness()
UI->>UI : Update arc and % label
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Light Entity State Model
- Brightness: Represented as an integer 0–255 in the LVGL arc; displayed as a percentage (0–100%) in the label. The arc value is clamped to 0–255 before rendering.
- Color: Two mechanisms:
  - Named whites via color_name (e.g., warmwhite, navajowhite, white).
  - Preset colors via color_name using standard names (e.g., gold, orange, red, blue, green).
- Group Membership: A “Turn off all” action targets a comma-separated list of light entities to switch them off together.

Data flows:
- On/off state and brightness are mirrored by ESPHome sensors bound to Home Assistant light entities.
- The popup reads these sensors to initialize and continuously refresh the UI.

### Multi-Light Control Architecture
- Shared Popup: A single popup instance manages three logical lights (Chambre, Salon, LEDs). Selection is tracked by index and reflected visually.
- Dynamic Targeting: All service calls use the dynamic id(current_light_entity) so the same UI can control any selected light without hardcoding entity IDs.
- Global Context: current_light_entity is set when opening the popup and drives which sensor updates apply to the UI.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Open Popup"]) --> Select["Set current_light_entity<br/>and read is_on[], brightness[]"]
Select --> Render["Render title, selection, power icon, arc"]
Render --> Interact{"User Action?"}
Interact --> |Toggle| Toggle["Call light.toggle on current_light_entity"]
Interact --> |All Off| AllOff["Call light.turn_off on grouped entities"]
Interact --> |Brightness| Bright["Debounced light.turn_on with brightness"]
Interact --> |Color| Color["Call light.turn_on with color_name"]
Toggle --> Sync["Sensor updates -> UI sync"]
AllOff --> Sync
Bright --> Sync
Color --> Sync
Sync --> End(["Updated UI"])
```

### Color Preset System
- Named Whites: Three buttons send color_name values representing white temperature variants.
- Preset Palette: A 4×3 grid of round buttons applies standard color names to the selected light. Each button is a reusable template that injects the color_name payload.

Usage examples:
- Warm white: send color_name = warmwhite
- Blue: send color_name = blue
- Green: send color_name = green

**Section sources**
- [light_popup.yaml:285-339](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/light_popup.yaml#L285-L339)

### Brightness Arc Implementation
- Arc Range: 0–255 mapped to 0–100% display.
- Live Percentage Label: Updated on every arc change.
- Debounced Updates: A script delays sending light.turn_on until the user stops dragging, preventing excessive network calls.
- Shortcuts: Four buttons set specific percentages (10%, 35%, 65%, 100%) and immediately update both the arc and label.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
A["Arc value changed"] --> B["Update % label"]
B --> C["Execute debounce script"]
C --> D{"Idle timeout elapsed?"}
D --> |No| E["Restart delay"]
D --> |Yes| F["Send light.turn_on with brightness"]
F --> G["HA returns new brightness"]
G --> H["sync_light_popup_brightness updates arc and label"]
```

## Performance Considerations
- Debouncing: Brightness adjustments are debounced to avoid flooding Home Assistant with requests during continuous slider movement.
- Conditional Updates: Brightness synchronization skips updates when the popup is hidden or when the user is actively dragging the arc, preventing visual jitter.
- Clamping: Arc values are clamped to valid ranges to ensure consistent behavior even if unexpected values arrive.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and mitigations:
- Invalid color values: If a color_name is not supported by the light, Home Assistant will reject the command. Verify the color name exists in your light integration.
- Out-of-range brightness settings: The arc enforces 0–255 internally; the percentage label displays 0–100%. If brightness appears incorrect, check the underlying light’s brightness scale and ensure the device supports the requested level.
- Network connectivity issues: During rapid brightness changes, only one request is sent after the user stops dragging. If the device is offline, the UI may lag behind; reconnecting will resynchronize via sensor updates.
- Popup state conflicts: If the popup is closed or the arc is being dragged, brightness updates from Home Assistant are ignored to prevent knob jumping. Ensure you are not interacting with the arc when expecting immediate sync.

## Conclusion
The Tab5 light system provides a robust, user-friendly interface for controlling multiple lights with precise brightness and color management. By centralizing UI updates in C++, debouncing network calls, and mirroring Home Assistant state through ESPHome sensors, it delivers a smooth and reliable experience. The modular design makes it easy to extend with additional lights, colors, or grouping strategies while maintaining consistency and performance.

## Introduction
This document specifies the weather data schemas used by the Tab5 system, focusing on:
- Hourly forecast payload format (temperature, humidity proxy via precipitation probability, wind speed where applicable, and precipitation probability).
- Daily forecast structure covering up to 15 days with condition codes, temperature ranges, and related flags.
- Meteo-France alert schema including vigilance levels and hazard types.
- Rain intensity levels and their visual mapping.
- Validation rules, error handling for malformed data, and backward compatibility considerations.

The goal is to provide a clear contract between Home Assistant (HA) and the Tab5 firmware so that updates remain robust and compatible over time.

## Project Structure
Weather data flows from HA templates and automations into ESPHome services, which parse compact payloads and update LVGL UI widgets. Key components:
- HA prepares serialized payloads for hourly/daily forecasts and alerts.
- ESPHome parses these payloads into internal structures and refreshes forecast tiles and panels.
- Rain intensity and alert visuals are updated based on parsed values.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant<br/>Templates & Automations"] --> |Bulk payloads| FW["ESPHome Firmware<br/>Parsing & UI Update"]
FW --> LVGL["LVGL Widgets<br/>Forecast Tiles & Panels"]
FW --> Alerts["Meteo-France Alerts<br/>Vigilance Levels"]
FW --> Rain["Rain Intensity Bars<br/>1h Forecast"]
```

## Core Components
- Hourly forecast data model:
  - Fields: index (0–14), hour text, condition code, temperature (float), precipitation amount/probability (float).
  - Stored in an array of 15 slots; UI renders 5 visible at a time across pages.
- Daily forecast data model:
  - Fields: day label, condition code, min/max temperature, flags (rest day, Sunday, past), optional opening hours string.
  - Stored in an array of 15 slots; UI renders 5 visible at a time across pages.
- Meteo-France alert payload:
  - Pipe-delimited fields: rain phrase, global vigilance level, and per-hazard vigilance levels (wind, flood, thunderstorms, rain-flood, snow/ice, cold wave, waves-submersion, heatwave, avalanches).
- Rain intensity levels:
  - Four levels mapped to colors and bar heights for a 1-hour short-term graph.

## Architecture Overview
The end-to-end flow:
1. HA templates build compact payloads for hourly and daily forecasts, plus alerts and rain intensity.
2. ESPHome receives bulk payloads and parses them into internal arrays.
3. UI refresh functions render forecast tiles and panels using parsed data.
4. Alert and rain panels update icons, colors, and bar heights based on vigilance levels and intensities.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant FW as "ESPHome Firmware"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
HA->>FW : Push hourly bulk payload
FW->>FW : Parse hourly records (index|hour|condition|temp|precip)
FW->>UI : Refresh hourly forecast tiles
HA->>FW : Push daily bulk payload
FW->>FW : Parse daily records (day|condition|tmin|tmax|flags|hours)
FW->>UI : Refresh daily forecast tiles
HA->>FW : Push Meteo-France alerts (pipe-delimited)
FW->>FW : Map vigilance levels to colors/icons
FW->>UI : Update alert panel
HA->>FW : Push 1h rain intensity (index_5mn, intensity)
FW->>FW : Map intensity to color/height
FW->>UI : Update rain bars
```

- [automations_examples.yaml.example:260-288](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L260-L288)

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Hourly Forecast Schema
- Payload format:
  - Delimiter: semicolon separates records; pipe separates fields within a record.
  - Record fields:
    - idx: integer 0–14
    - heure_texte: string like "HH:00"
    - condition: string code (e.g., sunny, cloudy, rainy, pouring)
    - temp: float temperature
    - pluvio: float precipitation amount or probability indicator
- Internal model:
  - Array of 15 entries with fields: hour text, condition, temperature, precipitation.
- UI rendering:
  - Five tiles shown per page; left-to-right order is reverse of index.
  - Temperature colored by gradient; precipitation displayed when > 0.

Validation rules:
- Max payload length enforced to avoid memory issues.
- Only indices within 0–14 are accepted; extra fields ignored.
- Missing or malformed numeric fields default safely via parsing.

Example construction (conceptual):
- Three chunks of five records each to keep payloads under the limit.
- Each chunk pushed separately to ESPHome.

### Daily Forecast Schema
- Payload format:
  - Delimiter: semicolon separates records; pipe separates fields within a record.
  - Record fields:
    - jour: integer 0–14
    - nom_jour: string day label
    - condition: string code
    - tmin: float minimum temperature
    - tmax: float maximum temperature
    - est_repos: boolean flag ("1"/"0")
    - est_dimanche: boolean flag ("1"/"0")
    - est_passe: boolean flag ("1"/"0")
    - heures_ouverture: optional string "HH:MM-HH:MM"
- Internal model:
  - Array of 15 entries with fields: day label, condition, min/max temps, flags, opening hours.
- UI rendering:
  - Five tiles shown per page; displays day label, min/max temperatures, and weather icon.
  - Past days show placeholders instead of temperatures.

Validation rules:
- Max payload length enforced to avoid memory issues.
- Indices within 0–14 accepted; extra fields ignored.
- Flags parsed as single-character booleans.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:384-436](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L384-L436)
- [tab5_custom.h:16-25](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.h#L16-L25)

### Meteo-France Alert Schema
- Payload format:
  - Pipe-delimited fields:
    - phrase_pluie: human-readable next-rain phrase
    - globale: overall vigilance level ("Vert", "Jaune", "Orange", "Rouge")
    - vent: wind vigilance level
    - inondation: flood vigilance level
    - orages: thunderstorm vigilance level
    - pluie_inondation: rain-flood vigilance level
    - neige_verglas: snow/ice vigilance level
    - grand_froid: cold wave vigilance level
    - vagues_submersion: waves/submersion vigilance level
    - canicule: heatwave vigilance level
    - avalanches: avalanche vigilance level
- UI behavior:
  - Date color changes based on global vigilance level.
  - Up to four active hazards displayed with icons and severity-based colors.
  - "Vert" or empty/unknown levels are treated as inactive.

Validation rules:
- Buffer size increased to accommodate longer phrases and full payloads.
- Missing fields default to empty strings; invalid levels ignored.

**Section sources**
- [automations_examples.yaml.example:325-331](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L325-L331)
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:200-279](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L200-L279)

### Rain Intensity Levels and Visual Mapping
- Supported levels:
  - Pluie faible (light rain)
  - Pluie modérée (moderate rain)
  - Pluie forte (heavy rain)
  - Pluie très forte / Pluie trés forte (extreme rain; both spellings supported)
- Visual mapping:
  - Each level maps to a specific color and bar height.
  - Empty state uses inactive color and zero height.
- Input:
  - index_5mn: integer 0–8 representing 5-minute intervals within a 1-hour window.
  - intensite: one of the above levels.

Validation rules:
- Index must be within 0–8; otherwise no bar is updated.
- Unknown intensity leaves the bar inactive.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:323-370](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L323-L370)

### Data Flow and Processing Logic
- Parsing:
  - In-place tokenization avoids heap fragmentation and respects SRAM constraints.
  - Strict field counts ensure robustness against malformed payloads.
- Rendering:
  - UI refresh functions update labels, icons, and colors based on parsed data.
  - Icon roll animations only trigger when conditions change.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Receive Payload"]) --> ValidateLen{"Payload Length OK?"}
ValidateLen --> |No| Reject["Reject to avoid OOM"]
ValidateLen --> |Yes| SplitRecords["Split by ';'"]
SplitRecords --> ForEachRecord["For each record"]
ForEachRecord --> SplitFields["Split by '|'"]
SplitFields --> ValidateFields{"Fields >= Required?"}
ValidateFields --> |No| Skip["Skip record"]
ValidateFields --> |Yes| MapFields["Map to internal model"]
MapFields --> UpdateUI["Refresh UI elements"]
UpdateUI --> End(["Done"])
Reject --> End
Skip --> End
```

## Performance Considerations
- Payload size limits prevent out-of-memory errors on constrained devices.
- In-place parsing reduces heap usage and fragmentation.
- UI updates are optimized to avoid redundant repaints (e.g., icon roll suppression when unchanged).
- Chunked hourly payloads reduce latency and risk of large transfers.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Malformed payload:
  - Symptom: No update or partial display.
  - Cause: Incorrect delimiters, missing fields, or excessive length.
  - Resolution: Ensure correct field order and count; keep payloads under the enforced limit.
- Invalid indices:
  - Symptom: Some tiles not updating.
  - Cause: Index outside 0–14 (hourly) or 0–14 (daily).
  - Resolution: Validate indices before sending.
- Unknown vigilance levels:
  - Symptom: Alerts not shown or miscolored.
  - Cause: Non-standard level strings.
  - Resolution: Use standard levels ("Vert", "Jaune", "Orange", "Rouge"); ignore unknowns.
- Rain intensity mismatches:
  - Symptom: Bars not reflecting expected intensity.
  - Cause: Unsupported spelling or index out of range.
  - Resolution: Use supported levels and indices 0–8; accept both "très" and "trés" variants.

## Conclusion
The Tab5 weather data schemas define a compact, robust contract between HA and the firmware. By adhering to the specified payload formats, validation rules, and visual mappings, integrators can ensure reliable display of hourly and daily forecasts, Meteo-France alerts, and rain intensity. Backward compatibility is maintained through graceful handling of missing or unexpected fields and support for known variations.

  - est_repos: "1"/"0"
  - est_dimanche: "1"/"0"
  - est_passe: "1"/"0"
  - heures_ouverture: optional "HH:MM-HH:MM"
- Alert payload fields:
  - phrase_pluie: string
  - globale: "Vert"/"Jaune"/"Orange"/"Rouge"
  - Hazard levels: same set of vigilance levels per type
- Rain intensity:
  - Levels: "Pluie faible", "Pluie modérée", "Pluie forte", "Pluie très forte"/"Pluie trés forte"
  - Index: integer 0–8

  - "0|Auj.|rainy|10.0|15.0|0|0|0|09:00-18:00;1|Dem.|cloudy|8.0|14.0|0|0|0|"

  - "Pluie dans 10 mn|Orange|Jaune|Vert|Jaune|Vert|Vert|Vert|Vert|Vert|Vert"

Note: These are illustrative; actual payloads must conform to the documented field order and delimiters.

- Tolerate missing fields by defaulting to safe values.
- Accept known variations (e.g., "très" vs "trés").
- Ignore unknown vigilance levels rather than failing.
- Maintain payload size limits to avoid breaking older firmware versions.

## Introduction
This document provides comprehensive API documentation for the alert management ESPHome services that power the Tab5 central rotating card system. It focuses on:
- Bulk Home Assistant alert updates via tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk, supporting up to 4 dismissible alerts with severity-based color coding and integration into the central rotator.
- Informational text updates via tab5_maj_info_texte, supporting multi-line text, color coding (Rouge/Orange/Blanc), and dismissal tracking using a local storage mechanism.
- Shutter status updates via tab5_maj_volet_etat, handling physical states (En_mouvement/Ouvert/Ferme/Partiel) and corresponding icon updates.
- Dismissal mechanisms using local storage and Home Assistant persistence, visual feedback patterns, and integration with wake word detection during shutter movement.
- Relationships between alerts and other system features such as planning banners and alarm scheduling.

## Project Structure
The alert system spans ESPHome service definitions, C++ UI logic, Home Assistant packages, and UI components:
- ESPHome services are declared in tab5-api-logic.yaml and route payloads to C++ functions in tab5_custom.cpp.
- Global state variables (alert flags, current panel, dismissed IDs) are defined in tab5-globals.yaml.
- Home Assistant configuration includes alert dismissal scripts, input text helpers, and automation examples.
- UI components define interactive elements (e.g., shutter controls) that integrate with alert and shutter state updates.

```mermaid

ESPhome --> Cpp["C++ Logic<br/>tab5_custom.cpp"]
Cpp --> Globals["Globals<br/>tab5-globals.yaml"]
Cpp --> LVGL["LVGL UI"]
HA --> Scripts["Dismiss Scripts<br/>tab5_alerts.yaml"]
LVGL --> UI["UI Components<br/>forecast_daily.yaml, switches_card.yaml"]
```

## Core Components
The core components include:
- **tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk**: Processes bulk alert payloads, updates up to 4 alert slots, applies color coding based on severity, and integrates with the central rotator.
- **tab5_maj_info_texte**: Updates informational text in the central card area, supports multi-line text, color coding, and dismissal tracking.
- **tab5_maj_volet_etat**: Handles shutter status updates, manages physical states, and updates icons accordingly.
- **Dismissal Mechanisms**: Use local storage (tab5_dismissed_local) and Home Assistant input_text.tab5_alerts_dismissed for persistent dismissal tracking.
- **Wake Word Integration**: Enables/disables wake word models during shutter movement for immediate stop commands.

## Architecture Overview
The alert management system follows a push-based architecture where Home Assistant sends updates to ESPHome services, which then update the UI through C++ functions. The central rotating card system manages visibility and transitions between different panels (planning, rain forecast, weather alerts, info panel, and HA alerts).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESPhome as "ESPHome Service"
participant Cpp as "C++ Logic"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
HA->>ESPhome : tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk(payload)
ESPhome->>Cpp : parse_and_update_ha_alerts_bulk()
Cpp->>Cpp : Process payload, apply colors
Cpp->>UI : Update alert slots 0-3
Cpp->>UI : Sync central panel visibility
UI-->>HA : User interaction (dismiss)
HA->>ESPhome : script.tab5_dismiss_alert(alert_id)
ESPhome->>Cpp : Update dismissed list
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk - Bulk Alert Updates
This service processes bulk alert payloads containing up to 4 alert entries. Each entry consists of three pipe-delimited fields: alert ID, color/severity code, and display text. Alerts are displayed in dedicated slots within the central rotating card system.

#### Payload Format
- Maximum 4 alert entries per payload
- Entry format: `alert_id|color_code|display_text`
- Entries separated by semicolons
- Example: `update.home_assistant_core_update|Rouge|Update available;binary_sensor.problem|Orange|System issue`

#### Color Coding System
- Rouge (Red): Critical alerts requiring immediate attention
- Orange: Warning-level alerts
- Blanc (White): Informational alerts
- Colors are applied based on severity codes in the payload

#### Dismissal Mechanism
- Each alert has a unique ID stored in ha_alert_id_0..3 globals
- Tapping an alert triggers dismissal through local storage (tab5_dismissed_local)
- Persistent dismissal tracked in Home Assistant's input_text.tab5_alerts_dismissed
- Dismissed alerts remain hidden until new content is pushed

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start([Service Call]) --> ParsePayload["Parse Payload<br/>Split by ';'"]
ParsePayload --> CheckLimit{"Entries <= 4?"}
CheckLimit --> |No| Truncate["Truncate to 4 entries"]
CheckLimit --> |Yes| ProcessEntry["Process Each Entry"]
ProcessEntry --> SplitFields["Split by '|'"]
SplitFields --> ValidateFields{"Valid Fields?"}
ValidateFields --> |No| SkipEntry["Skip Entry"]
ValidateFields --> |Yes| ApplyColor["Apply Color Based on Severity"]
ApplyColor --> UpdateSlot["Update Alert Slot"]
UpdateSlot --> CheckDismissed{"ID in Dismissed List?"}
CheckDismissed --> |Yes| HideAlert["Hide Alert"]
CheckDismissed --> |No| ShowAlert["Show Alert"]
ShowAlert --> NextEntry["Next Entry"]
HideAlert --> NextEntry
NextEntry --> End([Complete])
```

### tab5_maj_info_texte - Informational Text Updates
This service updates the central card area with informational text that can be either multi-line calendar recaps or single-line weather alerts. It supports color coding and dismissal tracking.

#### Text Processing
- Multi-line text support with newline characters
- Automatic font selection based on line count (large vs small fonts)
- UTF-8 normalization for proper character display
- Inline color markup support using LVGL recolor syntax

#### Color Coding
- Rouge (Red): Critical weather alerts or urgent information
- Orange: Warning-level information
- Blanc (White): Standard informational content
- Colors applied based on couleur parameter

#### Weather-Specific Dismissal Tracking
- meteo_id parameter enables weather-specific dismissal
- Dismissed weather alerts persist across device restarts
- Local storage (tab5_dismissed_local) tracks dismissed items
- Home Assistant synchronization for cross-device consistency

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant Service as "tab5_maj_info_texte"
participant Cpp as "update_info_text_ui"
participant UI as "Central Card"
HA->>Service : texte, couleur, meteo_id
Service->>Cpp : Process text and color
Cpp->>Cpp : Normalize UTF-8 text
Cpp->>Cpp : Check if multi-line
Cpp->>UI : Set appropriate font size
Cpp->>UI : Apply color coding
Cpp->>UI : Check dismissal status
alt Not dismissed
UI->>UI : Display text with animation
else Already dismissed
UI->>UI : Keep hidden
end
```

### tab5_maj_volet_etat - Shutter Status Updates
This service handles roller shutter status updates with physical state management and visual feedback.

#### Physical State Handling
- En_mouvement: Shutter is currently moving (animated arrow icon, INFO color)
- Ouvert: Shutter is fully open (up arrow icon, SUCCESS color)
- Ferme: Shutter is fully closed (down arrow icon, ERROR color)
- Partiel: Shutter is partially open (up arrow icon, SUCCESS color)
- open/closed: Legacy state support for compatibility

#### Visual Feedback Patterns
- Arrow direction changes based on target position (open/closed)
- Color coding reflects operational state (INFO for movement, SUCCESS for open, ERROR for closed)
- State labels update synchronously with icon changes
- Movement indicators provide real-time feedback during operation

#### Wake Word Integration During Movement
- micro_wake_word.stop model enabled when volet_en_mouvement = true
- Voice command "Stop" immediately halts shutter movement
- Model disabled when movement completes
- Provides low-latency voice control without network round-trips

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> Idle
Idle --> Moving : "En_mouvement"
Moving --> Open : "Ouvert/open"
Moving --> Closed : "Ferme/closed"
Moving --> Partial : "Partiel"
Open --> Idle : "Target reached"
Closed --> Idle : "Target reached"
Partial --> Idle : "Target reached"
note right of Moving : "Wake word 'Stop' enabled<br/>Arrow animated<br/>INFO color"
note right of Open : "Up arrow icon<br/>SUCCESS color"
note right of Closed : "Down arrow icon<br/>ERROR color"
```

### Dismissal Mechanisms and Local Storage
The system implements a two-tier dismissal mechanism combining local device storage with Home Assistant persistence.

#### Local Storage (tab5_dismissed_local)
- String-based storage of dismissed alert IDs
- Pruned automatically when alerts are refreshed
- Immediate effect on UI display
- Survives device restarts through ESPHome global persistence

#### Home Assistant Persistence (input_text.tab5_alerts_dismissed)
- Centralized dismissal tracking across multiple devices
- Automated cleanup of obsolete entries
- Synchronization with local storage
- Supports special IDs like 'ha:unavailable' and 'meteo:level'

#### Dismissal Flow
1. User taps alert banner on device
2. Device calls script.tab5_dismiss_alert with alert_id
3. Home Assistant updates input_text entity
4. Automation triggers screen refresh
5. Device receives updated payload with dismissed alerts filtered out

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Tap["User Taps Alert"] --> LocalCheck{"Local Dismissed?"}
LocalCheck --> |Yes| Hide["Hide Alert Immediately"]
LocalCheck --> |No| Show["Show Alert"]
Hide --> Persist["Persist to HA"]
Persist --> Refresh["Trigger Refresh"]
Refresh --> Filter["Filter Dismissed Alerts"]
Filter --> Update["Update UI"]
```
