### Integration with Planning Banners and Alarm Scheduling
Alerts integrate with other system features through shared global state and event-driven updates.

#### Planning Banner Integration
- Planning banners are derived locally from forecast data after tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk
- No separate push required for planning content
- Planning lines update automatically when forecast data changes
- Integration ensures consistent timing information across all displays

#### Alarm Scheduling Integration
- Alarm scheduling uses forecast data to calculate next alarm times
- Invalidated when planning data changes via alarm_invalidate()
- Ensures alarm calculations use current planning information
- Prevents stale alarm schedules after planning updates

#### Central Panel Coordination
- All panels share common visibility logic through sync_central_panel_visibility()
- Active panel tracking prevents conflicts between different content types
- Rotation logic prioritizes active content over passive planning display
- Smooth transitions between different content types

## Performance Considerations
The alert system is optimized for performance through several mechanisms:

- **Payload Size Limits**: Maximum 1024 bytes for alert payloads to prevent memory issues
- **Efficient Parsing**: Direct string parsing without complex object creation
- **Selective Updates**: Only visible panels are updated during refresh cycles
- **Batch Processing**: Multiple alerts processed in single service call
- **Smart Dismissal**: Local storage reduces unnecessary network requests
- **State Caching**: Previous alert IDs cached to detect new alerts efficiently

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and their solutions:

### Alerts Not Appearing
- Verify payload format matches expected structure (id|color|text)
- Check that alert IDs are unique and not already dismissed
- Ensure payload length doesn't exceed 1024 bytes
- Confirm Home Assistant entities exist and have correct states

### Dismissal Not Working
- Check local storage (tab5_dismissed_local) for corrupted entries
- Verify Home Assistant input_text entity is properly configured
- Ensure dismissal scripts are triggered correctly
- Check for duplicate alert IDs causing conflicts

### Shutter Status Issues
- Verify volet_en_mouvement global state updates correctly
- Check that wake word models are enabled/disabled appropriately
- Confirm shutter control scripts receive correct action parameters
- Validate icon updates match expected state transitions

### Color Coding Problems
- Ensure color codes match expected values (Rouge/Orange/Blanc)
- Check UTF-8 encoding for proper character display
- Verify LVGL recolor markup is properly formatted
- Test with known working payloads to isolate issues

- [tab5_custom.cpp:780-870](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L780-L870)

## Conclusion
The alert management system provides a robust, scalable solution for displaying and managing alerts across the Tab5 interface. Through careful design of payload formats, dismissal mechanisms, and integration points, it delivers a seamless user experience while maintaining high performance and reliability. The system's modular architecture allows for easy extension and modification while preserving backward compatibility.

Key strengths include:
- Efficient bulk processing of multiple alerts
- Sophisticated dismissal tracking with both local and persistent storage
- Seamless integration with the central rotating card system
- Robust error handling and validation
- Support for various alert types and severity levels

## Appendices

### A. Complete API Reference

#### tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk
- **Purpose**: Update up to 4 Home Assistant alerts in the central rotating card
- **Parameters**: 
  - payload: string (format: "id|color|text;id|color|text;...")
- **Behavior**: Parses payload, applies color coding, updates alert slots, syncs with central panel

#### tab5_maj_info_texte  
- **Purpose**: Update informational text in central card area
- **Parameters**:
  - texte: string (supports multi-line with \n)
  - couleur: string (Rouge/Orange/Blanc)
  - meteo_id: string (for weather-specific dismissal tracking)
- **Behavior**: Processes text, applies formatting, manages dismissal state

#### tab5_maj_volet_etat
- **Purpose**: Update roller shutter status and visual indicators
- **Parameters**:
  - etat_physique: string (En_mouvement/Ouvert/Ferme/Partiel/open/closed)
- **Behavior**: Updates icons, colors, and wake word model state

## Introduction
This document provides detailed API documentation for the tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk service endpoint that updates up to four Home Assistant alert entries on the Tab5 device. It explains the structured payload format, the local dismissal system using persistent storage, color coding based on severity, and integration with the central rotating card display. It also includes examples of constructing payloads from Home Assistant automations, handling alert state transitions, and managing the lifecycle through a dismissible notification system. Finally, it covers error handling for malformed payloads and performance considerations when multiple simultaneous updates occur.

## Project Structure
The bulk alert update mechanism spans both Home Assistant configuration and ESPHome firmware:
- Home Assistant defines the service contract and orchestrates automation triggers and persistence of dismissed alerts.
- ESPHome receives the service call, parses the payload, renders UI slots, manages dismissal state locally, and coordinates visibility within the central rotator.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant"] --> |service call| ESPhome["ESPHome (Tab5)"]
ESPhome --> LVGL["LVGL UI Slots (4 max)"]
ESPhome --> Rotator["Central Panel Rotator"]
HA --> Store["input_text.tab5_alerts_dismissed"]
ESPhome --> LocalStore["Local dismissed list (tab5_dismissed_local)"]
```

## Core Components
- Service definition: tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk accepts a single string payload and delegates processing to C++ logic.
- Payload parser: parse_and_update_ha_alerts_bulk splits the payload into up to four alert entries, applies dismissal filtering, sets colors, and updates UI slots.
- Dismissal system:
  - Local: tab5_dismissed_local persists per-device dismissed IDs to avoid re-displaying dismissed alerts across pushes.
  - Persistent: input_text.tab5_alerts_dismissed stores dismissed IDs in Home Assistant; scripts manage adding/cleaning IDs and trigger refresh.
- Central rotator integration: The function updates flags indicating which HA alert panels are active and synchronizes visibility so only active panels appear in rotation.

## Detailed Component Analysis

### API Endpoint: tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk
- Purpose: Update up to four HA alert entries in one push.
- Input:
  - payload: string containing up to four entries separated by semicolons (;). Each entry contains three fields separated by pipes (|):
    - id: stable identifier used for dismissal tracking (e.g., entity_id or special markers like ha:unavailable)
    - title: short title or severity label used for color mapping
    - subtitle: displayed text content
- Behavior:
  - Clears previous slot states before applying new data.
  - Parses entries and applies dismissal checks against local store.
  - Applies color based on title content (Rouge/Orange/Blanc).
  - Updates UI labels and visibility flags for each slot.
  - Synchronizes central rotator visibility based on active alerts.
  - Animates entry if a new alert appears while its panel is currently visible.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:427-451](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L427-L451)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:780-870](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L780-L870)

### Payload Format and Parsing
- Entry separator: semicolon (;)
- Field separator: pipe (|)
- Fields per entry:
  - id: unique stable ID for dismissal matching
  - title: used to determine color scheme
  - subtitle: normalized UTF-8 text rendered to the slot
- Constraints:
  - Maximum of four entries per payload.
  - Payload length limited to 1024 bytes; longer payloads are rejected with an error log.
  - Malformed entries (missing fields) are skipped without breaking the batch.

Parsing steps:
- Split payload by semicolons to get entries.
- For each entry, split by pipes to extract fields.
- Validate presence of at least three parts; otherwise skip.
- Normalize subtitle text to UTF-8.
- Apply dismissal filter using local store.
- Render valid entries into available slots.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:780-870](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L780-L870)

### Color Coding Scheme
Colors are derived from the title field:
- Rouge: maps to red alert color.
- Orange: maps to warning color.
- Blanc: maps to primary text color (default).

Mapping behavior:
- If title contains “Rouge”, use ALERT_RED.
- Else if title contains “Orange”, use WARNING.
- Otherwise, default to TEXT_PRIMARY.

This ensures consistent visual hierarchy aligned with severity levels.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:674-678](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L674-L678)

### Dismissal System
Two-tier dismissal:
- Local persistence:
  - tab5_dismissed_local stores dismissed IDs on the device.
  - Functions:
    - tab5_dismiss_local_add: add an ID to the local store.
    - tab5_dismiss_local_has: check if an ID is dismissed.
    - tab5_dismiss_local_prune: remove IDs no longer present in the current payload.
- Persistent persistence:
  - input_text.tab5_alerts_dismissed holds dismissed IDs in Home Assistant.
  - script.tab5_dismiss_alert adds an ID to this input_text and triggers a refresh automation.
  - An automation listens for firmware events and calls the script to persist dismissals.

Lifecycle:
- When a user taps to dismiss an alert:
  - Immediate UI hide occurs via dismiss_ha_alert_slot_immediate.
  - Local store is updated via tab5_dismiss_local_add.
  - A Home Assistant event triggers script.tab5_dismiss_alert to persist the ID.
  - On next push, dismissed alerts are filtered out by parse_and_update_ha_alerts_bulk.

Cleanup:
- A scheduled automation prunes obsolete dismissed IDs (e.g., when an update completes or sensors recover).

**Section sources**
- [tab5_alerts.yaml:16-46](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_alerts.yaml#L16-L46)
- [tab5_alerts.yaml:121-172](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_alerts.yaml#L121-L172)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:886-900](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L886-L900)

### Central Rotator Integration
- The function updates g_central_ctx.has_ha[i] flags for each slot based on whether the slot has content after parsing.
- sync_central_panel_visibility hides inactive panels and shows the active one.
- If the current panel corresponds to an HA alert and becomes active, it remains visible; otherwise, the rotator advances to the next active panel.
- New alert animation:
  - If an alert is newly introduced (ID absent from previous batch), animate_alert_enter is triggered when that panel is currently shown.

### Example: Constructing Payloads from Home Assistant Automations
Automations can construct payloads dynamically based on sensor states and conditions. Typical pattern:
- Build a list of active alerts with id, title, and subtitle.
- Join entries with semicolons.
- Call tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk with the constructed payload.

Example references:
- Alerts push automation demonstrates building payloads for other services; similar patterns apply for HA alerts.
- Use template expressions to assemble id/title/subtitle values and ensure proper escaping and normalization.

**Section sources**
- [automations_examples.yaml.example:297-399](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L297-L399)

### Handling Alert State Transitions
- Empty payload: clears all HA alert slots and resets visibility flags; rotator adjusts accordingly.
- Malformed payload: entries missing required fields are skipped; overall process continues safely.
- Oversized payload: rejected with an error log; no changes applied.
- New alert detection: compares current IDs with previous batch to detect new entries and animate their entrance.

## Performance Considerations
- Batch updates: Processing up to four entries in a single payload reduces network overhead and UI redraws compared to individual updates.
- Payload size limit: Enforced at 1024 bytes to prevent excessive memory usage and parsing time.
- Dismissal filtering: Local store lookup avoids unnecessary UI updates for dismissed alerts.
- Animation optimization: Only new alerts trigger slide-in animations, reducing redundant repaints.
- Concurrency: Home Assistant automations use queued mode to prevent overlapping executions that could cause inconsistent state.

Recommendations:
- Keep payloads concise and well-formed to minimize parsing overhead.
- Avoid frequent rapid updates; batch related changes where possible.
- Monitor payload sizes to stay under the 1024-byte limit.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Payload too long: Check payload construction logic to ensure it stays under 1024 bytes.
- Malformed entries: Verify each entry contains exactly three pipe-separated fields; missing fields result in skipped entries.
- Dismissed alerts not appearing: Ensure local and persistent dismissal stores are synchronized; check script execution and event handling.
- No UI update: Confirm that the service call reaches ESPHome and that slot references are valid.

Debugging steps:
- Inspect ESPHome logs for payload length errors.
- Verify Home Assistant automation triggers and script executions.
- Check input_text.tab5_alerts_dismissed for unexpected dismissed IDs.
- Test with minimal payloads to isolate issues.

- [tab5_custom.cpp:800-803](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L800-L803)

## Conclusion
The tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk service provides an efficient mechanism for updating multiple alert entries on the Tab5 device with robust dismissal handling, color-coded severity indicators, and seamless integration with the central rotating card display. By adhering to the defined payload format and leveraging both local and persistent dismissal systems, developers can create responsive and user-friendly alert notifications that adapt to changing conditions while maintaining optimal performance.

## Core Components
- Service endpoint: tab5_maj_info_texte accepts texte, couleur, and meteo_id.
- Update function: update_info_text_ui handles trimming, UTF-8 normalization, multi-line detection, font selection, recolor markup, and color mapping (Rouge/Orange/Blanc).
- Weather banner override: When couleur indicates a vigilance level (Rouge/Orange), a fixed firmware banner is shown; otherwise, custom texte is used.
- Dismiss persistence: meteo_id is stored locally; dismissed items are hidden until a new push arrives.
- Central rotator integration: The info panel participates in the central card rotation and can be dismissed immediately on tap.

Key behaviors:
- Multi-line support: newline characters trigger smaller font and enable LVGL label wrapping.
- Conditional styling: Rouge maps to alert red, Orange to warning, Blanc remains primary text color.
- Weather-specific ID tracking: meteo_id enables per-alert dismissal; empty id means non-dismissable banner.
- Integration points: HA automations push info text; dismiss events persist to HA input_text and re-trigger updates.

## Architecture Overview
The flow from Home Assistant to LVGL involves:
1. HA automation builds texte and couleur, optionally includes meteo_id.
2. ESPHome receives the service call and invokes update_info_text_ui.
3. The function normalizes text, detects multi-line, selects font, applies color, and sets LVGL label text.
4. If it’s a weather vigilance banner, a fixed firmware message is used unless dismissed by meteo_id.
5. The central panel rotator integrates the info panel; tapping dismisses it and persists the id.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome Service"
participant CPP as "update_info_text_ui()"
participant LV as "LVGL Label"
participant ROT as "Central Rotator"
participant DIS as "Dismiss Store"
HA->>ESP : "tab5_maj_info_texte(texte, couleur, meteo_id)"
ESP->>CPP : "Call update_info_text_ui(...)"
CPP->>CPP : "Normalize UTF-8, trim, detect newlines"
CPP->>LV : "Set font, color, text (recolor markup if any)"
alt "Vigilance banner"
CPP->>DIS : "Check dismissed by meteo_id"
CPP-->>LV : "Show fixed banner or hide if dismissed"
end
CPP->>ROT : "Update has_info and current panel"
Note over CPP,ROT : "Tap dismiss triggers immediate hide and rotation"
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Service Definition and Payload Contract
- Service name: tab5_maj_info_texte
- Variables:
  - texte: string (multi-line supported via newline)
  - couleur: string ("Rouge", "Orange", "Blanc")
  - meteo_id: string (weather-specific ID for dismissal persistence)
- Behavior:
  - Stores meteo_id in a global for later dismissal checks.
  - Calls update_info_text_ui with UI references and globals.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:348-358](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L348-L358)

### Update Function: update_info_text_ui
Responsibilities:
- Trim whitespace and normalize UTF-8.
- Detect multi-line content and select appropriate font size.
- Apply LVGL recolor markup when present.
- Map couleur to colors: Rouge → alert red, Orange → warning, Blanc → primary.
- Handle weather vigilance banners: show fixed firmware message unless dismissed by meteo_id.
- Manage has_info flag and central panel visibility.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Entry: update_info_text_ui"]) --> Normalize["Normalize UTF-8 and trim"]
Normalize --> CheckBanner{"Vigilance banner?"}
CheckBanner --> |Yes| BannerText["Use fixed firmware banner"]
CheckBanner --> |No| UseText["Use provided texte"]
BannerText --> CheckDismiss{"meteo_id dismissed?"}
UseText --> CheckDismiss
CheckDismiss --> |Yes| HideInfo["Hide info panel"]
CheckDismiss --> |No| MultiLine{"Contains newline?"}
MultiLine --> |Yes| SmallFont["Select small font"]
MultiLine --> |No| LargeFont["Select large font"]
SmallFont --> Recolor{"Has #RRGGBB markup?"}
LargeFont --> Recolor
Recolor --> |Yes| EnableRecolor["Enable LVGL recolor"]
Recolor --> |No| DisableRecolor["Disable LVGL recolor"]
EnableRecolor --> SetText["Set label text"]
DisableRecolor --> SetText
SetText --> UpdateRotator["Update has_info and panel visibility"]
HideInfo --> UpdateRotator
UpdateRotator --> End(["Exit"])
```

## Performance Considerations
- Multi-line text uses a smaller font to fit more content within the limited screen height.
- UTF-8 normalization ensures correct display of accents without extra allocations.
- Dismissal checks avoid unnecessary redraws by storing dismissed IDs and pruning obsolete entries.
- Weather banners bypass custom texte processing when applicable, reducing overhead.
- Central panel visibility sync prevents redundant animations and repaints.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Text not displaying: Ensure texte is non-empty after trimming and UTF-8 normalization.
- Wrong color: Verify couleur is one of "Rouge", "Orange", or "Blanc".
- Dismiss not working: Confirm meteo_id is provided and matches the pushed alert; check tab5_dismissed_local and HA input_text consistency.
- Weather banner always shows: If couleur indicates a vigilance level, the firmware banner overrides custom texte; use Blanc for custom messages.
- Overflow handling: Use multi-line format with newline characters to wrap content; ensure font selection is appropriate.

The tab5_maj_info_texte service provides a robust mechanism for displaying informational text in the central card area, supporting multi-line content, conditional styling, and weather-specific dismissal persistence. Its integration with Home Assistant and LVGL ensures efficient updates and a responsive user experience. By following the documented patterns for formatting, styling, and managing text overflow, developers can effectively leverage this service for forecasts, alerts, and seasonal information.

## Introduction
This document explains the tab5_maj_volet_etat service and how it synchronizes roller shutter status between Home Assistant and the Tab5 device UI. It covers the four shutter states (En_mouvement, Ouvert, Ferme, Partiel), icon updates, real-time synchronization with Home Assistant shutter entities, state validation, automation workflows, partial opening handling, conflict management, integration points with alarm scheduling, presence simulation, and energy systems, as well as error handling for stuck shutters, calibration, and recovery from communication failures.

## Project Structure
The shutter status update flow spans two layers:
- Home Assistant layer: a central script manages shutter actions and maintains helpers that represent motion and state.
- Tab5 firmware layer: an API service receives the physical state and updates the UI accordingly, including enabling local voice “Stop” during movement.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant<br/>script.tab5_volet_action"] --> Helpers["Helpers<br/>input_boolean + input_text"]
Helpers --> Push["Automation pushes<br/>etat_physique to Tab5"]
Push --> Service["ESPHome API service<br/>tab5_maj_volet_etat"]
Service --> UI["LVGL UI updates<br/>icons, colors, labels"]
UI --> Voice["Local wake word 'Stop'<br/>enabled while moving"]
```

- [volet_serre_tracking.yaml:40-90](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/volet_serre_tracking.yaml#L40-L90)

- [README.md:111-114](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/README.md#L111-L114)

## Core Components
- Home Assistant shutter action script: Central entry point for open/close/stop; arms a motion flag and sets a text state used by the push automation.
- Tab5 API service: Receives etat_physique and updates UI icons/colors and enables/disables local “Stop” wake word when moving.
- Local voice control: When En_mouvement is active, the device listens for “Stop” to interrupt movement via Home Assistant.

Key responsibilities:
- State propagation: HA helpers → Tab5 service → UI.
- Visual feedback: Icons and colors change per state.
- Safety: Local “Stop” available during movement.

**Section sources**
- [volet_serre_tracking.yaml:40-90](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/volet_serre_tracking.yaml#L40-L90)

## Architecture Overview
The system uses a push-based model:
- All shutter commands go through a single script to ensure consistent state tracking.
- The script updates helpers that are pushed to the device.
- The device updates its UI and optionally enables local voice interruption.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant Script as "script.tab5_volet_action"
participant Helpers as "Helpers"
participant Push as "Push Automation"
participant ESP as "ESPHome Service<br/>tab5_maj_volet_etat"
participant UI as "Tab5 UI"
User->>HA : Trigger open/close/stop
HA->>Script : Call with action
Script->>Helpers : Set motion flag + state
Script->>HA : Act on cover entity
Script-->>Helpers : After delay or stop -> set final state
Helpers->>Push : etat_physique value changes
Push->>ESP : Send etat_physique
ESP->>UI : Update icons/colors, enable/disable "Stop"
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Shutter States and UI Mapping
The service maps etat_physique to UI elements:
- En_mouvement: Shows a moving icon, sets motion global true, highlights state label, enables local “Stop”.
- Ouvert / Partiel / open: Shows open icon, success color, and updates state label.
- Ferme / closed: Shows closed icon, error/dim color, and updates state label.

Visual behavior:
- Arrow icon reflects target direction when idle.
- State label and switch icon reflect current physical state.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Receive etat_physique"]) --> CheckMove{"Is En_mouvement?"}
CheckMove --> |Yes| MovePath["Set motion=true<br/>Update arrow icon<br/>Highlight state label<br/>Enable 'Stop' wake word"]
CheckMove --> |No| IdlePath["Set motion=false<br/>Set arrow based on target<br/>Dim arrow color"]
IdlePath --> OpenCheck{"Is Ouvert/Partiel/open?"}
OpenCheck --> |Yes| OpenUI["Open icon<br/>Success color<br/>Label 'Ouvert'"]
OpenCheck --> |No| CloseCheck{"Is Ferme/closed?"}
CloseCheck --> |Yes| CloseUI["Closed icon<br/>Error/dim color<br/>Label 'Fermé'"]
CloseCheck --> |No| End(["No change"])
MovePath --> End
OpenUI --> End
CloseUI --> End
```

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:88-160](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L88-L160)

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:80-160](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L80-L160)

### Home Assistant Shutter Action Script
- Accepts open, close, stop.
- For stop: stops cover, clears motion flag, sets state to Partiel.
- For open/close: acts on cover, arms motion flag, sets state to En_mouvement, then after measured travel time sets final state to Ouvert or Ferme.

Important notes:
- Replace placeholder cover entity with your actual cover.
- Adjust travel delay to match your shutter’s full travel time.
- Route all shutter automations through this script so the screen knows about movement.

**Section sources**
- [volet_serre_tracking.yaml:40-90](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/volet_serre_tracking.yaml#L40-L90)
- [README.md:111-114](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/README.md#L111-L114)

### Real-Time Synchronization and Validation
- The push automation sends the helper’s text value as etat_physique to the device.
- The device validates the string and updates UI accordingly.
- If other integrations call cover.* directly, add an automation to mirror those calls into the helpers so the UI stays accurate.

Validation mechanisms:
- Device-side checks for known states before updating UI.
- Motion flag prevents conflicting operations until settled.

### Local Voice “Stop” During Movement
When En_mouvement is active:
- The device enables the local “Stop” wake word.
- Detecting “Stop” triggers a command to halt the shutter via Home Assistant and provides voice feedback.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Device as "Tab5 Device"
participant Wake as "Wake Word 'Stop'"
participant HW as "Hardware Layer"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant Script as "script.tab5_volet_action"
Device->>Device : Enable 'Stop' when En_mouvement
Wake->>HW : Detect "Stop"
HW->>HA : Call script.tab5_volet_action(action=stop)
HA->>Script : Execute stop sequence
Script-->>Device : State becomes Partiel, UI updated
```

### Shutter Control Automation Workflows
Recommended patterns:
- Sunrise/sunset automations should call script.tab5_volet_action instead of direct cover.* to keep UI synchronized.
- HA UI interactions can be intercepted by an automation that mirrors cover.* calls into the helpers.
- Use the same script for all shutter actions to maintain consistency.

Examples:
- Automate morning opening by calling open.
- Automate evening closing by calling close.
- Allow manual override via UI or voice.

**Section sources**

### Handling Partial Opening Positions
- Stop action sets state to Partiel, indicating an intermediate position without precise percentage.
- UI reflects Partiel alongside Ouvert using the same open icon path but distinct state semantics.
- Future enhancements could track approximate positions if hardware supports it.

### Managing Shutter Movement Conflicts
- The script runs in restart mode, so a new tap cancels the previous timer and resets motion tracking.
- The device disables local “Stop” when not moving, preventing unintended interruptions.
- Ensure all automations route through the central script to avoid divergent states.

**Section sources**
- [volet_serre_tracking.yaml:40-43](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/volet_serre_tracking.yaml#L40-L43)

### Integration with Other Home Automation Features
- Alarm scheduling: Shutter state can influence wake-up routines (e.g., open at sunrise). Keep automations consistent by using the central script.
- Presence simulation: Schedule openings/closings to simulate occupancy; ensure UI remains accurate by routing through the script.
- Energy management: Coordinate with solar production or peak pricing to adjust shutter positions; again, use the central script to maintain sync.

Note: These integrations rely on consistent state propagation via the helpers and push automation.

## Performance Considerations
- Use a single script for all shutter actions to minimize state divergence and reduce redundant updates.
- Tune the travel delay to match your shutter’s actual travel time to avoid premature state transitions.
- Avoid direct cover.* calls outside the script; they bypass state tracking and can cause UI desync.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Stuck shutter:
  - Use local “Stop” wake word to halt movement safely.
  - Verify the script’s stop sequence executes and sets state to Partiel.
- Incorrect travel time:
  - Adjust the delay in the script to match your shutter’s full travel duration.
  - Too short causes early “stopped”; too long keeps “moving” longer than necessary.
- Communication failure:
  - Ensure push automation sends etat_physique reliably.
  - If HA is down, the device retains last known UI state; reconnecting restores sync.
- Direct cover.* calls:
  - Add an automation to mirror cover.* events into helpers to keep UI accurate.

Recovery procedures:
- Re-run the script with appropriate action to reset state.
- If UI shows inconsistent state, trigger a fresh open/close cycle via the script.
- Validate that micro_wake_word “Stop” is enabled only during movement.

## Conclusion
The tab5_maj_volet_etat service provides robust synchronization between Home Assistant and the Tab5 UI for roller shutters. By centralizing shutter actions, maintaining clear state transitions, and enabling local voice control during movement, it ensures reliable operation and user feedback. Integrating with alarm scheduling, presence simulation, and energy management requires consistent use of the central script to keep states aligned across the ecosystem. Proper configuration of travel times and interception of direct cover calls further enhances reliability and user experience.

## Introduction
This document provides comprehensive API documentation for calendar-related ESPHome services that power the Tab5 device’s calendar UI, daily detail view, upcoming appointment announcements, and planning banner updates. It covers:
- Monthly calendar view updates via a service that pushes day codes, work hours, and optional embedded details.
- Daily detail view updates with structured event lines.
- Upcoming appointments with epoch-based scheduling and automatic announcement triggering on the device.
- Planning banner updates with two-line text display.
It also explains payload construction from Home Assistant scripts, caching mechanisms for calendar data, and integration with the alarm clock functionality for work schedule awareness.

## Project Structure
The calendar system spans Home Assistant scripts and ESPHome services:
- Home Assistant scripts build payloads from multiple calendars and push them to ESPHome services.
- ESPHome services parse payloads and update LVGL UI components through C++ helpers.
- The alarm clock uses cached work schedules to compute ring times and supports appointment announcements.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant Scripts"] --> SVC1["ESPHome Service<br/>tab5_maj_calendrier_mois"]
HA --> SVC2["ESPHome Service<br/>tab5_maj_calendrier_jour"]
HA --> SVC3["ESPHome Service<br/>tab5_maj_rdv_prochains"]
HA --> SVC4["ESPHome Service<br/>tab5_maj_planning"]
SVC1 --> CAL_CACHE["Calendar Month Cache"]
SVC2 --> DAY_DETAIL["Day Detail Renderer"]
SVC3 --> RDV_STORE["Upcoming Appointments Store"]
SVC4 --> PLANNING_UI["Planning Banner UI"]
CAL_CACHE --> MONTH_RENDER["Month Grid Render"]
DAY_DETAIL --> POPUP_DAY["Day Popup"]
RDV_STORE --> ALARM_ENGINE["Alarm Engine"]
ALARM_ENGINE --> ANNOUNCEMENT["Announcement Trigger"]
```

## Core Components
- Monthly calendar service: receives year, month, day codes (62 hex characters), work hours (31 fields), and optional details (31 fields).
- Daily detail service: receives date and payload with up to 6 lines of events.
- Upcoming appointments service: receives epoch-based list of appointments with titles.
- Planning banner service: receives two lines of text for display.

These services are defined in ESPHome and implemented in C++ to update LVGL widgets safely.

## Architecture Overview
The calendar architecture separates data preparation in Home Assistant from rendering in ESPHome:
- Home Assistant scripts query multiple calendars and construct compact payloads.
- ESPHome services validate and store data, then trigger UI updates.
- The alarm engine integrates with calendar data to compute ring times and announce appointments.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant HA as "Home Assistant Script"
participant ESP as "ESPHome Service"
participant Cpp as "C++ Logic"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
User->>HA : Open calendar popup
HA->>HA : Build codes/heures/details
HA->>ESP : tab5_maj_calendrier_mois(year, month, codes, heures, details)
ESP->>Cpp : cal_store_month_data()
Cpp->>UI : cal_render_month() if visible
Note over HA,UI : Cached month avoids re-fetch on navigation
User->>HA : Tap day cell
HA->>HA : Build day payload
HA->>ESP : tab5_maj_calendrier_jour(date, payload)
ESP->>Cpp : cal_render_day_detail()
Cpp->>UI : Update day popup lines
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Monthly Calendar View Updates
Service: `tab5_maj_calendrier_mois`
- Parameters:
  - `annee`: Year string
  - `mois`: Month string (1-12)
  - `codes`: 62 hex characters representing day properties (2 per day, 31 days max)
    - Bitmask: 1 = work day, 2 = holiday, 4 = school vacation, 8 = appointment, 16 = birthday
  - `heures`: 31 fields of work hours in HH:MM-HH:MM format separated by |
  - `details`: Optional 31 fields of day-specific information separated by ~
- Behavior:
  - Stores month data in cache
  - Re-renders month grid only if popup is currently viewing that month/year
  - Supports embedded details for instant day detail without round-trip

Payload construction in Home Assistant:
- Queries multiple calendars for work events, holidays, family events, birthdays
- Computes bitmask per day based on event types
- Extracts work hours for future days only
- Sanitizes text by replacing separators

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Script tab5_calendrier_mois"]) --> Query["Query calendars<br/>work/holidays/family/birthdays"]
Query --> ComputeCodes["Compute bitmask per day<br/>work=1, holiday=2, vacation=4,<br/>appointment=8, birthday=16"]
ComputeCodes --> ExtractHours["Extract work hours<br/>HH:MM-HH:MM for future days"]
ExtractHours --> BuildDetails["Build optional details<br/>type|text;... per day"]
BuildDetails --> PushService["Call ESPHome service<br/>tab5_maj_calendrier_mois"]
PushService --> CacheStore["Store in calendar cache"]
CacheStore --> RenderCheck{"Popup showing this month?"}
RenderCheck --> |Yes| RenderMonth["Render month grid"]
RenderCheck --> |No| End(["Done"])
```

### Daily Detail View Updates
Service: `tab5_maj_calendrier_jour`
- Parameters:
  - `date`: Date string in YYYY-MM-DD format
  - `payload`: Up to 6 lines of day events in format "type|text;..."
    - Types: travail, ferie, vacances, rdv, anniv, fete
    - Text sanitization: replaces | with /, ; with ,
- Behavior:
  - Only updates if day popup is visible and matches current date
  - Renders structured lines with icons and formatted text
  - Falls back to script call if embedded details not available

Payload construction:
- Queries same calendars as monthly view
- Prioritizes holidays and vacations first
- Adds work hours and appointments with time formatting
- Limits to 6 lines maximum

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome"
participant Cpp as "C++ Logic"
participant UI as "Day Popup"
User->>UI : Tap day cell
UI->>HA : Request day details
HA->>HA : Build payload with event lines
HA->>ESP : tab5_maj_calendrier_jour(date, payload)
ESP->>CPP : Validate date match
CPP->>UI : Render 6 lines with icons
Note over UI : Shows loading state during fetch
```

### Upcoming Appointments with Epoch Scheduling
Service: `tab5_maj_rdv_prochains`
- Parameter:
  - `payload`: String containing "epoch|title~epoch|title~..." (max 8 entries)
  - Epoch values are UTC timestamps of appointment start times
- Behavior:
  - Stores appointments locally on device
  - Triggers announcements automatically at precise times
  - Prevents duplicate announcements by tracking announced epochs
  - Works independently of Home Assistant connectivity

Implementation details:
- Parses payload into structured appointment records
- Maintains announcement status per epoch
- Calculates lead time notifications (configurable minutes before)
- Generates both screen text and speech output

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> Stored : "Receive payload"
Stored --> Announced : "Epoch reached + lead time"
Announced --> Stored : "New payload arrives"
Stored --> Ignored : "Already announced same epoch"
Ignored --> Stored : "Next check"
```

### Planning Banner Updates
Service: `tab5_maj_planning`
- Parameters:
  - `ligne1`: First line of planning text
  - `ligne2`: Second line of planning text
- Behavior:
  - Updates two-line planning banner display
  - Used for quick planning updates from Home Assistant
  - Now largely replaced by local computation from calendar data

Current usage:
- Primarily maintained for backward compatibility
- Main planning now computed from work schedule data
- Temporary planning displays show day-specific work hours

## Performance Considerations
- **Caching**: Month data is cached to avoid repeated network calls during navigation
- **Payload Optimization**: Compact binary-like formats (hex codes, delimited strings) minimize bandwidth
- **Conditional Rendering**: UI updates only occur when relevant screens are visible
- **Background Processing**: Calendar prefetching happens in background without blocking UI
- **Memory Management**: Efficient parsing using char buffers instead of string allocations

Key performance features:
- Month cache with TTL and eviction policies
- Stale-while-revalidate pattern for calendar data
- Local computation of dates to avoid timezone issues
- Minimal payload sizes through bitmasks and compression

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and solutions:

**Calendar Not Updating:**
- Check Home Assistant connectivity
- Verify calendar entities are accessible
- Ensure scripts have proper permissions

**Day Details Not Loading:**
- Confirm embedded details are available in monthly payload
- Check if day popup is still visible when response arrives
- Verify date matching between request and response

**Appointment Announcements Missing:**
- Validate epoch timestamps are correct
- Check lead time configuration
- Ensure device has valid time synchronization

**Planning Banner Issues:**
- Verify UI element pointers are initialized
- Check payload format matches expected structure
- Confirm service is being called with correct parameters

- [tab5_calendar_yaml:24-31](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L24-L31)
- [alarm_clock_cpp:155-193](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/alarm_clock.cpp#L155-L193)

## Conclusion
The calendar services provide a robust, efficient system for displaying and managing calendar information on the Tab5 device. The separation between Home Assistant data processing and ESPHome rendering ensures reliability and performance. Key strengths include:

- **Resilient Design**: Works independently of Home Assistant for core functions
- **Efficient Caching**: Minimizes network calls while maintaining fresh data
- **Flexible Payloads**: Support for various calendar data formats
- **Integrated Features**: Seamless integration with alarm clock and announcements
- **User Experience**: Instant feedback with embedded details and smooth navigation

The system successfully balances real-time responsiveness with resource efficiency, making it suitable for embedded devices with limited capabilities.

## Appendices

### Payload Format Reference

**Monthly Calendar Codes:**
- Format: 62 hex characters (2 per day, 31 days)
- Bitmask values: 1=work, 2=holiday, 4=vacation, 8=appointment, 16=birthday
- Example: "01" = work day, "0F" = all flags set

**Work Hours Format:**
- Format: HH:MM-HH:MM separated by |
- Empty field means no work scheduled
- Example: "09:00-17:00||10:00-15:00|"

**Day Details Format:**
- Format: type|text;... separated by ~
- Types: travail, ferie, vacances, rdv, anniv, fete
- Text sanitization: | → /, ; → ,

**Upcoming Appointments Format:**
- Format: epoch|title~epoch|title~...
- Epoch: UTC timestamp (integer)
- Maximum 8 entries
- Titles sanitized of protocol separators

## Introduction
This document specifies the API and behavior of the daily calendar detail service tab5_maj_calendrier_jour. It explains:
- The date parameter used to match the currently displayed day in the calendar popup.
- The payload format containing up to 6 lines of day events in "type|texte;" form, with supported types: travail, ferie, vacances, rdv, anniv, fete.
- The date matching mechanism that ignores responses when rapid navigation changes the displayed date before the response arrives.
- The UI rendering process that maps each payload line to a row in the day-detail popup with an icon and text.
- Examples for constructing payloads per event type, handling special characters, and integrating with the day cell component.
- Error handling for malformed payloads and graceful degradation when the popup is not visible or no events exist.

## Project Structure
The daily calendar detail feature spans Home Assistant (script), ESPHome API routing, and LVGL UI components:
- Home Assistant script builds the day’s detail payload from multiple calendars and pushes it via an ESPHome service.
- ESPHome receives the service call, validates the target date, and invokes C++ rendering logic.
- LVGL UI defines the day-detail popup layout and the 6 rows rendered by the firmware.

```mermaid

Svc --> FW["Firmware Logic<br/>tab5_custom.cpp/h"]
FW --> UI["LVGL UI<br/>calendar_popup.yaml + cal_day_cell.yaml"]
```

## Core Components
- Home Assistant script tab5_calendrier_jour:
  - Accepts a date field (YYYY-MM-DD).
  - Queries multiple calendars for the requested day.
  - Builds a payload of up to 6 lines in "type|texte;" format.
  - Calls ESPHome service esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_jour with date and payload.

- ESPHome service handler tab5_maj_calendrier_jour:
  - Receives variables date and payload.
  - Validates that the day-detail popup is visible and that the current displayed date matches the incoming date.
  - If valid, calls C++ renderer to populate the 6-row detail view.

- Firmware renderer:
  - Parses the payload into lines.
  - Maps each type to an MDI icon and semantic color.
  - Updates the LVGL labels for icons and text, hides unused rows, and sets status messages.

## Detailed Component Analysis

### API Definition: tab5_maj_calendrier_jour
- Purpose: Update the day-detail popup with the selected day’s events.
- Input variables:
  - date: string, ISO date YYYY-MM-DD representing the day whose details are being pushed.
  - payload: string, up to 6 entries separated by ";", each entry "type|texte;".
- Behavior:
  - If the day-detail popup is hidden, ignore the update.
  - If the currently displayed date does not match the incoming date, ignore the update (handles rapid navigation).
  - Otherwise, render the payload into the 6-row detail area.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:507-528](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L507-L528)

### Payload Format
- Separator: ";" between lines.
- Line format: "type|texte"
  - type must be one of: travail, ferie, vacances, rdv, anniv, fete.
  - texte is sanitized by the producer:
    - "|" replaced with "/"
    - ";" replaced with ","
    - "~" replaced with "-"
- Maximum lines: 6. Extra lines are ignored by the renderer.

Examples of payload construction by type:
- Travail: "travail|Travail 09:00 – 17:00"
- Ferie: "ferie|Le lundi de Pâques"
- Vacances: "vacances|Vacances de Noël (Zone A)"
- RDV: "rdv|14:30 · Réunion client"
- Anniv: "anniv|Anniversaire de Marie"
- Fete: "fete|Sainte Valentine"

Special character handling:
- Producer sanitizes reserved separators to avoid breaking parsing.
- Renderer normalizes UTF-8 text before display.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:259-342](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L259-L342)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:2884-2928](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L2884-L2928)

### Date Matching Mechanism
- The firmware stores the date associated with the currently open day-detail popup.
- On receiving tab5_maj_calendrier_jour:
  - If the popup is hidden, the update is ignored.
  - If the stored date differs from the incoming date, the update is ignored.
- This prevents stale updates caused by rapid month/day navigation.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:515-518](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L515-L518)

### UI Rendering Process
- The day-detail popup defines 6 rows, each with an icon label and a text label.
- The renderer:
  - Splits the payload by ";" into lines.
  - For each line, splits by "|" into type and texte.
  - Maps type to an MDI icon and semantic color.
  - Sets icon text and color, sets text content, and shows the row.
  - Hides any unused rows beyond the number of lines provided.
  - Shows a status message if there are no lines ("No events planned today").

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Receive payload"]) --> Split["Split by ';' into lines"]
Split --> Loop{"For each line"}
Loop --> Parse["Split by '|' into type and texte"]
Parse --> MapType{"Map type to icon/color"}
MapType --> SetRow["Set icon/text and show row"]
SetRow --> NextLine{"More lines?"}
NextLine --> |Yes| Loop
NextLine --> |No| HideUnused["Hide remaining rows"]
HideUnused --> Status{"Any lines?"}
Status --> |Yes| Done(["Done"])
Status --> |No| ShowEmpty["Show 'No events' status"]
ShowEmpty --> Done
```

### Type Mapping and Visual Semantics
- Types and their visual mapping:
  - travail: work-related icon, info color
  - ferie: holiday icon, error color
  - vacances: school holidays icon, accent-alt color
  - rdv: appointment icon, gold color
  - anniv: birthday icon, warm-pink color

## Performance Considerations
- Payload size is limited to 6 lines to keep rendering fast and UI readable.
- Text sanitization at the producer side avoids expensive parsing corrections in the firmware.
- Date matching prevents unnecessary re-renders during rapid navigation.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Popup not visible:
  - The service handler ignores updates if the day-detail popup is hidden. Ensure the popup is opened before expecting updates.
- Date mismatch due to rapid navigation:
  - If the user navigates away before the response arrives, the update is ignored. Reopen the same day to trigger a new request.
- Malformed payload:
  - Lines without a "|" separator or empty texte are skipped.
  - Unknown types are rendered with a default icon and dim color.
- No events:
  - If the payload yields zero valid lines, the status message indicates no events planned for the day.

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:515-518](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L515-L518)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:2884-2928](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L2884-L2928)

## Conclusion
The tab5_maj_calendrier_jour service delivers a robust, user-friendly daily calendar detail view. It uses a simple, well-defined payload format, enforces date matching to handle rapid navigation, and renders up to six categorized event lines with appropriate icons and colors. Proper sanitization and validation ensure resilience against malformed inputs, while graceful degradation keeps the UI responsive even when the popup is not visible or no events exist.

## Introduction
This document provides detailed API documentation for the monthly calendar service tab5_maj_calendrier_mois used by the Tab5 device to update its monthly calendar popup view. It explains the service parameters, payload contracts, caching and deferred rendering behavior, integration with Home Assistant scripts and LVGL UI components, and performance considerations for large datasets.

The monthly calendar is rendered locally on the device (month grid, weekends, “today” highlight), while Home Assistant enriches it with work days, holidays, school vacations, appointments, birthdays, and work hours. The service pushes compact payloads that are cached on-device; re-rendering only occurs when the calendar popup is open for the specific month/year.

## Project Structure
The monthly calendar feature spans three layers:
- Home Assistant backend: script.tab5_calendrier_mois builds the payload from multiple calendars and calls the ESPHome service.
- ESPHome API layer: service tab5_maj_calendrier_mois stores data in cache and triggers a re-render if the correct month is visible.
- Device UI: LVGL components render the 7x6 grid and day detail sub-popup.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant<br/>script.tab5_calendrier_mois"] --> API["ESPHome API<br/>service tab5_maj_calendrier_mois"]
API --> Cache["Device Cache<br/>s_cal_month_cache"]
API --> Render["Render Trigger<br/>tab5_cal_render"]
Render --> UI["LVGL UI<br/>calendar_popup + cal_day_cell"]
UI --> Detail["Day Detail Sub-popup<br/>cal_day_popup"]
```

## Core Components
- Service definition and handler: tab5_maj_calendrier_mois receives annee, mois, codes, heures, details; stores data via cal_store_month_data and re-renders if the popup is open for the same year/month.
- Payload builder: script.tab5_calendrier_mois aggregates events from multiple calendars and constructs codes (62 hex chars), heures (31 fields), and details (31 fields).
- Caching and rendering: cal_store_month_data persists month data with TTL; cal_month_needs_fetch decides whether to request new data; cal_render_month applies cached enrichment to the local grid.
- UI components: calendar_popup defines the modal and grid; cal_day_cell defines each cell’s widgets updated by the renderer.

Key responsibilities:
- Home Assistant: compute bit flags per day, build delimited strings, call the service.
- ESPHome API: validate inputs, store in cache, trigger UI refresh conditionally.
- LVGL: draw grid, apply colors and dots based on bits, show work hours, handle tap-to-detail.

**Section sources**

## Architecture Overview
The monthly calendar flow integrates Home Assistant event aggregation with on-device rendering and caching.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant FW as "Firmware"
participant Scripts as "tab5-scripts.yaml"
participant HA as "script.tab5_calendrier_mois"
participant API as "service tab5_maj_calendrier_mois"
participant Cache as "s_cal_month_cache"
participant UI as "LVGL calendar_popup"
FW->>Scripts : Open calendar / navigate months
Scripts->>FW : cal_render_month(cells, lbl_month, view_year, view_month, today...)
Scripts->>HA : homeassistant.service(tab5_calendrier_mois, annee, mois) IF needs fetch
HA->>HA : calendar.get_events(start,end)
HA-->>API : esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_mois(annee, mois, codes, heures, details)
API->>Cache : cal_store_month_data(...)
API->>UI : if popup open AND matches year/month -> execute tab5_cal_render
UI-->>UI : Apply cached codes/heures/details to cells
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Service: tab5_maj_calendrier_mois
- Purpose: Receive monthly calendar enrichment data and update the device UI if the calendar popup is currently showing the target month/year.
- Parameters:
  - annee: string representing the requested year.
  - mois: string representing the month (1–12).
  - codes: string of 62 hex characters (2 per day up to 31 days). Each byte encodes day properties using bit flags:
    - 1 = work days
    - 2 = holidays
    - 4 = school vacations (Zone A)
    - 8 = appointments
    - 16 = birthdays
  - heures: string with 31 fields separated by “|”, each field is “HH:MM-HH:MM” or empty if no work hours.
  - details: optional string with 31 fields separated by “~”, each field is “type|text;...” (same contract as daily detail); empty indicates absence of embedded details.
- Behavior:
  - Stores data in s_cal_month_cache via cal_store_month_data.
  - If the calendar popup is open and the current view matches the received year/month, executes tab5_cal_render to re-render the grid with enriched data.
  - Uses TTL-based staleness checks elsewhere to decide silent refreshes.

Payload construction examples (from Home Assistant):
- codes: built by iterating days 1..31, computing bit flags per day from calendar events and static vacation ranges, then formatting each day’s flag as two uppercase hex digits.
- heures: for each day, if there is a work event starting on that day, format start and end times as HH:MM-HH:MM; otherwise leave empty.
- details: optional; when provided, contains per-day detail lines; if absent or empty, the firmware falls back to fetching day details via tab5_maj_calendrier_jour.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_api_logic_yaml:481-505](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L481-L505)
- [tab5_calendar_yaml:137-221](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L137-L221)
- [tab5_custom_h:537-589](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.h#L537-L589)
- [tab5_custom_cpp:2664-2703](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L2664-L2703)

### Caching Mechanism
- Storage: s_cal_month_cache maps a key derived from year/month to CalMonthData containing codes, heures, details, has_details flag, and stored_at timestamp.
- Key generation: cal_cache_key(year, month) = year * 12 + (month - 1).
- Fetch decision: cal_month_needs_fetch returns true if the month is not present in cache.
- Staleness: cal_month_is_stale compares stored_at with current millis against TTL (default 10 minutes).
- Eviction: cal_cache_evict_distant keeps only months within ±1 of the current view, ensuring at most 3 entries.
- Store: cal_store_month_data validates year/month, sets has_details based on non-empty details, records stored_at, and inserts into cache.
- Retrieval: cal_month_has_details and cal_cached_day_detail allow checking and reading embedded details for a given day.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Receive tab5_maj_calendrier_mois"]) --> Validate["Validate annee/mois"]
Validate --> Store["Store in s_cal_month_cache"]
Store --> CheckPopup{"Popup open AND view == received year/month?"}
CheckPopup --> |Yes| ReRender["Execute tab5_cal_render"]
CheckPopup --> |No| End(["Idle until next open/render"])
```

### UI Integration and Rendering
- Grid layout: calendar_popup.yaml defines a 7x6 grid (42 cells) with Monday-first alignment, headers, navigation buttons, legend, and a day detail sub-popup.
- Cell template: cal_day_cell.yaml defines reusable cell widgets (number label, work hours label, appointment dot, birthday dot, invisible button for tap handling).
- Rendering: cal_render_month computes local date math (weekdays, weekends, “today”), then applies cached enrichment (codes, heures, details) to update cell backgrounds, borders, labels, and dots.
- Day detail: When a cell is tapped, the firmware opens cal_day_popup and either uses embedded details (if available) or requests day details via tab5_maj_calendrier_jour.

### Home Assistant Script: script.tab5_calendrier_mois
- Inputs: annee (year), mois (month).
- Data sources:
  - Work calendar (events with “Travail” in summary).
  - Public holidays calendar (filtered by known holiday names).
  - Family calendar (appointments).
  - Birthdays calendar (birthdays).
  - Static school vacation ranges (Zone A).
- Processing:
  - Computes start/end window for get_events; clamps to today for current month to avoid past events.
  - Iterates days 1..31, determines flags per day, builds codes string (62 hex chars).
  - Builds heures string (31 pipe-delimited fields).
  - Optionally builds details string (31 tilde-delimited fields); if empty, firmware falls back to daily detail service.
- Output: Calls esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_mois with constructed payload.

Bit flag calculation:
- For each day, initialize flags to zero.
- Set work flag if a work event covers the day.
- Set holiday flag if a public holiday covers the day and name is whitelisted.
- Set vacation flag if the day falls within any Zone A vacation interval.
- Set appointment flag if any family event covers the day.
- Set birthday flag if any birthday event covers the day.
- Combine flags into a single byte and format as two uppercase hex digits.

Example payload construction references:
- codes: loop over days, compute flags, append formatted hex.
- heures: loop over days, find first work event starting on that day, format time range.
- details: optional; same structure as daily detail payload.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_calendar_yaml:34-221](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L34-L221)

### Navigation and Pre-fetching
- On calendar open or month change, firmware renders the month locally and checks if data is needed via cal_month_needs_fetch.
- If needed, it calls script.tab5_calendrier_mois with the current view’s year/month.
- Pre-fetching adjacent months (M-1, M+1) can be triggered during navigation to keep cache warm.

## Performance Considerations
- Deferred rendering: The service only triggers re-rendering when the calendar popup is open and the view matches the received month/year, avoiding unnecessary UI updates.
- Caching with TTL: Month data is cached with timestamps; stale data (>10 minutes default) can trigger silent refreshes without blocking UI.
- Memory management: Cache eviction keeps only the current month and adjacent months (max 3 entries), preventing unbounded memory growth.
- Payload size: Compact encoding (hex flags, delimited strings) minimizes network overhead and parsing cost.
- Local computation: Date math (weekdays, weekends, “today”) is computed on-device, reducing dependency on HA for basic grid layout.

Optimization recommendations:
- Ensure details payload is provided when possible to avoid extra round-trips for day details.
- Use pre-fetching for adjacent months during navigation to reduce latency.
- Monitor cache size and TTL to balance freshness and memory usage.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Empty codes or heures: Verify Home Assistant script outputs non-empty strings; check calendar entity availability and event coverage.
- Missing details: If details is empty, firmware falls back to daily detail service; ensure tab5_maj_calendrier_jour is functional.
- Popup not updating: Confirm the calendar popup is open and the view matches the received year/month; check LVGL widget IDs and flags.
- Stale data: Increase TTL or force refresh by navigating away and back; verify stored_at timestamps in cache.

Debugging steps:
- Inspect script.tab5_calendrier_mois logs for calendar queries and payload construction.
- Check ESPHome API logs for service invocation and cache operations.
- Validate LVGL widget visibility and IDs in calendar_popup.yaml and cal_day_cell.yaml.

## Conclusion
The tab5_maj_calendrier_mois service provides a robust, efficient mechanism for updating the Tab5 monthly calendar popup with enriched data from Home Assistant. Its design emphasizes deferred rendering, compact payloads, and intelligent caching to maintain responsiveness and conserve resources. By integrating tightly with LVGL UI components and leveraging Home Assistant’s calendar capabilities, it delivers a seamless user experience for viewing work schedules, holidays, vacations, appointments, and birthdays.

## Introduction
This document provides comprehensive API documentation for the planning banner service on the Tab5 device, focusing on how work schedule information is displayed as a two-line text banner in the central card. It explains:
- The deprecated direct service tab5_maj_planning and its backward compatibility behavior
- The modern approach where the planning banner is derived locally from the daily forecast data via build_planning_lines_from_jours()
- How update_planning_text_ui() updates the UI labels and integrates with planning text storage
- Text formatting rules, multi-line display, and character encoding considerations for French text
- The relationship between planning data and the alarm clock functionality
- Deprecation path and migration guidance for existing automations still using tab5_maj_planning directly

## Project Structure
The planning banner feature spans Home Assistant services, ESPHome logic, and C++ firmware:
- Home Assistant exposes an ESPHome service that triggers firmware-side lambdas
- The firmware parses incoming payloads, updates internal state, and refreshes LVGL UI elements
- Planning data originates from daily forecasts pushed to the device and is used both for the banner and for alarm scheduling

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant"] --> |API service call| ESP["ESPHome (tab5-api-logic.yaml)"]
ESP --> |Lambda| FW["Firmware (tab5_custom.cpp)"]
FW --> |Update UI| LVGL["LVGL Labels (planning banner)"]
FW --> |Read/Invalidate| ALARM["Alarm Clock (alarm_clock.cpp)"]
```

## Core Components
- Service definition: tab5_maj_planning accepts ligne1 and ligne2 strings to update the planning banner
- UI update function: update_planning_text_ui() normalizes UTF-8, strips optional prefixes, stores lines, and renders combined text
- Derived planning builder: build_planning_lines_from_jours() computes the next two working shifts from calendar data
- Alarm integration: alarm_clock.cpp reads the same calendar data to compute next ring times based on work schedules

Key responsibilities:
- Accepting and validating input parameters
- Updating persistent planning line storage
- Rendering formatted text with color markup support
- Deriving planning automatically when daily forecasts are updated
- Coordinating with alarm scheduling to respect work hours and rest periods

## Architecture Overview
The planning banner system follows a layered architecture:
- Home Assistant layer defines the service contract and forwards calls to ESPHome
- ESPHome layer executes lambdas that call firmware functions
- Firmware layer handles data processing, UI updates, and cross-feature coordination

```mermaid

FW->>UI : update_planning_text_ui(lbl, l1, l2, plan_ligne_1, plan_ligne_2)
Note over HA,UI : Direct push via tab5_maj_planning remains supported for compatibility
HA->>ESP : Call tab5_maj_planning(ligne1, ligne2)
ESP->>FW : update_planning_text_ui(lbl, ligne1, ligne2, plan_ligne_1, plan_ligne_2)
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Service Definition and Parameters
The tab5_maj_planning service accepts two string parameters:
- ligne1: First line of planning text (supports optional "1/" or "1/ " prefix)
- ligne2: Second line of planning text (supports optional "2/" or "2/ " prefix)

Both parameters are optional and can be empty strings. The service maintains backward compatibility while the preferred approach is to let the system derive planning automatically from daily forecasts.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:453-463](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L453-L463)

### UI Update Mechanism
The update_planning_text_ui() function performs several operations:
- Strips optional line number prefixes ("1/", "1/ ", "2/", "2/ ")
- Stores the processed lines in global variables (plan_ligne_1, plan_ligne_2)
- Combines lines with a separator if both exist
- Normalizes UTF-8 encoding for proper French character display
- Updates the LVGL label with the final text


### Derived Planning Builder
The build_planning_lines_from_jours() function automatically generates planning text from calendar data:
- Scans up to 15 days of forecast data
- Filters out rest days and past time slots
- Formats day names in French (Auj., Dem., Lun., etc.)
- Applies color coding for early shifts (< 9:00)
- Returns up to two lines of upcoming work schedules

```mermaid
flowchart TD

FilterRest --> |Yes| SkipDay["Skip to Next Day"]
FilterRest --> |No| CheckPast{"Slot Already Started?"}
CheckPast --> |Yes| SkipDay
CheckPast --> |No| FormatLine["Format Day Name + Hours"]
FormatLine --> ColorEarly{"Early Shift (< 9h)?"}
ColorEarly --> |Yes| ApplyOrange["Apply Orange Color"]
ColorEarly --> |No| ApplyWhite["Apply White Color"]
ApplyOrange --> AddToLines["Add to Output Lines"]
ApplyWhite --> AddToLines
AddToLines --> MoreDays{"More Days to Process?"}
MoreDays --> |Yes| ScanDays
MoreDays --> |No| ReturnLines["Return Up to 2 Lines"]
SkipDay --> MoreDays
```

### Integration with Daily Forecasts
When daily forecasts are updated via tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk(), the system automatically:
- Parses and updates the calendar data
- Invalidates alarm clock calculations to reflect new schedules
- Derives planning lines from the updated data
- Updates the planning banner if not showing temporary content

This eliminates the need for separate planning pushes after forecast updates.

### Alarm Clock Relationship
The alarm clock functionality depends on the same planning data:
- Reads work schedules from cal_jours_data[] to determine next ring times
- Respects rest periods between work days
- Calculates lead times before work starts
- Uses the same shift parsing logic as the planning banner


## Performance Considerations
- The planning derivation runs only when daily forecasts are updated, minimizing redundant calculations
- UTF-8 normalization ensures proper character handling without performance penalties
- The system avoids unnecessary UI updates by checking current panel state
- Alarm clock invalidation uses caching to prevent excessive recalculations

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and solutions:
- **French characters not displaying correctly**: Ensure text passes through normalize_text_utf8() which converts Latin-1 to UTF-8
- **Planning not updating after forecast changes**: Verify alarm_invalidate() is called and planning banner is not showing temporary content
- **Direct service calls not working**: Check that LVGL labels are properly initialized before calling update_planning_text_ui()
- **Incorrect planning lines**: Validate that calendar data contains proper "HH:MM-HH:MM" format in heures_ouverture field

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:1024-1044](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L1024-L1044)
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:55-78](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L55-L78)

## Conclusion
The planning banner service provides a robust mechanism for displaying work schedule information on the Tab5 device. While the direct tab5_maj_planning service remains available for backward compatibility, the recommended approach is to use automatic derivation from daily forecasts via build_planning_lines_from_jours(). This approach ensures consistency between the planning display and alarm scheduling, reduces automation complexity, and provides better maintainability.

Migration from direct service calls to automatic derivation involves removing planning-specific automations and relying on the existing daily forecast update flow. The system will automatically generate appropriate planning text based on the latest calendar data.

## Appendices

### Text Formatting Examples
- Single line: "Lun. : 08:00-12:00"
- Two lines: "Lun. : 08:00-12:00 | Mar. : 14:00-18:00"
- Early shift highlighting: Automatic orange coloring for shifts starting before 9:00
- Rest days: Displayed as "repos" instead of time ranges

### Character Encoding Notes
- All text should be passed through normalize_text_utf8() for proper French character support
- The system handles accent marks and special characters in French day names and text
- LVGL labels receive properly encoded UTF-8 strings for correct rendering

### Migration Path
1. Remove any automations that call tab5_maj_planning directly
2. Ensure daily forecasts are being pushed via tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk
3. Verify planning banner updates automatically after forecast changes
4. Test alarm scheduling to ensure it respects new work schedules

## Introduction
This document provides detailed API documentation for the upcoming appointments service that powers automatic announcements on the device. The service receives a compact payload of upcoming appointments, stores them locally, and triggers precise second-level announcements based on configurable lead time. It integrates with the alarm clock subsystem to produce both on-screen notifications and spoken announcements via the notification pipeline.

Key capabilities:
- Receives a payload of upcoming appointments from Home Assistant every 5 minutes.
- Stores appointments locally and prevents duplicate announcements across repeated pushes or after power outages using epoch-based matching.
- Triggers announcements at exact second precision when an appointment is due within a configured lead window.
- Produces synchronized screen text and speech output through the device’s notification pipeline.

## Project Structure
The feature spans Home Assistant (payload construction and scheduling) and ESPHome firmware (storage, timing, and announcement triggering).

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant<br/>tab5_reveil.yaml"] --> |Pushes payload| API["ESPHome API<br/>tab5-api-logic.yaml"]
API --> Store["Firmware Storage<br/>rdv_store() in alarm_clock.cpp"]
Store --> Timer["1s Tick Loop<br/>tab5-alarm.yaml"]
Timer --> Due["Due Check<br/>rdv_due() in alarm_clock.cpp"]
Due --> Notify["Notification Pipeline<br/>tab5-alarm.yaml scripts"]
Notify --> TTS["TTS / Media Player<br/>speaker_player"]
```

## Core Components
- Payload contract: "epoch|titre~epoch|titre~…" where epoch is a UTC Unix timestamp and titre is a cleaned title (separators removed on the Home Assistant side).
- Local storage: rdv_store() parses the payload into an internal list of up to ALARM_RDV_MAX entries, preserving previously announced items by matching epochs to avoid re-announcing.
- Due detection: rdv_due(now, lead_min) checks if any stored appointment is within the lead window and not yet announced; it returns formatted screen and speech strings.
- Integration: A 1-second tick loop calls rdv_due() and triggers the announcement script when due.

## Architecture Overview
The system separates concerns between Home Assistant (data preparation and push scheduling) and the device firmware (persistence, timing, and audio/visual output).

```mermaid

API->>FW : rdv_store(payload)
Note over FW : Parse records, preserve announced epochs
LOOP->>FW : rdv_due(now, lead_min)

NTF-->>LOOP : Update UI state
else No appointment due
FW-->>LOOP : Continue
end
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### API: tab5_maj_rdv_prochains
- Purpose: Accepts a payload string of upcoming appointments and persists them locally.
- Input:
  - payload: string in format "epoch|titre~epoch|titre~…", max 8 entries, epoch is UTC Unix timestamp, titles are pre-cleaned (no |, ~, ;).
- Behavior:
  - Parses each record by splitting on ~ and then |.
  - Converts epoch to time_t and stores start time and title.
  - Preserves previously announced appointments by epoch to prevent re-announcement on subsequent pushes.
  - Updates next appointment label sensor.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:465-479](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L465-L479)
- [alarm_clock.cpp:431-463](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/alarm_clock.cpp#L431-L463)
- [alarm_clock.h:168-189](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/alarm_clock.h#L168-L189)

### Local Storage: rdv_store()
- Data structure: Fixed-size array of Rdv entries with fields start (time_t), announced (bool), titre (string).
- Parsing logic:
  - Splits payload by ~ to get records.
  - For each record, splits by | to extract epoch and titre.
  - Validates epoch > 0 and stores entry.
  - Marks entries as already announced if their epoch was previously announced before clearing and repopulating.
- Memory management:
  - Clears previous list before repopulating to avoid memory growth.
  - Enforces maximum number of entries to bound memory usage.

**Section sources**
- [alarm_clock.cpp:410-463](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/alarm_clock.cpp#L410-L463)
- [alarm_clock.h:168-189](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/alarm_clock.h#L168-L189)

### Due Detection: rdv_due()
- Inputs: current time (now), lead window in minutes (lead_min).
- Logic:
  - Iterates stored appointments.
  - Skips already announced or invalid entries.
  - Checks if now is within lead window before appointment start.
  - Handles late discovery: if appointment started more than 60 seconds ago, marks as announced without triggering.
  - Generates screen text (e.g., "HH:MM · Title (in X min)") and speech text (e.g., "Reminder: Title, at HH hours MM, in X minutes.").
- Output: Returns true if an appointment is due and sets output strings.

**Section sources**
- [alarm_clock.cpp:473-521](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/alarm_clock.cpp#L473-L521)
- [alarm_clock.h:182-189](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/alarm_clock.h#L182-L189)

### Notification Pipeline Integration
- Trigger: A 1-second interval loop checks for due appointments when the alarm is not ringing and RDV announcements are enabled.
- Action: When rdv_due() returns true, the system executes a script to announce the appointment via TTS using the media player.
- Audio handling: Ensures no overlap with alarm ringing or other announcements; uses media_player with announcement flag for proper bus management.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-alarm.yaml:1080-1091](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-alarm.yaml#L1080-L1091)
- [tab5-alarm.yaml:764-785](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-alarm.yaml#L764-L785)

### Home Assistant Script: tab5_rdv_prochains
- Purpose: Builds the payload from calendar events and pushes it to the device.
- Data sources: Family and work calendars, excluding "Work" events.
- Processing:
  - Filters events with timestamps (not all-day events).
  - Cleans titles by replacing separators (| → /, ~ → -, ; → ,).
  - Formats epoch with zero-padding for lexicographic sorting.
  - Sorts chronologically, deduplicates, and limits to 8 entries.
- Schedule: Runs every 5 minutes and on calendar changes or device connection.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_reveil.yaml:35-93](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_reveil.yaml#L35-L93)
- [tab5_reveil.yaml:161-199](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_reveil.yaml#L161-L199)

## Performance Considerations
- Payload size: Limited to 8 entries to prevent excessive memory usage and parsing overhead.
- Parsing efficiency: Simple string operations with fixed delimiters (~ and |) for fast processing.
- Announcement frequency: Controlled by lead_min configuration to avoid frequent interruptions.
- Time handling: Uses UTC timestamps to ensure consistent behavior across timezones and daylight saving transitions.
- Memory management: Regular clearing and repopulation of appointment list prevents memory leaks during long-running sessions.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and solutions:

1. **Duplicate announcements**: Ensure epoch values are unique and consistent. The system uses epoch-based matching to prevent re-announcements.
2. **Missed appointments**: Verify that Home Assistant is pushing updates every 5 minutes and that the device is connected.
3. **Timezone issues**: Confirm that epochs are in UTC and the device's timezone is correctly configured.
4. **Memory problems**: Check that the payload doesn't exceed 8 entries and that titles are properly truncated.
5. **Audio conflicts**: Ensure announcements don't overlap with alarm ringing or other media playback.

**Section sources**
- [alarm_clock.cpp:431-463](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/alarm_clock.cpp#L431-L463)

- [tab5-alarm.yaml:1080-1091](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-alarm.yaml#L1080-L1091)

## Conclusion
The upcoming appointments service provides a robust, efficient mechanism for managing and announcing scheduled events. By separating data preparation from execution and using epoch-based persistence, the system ensures reliable operation even during network interruptions or power cycles. The integration with the alarm clock system enables precise timing and seamless user experience through synchronized visual and audio notifications.

## Appendices

### Payload Format Examples
- Basic format: "1704067200|Meeting~1704070800|Dentist"
- With cleaned titles: "1704067200|Team Meeting~1704070800|Doctor Visit"
- Sorted chronologically with zero-padded epochs for proper ordering

### Configuration Parameters
- Lead time: Configurable in minutes (default 15 minutes)
- Maximum appointments: 8 entries
- Timezone: UTC timestamps with local time conversion for display

### Edge Cases Handling
- Overlapping appointments: Each appointment is processed independently based on its start time
- Past appointment cleanup: Automatically handled by marking appointments as announced when discovered late
- Memory management: Fixed-size array with regular clearing prevents memory growth
