## Introduction
This document provides detailed API documentation for the ESPHome climate control service tab5_maj_clim used to synchronize HVAC entity state with the Tab5 device UI. It explains how target temperature, current temperature, HVAC mode (cool/heat/dry/fan/off), preset modes (eco/boost/none), fan modes, and swing settings are pushed from Home Assistant to the device, how the UI updates through the arc thermostat and popup components, and how a centralized recoloring script keeps icons consistent. It also includes examples of calling the service from Home Assistant automations, formatting temperatures with degree symbols, and maintaining synchronization between device state and display. Finally, it outlines how climate controls integrate with other system features such as alarm scheduling based on work hours.

## Project Structure
The climate control feature spans several files:
- Service definition and UI update logic live in the ESPHome API logic file.
- Centralized icon recoloring is implemented in the scripts file.
- The UI components define the compact card and the full-screen popup that render the thermostat arc, labels, and buttons.
- Home Assistant automation examples show how to call the service with data from a climate entity.
- Documentation describes the two-level control model (compact card and popup).

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant<br/>automation"] --> |calls| SVC["ESPHome service<br/>tab5_maj_clim"]
SVC --> UI["LVGL UI objects<br/>labels + arc"]
SVC --> G["Globals<br/>clim_target_temp,<br/>clim_hvac_mode,<br/>clim_preset_mode,<br/>clim_fan_mode,<br/>clim_swing_mode"]
G --> RECOLOR["Centralized script<br/>tab5_clim_recolor"]
RECOLOR --> ICONS["Mode/preset/fan/swing<br/>icons"]
UI --> POPUP["Climate popup<br/>arc + labels"]
UI --> CARD["Compact card<br/>target label"]
```

## Core Components
- Service tab5_maj_clim: Accepts string parameters for target temperature, current temperature, HVAC mode, preset mode, fan mode, and swing mode. Converts temperature strings to floats, updates LVGL labels and arc, sets globals, then triggers centralized recoloring.
- Centralized recoloring script tab5_clim_recolor: Reads the four climate globals and applies active/inactive colors to mode, preset, fan quiet, swing, and windnice icons; also colors the target value based on HVAC mode.
- UI components:
  - Compact card displays the target temperature and allows ± adjustments with optimistic UI updates and debounced calls to Home Assistant.
  - Popup contains an arc thermostat (16–30 °C), center target label, room temperature label, and option buttons for presets, fan quiet, swing, and windnice.

Key behaviors:
- Temperature values are formatted with one decimal place; current temperature includes a degree symbol and unit.
- Mode-based coloring: cool targets blue, heat targets red, others white.
- Presets eco/away and boost toggle active colors; fan quiet and swing states highlight their respective icons.

## Architecture Overview
The flow begins when Home Assistant pushes climate state to the device via the tab5_maj_clim service. The service converts string inputs to numeric types where needed, updates UI elements directly, writes state into globals, and delegates visual styling to the centralized recoloring script. User interactions in the UI perform optimistic updates by setting globals and invoking the recoloring script before sending commands to Home Assistant. Debouncing ensures rapid taps only trigger a single set_temperature call.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome service<br/>tab5_maj_clim"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
participant SCR as "Script<br/>tab5_clim_recolor"
HA->>ESP : Call service with target,current,mode,preset,fan,swing
ESP->>UI : Update target label(s) and arc value
ESP->>UI : Update current temperature label with degree symbol
ESP->>ESP : Set globals clim_*
ESP->>SCR : Execute centralized recoloring
SCR-->>UI : Apply active/inactive colors to icons and target
Note over HA,UI : UI reflects authoritative state from HA
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Service: tab5_maj_clim
Purpose:
- Receives climate state from Home Assistant and synchronizes the device UI.
- Parameters:
  - target: string representing the desired temperature (converted to float internally).
  - current: string representing the current room temperature (converted to float internally).
  - mode: string HVAC mode (e.g., cool, heat, dry, fan_only, off).
  - preset: string preset mode (e.g., eco, away, boost, none).
  - fan: string fan mode (e.g., auto, low, quiet).
  - swing: string swing mode (e.g., off, vertical, horizontal, both, on, 3d, windnice).

Processing steps:
- Validates UI object references exist before updating.
- Parses target and current strings to floats.
- Updates the target temperature label in both compact card and popup.
- Sets the arc indicator value to the target temperature.
- Formats the current temperature label with one decimal place plus degree symbol and unit.
- Writes climate globals for mode, preset, fan, and swing.
- Executes the centralized recoloring script to apply consistent icon colors.

Example call from Home Assistant automation:
- The automation reads attributes from a climate entity and passes them to the service using template expressions. Replace the placeholder entity ID with your actual climate entity.

Temperature formatting:
- Target temperature is displayed with one decimal place.
- Current temperature is displayed with one decimal place followed by a degree symbol and unit.

Synchronization:
- After user actions, the UI performs optimistic updates by setting globals and running the recoloring script immediately. When Home Assistant responds with the authoritative state, tab5_maj_clim re-applies the correct state, ensuring consistency.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:162-198](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L162-L198)

### Centralized Recoloring Script: tab5_clim_recolor
Purpose:
- Single source of truth for icon colors across all climate controls.
- Reads the four climate globals and applies active or inactive colors to:
  - HVAC mode icons (cool, heat, dry, fan_only, off).
  - Preset icons (eco/away and boost).
  - Fan quiet icon.
  - Swing and windnice icons.
- Colors the target temperature label based on HVAC mode:
  - Cool: blue.
  - Heat: red.
  - Others: default text color.

Behavior highlights:
- If UI objects are not initialized, the script exits early to avoid errors.
- Uses predefined color constants for active and inactive states.
- Supports multiple swing modes including windnice for Daikin Onecta airflow.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:408-489](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L408-L489)

### UI Components: Compact Card and Popup
Compact card:
- Displays the target temperature and allows ± adjustments.
- Optimistic UI updates set the global target temperature and refresh the label immediately.
- Debounce groups rapid taps and sends a single set_temperature command after the gesture ends.

Popup:
- Full-screen modal with three glass cards:
  - MODE: stacked HVAC mode buttons (cool, heat, dry, fan_only, off).
  - TEMPÉRATURE: arc thermostat (16–30 °C), center target label, ± buttons, and room temperature label.
  - OPTIONS: presets (eco/boost toggles), fan quiet, swing, and windnice.
- Each button sets the appropriate global and runs the recoloring script before calling Home Assistant services.
- Arc changes update the target label and trigger debounce to send a single temperature change.

Templates and factorization:
- HVAC mode buttons use a reusable template with variables for suffix, mode, icon, and label.
- Preset toggle buttons use a template that toggles between the selected preset and none.
- Some buttons remain individual due to unique service calls and lambda logic.

### User Interaction Flow: Temperature Adjustment
When users adjust the target temperature:
- Immediate UI feedback updates the target label and arc.
- Rapid taps are grouped by a debounce mechanism.
- A single Home Assistant service call is sent after the gesture completes.
- The authoritative state is later pushed back via tab5_maj_clim to ensure consistency.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["User tap ± or arc"]) --> UpdateTarget["Update global target temp<br/>and UI labels"]
UpdateTarget --> Debounce["Debounce timer starts"]
Debounce --> Taps{"More taps?"}
Taps --> |Yes| UpdateTarget
Taps --> |No| SendHA["Send single set_temperature to HA"]
SendHA --> AwaitState["Await authoritative state"]
AwaitState --> PushBack["Push state via tab5_maj_clim"]
PushBack --> SyncUI["Reapply UI and colors"]
SyncUI --> End(["Stable synchronized state"])
```

## Dependency Analysis
- The service depends on LVGL UI object IDs for labels and arcs.
- Globals act as the shared state bridge between UI interactions and the recoloring script.
- Templates reduce duplication for mode and preset buttons while preserving unique behavior for specific controls.
- Home Assistant automations provide the authoritative state push to keep the device UI synchronized.

```mermaid
graph LR
UI["UI components<br/>popup + card"] --> G["Globals<br/>clim_*"]
G --> RECOLOR["tab5_clim_recolor"]
UI --> HA["Home Assistant services<br/>set_hvac_mode / set_preset_mode / set_fan_mode / set_swing_mode"]
HA --> SVC["tab5_maj_clim"]
SVC --> UI
SVC --> G
```

## Performance Considerations
- Optimistic UI updates improve perceived responsiveness by showing changes immediately.
- Debouncing reduces network overhead by grouping rapid temperature adjustments into a single command.
- Centralized recoloring avoids duplicated logic and ensures consistent visuals across all climate controls.
- Early-exit checks prevent unnecessary processing if UI objects are not yet initialized.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Icons not updating: Ensure the recoloring script is executed after setting globals. Verify that UI object IDs referenced by the script exist.
- Target temperature not reflecting changes: Confirm that the service receives valid numeric strings for target and current, and that labels and arc IDs are correctly bound.
- Stale state after user interaction: Check that Home Assistant returns authoritative state and that tab5_maj_clim is invoked to re-sync the UI.
- Degree symbol display: Verify that the current temperature label uses the proper format string with the degree symbol and unit.

## Conclusion
The tab5_maj_clim service is the central mechanism for synchronizing HVAC state between Home Assistant and the Tab5 device UI. It parses string inputs, updates LVGL elements, manages globals, and delegates styling to a centralized recoloring script. The UI employs optimistic updates and debouncing to deliver responsive interactions while maintaining consistency through authoritative state pushes. This design supports robust climate control across the compact card and popup, integrates seamlessly with Home Assistant automations, and complements other system features such as alarm scheduling based on work hours.

## Introduction
This document provides comprehensive API documentation for all ESPHome service endpoints exposed by the Tab5 device under the tab5_maj_* namespace. It covers parameter names, data types, payload formats, expected behavior, and UI impact for each service. It also includes example automation calls from Home Assistant YAML and explains error handling patterns, validation rules, and edge cases. Finally, it maps how each service updates LVGL components on the screen.

The services are defined in the ESPHome configuration and delegate most logic to C++ functions that safely update LVGL widgets. The push model is one-way: Home Assistant triggers automations that call these services; the device never initiates network requests.

**Section sources**
- [architecture.md:172-183](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L172-L183)

## Project Structure
At a high level:
- Service definitions live in the ESPHome API block.
- Each service receives parameters (often a single string payload), validates them, and invokes C++ helpers to parse and render UI changes.
- Shared state is kept in globals and passed into C++ context structures for rendering.
- UI components are declared in LVGL YAML files and referenced by IDs in lambdas.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant Automation"] --> |service call| ESP["ESPHome API Handler"]
ESP --> |lambda| Cpp["C++ Functions<br/>tab5_custom.*"]
Cpp --> LVGL["LVGL Widgets<br/>IDs in ui_components/*.yaml"]
Cpp --> G["Globals<br/>tab5-globals.yaml"]
```

## Core Components
- Service handlers: Define the contract between Home Assistant and the device. They accept typed variables or payloads and execute lambdas that call C++ functions.
- C++ layer: Implements parsing, color mapping, animations, and safe LVGL updates with null guards.
- Globals: Centralized state shared across scripts and services (e.g., current panel, flags for alerts/rain/info).
- Scripts: Reusable sequences for complex actions like debouncing, vocal responses, calendar rendering, and central rotator control.

Key responsibilities:
- Parsing delimited payloads (semicolon-separated records, pipe-separated fields).
- Updating forecast tiles, rain bars, climate cards, alerts, info panels, assistant popup, and calendar popups.
- Managing central card rotation and visibility based on active content.

- [tab5-custom.h:177-364](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.h#L177-L364)

## Architecture Overview
The Tab5 uses a push-based architecture where Home Assistant automations call ESPHome services. Each service handler validates inputs and delegates to C++ functions that update LVGL widgets. The central card rotates among planning, rain, weather alerts, info text, and up to four Home Assistant alert banners. Calendar and assistant features use additional scripts and caches.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant API as "ESPHome API"
participant L as "Lambda"
participant C as "C++ Layer"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
HA->>API : Call tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk(payload)
API->>L : Execute lambda
L->>C : parse_and_update_jours_bulk(payload)
C-->>UI : Update daily forecast slots & page title
L->>C : alarm_invalidate()
L->>C : build_planning_lines_from_jours(...)
C-->>UI : Update planning banner if needed
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Service: tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk
Purpose: Push hourly forecast data in bulk to refresh the hourly forecast tiles and page title.

Parameters:
- payload: string — semicolon-delimited records; each record has pipe-separated fields for time, condition, temperature, precipitation.

Behavior:
- Parses the payload via C++ function.
- Computes the correct hourly page index based on current forecast page.
- Refreshes hourly forecast slots and updates the page title to reflect the visible range.

UI components affected:
- Hourly forecast cards (time, temperature, probability labels).
- Page title wrapper and label showing the range of displayed hours.

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk
data:
  payload: "{{ hourly_payload }}"
```

Validation and errors:
- If the target time widget is not initialized, the handler returns early.
- Payloads exceeding internal buffer limits are silently rejected by C++ parsing.

Edge cases:
- Empty or partial chunks are tolerated; missing entries default to neutral values.
- Title refresh only occurs when the title area is currently shown.

### Service: tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk
Purpose: Push daily forecast data in bulk to refresh the daily forecast tiles, invalidate alarm calculations, and optionally rebuild the planning banner.

Parameters:
- payload: string — semicolon-delimited records; each record has pipe-separated fields for day name, condition, min/max temps, work hours, weekend flags.

Behavior:
- Parses the payload and updates daily forecast slots.
- Recomputes the daily page index and refreshes daily tiles.
- Invalidates alarm scheduling so next ring calculation uses updated planning.
- If temporary planning is not shown, builds two-line planning text from stored daily data and updates the planning banner.

UI components affected:
- Daily forecast cards (day labels, temperatures, icons).
- Planning banner lines.
- Alarm-related scheduling (indirectly via invalidation).

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk
data:
  payload: "{{ daily_payload }}"
```

Validation and errors:
- Early return if day slot widgets are not initialized.
- Payload size constraints enforced by C++ parser.

Edge cases:
- Weekend/holiday days suppress work hours display.
- Planning banner rebuild is skipped if a temporary planning overlay is active.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:55-78](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L55-L78)
- [tab5_custom.h:83-94](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.h#L83-L94)
- [forecast_daily.yaml:1-26](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/forecast_daily.yaml#L1-L26)

### Service: tab5_maj_clim
Purpose: Update the climate card with target temperature, current temperature, HVAC mode, preset, fan mode, and swing mode.

Parameters:
- target: string — float representation of target temperature.
- current: string — float representation of current temperature.
- mode: string — HVAC mode (e.g., cool, heat, off).
- preset: string — preset mode (e.g., eco, away, boost).
- fan: string — fan mode (e.g., auto, low, quiet).
- swing: string — swing mode (e.g., stop, vertical, horizontal, both).

Behavior:
- Converts strings to floats and updates global climate state.
- Updates target temperature labels and arc value.
- Updates current temperature label with degree symbol.
- Sets HVAC mode, preset, fan, and swing globals.
- Executes centralized recolor script to apply consistent icon colors.

UI components affected:
- Target temperature label and popup label.
- Popup arc value.
- Current temperature label.
- Climate mode/preset/fan/swing icons (via recolor script).

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_clim
data:
  target: "21.5"
  current: "19.8"
  mode: "cool"
  preset: "eco"
  fan: "auto"
  swing: "stop"
```

Validation and errors:
- Early return if climate widgets are not initialized.
- Recolor script ensures consistent visual state even before HA feedback arrives.

Edge cases:
- Optimistic UI updates occur on user taps; final state is corrected by this service when HA responds.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:162-198](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L162-L198)
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:383-408](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L383-L408)

### Service: tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france
Purpose: Push Meteo-France vigilance alerts and phrase to update the central alert panel.

Parameters:
- payload: string — pipe-delimited 11 fields: phrase_pluie, globale, vent, inondation, orages, pluie_inondation, neige_verglas, grand_froid, vagues_submersion, canicule, avalanches.

Behavior:
- Copies payload into a fixed-size buffer and tokenizes fields.
- Updates rain phrase label and hides numeric rain indicators.
- Colors the date label based on global vigilance level.
- Filters and displays up to four active alerts with appropriate icons and colors.
- Sets global flag indicating presence of alerts.

UI components affected:
- Rain phrase label.
- Date label color.
- Alert slots (up to four) with icons and colors.

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france
data:
  payload: "{{ alerte_payload }}"
```

Validation and errors:
- Buffer size limit enforced; long payloads are truncated safely.
- Missing fields default to empty or green status.

Edge cases:
- Only non-green and non-empty fields are shown.
- Alert count capped at four; extra alerts are ignored.

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:200-278](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L200-L278)

### Service: tab5_maj_probabilites
Purpose: Update probability indicators for UV, frost, and snow.

Parameters:
- uv: string — integer probability value.
- gel: string — integer probability value.
- neige: string — integer probability value.

Behavior:
- Converts strings to integers and updates global snow probability.
- Chooses rain prediction icon and color based on snow threshold and humidity.

UI components affected:
- Rain prediction icon and its color.

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_probabilites
data:
  uv: "30"
  gel: "10"
  neige: "6"
```

Validation and errors:
- Early return if day slot widgets are not initialized.

Edge cases:
- Snow probability above threshold forces warning color regardless of humidity.

Behavior:

### Service: tab5_maj_pluie_1h
Purpose: Update the 1-hour rain intensity bar chart with per-interval intensities.

Parameters:
- index_5mn: string — integer index from 0 to 8 representing 5-minute intervals.
- intensite: string — intensity level (e.g., Pluie faible, Pluie modérée, Pluie forte, Pluie très forte).

Behavior:
- Maps intensity to color and height.
- Updates the corresponding rain bar widget.
- Recomputes global rain presence based on any non-zero bar.

UI components affected:
- Rain bars (rb_0_in through rb_8_in).
- Global rain flag.

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_pluie_1h
data:
  index_5mn: "3"
  intensite: "Pluie modérée"
```

Validation and errors:
- Early return if rain bar widgets are not initialized.
- Unknown intensities result in empty bar.

Edge cases:
- Multiple calls update different bars; overall rain presence is derived from all bars.

Behavior:

- Updates info text UI with provided text, color, and dismissal context.
- Integrates with central panel rotation and visibility.

Validation and errors:

Edge cases:

### Service: tab5_assist_reponse
Purpose: Display a rich assistant response with Markdown support and optional image.

Parameters:
- texte: string — Markdown text (tables supported, aligned in monospace).
- image_url: string — optional URL for image display.

Behavior:
- Formats Markdown text for LVGL monospace font.
- Sets response text with appropriate font size.
- Optionally loads image and shows loading hint.
- Opens assistant popup automatically.

UI components affected:
- Assistant response label.
- Assistant image widget and hint.
- Assistant popup visibility.

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_assist_reponse
data:
  texte: "| Col1 | Col2 |\n|------|------|\n| A    | B    |"
  image_url: "https://example.com/image.png"
```

Validation and errors:
- Image loading is conditional; empty URL hides image area.
- Font size adapts to user preference.

Edge cases:
- Tables are aligned using monospace font.
- Loading hint appears while image downloads.

### Service: tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk
Purpose: Push Home Assistant alert banners in bulk to update up to four alert slots.

Parameters:
- payload: string — structured alert data for multiple slots.

Behavior:
- Builds UI slot structures referencing wrappers, labels, flags, and IDs.
- Syncs central context with current rain/alert/info states.
- Parses and updates alert slots with content and visibility.
- Writes back updated flags and panel state to globals.

UI components affected:
- Up to four alert wrappers and labels.
- Central panel visibility and rotation.

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk

  payload: "{{ ha_alerts_payload }}"
```

Validation and errors:
- Slot structure ensures safe access to LVGL objects.
- Context sync prevents inconsistent panel state.

Edge cases:
- Alerts are dismissed individually via tap.
- Dismissal persists locally and triggers HA script.

Purpose: Store upcoming appointments for alarm announcements and display.

Parameters:
- payload: string — pipe-delimited list of epoch|title pairs (max 8 entries).

Behavior:
- Stores appointment data internally.
- Updates next appointment sensor for alarm integration.
- Ensures announcements trigger precisely at scheduled times.

UI components affected:


Validation and errors:

Edge cases:

### Service: tab5_maj_calendrier_mois
Purpose: Cache and render monthly calendar data including codes, working hours, and optional details.

Parameters:
- annee: string — year (e.g., "2026").
- mois: string — month (1-12).
- codes: string — 62 hex characters (2 per day) representing work, holidays, school vacations, appointments, birthdays.
- heures: string — 31 fields of "HH:MM-HH:MM" separated by pipes.
- details: string — 31 fields of "type|text;..." separated by tildes.

Behavior:
- Stores month data in cache with TTL and eviction policy.
- If calendar popup is open for the same month, re-renders immediately.
- Supports embedded day details for instant tap responses.

UI components affected:
- Calendar popup grid and detail view.
- Day cells with dots for appointments/birthdays.

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_mois
data:
  annee: "2026"
  mois: "8"
  codes: "{{ codes_string }}"
  heures: "{{ heures_string }}"
  details: "{{ details_string }}"
```

Validation and errors:
- Year/month bounds checked before caching.
- Stale cache triggers silent refresh.

Edge cases:
- Details field optional; absence falls back to day-specific script.
- Cache evicts distant months to conserve memory.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:486-505](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L486-L505)
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:34-222](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L34-L222)

### Service: tab5_maj_calendrier_jour
Purpose: Render day detail information in the calendar popup.

Parameters:
- date: string — ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).
- payload: string — semicolon-delimited lines of "type|text;" (max 6 lines).

Behavior:
- Validates that calendar popup is open and detail date matches.
- Renders day detail lines with icons and text.
- Ignores updates if detail date has changed (navigation).

UI components affected:
- Day detail popup status label and line items.

Example automation call:
```yaml
action: esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_jour
data:
  date: "2026-08-15"
  payload: "ferie|Fête du Travail;rdv|14:00 · Réunion"
```

Validation and errors:
- Early return if popup or detail label not initialized.
- Silently ignores mismatched dates.

Edge cases:
- Fallback to month-level details if available.
- Line count limited to six.

## Performance Considerations
- Bulk services split large payloads into chunks to avoid buffer overflows.
- Calendar cache evicts distant months to manage memory usage.
- Central rotator pauses during vocal responses to prevent conflicts.
- Null checks prevent crashes when LVGL widgets are not yet initialized.
- Debounce scripts reduce network calls for volume and brightness adjustments.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Service calls fail due to uninitialized widgets: Ensure LVGL initialization completes before sending updates.
- Payload too large: Split bulk payloads into smaller chunks; respect buffer limits.
- Calendar popup not updating: Verify cache TTL and ensure month/year match current view.
- Climate UI inconsistent: Use recolor script to synchronize icon states after updates.
- Assistant popup not opening: Check image URL validity and font size settings.

Error handling patterns:
- Early returns when widgets are null.
- Safe string copying with buffer bounds checking.
- Graceful degradation when optional fields are missing.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:45-53](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L45-L53)
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:205-211](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L205-L211)

## Conclusion
The Tab5 ESPHome services provide a robust interface for pushing data from Home Assistant to update the device's UI. Each service is designed with safety checks, efficient parsing, and clear separation between YAML handlers and C++ logic. The push-based architecture ensures reliable updates while minimizing network overhead. Proper payload formatting and adherence to buffer limits are essential for optimal performance.

```yaml
alias: "Update Tab5 Daily Forecasts"
trigger:
```

```yaml
trigger:
```

## Introduction
This document provides detailed API documentation for the Tab5 ESPHome voice assistant services that render spoken responses on the device. It covers:
- tab5_maj_reponse_vocale: simple text-only response shown briefly on the main interface.
- tab5_assist_reponse: rich response with Markdown formatting (including tables aligned in monospace), optional image URL with loading indicator, and automatic popup opening.

It also explains font size selection logic (roboto_mono_20/24/28), image loading states, integration with the Home Assistant Wyoming STT/TTS pipeline, and how these services interact with dismissal handling and context preservation.

## Project Structure
The voice assistant UI and services are implemented across several files:
- ESPHome API services are declared in tab5-api-logic.yaml.
- The assistant popup UI is defined in assistant_popup.yaml.
- Scripts orchestrate popup lifecycle, settings sync, and text sizing in tab5-scripts.yaml.
- C++ helpers implement Markdown formatting and LVGL updates in tab5_custom.cpp/.h.
- Monospace fonts used for table alignment are declared in tab5-styles.yaml.
- The broader voice pipeline (wake word, STT/TTS, playback) is described in docs/voice_assistant.md.

```mermaid
subgraph "ESPHome"

end
```

## Core Components
- Service tab5_maj_reponse_vocale
  - Purpose: Show a simple text-only response on the main interface for a short duration.
  - Behavior: Executes a script to display the vocal response, pauses the central panel rotator, shows the message, then hides it after a delay and resumes rotation.
  - Integration: Uses a dedicated UI helper to render the text on the main card area.

- Service tab5_assist_reponse
  - Purpose: Render a rich response in the assistant popup with Markdown support, optional image, and automatic popup open.
  - Behavior: Selects the correct monospace font based on user preference, formats and sets the response text, handles image URL (showing a loading hint while downloading), and opens the assistant popup.

- Assistant popup UI
  - Displays “Your request” (STT text) and “Response” (formatted Markdown + optional image).
  - Provides controls for mode selection, wake word, mute/volume, and text size (S/M/L).

- Font selection
  - Three Roboto Mono sizes: 20, 24, 28.
  - Selected by a persisted setting; applied to the response label when rendering or changing size.

- Image handling
  - Optional image_url triggers online_image download and display within the popup.
  - A transient hint (“Loading image...”) is shown while the image loads.

## Architecture Overview
The voice assistant flow integrates Home Assistant’s Wyoming-based STT/TTS pipeline with ESPHome services that update the UI.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant HW as "ESPHome Device"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant VA as "Voice Assistant Pipeline"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
User->>HW : Wake word / Tap mic
HW->>VA : Stream audio (I2S capture)
VA-->>HW : TTS audio stream
HW->>UI : Update mic icon state
Note over HW,UI : Playback via ES8388 speaker
VA-->>HA : Conversation result (text/image)
HA->>HW : Call tab5_assist_reponse(text, image_url)
HW->>UI : Format Markdown, set font, show image if provided
HW->>UI : Open assistant popup automatically
UI-->>User : Rich response visible
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Service: tab5_maj_reponse_vocale
- Input variables
  - texte: string — the plain text to display.
- Behavior
  - Executes a script to show the vocal response on the main interface.
  - Pauses the central panel rotator, renders the text, waits briefly, then hides it and resumes rotation.
  - Uses a dedicated UI helper to manage visibility and layout without direct LVGL calls from YAML.
- Interaction with system features
  - Temporarily overrides the central panel view but preserves context so rotation can resume correctly afterward.
  - Does not open the assistant popup; intended for quick, text-only feedback.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Service call"]) --> ExecScript["Execute 'show vocal response' script"]
ExecScript --> PauseRotator["Pause central rotator"]
PauseRotator --> RenderText["Render text on main card"]
RenderText --> Wait["Wait (short duration)"]
Wait --> HideText["Hide text"]
HideText --> ResumeRotator["Resume central rotator"]
ResumeRotator --> End(["Done"])
```

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:387-393](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L387-L393)

### Service: tab5_assist_reponse
- Input variables
  - texte: string — Markdown-formatted response text.
  - image_url: string — optional URL to an image to display below the text.
- Behavior
  - Selects the monospace font based on the persisted text size setting:
    - 0 → roboto_mono_20
    - 1 → roboto_mono_24
    - 2 → roboto_mono_28
  - Formats the Markdown (strips inline markers, converts bullets, aligns tables) and applies the selected font to the response label.
  - If image_url is non-empty:
    - Shows a “Loading image...” hint.
    - Hides any previously displayed image.
    - Sets the online_image URL to fetch and display the image.
  - Automatically opens the assistant popup and brings it to the foreground.
  - Resets activity timer to prevent auto-closing during response display.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
participant IMG as "Online Image"
HA->>ESP : tab5_assist_reponse(texte, image_url)
ESP->>ESP : Select font by assist_text_size
ESP->>UI : Format Markdown + set font + set text
alt image_url present
ESP->>UI : Show "Loading image..." hint
ESP->>IMG : Set URL to load image
IMG-->>UI : Display image when ready
else no image
ESP->>UI : Hide image widget and hint
end
ESP->>UI : Open assistant popup
```

### Markdown Formatting and Tables
- The C++ implementation normalizes UTF-8 input, strips inline Markdown markers, converts list bullets to a consistent symbol, and aligns tables using fixed-width columns.
- Separator rows are removed; only content rows are rendered.
- This ensures tables remain readable in monospace without a full Markdown engine.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
In["Input Markdown"] --> Normalize["Normalize UTF-8"]
Normalize --> ParseLines["Split into lines"]
ParseLines --> DetectTables{"Table block?"}
DetectTables --> |Yes| AlignCols["Compute column widths<br/>and pad cells"]
DetectTables --> |No| StripInline["Strip inline markers<br/>(bold/code/titles)"]
AlignCols --> BulletFix["Convert bullets to •"]
StripInline --> BulletFix
BulletFix --> Out["Formatted text for LVGL"]
```

### Font Size Selection Logic
- The assistant popup supports three text sizes mapped to monospace fonts:
  - Small (S): roboto_mono_20
  - Medium (M): roboto_mono_24
  - Large (L): roboto_mono_28
- The current size is stored in a global and applied whenever the response is set or when the user changes the size.

```mermaid

+btn_assist_size_l
}

+roboto_mono_24
+roboto_mono_28
}

```

### Image Loading States
- When an image URL is provided:
  - A transient hint (“Loading image...”) appears above the image area.
  - The image widget is hidden until the image is fetched.
  - Once loaded, the image replaces the hint and becomes visible.
- When no image URL is provided:
  - Both the image widget and hint are hidden.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Service call"]) --> CheckURL{"image_url empty?"}
CheckURL --> |Yes| HideAll["Hide image widget and hint"]
CheckURL --> |No| ShowHint["Show 'Loading image...' hint"]
ShowHint --> LoadImg["Set online_image URL"]
LoadImg --> Ready{"Image loaded?"}
Ready --> |Yes| ShowImg["Display image"]
Ready --> |No| KeepHint["Keep hint until loaded"]
HideAll --> End(["Done"])
ShowImg --> End
KeepHint --> End
```

### Automatic Popup Opening Behavior
- The assistant popup opens automatically when:
  - A rich response arrives via tab5_assist_reponse.
  - A new request is detected in Discussion mode or if the popup is already open.
- Activity timers are reset to avoid auto-closing during interactions or while a response is being displayed.

```mermaid
UI-->>User : Popup visible with response
```

### Integration with Wyoming Protocol STT/TTS Pipeline
- The device acts as a Home Assist satellite:
  - Local wake-word detection streams audio only when needed.
  - STT (Whisper) and TTS (Piper/cloud) run in Home Assistant.
  - The device displays pipeline states and plays back TTS through its DAC.
- The services documented here are invoked by the conversation agent to render textual responses and optional images alongside audio playback.

**Section sources**
- [voice_assistant.md:7-19](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/voice_assistant.md#L7-L19)

### Relationship to Dismissal Handling and Context Preservation
- Simple vocal responses temporarily override the main interface but preserve context so the central panel rotation resumes correctly after the brief display.
- Dismissal flows for alerts/info panels are separate and do not interfere with assistant popup behavior.
- The assistant popup remains open during active conversations and closes after inactivity or explicit user action.

## Performance Considerations
- Markdown formatting runs on-device; keep responses concise to minimize CPU usage on the ESP32-P4.
- Image downloads occur over Wi-Fi; large images may introduce latency. Prefer small, optimized PNGs.
- Avoid excessive push payloads during TTS playback to prevent collisions with I2S DMA traffic.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- No popup appears for rich responses
  - Ensure the service includes a non-empty texte field.
  - Verify assist_text_size is set to a valid value (0/1/2).
  - Confirm the assistant popup is not blocked by another modal.
- Images not showing
  - Check that image_url is a valid, reachable URL.
  - Confirm the online_image component is configured and the device has network access.
  - Look for the “Loading image...” hint; if it persists, the image may be failing to load.
- Markdown tables misaligned
  - Use pipe-delimited rows consistently.
  - Avoid mixing tabs/spaces inconsistently; rely on the formatter to align columns.
- Popup closes unexpectedly
  - Interact with the popup to reset the inactivity timer.
  - Be aware of automatic closing after prolonged inactivity.

## Conclusion
The Tab5 voice assistant services provide two complementary ways to present responses:
- tab5_maj_reponse_vocale for quick, text-only feedback on the main interface.
- tab5_assist_reponse for rich, formatted responses with optional images in a dedicated popup.

Together with robust Markdown formatting, configurable font sizes, and careful integration with the Home Assistant Wyoming STT/TTS pipeline, they deliver clear, accessible feedback for both hands-free and interactive use cases.

## Introduction
This document provides detailed API documentation for the current weather service used by the Tab5 HMI, specifically the `tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle` ESPHome service. It explains the payload structure, how it integrates with Home Assistant to push real-time conditions, and how the UI displays current weather alongside forecast data. It also covers refresh intervals, caching strategies, and validation considerations to ensure accurate sensor data on the device.

## Project Structure
The current weather flow spans three layers:
- Home Assistant automations that read local or online weather entities and push updates via ESPHome services.
- ESPHome API logic that receives the service call and updates internal state and UI elements.
- LVGL-based UI components that render current conditions and forecasts.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant<br/>Automations"] --> |Pushes| ESP_API["ESPHome API<br/>tab5-api-logic.yaml"]
ESP_API --> |Updates| FW_STATE["Firmware State<br/>tab5_custom.cpp/.h"]
FW_STATE --> |Renders| UI_LVGL["LVGL UI<br/>forecast_daily/hourly"]
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### ESPHome Service: tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle
- Purpose: Push current weather conditions to the device to update the predictive rain icon and humidity display context.
- Input payload:
  - condition: string (weather condition code from Home Assistant)
  - temperature: string (current temperature)
  - humidite: string (current humidity percentage)
- Processing:
  - Converts humidity to float and stores it globally.
  - If snow probability is below threshold, sets the predictive rain icon color based on humidity using a dedicated color function.
- Output: Updates UI elements without returning data to Home Assistant.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Service Entry"]) --> Parse["Parse payload:<br/>condition, temperature, humidite"]
Parse --> StoreHumidity["Store humidity in global state"]
StoreHumidity --> CheckSnow{"Snow prob < 5?"}
CheckSnow --> |Yes| ColorIcon["Compute humidity-based color<br/>and set predictive rain icon"]
CheckSnow --> |No| SkipColor["Skip color change (snow overrides)"]
ColorIcon --> End(["UI Updated"])
SkipColor --> End
```

### Home Assistant Automation: Pushing Current Weather
- Triggers include state changes of weather entities, time patterns, and connection events.
- For current weather:
  - Reads the weather entity’s state and attributes (condition, temperature, humidity).
  - Calls the ESPHome service with these values.
- Robustness:
  - Uses continue_on_error to prevent failures from blocking subsequent updates.
  - Includes delays between pushes to avoid saturating the ESP TCP socket during audio streams.

```mermaid

ESP-->>HA : Acknowledge (no payload response)
```

## Performance Considerations
- Refresh intervals:
  - The main automation triggers every 10 minutes via a time pattern, plus event-driven triggers for weather and calendar changes.
  - Delays between service calls protect the ESP32-P4 TCP socket while audio streams may be active.
- Caching strategies:
  - Firmware caches previous weather condition per tile to avoid unnecessary icon redraws and animations.
  - Calendar data is cached and re-rendered only when needed.
- Network optimization:
  - Bulk payloads reduce the number of service calls for forecasts.
  - Shorter “alerts push” automation minimizes network usage for non-critical updates.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Missing or invalid payload fields:
  - Ensure condition, temperature, and humidite are provided as strings; defaults should be applied if unavailable.
- Sensor accuracy:
  - Validate that the weather entity exposes expected attributes; use safe defaults in templates to avoid empty values.
- Connection issues:
  - Use continue_on_error to prevent automation halts; check ESPHome connectivity and reboot timeout settings.
- UI not updating:
  - Verify humidity storage and snow probability thresholds; confirm that the predictive rain icon color logic runs.

## Conclusion
The `tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle` service provides a lightweight mechanism to push current weather conditions into the Tab5 HMI, complementing forecast data with real-time humidity and condition context. Home Assistant automations handle data acquisition and robust pushing, while the firmware efficiently updates UI elements with minimal network overhead. Proper payload formatting, validation, and adherence to refresh intervals ensure reliable operation and optimal performance.

## Introduction
This document describes the tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk weather service used by the Tab5 device to display a 15-day daily forecast. It explains the payload format, how Home Assistant pushes data via ESPHome services, how the C++ layer parses and renders the forecast into a swipeable 5-window interface (3 days per window), and how errors and missing data are handled.

## Project Structure
The daily forecast UI is composed of LVGL components that render five cards per page, with three pages for 15 days total. The service handler updates internal arrays and refreshes the UI.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant"] --> |service call| ESP["ESPHome Core"]
ESP --> |payload string| API["tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk handler"]
API --> Parse["C++ parse_and_update_jours_bulk()"]
Parse --> Data["cal_jours_data[15]"]
Data --> Render["refresh_daily_forecast()"]
Render --> LVGL["LVGL widgets<br/>forecast_daily.yaml"]
```

## Core Components
- Service handler: tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk receives a single string payload and updates the day forecast arrays, then refreshes the UI.
- Data model: DayForecastData holds per-day fields including name, condition, min/max temperatures, flags (rest day, Sunday, past), and opening hours.
- Parsing: In-place tokenization using strtok_r avoids heap fragmentation; each record contains nine pipe-delimited fields.
- Rendering: refresh_daily_forecast maps parsed data to LVGL slots, colors temperatures, sets icons, and hides/shows action buttons based on the current page.

Key responsibilities:
- Payload validation and sanitization occur before parsing (length check, safe copy).
- UI rendering uses cached icon states to avoid unnecessary redraws.
- Page index determines which 5-day window is visible (0–2 for daily pages).

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Payload Format (Daily Forecast)
- Transport: Single UTF-8 string passed as the payload parameter to the service.
- Record separator: Semicolon “;” between records; trailing semicolon allowed.
- Field separator: Pipe “|” within each record.
- Fields per record (nine):
  - Index: integer 0–14
  - Day label: string (e.g., “Auj 15”, “Mer 16”)
  - Condition: string mapped to weather icons
  - Min temperature: float
  - Max temperature: float
  - Rest day flag: “1” or “0”
  - Sunday flag: “1” or “0”
  - Past day flag: “1” or “0”
  - Opening hours: string (e.g., “09h00 - 17h30”)
- Size limit: Firmware rejects payloads longer than 2048 bytes to prevent out-of-memory conditions.

Example construction (conceptual):
- Build an array of 15 records with the above fields.
- Join records with “;”.
- Ensure total byte length ≤ 2048.

Validation and sanitization:
- Empty payload is ignored.
- Length guard prevents oversized payloads.
- Safe stack buffer copy ensures null termination.
- Each record must have at least nine fields; otherwise it is skipped.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom_cpp_parsing_length_check:384-399](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L384-L399)
- [tab5_custom_cpp_parsing_fields:400-436](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L400-L436)
- [scenarios_payload_builders:139-152](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/tools/demo/scenarios.py#L139-L152)

### C++ Parsing Logic
- Uses strtok_r to split records by “;” and fields by “|” in place.
- Converts numeric fields with atoi/atof.
- Maps boolean flags by checking first character (“1” vs others).
- Stores results into cal_jours_data[jour] for jour in 0..14.

Complexity:
- Time: O(N) where N is number of characters in payload.
- Space: O(1) extra beyond the fixed-size stack buffer.

Edge cases:
- Missing or malformed fields cause the record to be skipped.
- Out-of-range indices are ignored.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom_cpp_parsing:384-436](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L384-L436)

### UI Rendering and Swipeable Interface
- Five cards per page, three pages for 15 days.
- Page index mapping:
  - Daily pages start at index 2; page 2 shows days 0–4, page 3 shows 5–9, page 4 shows 10–14.
- For each card:
  - Title label set to either HA-provided day name or computed short date.
  - Temperature labels colored by value; hidden if past day.
  - Weather icons updated only when condition changes; animated roll-in effect applied.
  - Action buttons shown only on the first daily page (page 2).

Swipe navigation:
- Gesture handling supports left/right swipes across forecast pages.
- Returns automatically to main forecast page after inactivity.

### Home Assistant Integration Examples
Service call pattern:
- Invoke service tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk with variable payload of type string.
- Inside the ESPHome lambda:
  - Call parse_and_update_jours_bulk(payload).
  - Compute daily page index from forecast_page_index.
  - Call refresh_daily_forecast with global slot arrays and fonts.
  - Refresh central page title to reflect current range.
  - Invalidate alarm planning and update derived planning banner.

Concrete example (conceptual steps):
- Prepare a payload string containing 15 daily records.
- Call the service with payload set to that string.
- On success, the UI updates immediately without additional pushes.

### Data Models
- DayForecastData fields:
  - nom_jour: string
  - condition: string
  - tmin: float
  - tmax: float
  - est_repos: bool
  - est_dimanche: bool
  - est_passe: bool
  - heures_ouverture: string
- HourForecastData fields (used for hourly view but relevant for context):
  - heure_texte: string
  - condition: string
  - temp: float
  - pluvio: float

These structures are populated by the parser and consumed by the renderer.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom_h_structures:16-35](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.h#L16-L35)

### Error Handling and Fallback Behavior
- Oversized payload: Rejected early with logging; no state change.
- Malformed records: Skipped silently; existing values remain unchanged.
- Missing data:
  - If SNTP not synchronized, long date labels fall back to short names pushed by HA.
  - Past days hide temperature ranges and reduce opacity.
  - Icons do not animate on first boot fill to avoid unnecessary repaints.

## Performance Considerations
- In-place parsing with strtok_r minimizes heap usage and avoids memory fragmentation on constrained devices.
- Stack-based buffer copy ensures safe handling of up to 2048 bytes.
- Icon change caching prevents redundant LVGL invalidations when conditions do not change.
- Staggered icon animations create a wave effect while limiting repaint cost.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- No UI update after service call:
  - Verify payload length ≤ 2048 bytes; oversized payloads are rejected.
  - Confirm payload has exactly nine fields per record and indices 0–14.
- Partial updates:
  - Check logs for “Payload jours trop long” messages indicating rejection.
  - Validate field order and types; non-numeric temps will parse to zero.
- Incorrect dates on later pages:
  - Ensure SNTP synchronization; otherwise titles fall back to HA-pushed short names.
- Excessive icon flicker:
  - Confirm condition strings are stable; repeated identical conditions should not trigger animations.

## Conclusion
The tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk service delivers a compact, efficient 15-day forecast payload to the Tab5 device. The C++ layer parses the string safely and updates LVGL widgets to show a swipeable 5-window interface with three days per window. Robust error handling and fallbacks ensure reliable operation even with incomplete or delayed data. Integrators should construct payloads according to the documented format and keep them within size limits for optimal performance.

It defines the payload format, field semantics, validation rules, and the end-to-end flow from Home Assistant automation through ESPHome to the LVGL UI. It also documents how the 15-slot horizontal forecast is rendered and updated in real time.

The hourly forecast feature spans several components:
- ESPHome API service definition and wiring to C++ logic
- C++ parsing and rendering functions
- LVGL UI components for the hourly forecast cards
- Home Assistant automation examples that build and push payloads

## Core Components
- ESPHome service: tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk accepts a single string payload and triggers C++ parsing and UI refresh.
- C++ parser: parse_and_update_heures_bulk() validates length, splits records by semicolon, then fields by pipe, and updates slot data.
- UI renderer: refresh_hourly_forecast() maps parsed data to LVGL widgets on the hourly page.
- Home Assistant automation: builds chunked payloads (5 slots per call) to respect firmware limits and calls the ESPHome service.

Key responsibilities:
- Payload construction in Home Assistant templates
- Robust parsing with bounds checking in C++
- Efficient UI updates without redundant redraws

## Architecture Overview
The hourly forecast update follows a push-only pattern:
1. Home Assistant automation gathers weather forecast data and constructs a pipe-delimited string for each 5-slot chunk.
2. The automation calls the ESPHome service tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk three times to cover all 15 slots.
3. ESPHome invokes the C++ parser to validate and store data into g_hour_slots (internal array).
4. The UI refresh function renders the current page’s five visible cards based on the active page index.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant API as "ESPHome API"
participant CPP as "C++ Logic"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
HA->>API : Call tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk(payload)
API->>CPP : parse_and_update_heures_bulk(payload)
CPP-->>CPP : Validate length, split by ';' and '|'
CPP-->>CPP : Update cal_heures_data[idx]
API->>CPP : refresh_hourly_forecast(...)
CPP-->>UI : Update labels/icons/colors
UI-->>HA : Next chunk after delay
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### API Service Definition
- Service name: tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk
- Input variable: payload (string)
- Behavior:
  - Calls parse_and_update_heures_bulk(payload)
  - Computes the hourly page index based on forecast_page_index
  - Invokes refresh_hourly_forecast() to render the visible 5-card window

Notes:
- Encryption key is configured at the API layer.
- Reboot timeout is set to avoid zombie states when HA is unreachable.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:41-53](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L41-L53)

### Payload Format and Validation Rules
- Record separator: semicolon (;)
- Field separator within each record: pipe (|)
- Each hourly record contains 5 fields:
  1) idx: integer index 0..14
  2) heure_texte: time label string (e.g., "HH:00")
  3) condition: weather condition code string used by the icon renderer
  4) temp: numeric temperature value (°C)
  5) pluvio: numeric precipitation amount (mm)
- Total payload size must not exceed 2048 bytes; larger payloads are rejected silently by the firmware to prevent memory issues.
- Parsing uses strtok_r for robust tokenization and bounds checks ensure only valid indices update slots.

Validation behavior:
- Empty payload: ignored
- Over-length payload: logged and rejected
- Malformed record (fewer than 5 fields): skipped
- Out-of-range index: ignored

Data binding:
- Parsed values are stored in an internal array (g_hour_slots / cal_heures_data[])
- UI refresh reads this array to update LVGL widgets

Example payload construction patterns:
- Home Assistant template builds chunks of 5 records separated by semicolons and ends with a trailing semicolon
- Demo utility models the same structure and enforces the 2048-byte limit

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:339-382](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L339-L382)

- [scenarios.py:131-136](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/tools/demo/scenarios.py#L131-L136)

### UI Rendering of the 15-Slot Horizontal Interface
- The hourly forecast container displays 5 cards at a time, paged across 3 pages to show 15 slots total.
- Page navigation is driven by forecast_page_index; the hourly page is shown when the index is less than 2.
- Each card is defined by a reusable template (forecast_hour_card.yaml) and positioned horizontally via x_pos variables.
- Visual order is left-to-right but corresponds to decreasing data indices so that the rightmost card shows the earliest hour in the window.

Rendering details:
- Time label, temperature, and precipitation indicators are bound to widget IDs like hN_time, hN_temp, hN_prob
- Temperature color is computed dynamically based on value ranges
- Precipitation is shown as a numeric value or a dash when zero
- Weather icons are updated using condition codes and animated on change

Real-time updates:
- After each payload, refresh_hourly_forecast() re-renders the current page’s 5 cards
- Title and context elements are refreshed to reflect the visible range

### Home Assistant Automation Example
- The automation retrieves hourly forecast data and builds three payloads, each containing 5 records.
- Each call includes a small delay to pace updates and avoid overwhelming the device.
- Fields mapped include time, condition, temperature, and precipitation.
- continue_on_error ensures partial updates do not abort the sequence.

Typical flow:
- Gather forecast list
- Loop over 3 chunks
- Build pipe-delimited records joined by semicolons
- Call esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk with payload

### Data Binding Patterns and Real-Time Updates
- Data binding is indirect: Home Assistant sends serialized strings; ESPHome parses them into structured arrays; LVGL reads those arrays during refresh.
- Real-time updates occur immediately upon receiving a payload; there is no polling from the device.
- The system avoids redundant UI work by caching previous icon conditions and animating only when they change.

## Performance Considerations
- Chunked payloads: Sending 5 slots per call keeps payloads under the 2048-byte limit and reduces memory pressure.
- In-place parsing: Uses strtok_r and stack buffers to avoid heap fragmentation.
- Conditional animations: Icon roll animations trigger only when the condition changes, minimizing unnecessary redraws.
- Efficient UI mapping: Only the currently visible page is refreshed, reducing LVGL workload.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Payload too long: If the payload exceeds 2048 bytes, it is rejected. Split into multiple calls of 5 slots each.
- Malformed records: Records missing fields or with invalid indices are ignored. Ensure each record has exactly 5 fields and idx in 0..14.
- No UI update: Verify that forecast_page_index places the hourly page in view and that the service lambda executes without early return due to null UI references.
- Stale data: Confirm that automations run in sequence with delays between chunks and that errors do not abort processing.

Error handling specifics:
- Length check: Logs an error and returns early if payload > 2048 bytes
- Tokenization: Safely handles missing separators and short records
- Index bounds: Only updates slots within 0..14

## Conclusion
The tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk service provides a robust, efficient mechanism to push hourly weather forecasts to the Tab5 device. By using a compact pipe-and-semicolon payload, chunking to respect firmware limits, and leveraging in-place parsing and targeted UI refresh, the system delivers real-time updates with minimal overhead. Home Assistant automations should follow the documented payload structure and pacing to ensure reliable rendering of the 15-slot horizontal forecast interface.

## Introduction
This document provides comprehensive API documentation for the tab5_maj_probabilites weather probability service used by the Tab5 device. It explains how Home Assistant pushes UV index, frost probability, and snow probability values to the device, how these values influence the UI (including the predictive rain icon and hourly forecast), and how related services coordinate to keep the interface consistent. It also includes example service calls, data validation notes, and guidance on visual representation of probabilities.

## Project Structure
The probability update flow spans three layers:
- Home Assistant automation builds payloads from weather entities and calls ESPHome services.
- ESPHome service handlers parse payloads and update LVGL widgets via C++ logic.
- UI components render the updated state on screen.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant Automation"] --> |Calls| ESPService["ESPHome Service Handler<br/>tab5_maj_probabilites"]
ESPService --> |Updates| Globals["Device Globals<br/>global_neige, global_humidite"]
ESPService --> |Updates| Icon["Predictive Rain Icon<br/>icon_rain_predict"]
HA --> |Also updates| CurrentWeather["Current Weather Service<br/>tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle"]
CurrentWeather --> |Updates| Humidity["Humidity Global<br/>global_humidite"]
HA --> |Pushes| HourlyBulk["Hourly Forecasts Bulk<br/>tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk"]
HourlyBulk --> |Refreshes| HourlyUI["Hourly Forecast Cards<br/>refresh_hourly_forecast()"]
```

## Core Components
- Service: tab5_maj_probabilites
  - Purpose: Update device globals and switch the predictive rain icon to a snowflake when snow probability is significant; otherwise color it based on humidity.
  - Payload fields:
    - uv: string (UV index value)
    - gel: string (frost probability percentage)
    - neige: string (snow probability percentage)
  - Behavior:
    - Stores snow probability in a device global.
    - If snow probability >= 5, sets the predictive rain icon to a snowflake and colors it with a warning tone.
    - Otherwise, keeps or re-applies a humidity-based color to the same icon.

- Related service: tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle
  - Purpose: Push current condition, temperature, and humidity to the device.
  - Interaction: When snow probability is below the threshold, the predictive rain icon color is derived from humidity using a dedicated function.

- Hourly forecast integration:
  - The hourly forecast cards display precipitation amounts per hour. While not directly driven by tab5_maj_probabilites, they are part of the broader weather UI that shares context (e.g., has_rain flag).

## Architecture Overview
The end-to-end flow for probability updates:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome Device"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
HA->>ESP : Call esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_probabilites(uv, gel, neige)
ESP->>ESP : Parse strings to integers
ESP->>ESP : Store neige in global_neige
alt neige >= 5
ESP->>UI : Set icon_rain_predict to snowflake icon
ESP->>UI : Color icon with warning color
else neige < 5
ESP->>UI : Keep or set icon based on humidity
end
Note over HA,ESP : tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle may run before/after to set humidity
HA->>ESP : Call esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle(condition, temperature, humidite)
ESP->>ESP : Store humidite in global_humidite
ESP->>UI : Apply humidity-based color to icon if neige < 5
```

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:281-319](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L281-L319)

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Service: tab5_maj_probabilites
- Input payload:
  - uv: string representing UV index
  - gel: string representing frost probability percentage
  - neige: string representing snow probability percentage
- Processing:
  - Converts string inputs to integers.
  - Persists snow probability into a device global.
  - Switches the predictive rain icon to a snowflake and applies a warning color when snow probability meets or exceeds a threshold.
  - Otherwise, ensures the icon reflects humidity-based coloring.
- Output:
  - No direct return value; updates device state and UI elements.

Validation and ranges:
- The service expects integer-like strings for all fields.
- Snow probability threshold triggers icon change at a specific value.
- Frost and UV fields are accepted but do not alter UI behavior in this service; they are part of the payload contract.

Example service call (from automation):
- Fields passed include uv, gel, neige sourced from Home Assistant sensors.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:281-319](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L281-L319)
- [automations_examples.yaml.example:64-70](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L64-L70)

### Service: tab5_maj_meteo_actuelle
- Input payload:
  - condition: string
  - temperature: string
  - humidite: string
- Processing:
  - Stores humidity in a device global.
  - Applies humidity-based color to the predictive rain icon when snow probability is below the threshold.
- Interaction:
  - Works together with tab5_maj_probabilites to ensure the icon reflects either snow conditions or humidity-driven color.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:305-319](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L305-L319)

### Hourly Forecast Integration
- The hourly forecast cards show time slots with temperature and precipitation amount.
- Precipitation amount is displayed when present; otherwise a placeholder is shown.
- The presence of any non-empty bar updates a global flag indicating rain activity.

Visual representation:
- Each card displays time, temperature, and precipitation info.
- Colors follow theme tokens for consistency.

- Minimal UI changes: Services update only necessary widgets and rely on shared functions for consistent styling.

  - Snow probability threshold determines icon behavior; confirm expected values.
- Inconsistent colors:
  - Humidity-based coloring applies when snow probability is below threshold; ensure current weather humidity is updated.

## Introduction
This document describes the tab5_maj_pluie_1h rain intensity visualization service used by the Tab5 ESPHome dashboard to render a short-term (1-hour) rain forecast as a 9-bar chart. The service receives one bar at a time from Home Assistant automations, maps textual precipitation levels to colors and heights, and updates a rotating central panel that shows current weather, planning, alerts, and the rain chart. It integrates with broader weather forecasting data and supports frequent updates while preserving device performance.

## Project Structure
The rain visualization spans three layers:
- Home Assistant automation builds the 9-slot payload from Météo-France’s next-rain hourly forecast and pushes each slot via the tab5_maj_pluie_1h service.
- ESPHome API logic interprets the payload, sets bar color and height, and toggles a has_rain flag.
- LVGL UI renders 9 bars (rb_0_in … rb_8_in) inside a container; the central card rotates among panels including the rain chart when rain is present.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant Automation"] --> |Pushes index_5mn + intensite| API["ESPHome API Service<br/>tab5_maj_pluie_1h"]
API --> |Updates LVGL objects| UI["LVGL Rain Bars<br/>rb_0_in … rb_8_in"]
API --> |Sets global| G["Global has_rain"]
UI --> |Visible when has_rain=true| Panel["Central Rotator Panel"]
```

- [automations_examples.yaml.example:72-86](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L72-L86)

## Core Components
- Home Assistant automation: Iterates 9 slots (0–8), reads the 1-hour forecast keys for minutes 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 35, 45, 55, and calls the service per slot with a 50 ms delay between calls.
- ESPHome service handler: Maps textual intensity values to colors and bar heights, updates the corresponding LVGL object, and recomputes has_rain based on whether any bar has non-zero height.
- LVGL layout: Defines 9 bars with fixed maximum height 50 px; each bar’s inner object (rb_N_in) grows from 0 to a level representing intensity.

Key payload fields:
- index_5mn: string “0”..“8”, mapping to time slots 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 35, 45, 55 minutes.
- intensite: string representing precipitation level for that slot.

Supported intensite values and their visual mapping:
- Empty or unknown: no bar (height 0, inactive color).
- Pluie faible: light blue, height ~13 px (~1/4).
- Pluie modérée: medium blue, height ~25 px (~1/2).
- Pluie forte: darker blue, height ~38 px (~3/4).
- Pluie très forte / Pluie trés forte: deepest blue, height 50 px (full).

Color tokens used:
- RAIN_LIGHT, RAIN_MODERATE, RAIN_HEAVY, RAIN_EXTREME defined in C++ constants.
- Inactive track color used for empty bars.

**Section sources**
- [automations_examples.yaml.example:72-86](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L72-L86)

## Architecture Overview
The end-to-end flow:
1. Home Assistant triggers on weather or sensor changes and constructs the 9-slot rain payload from the next_rain entity’s 1_hour_forecast attribute.
2. For each slot, it calls esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_pluie_1h with index_5mn and intensite.
3. The ESPHome service handler selects the target LVGL object by index, applies color and height, then scans all 9 bars to set has_rain.
4. The central panel rotator includes the rain panel only when has_rain is true; otherwise it cycles through other panels.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant API as "ESPHome API<br/>tab5_maj_pluie_1h"
participant LV as "LVGL UI"
participant G as "Globals<br/>has_rain"
loop 9 times (0..8)
HA->>API : index_5mn, intensite
API->>LV : Set bg_color and height on rb_N_in
API->>G : Recompute has_rain from bar heights
end
Note over HA,LV : Each call separated by ~50ms to avoid TCP saturation
```

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:323-370](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L323-L370)

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Home Assistant Payload Construction
- Source: Next-rain entity’s 1_hour_forecast attribute provides minute-level keys.
- Keys used: “0 min”, “5 min”, “10 min”, “15 min”, “20 min”, “25 min”, “35 min”, “45 min”, “55 min”.
- Loop: repeat count 9, calling the service per index with a small delay to protect the ESPHome TCP socket.
- Fallback: If forecast data is missing, “Inconnu” is sent, which results in an empty bar.

Example references:
- Automation snippet building and pushing the 9 slots.
- Demo scenarios defining sample rainfall sequences for testing.

**Section sources**
- [automations_examples.yaml.example:72-86](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L72-L86)
- [scenarios.py:201-279](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/tools/demo/scenarios.py#L201-L279)
- [demo_pusher.py:49-114](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/tools/demo/demo_pusher.py#L49-L114)

### ESPService Handler Logic
- Input variables: index_5mn (string), intensite (string).
- Mapping:
  - Unknown/empty → inactive color, height 0.
  - Pluie faible → RAIN_LIGHT, height 13.
  - Pluie modérée → RAIN_MODERATE, height 25.
  - Pluie forte → RAIN_HEAVY, height 38.
  - Pluie très forte / Pluie trés forte → RAIN_EXTREME, height 50.
- Target selection: switch on index to pick rb_0_in … rb_8_in.
- Global update: after setting the bar, scan all 9 bars; if any has height > 0, set has_rain = true.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Receive index_5mn, intensite"]) --> Map{"Map intensite"}
Map --> |Unknown/Empty| Empty["Set inactive color<br/>Height 0"]
Map --> |Faible| Light["Set RAIN_LIGHT<br/>Height 13"]
Map --> |Modérée| Moderate["Set RAIN_MODERATE<br/>Height 25"]
Map --> |Forte| Heavy["Set RAIN_HEAVY<br/>Height 38"]
Map --> |Très forte| Extreme["Set RAIN_EXTREME<br/>Height 50"]
Empty --> UpdateBar["Update LVGL object"]
Light --> UpdateBar
Moderate --> UpdateBar
Heavy --> UpdateBar
Extreme --> UpdateBar
UpdateBar --> Scan["Scan all 9 bars"]
Scan --> AnyRain{"Any height > 0?"}
AnyRain --> |Yes| SetTrue["Set has_rain = true"]
AnyRain --> |No| SetFalse["Set has_rain = false"]
SetTrue --> End(["Done"])
SetFalse --> End
```

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:323-370](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L323-L370)

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:323-370](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L323-L370)

### LVGL Visualization
- Container: rain_bar_container holds 9 bars aligned bottom-up.
- Bar structure: Outer wrapper (rb_N) with fixed max height 50; inner object (rb_N_in) grows from 0 to mapped height.
- Colors: Inactive background uses a slate tone; active bars use rain color tokens.
- Visibility: The rain panel is hidden unless has_rain is true; when true, it participates in the central panel rotation.

```mermaid
classDiagram
class RainPanel {
+id : rain_wrapper
+hidden : bool
+widgets : [icon_rain_predict, rain_bar_container]
}
class BarContainer {
+id : rain_bar_container
+layout : ROW
+widgets : [rb_0 .. rb_8]
}
class Bar {
+id : rb_N
+width : 25 or 55
+height : 50
+inner : rb_N_in
}
class InnerBar {
+id : rb_N_in
+height : 0..50
+bg_color : inactive or rain token
}
RainPanel --> BarContainer : "contains"
BarContainer --> Bar : "contains x9"
Bar --> InnerBar : "grows"
```

### Integration With Forecasting System
- Data source: Météo-France next_rain 1_hour_forecast attribute provides minute-level precipitation categories.
- Hourly forecast cards: Separate bulk services push 15 hourly tiles; the rain chart complements these with high-resolution short-term intensity.
- Central panel rotation: When has_rain is true, the rain panel becomes part of the rotating central card sequence alongside planning, alerts, and info panels.

## Performance Considerations
- Push pacing: Automations include a 50 ms delay between each of the 9 calls to avoid saturating the ESPHome TCP socket while I2S audio may be active.
- Bulk alternatives: Other forecasts use bulk payloads to reduce network overhead; the rain chart uses per-slot calls due to its incremental nature but remains lightweight.
- UI updates: Only the targeted bar is updated per call; has_rain recomputation scans 9 objects, which is negligible.
- Rotation behavior: The central panel rotation pauses when not on default forecast windows; rain visibility is gated by has_rain to minimize unnecessary redraws.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and checks:
- Missing forecast data: If the 1_hour_forecast attribute is unavailable, “Inconnu” is pushed, resulting in empty bars. Verify the next_rain entity and its attributes.
- Incorrect intensite values: Ensure the automation maps forecast keys to supported strings (“Pluie faible”, “Pluie modérée”, “Pluie forte”, “Pluie très forte”). Unknown values produce empty bars.
- No rain panel visible: Confirm has_rain is set to true when any bar has height > 0. Check that the rain panel is included in the central rotator and not hidden by other conditions.
- Network errors: If ESPHome API calls fail, ensure delays are present and the device is connected. Use continue_on_error in automations to prevent blocking.

**Section sources**
- [automations_examples.yaml.example:72-86](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L72-L86)
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:323-370](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L323-L370)
- [tab5-lvgl.yaml:397-457](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-lvgl.yaml#L397-L457)

## Conclusion
The tab5_maj_pluie_1h service provides a concise, real-time view of rain intensity over the next hour using a 9-bar chart. It translates textual precipitation levels into intuitive colors and heights, integrates seamlessly with Home Assistant weather data, and updates efficiently with minimal network and CPU impact. When rain is detected, the chart appears in the rotating central panel, complementing broader forecasting features and alerting users to short-term precipitation changes.

## Introduction
This document specifies the API for the tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france weather alert service used by the Tab5 device to display Meteo-France vigilance alerts and related weather information. It defines the pipe-delimited payload format, explains how vigilance levels map to visual indicators on the device, and provides examples of Home Assistant automations that convert Meteo-France data into the required payload. It also documents the UI integration with the daily forecast component and the alert banner system.

## Project Structure
The weather alert pipeline spans Home Assistant (data preparation and automation), ESPHome API logic (payload parsing and UI updates), and LVGL-based UI components (display rendering). Key files:
- Home Assistant automations build and push the alert payload via an ESPHome service.
- ESPHome API logic parses the payload and updates UI elements (alert icons, date color, info banner).
- UI components define the layout for forecast cards and alert slots.

```mermaid

API --> UI["LVGL UI<br/>Alert slots + Date color + Info banner"]
UI --> Cards["Forecast Daily Cards<br/>Icons + Tabs"]
```

## Core Components
- Alert Payload Service: tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france accepts a single string payload with 11 pipe-separated fields representing Meteo-France vigilance levels for different phenomena.
- UI Mapping: The firmware maps vigilance levels to colors and icons, updates the date label color based on global vigilance, and shows up to four active alerts.
- Dismiss System: A persistent list tracks dismissed alerts so users can clear banners until conditions change or new IDs appear.

Key responsibilities:
- Home Assistant templates and automations assemble the payload from Meteo-France sensor states and attributes.
- ESPHome service parses the payload and updates UI elements accordingly.
- UI components render alert slots and integrate with forecast cards.
