## Detailed Component Analysis

### API Definition: tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france
- Service name: tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france
- Input variable: payload (string)
- Payload format: 11 pipe-delimited fields
  - Field order:
    1. phrase_pluie (next rain phrase)
    2. globale (overall vigilance level)
    3. vent (wind)
    4. inondation (flood)
    5. orages (thunderstorms)
    6. pluie_inondation (rain-flood)
    7. neige_verglas (snow/ice)
    8. grand_froid (extreme cold)
    9. vagues_submersion (waves/submersion)
    10. canicule (heat wave)
    11. avalanches (avalanches)
- Default values: All fields default to “Vert” except phrase_pluie which defaults to empty; ensure capitalization matches expected levels.
- Severity mapping:
  - Vert: No alert (hidden or muted)
  - Jaune: Yellow warning
  - Orange: Warning
  - Rouge: Critical alert
- UI effects:
  - Date label color changes based on globale level (Yellow/Orange/Red).
  - Up to four active alerts are shown with icons and severity-appropriate colors.
  - Rain phrase is updated; specific numeric rain indicators are hidden when using this alert path.

Payload construction example (Home Assistant):
- Build the payload by concatenating state and attribute values with pipe separators, ensuring proper capitalization and defaults.

Firmware parsing and UI update:
- The service copies the payload into a buffer, tokenizes by pipe, and updates UI elements accordingly.
- Active alerts are filtered to exclude “Vert”, empty, or unknown levels.
- Colors are applied per severity: Yellow, Warning (Orange), Alert Red (Rouge).

### Vigilance Levels and Visual Indicators
- Global vigilance (globale) controls the date label color:
  - Jaune → Yellow
  - Orange → Orange
  - Rouge → Red
- Per-phenomena vigilance levels control alert slot visibility and color:
  - Vert → Hidden/muted
  - Jaune → Yellow icon
  - Orange → Warning color
  - Rouge → Alert red color
- Maximum of four active alerts displayed at once.

Color constants and semantics are defined in the firmware’s UI color definitions.

### Home Assistant Automation Examples
- Primary automation pushes the full set of screen data including the alert payload every ten minutes and on relevant state changes.
- Lightweight automation pushes only alerts/info text on rapid triggers (rain phrase changes, vigilance updates, dismiss actions).
- Both automations call the same service with the same payload template to keep behavior consistent.

Example references:
- Full refresh automation includes the alert payload push alongside current weather, probabilities, hourly/daily forecasts, and climate data.
- Lightweight automation focuses on alert/info updates without heavy calendar/weather calls.

### Template Sensors for Next Rain Phrase
- A template sensor computes a concise next-rain phrase based on Météo-France’s 1-hour forecast and reference time.
- It normalizes intensity labels and calculates delay until next rain, producing a short human-readable string suitable for the alert payload.

Usage:
- Include this template sensor in your Home Assistant configuration to provide the first field of the alert payload (phrase_pluie).

- The daily forecast component renders five cards showing weather icons, titles, and temperatures.

- When alert data changes, the firmware may refresh forecast page titles to reflect updated bounds or context.

Integration notes:
- Icons are updated by firmware functions; do not assign text/colors directly in UI YAML.
- The alert system complements the forecast display by adding severity-aware banners and colored dates.

- Scripts handle dismissing individual alerts or clearing the entire info panel, including weather alerts and system issues.

Behavior:
- Weather alert banners use IDs like “meteo:jaune/orange/rouge” to allow targeted dismissal.
- Dismiss events from the device trigger Home Assistant scripts to update the dismissed list and push updates back to the device.

## Performance Considerations
- Payload size limits:
  - Alert payload buffer is sized to avoid truncation; ensure payloads stay within limits.
  - Bulk payloads (daily/hourly forecasts) have strict byte limits enforced by firmware to prevent memory issues.
- Push frequency:
  - Use lightweight automations for frequent alert/info updates to avoid saturating the device’s TCP socket during audio activity.
- Template efficiency:
  - Preprocess long strings in Home Assistant to reduce firmware processing overhead.

Recommendations:
- Keep payload fields concise and capitalized consistently.
- Avoid unnecessary delays in alert-only automations.
- Monitor payload lengths in tests to prevent silent truncation.

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Missing or incorrect vigilance levels:
  - Ensure all attributes are present and capitalized; defaults to “Vert” if missing.
  - Verify the sensor entity ID matches your region (replace placeholders).
- Truncated payload:
  - Check payload length; firmware enforces buffer limits.
  - Shorten phrases or remove non-essential details.
- Alerts not dismissing:
  - Confirm meteo_id is provided in info text pushes; mismatched IDs prevent dismissal.
  - Use the dismiss script to update the dismissed list and trigger a refresh.
- UI not updating:
  - Verify the service call reaches ESPHome; check logs for errors.
  - Ensure UI element IDs exist and are initialized before updates.

Debugging steps:
- Inspect Home Assistant template outputs for correct field values.
- Validate payload structure against the 11-field specification.
- Review firmware logs for payload length warnings or parsing errors.

## Conclusion
The tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france service provides a robust mechanism to display Meteo-France vigilance alerts on the Tab5 device. By constructing a well-formed pipe-delimited payload in Home Assistant and leveraging the ESPHome API logic, you can show severity-aware alerts, update date colors, and manage dismissible banners. Integrating with the daily forecast component ensures a cohesive weather experience, while performance-conscious automation design keeps the device responsive. Follow the payload specification and troubleshooting guidance to maintain reliable operation.

## Introduction
This document provides comprehensive API documentation for all weather-related ESPHome services exposed by the Tab5 device. It covers payload formats, validation rules, error handling patterns, and UI interactions for:
- Hourly forecast updates (15 time slots)
- Daily forecast updates (15-day forecast)
- Meteo-France weather alerts with vigilance levels
- UV index, frost probability, and snow probability updates
- Current weather conditions
- Real-time rain intensity visualization (9 time slots)

Each service is designed to be called from Home Assistant automations using push-only updates. The firmware parses payloads, validates them, and updates LVGL-based UI components accordingly.

The weather services are defined in the ESPHome configuration file and implemented in C++ code. The architecture follows a clear separation between:
- Service definitions in YAML (API contract)

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Hourly Forecast Service (tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk)
This service handles 15-hour forecast updates with detailed weather information for each time slot.

#### Payload Format
The service accepts a string payload containing 15 time slots, each with 5 pipe-delimited fields:
- Field 1: Time slot index (0-14)
- Field 2: Time label (e.g., "14:00")
- Field 3: Weather condition code
- Field 4: Temperature (float)
- Field 5: Precipitation amount (float)

Records are separated by semicolons.

#### Processing Logic
```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start([Service Entry]) --> CheckEmpty{"Payload Empty?"}
CheckEmpty --> |Yes| Return[Return Immediately]
CheckEmpty --> |No| CheckLength{"Length < 2048 bytes?"}
CheckLength --> |No| LogError["Log Error: Payload Too Long"]
CheckLength --> |Yes| ParseTokens["Parse Semicolon Tokens"]
ParseTokens --> ParseFields["Parse Pipe-Delimited Fields"]
ParseFields --> ValidateIndex{"Valid Index (0-14)?"}
ValidateIndex --> |No| NextToken["Next Token"]
ValidateIndex --> |Yes| UpdateData["Update Weather Data Array"]
UpdateData --> NextToken
NextToken --> MoreTokens{"More Tokens?"}
MoreTokens --> |Yes| ParseFields
MoreTokens --> |No| RefreshUI["Refresh Hourly Forecast UI"]
RefreshUI --> End([Service Complete])
```

**Diagram sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:339-382](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L339-L382)

#### UI Updates
The service triggers hourly forecast refresh with:
- Animated icon transitions with staggered roll effects
- Temperature-based color coding
- Precipitation amount display with appropriate styling
- Time range title updates for current page

### Daily Forecast Service (tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk)
This service manages 15-day forecast data with comprehensive weather information.

#### Payload Format
Each day contains 9 pipe-delimited fields:
- Field 1: Day index (0-14)
- Field 2: Day name (e.g., "Mer 05")
- Field 3: Weather condition code
- Field 4: Minimum temperature (float)
- Field 5: Maximum temperature (float)
- Field 6: Rest day flag ("1" or "0")
- Field 7: Sunday flag ("1" or "0")
- Field 8: Past day flag ("1" or "0")
- Field 9: Opening hours (time range string)

#### Processing Logic
```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start([Service Entry]) --> ValidatePayload["Validate Payload Length"]
ValidatePayload --> ParseDays["Parse Day Records"]
ParseDays --> ExtractFields["Extract 9 Fields per Day"]
ExtractFields --> ValidateDayIndex{"Valid Day Index (0-14)?"}
ValidateDayIndex --> |No| SkipDay["Skip Invalid Day"]
ValidateDayIndex --> |Yes| UpdateDayData["Update Day Forecast Data"]
UpdateDayData --> UpdatePlanning["Update Planning Lines"]
UpdatePlanning --> TriggerAlarm["Invalidate Alarm Schedule"]
TriggerAlarm --> RefreshDailyUI["Refresh Daily Forecast UI"]
RefreshDailyUI --> End([Service Complete])
```

**Diagram sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:384-436](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L384-L436)

#### UI Features
- Color-coded day names (today, weekends, work days, past days)
- Temperature range display with gradient coloring
- Animated weather icons with wave effects
- Action buttons visibility control based on forecast page

### Meteo-France Alerts Service (tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france)
This service processes weather alerts from Meteo-France with vigilance levels.

#### Payload Format
Pipe-delimited string with 11 fields:
- Field 1: Rain phrase text
- Field 2: Global vigilance level (Vert/Jaune/Orange/Rouge)
- Field 3: Wind vigilance level
- Field 4: Flood vigilance level
- Field 5: Storm vigilance level
- Field 6: Rain-flood vigilance level
- Field 7: Snow-ice vigilance level
- Field 8: Extreme cold vigilance level
- Field 9: Wave-submersion vigilance level
- Field 10: Heatwave vigilance level
- Field 11: Avalanche vigilance level

#### Alert Processing Logic
```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start([Service Entry]) --> CopyPayload["Copy Payload to Buffer"]
CopyPayload --> SplitFields["Split by Pipe Delimiter"]
SplitFields --> ExtractGlobal["Extract Global Vigilance Level"]
ExtractGlobal --> SetDateColor["Set Date Label Color Based on Level"]
SetDateColor --> ProcessAlerts["Process Individual Alert Levels"]
ProcessAlerts --> FilterActive["Filter Active Alerts (Non-Vert)"]
FilterActive --> LimitSlots["Limit to 4 Active Slots"]
LimitSlots --> UpdateIcons["Update Alert Icons with Colors"]
UpdateIcons --> HideRainDisplay["Hide Rain Display"]
HideRainDisplay --> SetAlertFlag["Set has_alerts Flag"]
SetAlertFlag --> End([Service Complete])
```

**Diagram sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:200-280](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L200-L280)

#### Visual Indicators
- Color-coded date labels based on global vigilance level
- Up to 4 active alert slots with appropriate icons
- Dynamic color assignment (Yellow/Orange/Red) based on severity
- Automatic hiding of rain precipitation display during alerts

**Section sources**

### Probability Updates Service (tab5_maj_probabilites)
This service handles UV index, frost probability, and snow probability updates.

#### Input Parameters
- `uv`: UV index value (integer)
- `gel`: Frost probability percentage (integer)
- `neige`: Snow probability percentage (integer)

#### Processing Logic
```mermaid
flowchart TD

UpdateSnowProb --> CheckSnowLevel{"Snow Probability >= 5%?"}
CheckSnowLevel --> |Yes| ShowSnowIcon["Show Snow Icon with Warning Color"]
CheckSnowLevel --> |No| CheckHumidity["Check Current Humidity"]
CheckHumidity --> GetHumidityColor["Get Humidity-Based Color"]
GetHumidityColor --> ShowRainIcon["Show Rain Icon with Appropriate Color"]
ShowSnowIcon --> End([Service Complete])
ShowRainIcon --> End
```

### Rain Intensity Service (tab5_maj_pluie_1h)
This service provides real-time rain intensity visualization with 9 time slots showing precipitation levels.

#### Input Parameters
- `index_5mn`: Time slot index (0-8) representing 5-minute intervals
- `intensite`: Rain intensity level (French strings)

#### Intensity Levels
- "Pluie faible": Light rain (~25% height)
- "Pluie modérée": Moderate rain (~50% height)  
- "Pluie forte": Heavy rain (~75% height)
- "Pluie très forte": Extreme rain (100% height)

#### Visualization Logic
```mermaid

MapIntensity --> FindTarget["Find Target UI Element"]
FindTarget --> UpdateBar["Update Bar Height and Background Color"]
UpdateBar --> CheckAllBars["Check All 9 Bars"]
CheckAllBars --> SetRainFlag["Set has_rain Flag Based on Activity"]
SetRainFlag --> End([Service Complete])
```

## Performance Considerations
The weather services are optimized for efficient operation on embedded hardware:

### Memory Management
- Stack-based buffer allocation for payload processing (avoiding heap fragmentation)
- Maximum payload size limits (2048 bytes) to prevent memory overflow
- Efficient string parsing without temporary object creation

### UI Optimization
- Conditional animation triggering only when content actually changes
- Staggered animations to reduce rendering load
- Reuse of existing UI components rather than recreation

### Network Efficiency
- Bulk data transmission reducing network overhead
- Push-only architecture minimizing polling
- Delay mechanisms to prevent TCP socket saturation

## Troubleshooting Guide

### Common Issues and Solutions

#### Payload Too Long Errors
**Symptom**: Logs show "Payload trop long" errors
**Cause**: Exceeding 2048-byte limit for bulk forecast data
**Solution**: Reduce payload size by limiting data fields or splitting into smaller chunks

#### Missing UI Components
**Symptom**: Services execute but no visual changes occur
**Cause**: UI components not yet initialized or null pointers
**Solution**: Ensure proper initialization sequence and check component availability

#### Incorrect Data Display
**Symptom**: Weather data shows incorrectly formatted or missing information
**Cause**: Malformed payload structure or incorrect field mapping
**Solution**: Verify payload format matches expected structure exactly

#### Animation Issues
**Symptom**: Weather icons not animating properly
**Cause**: Animation suppression flags or timing conflicts
**Solution**: Check animation state and ensure proper sequencing

### Debugging Techniques
- Enable detailed logging in ESPHome configuration
- Monitor payload sizes and parsing results
- Use Home Assistant developer tools to test service calls
- Check LVGL component initialization status

- [tab5_custom.cpp:341-344](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L341-L344)

## Conclusion
The weather services provide a comprehensive solution for displaying weather information on the Tab5 device. The architecture ensures reliable data processing, efficient resource usage, and responsive user interface updates. By following the documented payload formats and integration patterns, developers can create robust weather monitoring solutions that leverage the full capabilities of the ESPHome ecosystem.

The system's design emphasizes reliability through input validation, graceful error handling, and performance optimization suitable for embedded environments. The modular approach allows for easy extension and maintenance while maintaining compatibility with existing Home Assistant integrations.

## Introduction
This document explains how Tab5 integrates an event bus between Home Assistant (HA), ESPHome, and internal C++ processing to update the UI without polling. The system is push-only: HA automations detect state changes and call ESPHome API services on the device; each service handler parses payloads and updates LVGL widgets via centralized C++ helpers. There are no device-side polls for displayed state.

Key principles:
- One-directional data flow: HA → ESPHome services → C++ handlers → LVGL UI.
- All non-trivial LVGL logic lives in C++; YAML only wires triggers and calls helpers.
- Robustness guards exist for boot state, connection state, payload sizes, and UTF-8 text.

**Section sources**
- [ADR-0001: Push-only architecture, zero polling from the device:1-18](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-push-only-zero-polling.md#L1-L18)
- [architecture.md:82-100](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L82-L100)
- [ADR-0006: Centralize LVGL logic in C++:1-18](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0006-centralize-lvgl-logic-in-cpp.md#L1-L18)

## Project Structure
The event bus spans three layers:
- Home Assistant layer: automations/scripts that serialize state into payloads and call ESPHome services.
- ESPHome layer: `api: services:` definitions that receive payloads and invoke C++ lambdas.
- C++ layer: parsing, validation, and LVGL updates through helper functions.

```mermaid
graph TB
subgraph "Home Assistant"
A["Automations / Scripts"]
end
subgraph "ESPHome Device"
B["API Services<br/>tab5_maj_*"]
C["C++ Handlers<br/>tab5_custom.*"]
D["LVGL UI"]
end
A --> |"esphome.service calls"| B
B --> |"lambda calls"| C
C --> |"update helpers"| D
```

## Core Components
- ESPHome API services: Each `tab5_maj_*` service defines variables and a lambda that validates inputs and calls a C++ function to parse and apply updates.
- C++ handlers: Centralized in `tab5_custom.cpp`, with declarations in `tab5_custom.h`. They perform parsing, UTF-8 normalization, bounds checks, and LVGL updates.
- Globals: Shared state such as current panel, flags for alerts/rain/info, and view contexts live in `tab5-globals.yaml` and are synchronized by handlers before rendering.
- HA control surface: `tab5-ha-controls.yaml` exposes entities to observe and drive screens from HA, reusing the same paths as on-device actions.

Examples of event types and payloads:
- Weather bulk updates: `tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk`, `tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk` with serialized payloads parsed into forecast structs.
- Climate state: `tab5_maj_clim` with target/current/mode/preset/fan/swing strings.
- Shutter state: `tab5_maj_volet_etat` with physical state string; also toggles wake-word model while moving.
- Alerts: `tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france` (11 pipe-delimited fields), `tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk` (up to 4 banners).
- Calendar: `tab5_maj_calendrier_mois` and `tab5_maj_calendrier_jour` with codes/hours/details.
- Voice assistant response: `tab5_assist_reponse` with Markdown text and optional image URL.

## Architecture Overview
The event bus follows a strict contract:
- HA side: Automations serialize state into compact strings and call specific ESPHome services.
- ESPHome side: Service handlers validate and forward to C++ handlers; they avoid direct LVGL calls except trivial cases.
- C++ side: Parse payloads safely (stack buffers, strtok_r), normalize UTF-8, guard against null LVGL objects, and update UI deterministically.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ES as "ESPHome API Service"
participant CPP as "C++ Handler"
participant LV as "LVGL UI"
HA->>ES : "call tab5_maj_* with payload"
ES->>CPP : "lambda invokes parser/update helper"
CPP->>CPP : "validate payload size, parse fields"
CPP->>LV : "update labels/icons/colors"
LV-->>ES : "UI reflects new state"
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Weather Forecast Events (Hourly and Daily)
- Trigger: HA pushes serialized hourly/daily forecasts via `tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk` and `tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk`.
- Processing: C++ parsers split payloads using stack buffers and delimiters, populate forecast arrays, then refresh UI slots with color-coded temperatures and icons.
- Ordering: Each service call updates its own dataset; subsequent UI refresh uses current page index to render the correct window.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Service Received"]) --> Validate["Validate payload length"]
Validate --> |OK| Parse["Parse fields with strtok_r"]
Validate --> |Too long| Drop["Drop payload to avoid OOM"]
Parse --> UpdateData["Update forecast arrays"]
UpdateData --> RefreshUI["Refresh daily/hourly slots"]
RefreshUI --> End(["UI Updated"])
Drop --> End
```

### Météo-France Vigilance and Rain Events
- Trigger: `tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france` (11 pipe-delimited fields) and `tab5_maj_pluie_1h` (per-bar updates).
- Processing: Parses vigilance levels, maps to colors, hides/shows alert slots; rain bars update intensity and aggregate `has_rain`.
- Result: Central rotator displays weather alerts and rain visualization.

```mermaid

end
```

### HA Alert Queue Events
- Trigger: `tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk` with up to 4 banners.
- Processing: Builds slot structures, syncs context flags, parses and renders alerts; supports local dismiss tracking.
- Result: Central rotator cycles through active alerts with tap-to-dismiss behavior.


### Calendar Events
- Trigger: `tab5_maj_calendrier_mois` and `tab5_maj_calendrier_jour`.
- Processing: Stores month codes/hours/details; renders month grid locally and enriches with HA details if visible; day detail updates ignored if date changed.
- Result: Calendar popup shows workdays, holidays, school vacations, appointments, birthdays with embedded details.

```mermaid
CM->>UI : "cache month data"
Note over CM,UI : "re-render only if month matches view"
HA->>CJ : "date, payload"
CJ->>UI : "render day detail if still visible"
```

### Alarm/Rendez-vous Events
- Trigger: `tab5_maj_rdv_prochains` pushes upcoming appointments; firmware stores and announces locally at exact time.
- Processing: Deduplicates announcements by epoch to avoid loops; updates next-alarm sensor.
- Result: Reliable alarm announcements even if HA goes down between push and trigger.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
In["payload: epoch|titre~..."] --> Store["rdv_store(payload)"]
Store --> Announce{"Next appointment due?"}
Announce --> |Yes| Ring["Announce locally"]
Announce --> |No| Wait["Wait for tick"]
Ring --> Update["Update next sensor"]
Wait --> Update
```

## Dependency Analysis
- HA to ESPHome: Automations call `esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_*` services with typed payloads.
- ESPHome to C++: Lambdas in `tab5-api-logic.yaml` call functions declared in `tab5_custom.h` and implemented in `tab5_custom.cpp`.
- C++ to LVGL: Helpers update widgets; all non-trivial LVGL logic is centralized to ensure consistency and testability.
- Globals synchronization: Handlers update shared flags and indices before rendering to keep UI state coherent.

```mermaid
graph LR
HA["HA Automations"] --> SVC["ESPHome Services"]
SVC --> HLP["C++ Helpers"]
HLP --> LV["LVGL Widgets"]
HLP --> GLB["Globals (tab5-globals.yaml)"]
```

## Performance Considerations
- Zero polling: Device never requests state; CPU/network usage stays near idle until events arrive.
- Payload sizing: Handlers reject oversized payloads to prevent out-of-memory conditions.
- Efficient parsing: Stack-based buffers and `strtok_r` minimize heap allocations during parsing.
- Animation costs: Short durations and reduced amplitudes reduce repaint overhead; roll effects are staged to avoid redundant redraws.
- Reuse of global slot pointers: Avoids reconstructing LVGL references in every handler.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and mitigations:
- Stale screen after missed pushes: Because the device does not poll, missing HA automations can leave UI stale. Use HA-side guards and `continue_on_error: true` to improve reliability.
- HA restarts causing NaN or crashes: Always check `boot_complete` and `api.connected()` before LVGL calls in lambdas.
- Duplicate or stuck flags in multi-instance setups: The project uses a single HA instance to avoid entity ID collisions and stuck flags.
- Demo tool mismatches: If expected services are absent, the demo logs warnings indicating firmware/automation mismatch.

Debugging techniques:
- Observe service calls in demo mode to verify touch and service routing.
- Use diagnostic entities exposed by `tab5-ha-controls.yaml` to monitor current screen and volume state from HA.
- Inspect logs for payload size rejections and parsing errors in C++ handlers.

**Section sources**
- [ADR-0001: Push-only architecture, zero polling from the device:1-18](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-push-only-zero-polling.md#L1-L18)
- [architecture.md:82-100](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L82-L100)

## Conclusion
Tab5’s event bus is a robust, push-only integration that minimizes device resource usage while delivering near-real-time UI updates. By centralizing LVGL logic in C++, validating payloads, normalizing text, and synchronizing globals, the system maintains stability and performance. Extending the event system requires adding both HA-side automation and a corresponding ESPHome service handler that delegates to C++ helpers, ensuring consistent behavior and maintainability.

## Appendices

### Event Types and Payloads Summary
- Weather hourly: `tab5_maj_previsions_heures_bulk` — serialized hourly forecast chunks.
- Weather daily: `tab5_maj_previsions_jours_bulk` — serialized daily forecast window.
- Climate: `tab5_maj_clim` — target/current/mode/preset/fan/swing strings.
- Shutter: `tab5_maj_volet_etat` — physical state string.
- Météo-France: `tab5_maj_alerte_meteo_france` — 11 pipe-delimited fields.
- Rain chart: `tab5_maj_pluie_1h` — per-bar index/intensity.
- Info banner: `tab5_maj_info_texte` — text/color/dismiss id.
- Voice response: `tab5_assist_reponse` — Markdown text + optional image URL.
- HA alerts: `tab5_maj_alertes_ha_bulk` — up to 4 banners.
- Calendar month: `tab5_maj_calendrier_mois` — codes/hours/details.
- Calendar day: `tab5_maj_calendrier_jour` — date + detail lines.
- Appointments: `tab5_maj_rdv_prochains` — epoch|title entries.

### Guidelines for Extending the Event System
- Add a new HA-side automation/script that serializes state into a compact string and calls a new `tab5_maj_*` service.
- Define the service in `tab5-api-logic.yaml` with typed variables and a lambda that calls a C++ helper.
- Implement parsing and LVGL updates in `tab5_custom.cpp`, using stack buffers and avoiding heap churn.
- Update globals in `tab5-globals.yaml` only if cross-handler state is required; synchronize them before rendering.
- Guard LVGL calls with boot/connection checks; handle malformed payloads gracefully.
- Keep animations short and reuse existing helpers to maintain performance.

## Introduction
This document explains the Home Assistant control entities that allow remote operation of the Tab5 device, focusing on:
- Volume control entity (number.tab5_volume_pct): percentage-based interface, integration with the tab5_volume_apply script, and synchronization between device and Home Assistant.
- Screen navigation entity (select.tab5_goto_screen): available screens, navigation logic, popup management, and activity state handling to prevent auto-closing.

It also provides automation examples, state synchronization patterns, and troubleshooting guidance for common issues such as stuck popups or volume desynchronization.

## Project Structure
The control surface is implemented in ESPHome and exposed to Home Assistant through a dedicated controls file. The main entry point includes this controls package after LVGL initialization so that LVGL IDs referenced by the controls are available.

```mermaid
graph TB
A["tab5-ha-hmi.yaml<br/>Main ESPHome entry"] --> B["Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml<br/>HA control entities"]
B --> C["Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml<br/>Shared scripts (volume apply, debounces)"]
B --> D["Tab5/tab5-globals.yaml<br/>Globals (volume_push_ts, assist flags)"]
B --> E["Tab5/tab5-custom.h<br/>UI idle, popup animations, helpers"]
A --> F["Tab5/tab5-lvgl.yaml<br/>LVGL pages/widgets"]
```

- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:1-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L1-L17)

## Core Components
- number.tab5_volume_pct: Template number exposing system volume to Home Assistant. Reading returns the device’s source-of-truth volume; writing calls the single entry-point script to update UI, speaker, and HA state.
- select.tab5_goto_screen: Optimistic select used to open specific screens or popups from Home Assistant. It closes all overlays first, then opens the requested target using the same code paths as on-device interactions.
- text_sensor.tab5_screen_name: Diagnostic sensor reporting the currently visible screen or popup, including game overlays and central rotator panels.

Key behaviors:
- All volume changes go through one script to keep device UI, media player, and HA consistent.
- Navigation via select triggers the same popup open/close routines as touch input, ensuring identical behavior whether controlled locally or remotely.
- Activity marking prevents automatic popup dismissal when opening via Home Assistant.

## Architecture Overview
The control flow ensures a single source of truth for volume and consistent popup lifecycle across device and Home Assistant.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome Controls"
participant Script as "tab5_volume_apply"
participant MP as "media_player.speaker_player"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
HA->>ESP : set number.tab5_volume_pct (0..100)
ESP->>Script : execute vol=x/100, push_device=true
Script->>UI : sync sliders + mute icons
Script->>MP : debounce -> volume_set(system_volume)
Script-->>ESP : publish_state(system_volume*100)
Note over ESP,UI : Device UI reflects new volume immediately
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Volume Control Entity: number.tab5_volume_pct
- Purpose: Expose system volume as a percentage (0–100) to Home Assistant.
- Read path: Returns id(system_volume) * 100, which is the authoritative value shown on device sliders and used by mute logic.
- Write path: Calls script.tab5_volume_apply with normalized volume and push_device=true.
- Synchronization:
  - Updates both device-side sliders and mute icons.
  - Debounces actual media_player.volume_set to avoid spamming during slider drags.
  - Publishes updated state back to Home Assistant.
  - Background interval catches volume changes made directly in Home Assistant (e.g., mobile app) and pushes them back to the device UI.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Set number.tab5_volume_pct"]) --> Normalize["Normalize 0..1"]
Normalize --> UpdateState["Update system_volume and un-mute"]
UpdateState --> SyncUI["Sync sliders + mute icons on device"]
SyncUI --> Debounce{"push_device?"}
Debounce --> |Yes| CallSet["Debounce media_player.volume_set"]
Debounce --> |No| SkipSet["Skip redundant set"]
CallSet --> Publish["Publish state to HA"]
SkipSet --> Publish
Publish --> End(["Done"])
```

- [tab5-scripts.yaml:324-368](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L324-L368)

### Screen Navigation Entity: select.tab5_goto_screen
- Purpose: Open specific screens or popups from Home Assistant, mirroring exact on-device behavior.
- Available options:
  - “—” (reset/no-op)
  - “Accueil” (Home dashboard)
  - “Assistant vocal” (Voice Assistant popup)
  - “Calendrier” (Calendar popup)
  - “Réveil” (Alarm popup)
  - “Climatisation” (Climate popup)
  - “Plantes” (Plants detail popup)
  - “Télécommande TV” (TV Remote popup)
  - “Console système” (System Console overlay)
- Behavior:
  - If not already on the main page, it closes any running games and shows page_main first.
  - Closes all known popups and confirm overlays to ensure a clean state before opening the target.
  - Uses the same open routines as on-device interactions (animations, foregrounding).
  - For non-Home targets, marks activity to prevent auto-close due to idle timeout.
  - Resets itself to “—” so the same destination can be re-triggered immediately.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
S(["Select option"]) --> CheckHome{"On page_main?"}
CheckHome --> |No| CloseGames["Close all games"]
CloseGames --> ShowHome["Show page_main"]
CheckHome --> |Yes| NextStep["Next step"]
ShowHome --> NextStep
NextStep --> ClosePopups["Close all popups + confirm overlays"]
ClosePopups --> Target{"Target already visible?"}
Target --> |Yes| MarkAct["Mark activity (non-Home)"]
MarkAct --> ResetSel["Reset select to '—'"]
Target --> |No| OpenTarget["Open via animate_popup_open or direct layer"]
OpenTarget --> MarkAct
ResetSel --> End(["Done"])
```

- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:99-224](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L99-L224)

- [screens.md:21-35](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/screens.md#L21-L35)

### State Synchronization Patterns
- Volume:
  - Single entry point script ensures device UI, media player, and HA state stay consistent.
  - Debounce avoids repeated media_player.volume_set calls during slider interaction.
  - Background interval reconciles volume changed directly in Home Assistant back to the device UI.
- Screens:
  - Diagnostics sensor reports the current visible screen or popup, including games and central rotator panels.
  - Navigation uses the same popup lifecycle functions as touch input, preventing divergence between local and remote control.

- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:41-97](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L41-L97)

- [tab5-scripts.yaml:324-368](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L324-L368)

## Dependency Analysis
- tab5-ha-controls.yaml depends on:
  - tab5-scripts.yaml for shared scripts (volume apply, debounces).
  - tab5-globals.yaml for globals like volume_push_ts and assist flags.
  - LVGL components defined elsewhere (pages, popups) for IDs referenced in navigation logic.
- tab5-scripts.yaml implements the unified volume path and debounces.
- tab5-custom.h defines idle timeouts and popup animation helpers used by navigation.

```mermaid
graph LR
HA["Home Assistant"] --> CTRL["tab5-ha-controls.yaml"]
CTRL --> SCRIPTS["tab5-scripts.yaml"]
CTRL --> GLOBALS["tab5-globals.yaml"]
CTRL --> LVGL["LVGL pages/popups"]
SCRIPTS --> MEDIA["media_player.speaker_player"]
CTRL --> CUSTOM["tab5-custom.h"]
```

## Performance Considerations
- Volume changes are debounced to reduce network and I2S load during slider drags.
- Navigation avoids unnecessary re-shows of the main page and closes only what is needed.
- Activity marking prevents premature popup closure, reducing flicker and re-open loops.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide

### Stuck Popup or Wrong Screen Reported
- Symptom: Home Assistant shows “Accueil” while a popup is actually covering the screen.
- Cause: New popups must be added to both the diagnostic table and the navigation close list; otherwise, remote navigation may not close them properly.
- Resolution: Ensure any new modal is included in the kScreens array and the kPopups list used by tab5_goto_screen. Use text_sensor.tab5_screen_name to verify the actual visible layer.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:41-97](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L41-L97)
- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:168-180](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L168-L180)

### Volume Desynchronization
- Symptom: Slider on device differs from Home Assistant number entity or vice versa.
- Causes:
  - Volume changed directly in Home Assistant without device refresh.
  - Muted state causing speaker volume to be zero while system_volume holds the remembered level.
- Resolution:
  - Use number.tab5_volume_pct to set volume consistently via the single script.
  - Rely on the background interval that reconciles media_player volume back to device UI when not muted and outside the debounce window.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:19-39](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L19-L39)
- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:237-265](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L237-L265)
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:324-368](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L324-L368)

### Popup Auto-Closes Immediately After Opening from Home Assistant
- Symptom: Selecting a screen from Home Assistant appears to do nothing because the popup closes quickly.
- Cause: Idle timer may have already passed; opening via Home Assistant must mark activity to prevent auto-close.
- Resolution: The select entity already calls ui_mark_activity for non-Home targets. Verify you selected a valid target (not “—”) and that the popup is not already hidden.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:207-224](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L207-L224)
- [tab5-custom.h:137-164](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-custom.h#L137-L164)

### General Issues Referenced in Troubleshooting Docs
- Black screen after software reboot: requires a boot delay for GPIO expander stability.
- Push automations gated by helper flag: ensure the active-instance helper is enabled.
- Touch service calls rejected: enable “Allow service calls” in ESPHome integration options.

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:13-19](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L13-L19)
- [troubleshooting.md:23-29](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L23-L29)
- [troubleshooting.md:43-49](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L43-L49)

## Automation Examples
Below are conceptual examples illustrating how to use the control entities in Home Assistant. Replace entity IDs and names with your configuration.

- Set volume to 75%:
  - Action: call service number.set_value on number.tab5_volume_pct with value 75.
  - Effect: device UI updates, speaker volume is debounced and applied, HA state reflects current system volume.

- Open Calendar popup:
  - Action: call select.select_option on select.tab5_goto_screen with option “Calendrier”.
  - Effect: closes any running games, ensures main page is shown, closes all popups, opens calendar popup, marks activity to prevent auto-close, resets select to “—”.

- Return to Home dashboard:
  - Action: call select.select_option on select.tab5_goto_screen with option “Accueil”.
  - Effect: closes all popups and games, shows main page without marking activity (to allow normal forecast rotation).

- Refresh calendar data:
  - Action: call button.press on button.tab5_reload_calendar.
  - Effect: executes the same prefetch script used at boot to load current month and next month.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:19-39](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L19-L39)
- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:99-224](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L99-L224)
- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:226-235](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L226-L235)
- [automations_examples.yaml.example:25-46](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/automations_examples.yaml.example#L25-L46)

## Conclusion
The Tab5 exposes two primary control surfaces to Home Assistant:
- number.tab5_volume_pct for robust, synchronized volume control via a single script.
- select.tab5_goto_screen for reliable, consistent screen navigation that mirrors on-device behavior.

Together with diagnostics and background reconciliation, these entities provide a stable remote control experience. Use the provided automation patterns and troubleshooting guidance to maintain consistency between device and Home Assistant states.

## Introduction
This document describes all Home Assistant entities exposed by the Tab5 device and how they are used to control volume, manage screens, navigate between UI panels, and monitor system status. It explains entity states, attributes, available actions, state transitions, event-driven updates, availability logic, connection handling, recovery mechanisms when Home Assistant is unavailable, and provides examples for UI interactions, automations, and scripts. It also includes troubleshooting guidance and performance tips for high-frequency state updates.

## Project Structure
The Tab5 integrates with Home Assistant via ESPHome’s native API. The main entry point configures boot behavior, packages, and exposes services that update the UI. Supporting packages define diagnostics sensors, domotique sensors, HA-facing controls, and health monitoring.

```mermaid
graph TB

J["tab5_calendar.yaml<br/>Calendar scripts"] --> B
K["tab5_tv.yaml<br/>TV app launcher"] --> L["media_player / remote"]
```

## Core Components
- Volume control:
  - Number entity “Volume” (percentage) reads and writes the global system volume and applies it to the speaker media player through a single script.
  - Mute/unmute is managed via a global flag and applied to the media player; a background interval reconciles changes made from Home Assistant back to the device.
- Current screen management:
  - Text sensor reports the currently visible screen or popup, including games, assistant, calendar, alarm, climate, plants, TV remote, and system console.
  - Select entity “Go to screen” navigates to a target screen, closing any active game or popup as needed and refreshing activity timers.
- Screen navigation:
  - Navigation uses LVGL page/popup APIs and shared globals to track current panel indices and visibility flags.
- System status monitoring:
  - Diagnostics expose WiFi, IP/SSID, RSSI, core temperature, uptime, free heap, loop time, and HA API status.
  - Health package monitors primary instance activity, unexpected reboots, and API disconnections.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:19-266](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L19-L266)
- [tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml:16-310](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-sensors-diagnostics.yaml#L16-L310)
- [tab5-health.yaml:43-176](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_health.yaml#L43-L176)

## Architecture Overview
The Tab5 follows a push-only model: Home Assistant pushes data to the device via ESPHome services. The device renders UI locally using LVGL and maintains internal state in globals. When Home Assistant is unavailable, the device continues operating locally (clock, games, last cached UI). Recovery includes periodic reconnection checks and pre-fetching calendars on reconnect.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ESP as "ESPHome (Tab5)"
participant API as "API Services"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
participant G as "Globals"
HA->>ESP : Call service tab5_maj_* (payload)
ESP->>API : Route to handler
API->>G : Update globals (e.g., forecast, alerts, climate)
API->>UI : Refresh widgets (labels, icons, colors)
Note over ESP,UI : Device remains usable without HA
ESP-->>HA : Events (connected/disconnected)
```

- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:41-529](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L41-L529)

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Volume Control Entity
- Entity ID: number.tab5_volume_pct (template number)
- State: percentage (0–100), derived from global system_volume
- Attributes: unit_of_measurement "%", icon mdi:volume-high
- Actions:
  - Set value triggers script to apply volume to the speaker media player and optionally push back to device if changed remotely.
- Behavior:
  - Muting sets volume to 0 and toggles a mute flag; unmuting restores previous volume.
  - A background interval reconciles differences between the device’s media player volume and the stored system volume after user interaction or HA changes.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Set volume"]) --> Apply["Execute volume script"]
Apply --> CheckMuted{"Is muted?"}
CheckMuted --> |Yes| Unmute["Unset mute flag"]
CheckMuted --> |No| KeepMute["Keep mute flag"]
Unmute --> SetVol["Apply volume to media player"]
KeepMute --> SetVol
SetVol --> SyncInterval["Background sync interval checks drift"]
SyncInterval --> End(["Done"])
```

- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:19-39](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L19-L39)

### Current Screen Management Entity
- Entity ID: text_sensor.tab5_screen_name
- State: Human-readable name of the currently visible screen or popup (e.g., “Accueil · Planning”, “Assistant vocal”, “Console système”, “Jeu · Arcanoïde”)
- Purpose: Remote visibility of what is shown on the device, including whether a popup covers the dashboard or which central panel is active.

```mermaid
flowchart TD

CheckPopup --> |No| PanelIndex["Read current_central_panel"]
PanelIndex --> PanelName["Map index to panel name"]
PopupName --> End(["Return screen name"])
PanelName --> End
```

### Screen Navigation Entity

- Options: “—”, “Accueil”, “Assistant vocal”, “Calendrier”, “Réveil”, “Climatisation”, “Plantes”, “Télécommande TV”, “Console système”
- Actions:
  - Closes any open games/popups, shows the target screen, and refreshes activity timers to prevent auto-close.

## Dependency Analysis
- Boot sequence initializes LVGL, backlight, speaker enable, waits for API connection, emits connected event, and runs initial scripts.
- API services depend on LVGL widget IDs and globals; they update UI directly via C++ helpers.
- Diagnostics sensors update UI conditionally based on console visibility.
- Health automations rely on binary_sensor.ha_api_status and sensor.tab5_uptime to detect issues.

```mermaid
graph LR
Boot["Boot handlers"] --> API["API services"]
API --> Globals["Globals"]
```

## Performance Considerations
- Push-only design avoids polling; updates are event-driven from Home Assistant.
- High-frequency updates (e.g., weather, rain bars) batch data where possible and guard UI updates to avoid unnecessary redraws.
- Background intervals reconcile state drift (e.g., volume) with minimal overhead.
- Avoid raw now() in templates; use bounded windows and trigger-based logic to reduce template churn.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Screen freezes when Home Assistant is down:
  - The device continues running locally; check binary_sensor.ha_api_status and ensure push automations are enabled.
  - Use health automations to detect prolonged downtime and notify.
- Unexpected reboots:
  - Monitor sensor.sys_uptime; health automation detects drops indicating reboot.
  - Check power supply and logs for brownouts.
- API disconnected:
  - binary_sensor.ha_api_status indicates connection; health automation alerts after 2 minutes.
  - Ensure WiFi credentials and AP fallback are configured correctly.
- Volume mismatch between device and HA:
  - The background interval reconciles differences; verify script execution and mute state.
- Calendar not updating:
  - Trigger script.tab5_calendrier_mois or press “Reload calendar” button; ensure calendars are accessible and queries succeed.
- TV app launch failures:
  - Verify app IDs and REST endpoint; confirm TV is reachable and powered on; use remote key sequences for physical inputs if needed.

## Conclusion
The Tab5 exposes a focused set of Home Assistant entities to control volume, manage and navigate screens, and monitor system health. Its push-only architecture ensures efficient updates while maintaining local usability during outages. Robust recovery mechanisms, health monitoring, and clear entity behaviors make it reliable for daily use. For best results, configure entity IDs in user_entities.yaml, keep push automations active, and leverage health alerts to maintain system stability.

## Introduction
This document explains the status monitoring entities that provide visibility into the Tab5 device state, with a focus on:
- The current screen entity (tab5_screen_name), including its complex state machine for active popups, games, and dashboard panels
- The priority system for screen detection and game overlay handling
- Central panel rotation states (planning, rain, weather alerts, info, Home Assistant alerts)
- Connection status monitoring, device availability indicators, and diagnostic information exposure
- Practical examples for dashboards, alerting automations when the device is unresponsive, and debugging tools to identify UI state issues

## Project Structure
The status system spans ESPHome firmware configuration, LVGL UI layout, shared C++ logic, and Home Assistant packages:
- ESPHome exposes diagnostic sensors and a template text sensor that reports the currently visible screen
- LVGL defines pages, popups, layers, and the central card where panels rotate
- Shared C++ structures and helpers manage idle timeouts, animations, and central panel visibility
- Home Assistant packages monitor health and expose alert dismissal flows

## Core Components
- Current screen entity (tab5_screen_name): A template text sensor that inspects LVGL page state and popup visibility to report the exact screen or overlay shown. It includes a strict priority order so that alarm ring overlays, popups, and games are correctly reported even when underlying pages remain technically “shown.”
- Central panel rotator: Tracks which of the eight central panels (planning, rain, weather alerts, info, up to four HA alerts) is currently active and rotates them with smooth transitions.
- Device diagnostics: WiFi SSID/IP, RSSI, core temperature, free heap, loop time, SNTP time, and HA API status are exposed as sensors and binary sensors, updated periodically and refreshed when the system console layer is visible.
- Health monitoring: Home Assistant automations watch for push pipeline degradation, unexpected reboots, and loss of native API connectivity.

## Architecture Overview
The current screen determination follows a layered priority model:
1. If the main dashboard page is not showing, check if any game is open and return the corresponding game name.
2. If the main page is showing, scan a fixed list of popups/layers in priority order (alarm ring overlay first, then alarm popup, voice assistant, calendar, lights, climate, plants, TV remote, system console).
3. If no overlay is visible, read the central panel index to determine which dashboard panel is active (planning, rain, weather alerts, info, or HA alerts).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Read tab5_screen_name"]) --> CheckMain{"Is main page showing?"}
CheckMain --> |No| GameCheck["Check game overlays:<br/>Marble, Arkanoid, Lode, Go, Trivia, Draughts, Chess, Pinball"]
GameCheck --> GameFound{"Any game open?"}
GameFound --> |Yes| ReturnGame["Return 'Jeu · <game>'"]
GameFound --> |No| ReturnArcade["Return 'Arcade'"]
CheckMain --> |Yes| PopupScan["Scan priority list:<br/>Alarm ring, Alarm popup, Voice assistant,<br/>Calendar, Lights, Climate, Plants, TV remote, Console"]
PopupScan --> PopupFound{"Any popup visible?"}
PopupFound --> |Yes| ReturnPopup["Return popup name"]
PopupFound --> |No| PanelRead["Read current_central_panel"]
PanelRead --> PanelType{"Panel type"}
PanelType --> |0| ReturnPlanning["Return 'Accueil · Planning'"]
PanelType --> |1| ReturnRain["Return 'Accueil · Pluie'"]
PanelType --> |2| ReturnWeather["Return 'Accueil · Vigilance météo'"]
PanelType --> |3| ReturnInfo["Return 'Accueil · Info'"]
PanelType --> |4..7| ReturnHAAlert["Return 'Accueil · Alerte HA'"]
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Current Screen Entity (tab5_screen_name)
- Purpose: Expose the exact screen/overlay currently visible to Home Assistant for dashboards and automations.
- Priority rules:
  - Games take precedence when the main page is hidden; each game namespace provides an is_open() check.
  - On the main page, a fixed priority list ensures the highest-layer overlay wins (e.g., alarm ring overlay before other popups).
  - When no overlay is visible, the central panel index determines the dashboard panel label.
- Update cadence: Template updates every 5 seconds to reflect changes without excessive CPU usage.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant ES as "ESPHome"
participant TS as "text_sensor : tab5_screen_name"
participant LV as "LVGL"
participant G as "Globals : current_central_panel"
HA->>ES : Poll text_sensor every 5s
ES->>TS : Evaluate lambda
TS->>LV : Check page_main->is_showing()
alt Main page hidden
TS->>LV : Query game overlays (is_open())
TS-->>HA : "Jeu · <game>" or "Arcade"
else Main page visible
TS->>LV : Scan popup layers in priority order
alt Popup found
TS-->>HA : "Réveil qui sonne", "Réveil", "Assistant vocal", etc.
else No popup
TS->>G : Read current_central_panel
TS-->>HA : "Accueil · Planning/Pluie/Vigilance météo/Info/Alerte HA"
end
end
```

### Central Panel Rotation State Machine
- Context structure: CentralPanelCtx aggregates wrapper objects, activity flags (rain, MF alerts, info, HA alerts), and the current panel index.
- Rotation behavior:
  - advance_central_panel_rotator cycles through panels, skipping inactive ones based on flags.
  - sync_central_panel_visibility hides all wrappers and shows only the active one, resetting to planning if needed.
  - update_central_forecast_page_ui and related helpers refresh titles and content for forecast pages.
- Integration: The central card contains multiple wrappers (alerts, rain, info, HA alerts) plus a page title wrapper used on forecast pages.

```mermaid
classDiagram
class CentralPanelCtx {
+lv_obj_t* planning_wrap
+lv_obj_t* rain_wrap
+lv_obj_t* alert_cont
+lv_obj_t* info_wrap
+lv_obj_t* ha_wrap[4]
+lv_obj_t* page_title_sub
+bool has_rain
+bool has_mf_alerts
+bool has_info
+bool has_ha[4]
+int current_panel
}
class Rotator {
+advance_central_panel_rotator(ctx)
+sync_central_panel_visibility(ctx)
+update_central_forecast_page_ui(forecast_page, wrap, lbl, ctx)
}
Rotator --> CentralPanelCtx : "reads/writes"
```

### Game Overlay Handling
- Each game resides on its own LVGL page marked with skip: true to prevent swipe navigation from interfering with game timers and state.
- The current screen entity checks game-specific is_open() methods to accurately report the active game when the main page is hidden.
- Closing all games via a dedicated script ensures consistent cleanup and restores landscape orientation after portrait games like pinball.

```mermaid
flowchart TD

HideMain --> ReportScreen["tab5_screen_name returns 'Jeu · <game>'"]
CloseGame["Close all games"] --> RestoreMain["Restore main page"]
RestoreMain --> ResetIdle["Reset idle timer via ui_mark_activity()"]
```

### Connection Status Monitoring and Device Availability
- HA API Status: A binary sensor indicates whether the native Home Assistant API connection is available; it also drives UI color changes and console status text.
- WiFi diagnostics: SSID, IP address, and signal strength are exposed as text sensors and sensors, updated at intervals and refreshed when the system console is visible.
- Uptime and core metrics: Internal uptime, free heap, loop time, and core temperature are exposed for diagnostics.
- Health automations: Home Assistant watches for primary instance inactivity, unexpected reboots (uptime decrease), and extended API disconnection to alert operators.

### Diagnostic Information Exposure
- System console layer: Provides real-time diagnostics (uptime, RSSI, core temp, SRAM/PSRAM usage, loop time, WiFi IP/SSID, HA connection status).
- Visibility gating: Diagnostics UI updates are guarded by a check to avoid LVGL calls when the console layer is hidden, reducing unnecessary work.
- Refresh triggers: Opening the console button immediately refreshes status rows; background intervals keep values current.

## Dependency Analysis
- tab5_screen_name depends on:
  - LVGL page state (page_main visibility)
  - Game overlay states (namespace is_open() methods)
  - Popup layer visibility (priority list)
  - Central panel index (current_central_panel global)
- Central panel logic depends on:
  - CentralPanelCtx fields (flags and wrappers)
  - LVGL wrapper visibility and transitions
- Diagnostics depend on:
  - ESPHome platform sensors (wifi_info, internal_temperature, debug, uptime)
  - Binary sensor for HA API status
  - Console layer visibility checks

## Performance Considerations
- Push-only architecture: The screen is updated via pushes; absence of pulls means stale screens do not self-report errors. Health automations act as a safety net.
- Idle management: Popups and forecast pages auto-return after inactivity thresholds defined in UIIdle constants, preventing stuck overlays.
- Diagnostics gating: LVGL updates are skipped when the console layer is hidden to reduce overhead.
- Central panel transitions: Short animation durations and small offsets minimize repaint costs while maintaining responsiveness.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and how to diagnose them:
- Stuck popup or game: Use tab5_screen_name to verify what the device reports; if it shows a popup/game unexpectedly, close all games and return to the main page using the provided controls.
- Unresponsive device: Check HA API Status and WiFi diagnostics; health automations will alert on prolonged disconnections or unexpected reboots.
- Central panel not rotating: Verify flags in CentralPanelCtx (rain, MF alerts, info, HA alerts) and ensure the current panel index aligns with expected content.
- Alert dismissal: Use the alert dismissal scripts to mark alerts as read; the system will refresh the rotator accordingly.

- [tab5-ha-controls.yaml:99-225](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ha-controls.yaml#L99-L225)

## Conclusion
The Tab5 status system combines a robust current screen reporter, a well-defined central panel rotator, comprehensive diagnostics, and Home Assistant health monitoring to provide full visibility into device state. By leveraging tab5_screen_name, central panel context, and diagnostic sensors, you can build dashboards, automate alerts for unresponsive devices, and quickly debug UI state issues.

## Introduction
This document explains the utility entities that provide maintenance and administrative functions for the Tab5 calendar subsystem, with a focus on the calendar reload button (tab5_reload_calendar). It covers:
- Purpose: refresh calendar data when events do not appear immediately after creation or modification in Home Assistant.
- Use cases: newly added meetings, calendar sync delays, stale cache, or missing day details.
- Relationship to boot-time prefetch: how the reload button reuses the same background preloading mechanism used at device boot and HA reconnection.
- Integration points: ESPHome services, Home Assistant scripts, and calendar integrations.
- Performance impact and appropriate usage patterns.
- Automation triggers based on calendar sync status and troubleshooting steps for calendar display issues.

## Project Structure
The calendar reload functionality spans firmware and Home Assistant configuration layers:
- Firmware exposes a template button entity that triggers a script to preload current and next month calendar data.
- The script calls a Home Assistant service which queries multiple calendars and pushes enriched data back to the device.
- The UI layer renders the calendar grid and day detail popups, using cached data and refreshing as needed.

```mermaid

C --> D["Home Assistant service: script.tab5_calendrier_mois<br/>Current month + Next month"]
D --> E["Home Assistant: calendar.get_events<br/>Multiple calendar sources"]
E --> F["Push via esphome.* services<br/>to device UI"]
F --> G["LVGL calendar popup renders<br/>with enriched metadata"]
```

## Core Components
- Calendar reload button (tab5_reload_calendar): A template button exposed by ESPHome that executes the same background preloading logic used at boot and HA reconnection. It is intended for manual refresh when calendar changes are not yet visible.
- Boot-time prefetch (tab5_cal_prefetch_boot): Loads current and next month calendar data into the device cache without opening the calendar popup. It runs on boot and on HA connection recovery to minimize perceived latency.
- Calendar scripts (tab5_calendrier_mois, tab5_calendrier_jour): Home Assistant scripts that query multiple calendar sources, compute per-day codes (workdays, holidays, school vacations, appointments, birthdays), and push results to the device. They also build detailed day lines for the day-detail popup.
- Calendar UI components: LVGL-based calendar popup and day-detail popup that render local grid layout immediately and enrich with Home Assistant data from cache or on-demand requests.

## Architecture Overview
The calendar system uses a push-only model from Home Assistant to the device. The reload button triggers the same background prefetch used at boot, ensuring consistency between manual refresh and automatic preloading.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant Button as "ESPHome Button : tab5_reload_calendar"
participant Script as "Firmware Script : tab5_cal_prefetch_boot"
participant HA as "Home Assistant Scripts"
participant Cal as "Calendar Integrations"
participant Device as "Device UI (LVGL)"
User->>Button : Press "Recharger le calendrier"
Button->>Script : Execute tab5_cal_prefetch_boot
Script->>HA : Call script.tab5_calendrier_mois (current month)
Script->>HA : Call script.tab5_calendrier_mois (next month)
HA->>Cal : calendar.get_events (multiple calendars)
Cal-->>HA : Events (work, holidays, vacations, appointments, birthdays)
HA-->>Device : Push enriched month/day data via esphome services
Device->>Device : Render calendar grid and enrich cells
Note over Device : Cache updated; day taps can show details instantly if available
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Calendar Reload Button (tab5_reload_calendar)
- Purpose: Manually refresh the current and next month calendar data when events added or modified in Home Assistant do not appear immediately on the device.
- Behavior: Executes the same background prefetch script used at boot and HA reconnection, avoiding UI disruption while updating the cache.
- When to use:
  - After adding or editing an appointment in Home Assistant calendars.
  - If the calendar popup shows stale data or missing day details.
  - When calendar sync delays cause events to be absent until the next scheduled refresh cycle.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Press 'Recharger le calendrier'"]) --> Exec["Execute tab5_cal_prefetch_boot"]
Exec --> CurrentMonth["Request current month via script.tab5_calendrier_mois"]
Exec --> NextMonth["Request next month via script.tab5_calendrier_mois"]
CurrentMonth --> Push["Push enriched data to device"]
NextMonth --> Push
Push --> UpdateCache["Update device calendar cache"]
UpdateCache --> End(["Calendar refreshed"])
```

### Boot-Time Prefetch Mechanism (tab5_cal_prefetch_boot)
- Purpose: Preload current and next month calendar data in the background to reduce perceived latency when the user opens the calendar popup.
- Trigger points:
  - On device boot (when SNTP time is valid and HA is connected).
  - On HA connection recovery (status_ha rising edge).
- Behavior:
  - Calls script.tab5_calendrier_mois for current month and next month with a short delay between requests to avoid saturating the device’s TCP socket.
  - Updates the device cache so that subsequent navigation or day taps can render quickly.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Boot as "Boot / HA Reconnect"
participant FW as "Firmware : tab5_cal_prefetch_boot"
participant HA as "Home Assistant : script.tab5_calendrier_mois"
participant Cal as "Calendar Sources"
participant Dev as "Device Cache"
Boot->>FW : Trigger prefetch
FW->>HA : Request current month
HA->>Cal : calendar.get_events (bounded window)
Cal-->>HA : Events
HA-->>Dev : Push month payload (codes, hours, details)
FW->>HA : Request next month (delayed)
HA->>Cal : calendar.get_events
Cal-->>HA : Events
HA-->>Dev : Push next month payload
```

### Calendar Scripts and Data Enrichment
- Month script (tab5_calendrier_mois):
  - Queries multiple calendar sources (work calendar, French holidays, family calendar, birthdays).
  - Computes per-day bitmask codes indicating workdays, holidays, school vacations, appointments, and birthdays.
  - Builds work hours strings for each day and pushes them to the device.
  - Uses bounded date windows to avoid unnecessary past events and ensures correct behavior even for fully past months.
- Day script (tab5_calendrier_jour):
  - Builds detailed lines for the selected day (holidays named, school vacations, work hours, appointments, birthdays, civil holidays).
  - Pushes up to six lines to the day-detail popup.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Input["script.tab5_calendrier_mois(date range)"] --> Query["calendar.get_events (multiple calendars)"]
Query --> Compute["Compute per-day codes and work hours"]
Compute --> PushMonth["Push month payload to device"]
InputDay["script.tab5_calendrier_jour(date)"] --> QueryDay["calendar.get_events (single day)"]
QueryDay --> BuildLines["Build detail lines (max 6)"]
BuildLines --> PushDay["Push day payload to device"]
```

### UI Rendering and Cache Behavior
- Calendar popup:
  - Renders local grid immediately (numbers, alignment, weekends, “today”).
  - Enriches cells with Home Assistant data from cache; if absent or stale (>10 minutes), triggers a silent refresh.
  - Day taps open a detail popup; if embedded details exist in cache, rendering is instant; otherwise, it requests day details from Home Assistant.
- Cache eviction:
  - Keeps only nearby months (previous, current, next) to balance memory and responsiveness.

```mermaid

+render_month()
+open_day_detail(date)
+use_cache_or_refresh()
}
class Cache {
+get_month(year, month)
+set_month(year, month, payload)
+evict_distant(year, month)
}
class Scripts {
+tab5_calendrier_mois(year, month)
+tab5_calendrier_jour(date)
}
CalendarPopup --> Cache : "reads/writes"
CalendarPopup --> Scripts : "requests enrichment"
```

## Performance Considerations
- Background prefetch minimizes perceived latency by loading current and next month data ahead of user interaction.
- Short delays between requests prevent saturating the device’s TCP socket during push operations.
- Stale-while-revalidate caching allows immediate rendering with background refresh when data is older than a threshold.
- Using the reload button manually should be reserved for cases where automatic mechanisms have not yet propagated changes (e.g., newly created events or sync delays).

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common symptoms and resolutions related to calendar display issues:
- Events not appearing immediately:
  - Cause: Calendar sync delays or stale cache.
  - Resolution: Press the “Recharger le calendrier” button to trigger background prefetch and update the device cache.
- Weather/planning/climate data missing despite online status:
  - Cause: Push automations gated behind a shared helper flag that may be off.
  - Resolution: Ensure the helper flag is on and the guard automation is enabled; manually trigger the push once.
- Calendar push breaking rest of automation:
  - Cause: Passing raw datetime objects to calendar.get_events causes validation failures.
  - Resolution: Format datetimes explicitly and add continue_on_error guards to individual actions.
- Touch not working but touchscreen detects presses:
  - Cause: Home Assistant rejecting service calls due to integration options.
  - Resolution: Enable “Allow service calls” in the ESPHome integration options for the device.

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:23-29](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L23-L29)
- [troubleshooting.md:53-59](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L53-L59)
- [troubleshooting.md:43-49](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L43-L49)

## Conclusion
The calendar reload button (tab5_reload_calendar) provides a reliable maintenance tool for refreshing calendar data when automatic mechanisms have not yet propagated changes. It leverages the same background prefetch used at boot and HA reconnection, ensuring consistent behavior and minimal performance impact. Proper usage involves triggering the reload after creating or modifying events, monitoring calendar sync status through automations, and following troubleshooting steps when display issues arise.

## Introduction
This document explains the embedded arcade games collection built as proof-of-concept prototypes on an ESP32-P4 device. It covers the shared game module architecture, input handling (touch and IMU), per-game characteristics, persistence via NVS, and performance strategies to sustain smooth gameplay. The eight consoles are:
- Fil d’Or (marble roguelite with tilt controls)
- Arkanoid (breakout clone with power-ups)
- Neon Apron (portrait-mode pinball)
- Coureur d’Or (Lode Runner)
- Go Tab (strategy game with AI)
- Trial Poursuite (trivia quiz)
- Dames Tab (draughts with AI)
- Roi Noir (FIDE chess with 5 AI levels)

All games run as standalone LVGL pages with skip:true, empty YAML containers, C++-built content, lv_timer lifecycle management, and NVS persistence for state. They operate fully offline with zero Home Assistant dependency during gameplay.

## Project Structure
The firmware is organized into modular ESPHome packages and C++ modules. The dashboard lives on a single LVGL page; the nine gaming pages (arcade selector plus one per console) are declared separately and skipped from swipe navigation. Each game has:
- A dedicated LVGL page entry with skip:true
- A minimal YAML component file declaring only container widgets
- A C++ namespace implementing open/close/is_open/on_imu and persistence
- An opening script that injects LVGL pointers and fonts

## Core Components
- Shared game interface pattern: each game exposes open(ui), close(), is_open(), on_imu(ax, ay, az), calibrate()/calibrate_flat(), persist_save(), persist_load().
- UI struct injection: scripts build a UI struct with LVGL object pointers and font references, then call the game’s open().
- lv_timer lifecycle: created when a game opens, destroyed when closed; no CPU cost when idle.
- NVS persistence: each game defines a save struct with a magic constant; layout changes require bumping the magic to avoid reading stale data.
- Adaptive IMU polling: default 10 Hz at rest; increases to ~30 Hz when tilt-controlled games are active.

Key files defining these patterns:
- Open scripts centralize UI pointer injection and invocation
- IMU routing calls each game’s on_imu handler based on active consumers
- Page definitions ensure games are isolated and not reachable by swipe

## Architecture Overview
The arcade subsystem follows a strict separation between UI definition (minimal YAML) and logic (C++). Navigation uses lvgl.page.show or lv_scr_load. The adaptive IMU system routes acceleration samples to active games. Persistence is local and robust via NVS with magic validation.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant LVGL as "LVGL Pages"
participant Scripts as "Open Scripts"
participant Game as "Game Namespace"
participant IMU as "BMI270"
participant NVS as "NVS Storage"
User->>LVGL : Tap game card
LVGL->>Scripts : Execute tab5_<game>_open
Scripts->>Game : Build UI struct and call open(ui)
Game->>Game : Create lv_timer, preallocate LVGL pool
Note over Game : Game loop runs until close()
IMU-->>Game : on_imu(ax, ay, az)
Game->>Game : Update input/filtering
Game->>NVS : persist_save() at key moments
User->>Game : Close game
Game->>Game : Destroy lv_timer, save state
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Shared Game Module Architecture
Each game implements a consistent API:
- open(ui): constructs UI once, starts lv_timer
- close(): stops timer, saves state, hides overlay
- is_open(): used for IMU routing and closing all games
- on_imu(...): lightweight filtering and state update
- calibrate()/calibrate_flat(): sets flat reference offsets
- persist_save()/persist_load(): NVS read/write with magic validation

### Input Handling Mechanisms
- Touch controls: Each game handles taps, holds, and gestures through LVGL events injected via scripts and YAML containers.
- Tilt sensing via BMI270 IMU: Acceleration samples are routed to active games. For marble, arkanoid, lode, go, trivia, and pinball (nudge), this provides responsive control.
- Adaptive polling: Default 10 Hz at rest; increases to ~30 Hz when tilt-controlled games are open. This balances responsiveness and power efficiency.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start([IMU Sample]) --> CheckActive{"Any tilt game open?"}
CheckActive --> |Yes| FastPoll["Set interval 33ms<br/>Restart poller"]
CheckActive --> |No| SlowPoll["Set interval 100ms<br/>Restart poller"]
FastPoll --> Route["Route to Marble/Arkanoid/Lode/Go/Trivia/Pinball on_imu"]
SlowPoll --> Route
Route --> Filter["Lightweight filtering per game"]
Filter --> End([Update game state])
```

## Performance Considerations
- 60 FPS target on ESP32-P4 achieved through:
  - Pre-allocated LVGL pools with zero runtime allocation
  - lv_timer lifecycle management (create on open, destroy on close)
  - Adaptive IMU polling (10 Hz vs 30 Hz)
  - Minimal redraws (only changed values updated)
  - Efficient collision and physics with sub-stepping
- Memory management:
  - Static buffers for complex games (chess move history, Zobrist tables)
  - Local palettes to avoid global conflicts
  - NVS persistence with magic validation to prevent corruption
- Experimental nature:
  - AI-generated code prototypes focused on functionality over polish
  - Conservative design choices prioritize stability and performance

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and solutions:
- Screen orientation problems in pinball: Ensure rotation switching works correctly and LVGL component pointer is properly injected
- IMU not responding: Check adaptive polling intervals and verify game is marked as open
- NVS corruption: Magic validation will reset to defaults if format mismatch detected
- Game not appearing: Verify page definition with skip:true and proper include in scripts
- Performance drops: Monitor lv_timer usage and ensure proper cleanup on game close

## Conclusion
The arcade games collection demonstrates a robust, modular approach to embedded game development on resource-constrained hardware. The shared architecture enables rapid prototyping while maintaining performance and reliability. Each game leverages local persistence, efficient input handling, and careful memory management to deliver engaging experiences on the ESP32-P4 platform. The experimental nature of the AI-generated code provides a foundation for future enhancements and refinements.

## Introduction
Arkanoid is a breakout-style arcade game implemented for the Tab5 platform using LVGL and ESPHome. It features progressive difficulty across eight levels, a robust ball physics engine with sub-stepping to prevent tunneling, paddle controls via IMU tilt and/or touch buttons, brick destruction with multiple brick types, and a power-up system that includes expand/shrink paddle, slow/fast ball, multi-ball, glue (launch on tap), and extra life. The game persists high scores and settings in NVS, provides a compact HUD, and uses a retro Atari-inspired color palette.

## Project Structure
The Arkanoid implementation is split across:
- A C++ module implementing game logic, physics, UI construction, and persistence
- A minimal YAML page declaring four containers (root, field, HUD, panel)
- Integration points for IMU input, scripts to open/close the game, and style tokens

```mermaid
graph TB
A["LVGL Page<br/>arkanoid_game.yaml"] --> B["Game UI Containers<br/>field / hud / panel"]
B --> C["C++ Game Module<br/>arkanoid_game.cpp/.h"]
D["IMU Input<br/>tab5-imu.yaml"] --> C
E["Scripts & Navigation<br/>tab5-scripts.yaml"] --> C
F["Style Tokens<br/>tab5-styles.yaml"] --> C
```

## Core Components
- Game state machine and screens: hub, settings, playing, paused, level clear, game over, high scores
- Physics loop at ~30 Hz with sub-steps for collision stability
- Paddle control via IMU tilt and/or touch buttons
- Ball management with glued launch, multi-ball support, speed normalization
- Brick grid with multiple types and per-level layouts
- Power-up spawning, falling, and application
- HUD updates with caching to minimize redraws
- NVS persistence for top scores and user settings

## Architecture Overview
The game runs as a full-screen LVGL page. The YAML declares only four containers; all gameplay objects are created once in C++ and reused by moving/hiding them each frame. An LVGL timer drives the tick loop while the game is open. IMU data flows into the game via a callback. Settings and scores persist in NVS.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant Scripts as "tab5-scripts.yaml"
participant LVGL as "LVGL Timer"
participant Game as "Arkanoid : : tick_cb()"
participant IMU as "tab5-imu.yaml"
participant NVS as "NVS Persistence"
User->>Scripts : Open Arkanoid
Scripts->>Game : open(ui)
Game->>LVGL : lv_timer_create(tick_cb, 33ms)
LVGL->>Game : tick_cb() every ~33ms
IMU->>Game : on_imu(ax, ay, az)
Game->>Game : update paddle/balls/bricks/power-ups
Game->>NVS : persist_save() on key moments
Game-->>LVGL : move LVGL objects (no allocations)
```
