## Introduction
This document explains the calendar data integration between the Tab5 device and Home Assistant. It focuses on a push-based architecture where Home Assistant computes calendar information and pushes it to the device via ESPHome API services. The system combines work days, public holidays, school vacation periods, appointments, and birthdays into compact payloads using a bitmask encoding. On the Home Assistant side, template scripts compute these payloads from multiple calendar sources and send them to the device. On the device side, ESPHome services store and render the data with an efficient caching strategy and pre-fetch mechanism for fast navigation and resilience during boot or reconnection scenarios. Timezone handling, locale-specific holiday detection, and visual mapping of calendar entity types are also covered.

## Project Structure
The calendar integration spans two sides:
- Home Assistant configuration defines scripts that query calendars, compute day codes and details, and call ESPHome services to push updates.
- Tab5 firmware exposes ESPHome API services that receive payloads, cache month data, and update the UI. A popup UI renders the calendar grid and day detail sub-popup.

```mermaid
graph TB
HA["Home Assistant<br/>scripts.tab5_calendrier_mois / script.tab5_calendrier_jour"] --> |ESPHome service calls| ESP["ESPHome API<br/>tab5_maj_calendrier_mois / tab5_maj_calendrier_jour"]
ESP --> |Store + Render| FW["Firmware Cache & UI<br/>cal_store_month_data / cal_render_*"]
FW --> |LVGL widgets| UI["Calendar Popup UI<br/>calendar_popup.yaml"]
FW --> |SNTP time| TZ["Local date/time<br/>timezone-safe"]
```

## Core Components
- Home Assistant scripts:
  - script.tab5_calendrier_mois: Computes per-day bitmask (work, holiday, school vacation, appointment, birthday), work hours, and optional day details; pushes via ESPHome service.
  - script.tab5_calendrier_jour: Builds detailed lines for a selected day and pushes via ESPHome service.
- ESPHome API services:
  - esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_mois: Stores month payload in cache and triggers rendering if the current month is visible.
  - esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_jour: Renders day detail lines into the sub-popup.
- Firmware cache and rendering:
  - Month cache with TTL and eviction policy (max 3 months around view).
  - Local rendering of calendar grid using SNTP-derived local dates.
  - Day detail rendering from embedded details or fallback to day script response.

## Architecture Overview
The system uses a push-only model:
- When the calendar popup opens or navigates, the device requests month data from Home Assistant.
- Home Assistant queries multiple calendar entities, merges events, applies timezone-aware logic, and builds compact payloads.
- The device stores payloads in a small cache and renders immediately; stale data is refreshed silently after a TTL threshold.
- Pre-fetching adjacent months improves navigation responsiveness.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant UI as "Calendar Popup UI"
participant FW as "Firmware Scripts"
participant ESP as "ESPHome API Services"
participant HA as "Home Assistant Scripts"
participant Cal as "Calendar Entities"
User->>UI : Open calendar
UI->>FW : tab5_calendar_open()
FW->>FW : cal_cache_evict_distant(view_year, view_month)
FW->>FW : cal_render_month(...)
alt Month missing or stale
FW->>HA : script.tab5_calendrier_mois(year, month)
HA->>Cal : get_events(start,end)
Cal-->>HA : events
HA->>HA : build bitmask + heures + details
HA->>ESP : tab5_maj_calendrier_mois(codes,heures,details)
ESP->>FW : cal_store_month_data(...)
FW->>FW : cal_render_month(...)
end
FW->>FW : Pre-fetch M-1 and M+1 if absent
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Bitmask Encoding System
Each day’s status is encoded into a two-character hex value representing a 5-bit mask:
- Bit 1: Work day
- Bit 2: Public holiday
- Bit 4: School vacation period (Zone A)
- Bit 8: Appointment
- Bit 16: Birthday

These bits are computed per day by scanning events from multiple calendar sources and applying filters such as “future-or-today” and title matching for work events. The resulting string is 62 hex characters (two per day up to 31 days).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Per-day loop"]) --> CheckVac["Check school vacation intervals"]
CheckVac --> FutureOrToday{"Future or today?"}
FutureOrToday --> |No| SetBits["Set bits based on matches"]
FutureOrToday --> |Yes| ScanWork["Scan work events"]
ScanWork --> MarkWork{"'Travail' in summary?"}
MarkWork --> |Yes| SetWork["Set work bit"]
MarkWork --> |No| MarkRDV["Set appointment bit"]
ScanWork --> ScanHolidays["Scan holiday events"]
ScanHolidays --> MatchHoliday{"Title in known holidays?"}
MatchHoliday --> |Yes| SetHoliday["Set holiday bit"]
ScanHolidays --> ScanFamily["Scan family events"]
ScanFamily --> MarkFamilyRDV["Set appointment bit"]
ScanFamily --> ScanBirthdays["Scan birthday events"]
ScanBirthdays --> MarkBirthday["Set birthday bit"]
SetWork --> SetBits
MarkRDV --> SetBits
SetHoliday --> SetBits
MarkFamilyRDV --> SetBits
MarkBirthday --> SetBits
SetBits --> Encode["Encode bits to hex pair"]
Encode --> NextDay["Next day"]
NextDay --> End(["Month codes string"])
```

### Home Assistant Calendar Processing
- Data sources:
  - Work calendar with events labeled “Travail*” and timestamped entries.
  - French holidays calendar containing both official holidays and civil celebrations; only whitelisted titles are treated as holidays.
  - Family and birthday calendars for appointments and birthdays.
- Query window:
  - For month requests, events are fetched from the first of the month to the first of the next month. If the current month is already past, the start is clamped to today to avoid empty windows and unnecessary processing.
- Output:
  - codes: bitmask string for each day.
  - heures: work hours per day in “HH:MM-HH:MM” format separated by pipes.
  - details: optional per-day detail lines embedded in the month payload to avoid round-trips when tapping a day.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:55-131](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L55-L131)
- [tab5_calendar.yaml:132-221](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/HomeAssistant_Config/packages/tab5_calendar.yaml#L132-L221)

### ESPHome Service Handlers
- tab5_maj_calendrier_mois:
  - Receives year, month, codes, heures, and details.
  - Stores month data in the firmware cache and triggers rendering only if the calendar popup is currently showing the same month.
- tab5_maj_calendrier_jour:
  - Receives date and payload lines.
  - Renders up to six detail lines into the day sub-popup, ignoring responses if the displayed date has changed due to rapid navigation.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant FW as "Firmware"
participant ESP as "ESPHome API"
participant UI as "Calendar UI"
FW->>ESP : tab5_maj_calendrier_mois(year,month,codes,heures,details)
ESP->>FW : cal_store_month_data(...)
alt Visible month matches
ESP->>FW : script.execute tab5_cal_render
FW->>UI : Update grid and dots/colors
else Not visible
ESP-->>FW : No-op render
end
FW->>ESP : tab5_maj_calendrier_jour(date,payload)
ESP->>FW : cal_render_day_detail(payload,...)
FW->>UI : Populate detail lines
```

### Caching Strategy and Eviction Policies
- Cache structure:
  - In-memory map keyed by year-month combination.
  - Each entry stores codes, heures, details, a flag indicating whether details were provided, and a timestamp of storage.
- TTL and staleness:
  - A month is considered stale if stored more than a configurable TTL ago (default 10 minutes). Stale data can still be displayed while a silent refresh is triggered.
- Eviction:
  - Only keep months within one month of the current view (M-1, M, M+1). This limits memory usage and ensures recent data remains available.
- Accessors:
  - Functions to check if a month needs fetching, if it is stale, and to retrieve embedded day details for quick taps.

```mermaid
classDiagram
class CalMonthData {
+string codes
+string heures
+string details
+bool has_details
+uint32_t stored_at
}
class CalendarCache {
+map<int, CalMonthData> s_cal_month_cache
+cal_cache_clear()
+cal_month_needs_fetch(year, month) bool
+cal_month_is_stale(year, month, ttl_ms) bool
+cal_cache_evict_distant(year, month)
+cal_store_month_data(annee, mois, codes, heures, details)
+cal_cached_day_detail(year, month, day) string
}
CalendarCache --> CalMonthData : "stores"
```

### Pre-Fetch Mechanism for Boot and Reconnection
- On opening the calendar popup:
  - Clear distant cached months to free space.
  - Render the current month immediately from cache if available.
  - If missing or stale, request month data from Home Assistant.
  - Silently pre-fetch adjacent months (previous and next) if not present in cache.
- Benefits:
  - Instant display even if data is slightly outdated.
  - Smooth navigation without waiting for network responses.
  - Resilience during boot or reconnection by warming the cache proactively.

**Section sources**
- [tab5_scripts.yaml:657-786](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L657-L786)
- [calendar_popup.yaml:1-229](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/calendar_popup.yaml#L1-L229)

### Error Handling for Network Failures and Data Inconsistencies
- Network failures:
  - ESPHome API services use continue_on_error patterns in Home Assistant scripts to prevent automation halts when calendar queries fail.
  - Device-side services guard against null UI pointers and ignore out-of-date day detail responses during rapid navigation.
- Data inconsistencies:
  - Payloads are validated (e.g., length checks for bulk payloads) to avoid memory issues.
  - Fallback behavior: if embedded details are absent or outdated, tapping a day falls back to requesting day details via the day script.
- Reboot protection:
  - A reboot timeout prevents zombie states where the device remains online but unresponsive due to lost API connections.

### Timezone Handling and Locale-Specific Holiday Detection
- Timezone safety:
  - Local dates are derived from SNTP time and normalized to avoid DST edge cases near midnight. This ensures consistent day boundaries across systems.
- Locale-specific holidays:
  - Holidays are filtered by a whitelist of known French holiday titles to avoid misclassifying non-holiday celebrations.
  - School vacation periods are defined statically for Zone A (Bordeaux/Landes) and checked against local dates.

### Relationship Between Calendar Entity Types and Visual Representations
- Work days:
  - Highlighted background and work hours shown under the day number.
- Public holidays:
  - Distinct color applied to the day cell.
- School vacations:
  - Background tint indicates vacation periods.
- Appointments:
  - Gold dot indicator appears on cells with appointments.
- Birthdays:
  - Pink dot indicator appears on cells with birthdays.
- Day detail sub-popup:
  - Up to six lines with typed icons and sanitized text describe holidays, vacations, work hours, appointments, birthdays, and civil celebrations.

## Dependency Analysis
- Home Assistant scripts depend on calendar entities and produce payloads consumed by ESPHome services.
- ESPHome services depend on firmware functions to store and render data.
- UI components depend on firmware rendering functions to update LVGL widgets.
- Time synchronization depends on SNTP to ensure correct local dates.

## Performance Considerations
- Compact payloads:
  - Bitmask encoding reduces bandwidth and simplifies parsing on the device.
- Efficient caching:
  - Small cache size (max three months) minimizes memory usage while keeping frequently accessed data ready.
- Stale-while-revalidate:
  - Immediate display of cached data improves perceived performance; background refresh keeps data fresh.
- Pre-fetching:
  - Proactive loading of adjacent months reduces latency during navigation.
- Safe date arithmetic:
  - Normalized local dates avoid off-by-one errors around DST transitions.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Device reboots while Home Assistant is unreachable:
  - Caused by ESPHome API reboot timeout; adjust or monitor the setting to avoid frequent cycles during HA startup delays.
- Missing weather/planning/climate updates:
  - Ensure push automations are enabled and not blocked by shared flags; verify the guard automation runs at HA boot.
- Calendar popup shows stale data:
  - Check TTL thresholds and network connectivity; confirm pre-fetch triggers and cache eviction behavior.
- Day detail not updating:
  - Verify embedded details presence and fallback to day script; ensure the displayed date matches the received payload date.

**Section sources**
- [troubleshooting.md:83-145](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md#L83-L145)
- [tab5_api_logic.yaml:13-37](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L13-L37)

## Conclusion
The Tab5–Home Assistant calendar integration leverages a push-based architecture with compact bitmask payloads, robust caching, and proactive pre-fetching to deliver responsive and reliable calendar visualization. Home Assistant handles complex event merging and locale-specific logic, while the device focuses on efficient storage and rendering. Timezone safety and careful error handling ensure stability across network conditions and system changes. This design balances performance, maintainability, and user experience for real-time calendar updates on the Tab5 device.

## Introduction
This document explains the day detail popup that appears when users tap a calendar cell on the monthly calendar view. It covers the nested modal architecture (day detail overlaying the main calendar popup), the six-line detail display with icon-text pairs, dynamic content loading from Home Assistant via specific service calls, and the status message system for loading states and connection issues. It also documents event handling for closing the popup, how calendar entities map to displayed information, and how template logic in Home Assistant derives additional calendar data.

## Project Structure
The day detail popup is implemented as a sub-popup layered over the main calendar popup:
- The main calendar popup defines the month grid and includes a hidden sub-popup container for day details.
- Each calendar cell triggers a script to open the day detail popup and load data.
- Home Assistant scripts compute calendar data and push updates back to the device through ESPHome services.

```mermaid

D --> E["Tap Handler<br/>tab5_scripts tab5_cal_day_tap"]
E --> F["HA Script: Month Data<br/>tab5_calendar.yaml tab5_calendrier_mois"]
E --> G["HA Script: Day Data<br/>tab5_calendar.yaml tab5_calendrier_jour"]

G --> I["ESPHome Service: Day Update<br/>tab5_api_logic tab5_maj_calendrier_jour"]

```

## Core Components
- Calendar cells: Each cell contains labels for the day number, work hours, and indicator dots for appointments and birthdays. Tapping a cell executes a script to open the day detail popup.
- Day detail sub-popup: A 780×540 overlay with its own scrim at reduced opacity, a header, a central status label, and six icon-text rows for detailed information.
- Scrim overlays: The main calendar uses an 85% opaque scrim; the day detail sub-popup stacks a 60% opaque scrim on top.
- Home Assistant scripts: Compute monthly codes/hours and daily detail lines from multiple calendar sources and push them back via ESPHome services.
- ESPHome API services: Receive payloads and update UI elements or trigger rendering functions in C++.
- C++ renderers: Map payload types to icons/colors and manage status messages and line rendering.

## Architecture Overview
The day detail popup follows a nested modal pattern:
- User taps a calendar cell → script opens the day detail sub-popup.
- If cached day details exist, they are rendered instantly; otherwise, a “Loading…” status is shown while Home Assistant computes the day’s details.
- Home Assistant queries multiple calendars and templates to build a list of up to six detail lines, then pushes them back to the device.
- The device maps each line type to an icon and color, displays them, and updates the status to reflect availability or offline state.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant U as "User"
participant Cell as "Calendar Cell"
participant Script as "tab5_cal_day_tap"
participant HA as "HA Scripts"
participant Svc as "ESPHome Services"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
U->>Cell : Tap
Cell->>Script : Execute with cell index
Script->>UI : Open cal_day_popup (780x540)<br/>Set status "Loading..."
Script->>HA : Call tab5_calendrier_jour(date)
HA-->>Svc : Push tab5_maj_calendrier_jour(payload)
Svc->>UI : Render 6 icon-text lines<br/>Update status based on payload
Note over UI : If no payload or HA offline,<br/>status shows "Nothing planned" or "HA offline"
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Nested Modal Architecture
- Main calendar popup: Full-screen modal with 85% scrim opacity and a month grid.
- Day detail sub-popup: 780×540 card layered on top with its own 60% scrim. Both use the shared scrim component but with different opacities to visually indicate nesting.
- Close behavior: Closing the day detail popup returns focus to the calendar popup; closing the calendar popup dismisses both.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Open Calendar"]) --> Grid["Render Month Grid"]
Grid --> Tap{"Tap Cell?"}
Tap -- Yes --> OpenDetail["Open Day Detail Popup<br/>780x540"]
OpenDetail --> Scrim60["Apply 60% Scrim Overlay"]
Scrim60 --> LoadStatus["Show Status Label"]
LoadStatus --> Fetch{"Cached Details?"}
Fetch -- Yes --> RenderInstant["Render Icon-Text Lines Instantly"]
Fetch -- No --> HAQuery["Call HA Script for Day Details"]
HAQuery --> Update["Receive Payload via Service"]
Update --> RenderLines["Map Types to Icons/Colors<br/>Populate 6 Rows"]
RenderLines --> Done(["Close Popup"])
Tap -- No --> End(["Exit"])
```

### Six-Line Detail Display Format
- Layout: Six rows, each with an icon label and a text label aligned left within the 780×540 card.
- Content: Up to six lines derived from Home Assistant, including holidays, school vacations, work hours, appointments, birthdays, and civil holidays.
- Mapping: Each line type maps to a specific MDI icon and color in C++, ensuring consistent visual cues across the UI.

### Dynamic Content Loading from Home Assistant
- Monthly enrichment: When opening or navigating months, the device requests monthly data via a script that computes bitmask flags per day (work, holiday, school vacation, appointment, birthday) and work hours.
- Daily detail: On tapping a cell, the device requests day-specific details. If cached details exist, they are rendered instantly; otherwise, a loading status is shown while HA computes the result.
- Payload contract:
  - Monthly: codes (hex bitmask per day), heures (work hours per day), details (optional embedded day details).
  - Daily: payload string of up to six lines formatted as type|text pairs separated by semicolons.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Dev as "Device"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant Svc as "ESPHome Services"
participant UI as "LVGL UI"
Dev->>HA : script.tab5_calendrier_mois(year, month)
HA-->>Svc : esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_mois(codes, heures, details)
Svc->>UI : Store month data & re-render if visible
Dev->>HA : script.tab5_calendrier_jour(date)
HA-->>Svc : esphome.tab5_ha_hmi_tab5_maj_calendrier_jour(date, payload)
Svc->>UI : Render day detail lines & update status
```

### Status Message System
- States:
  - “Loading...” shown immediately upon opening the day detail popup when details are not cached.
  - “Nothing planned” when the payload contains no relevant lines for the selected date.
  - “HA offline” when Home Assistant is unreachable or fails to respond.
- Implementation: The status label is updated by the day detail renderer based on payload presence and connection state.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Open["Open Day Detail"] --> CheckCache{"Cached Details?"}
CheckCache -- Yes --> ShowDetails["Render Lines"]
CheckCache -- No --> ShowLoading["Show 'Loading...'"]
ShowLoading --> QueryHA["Query HA for Day Details"]
QueryHA --> Response{"Response Received?"}
Response -- Yes --> UpdateStatus["Update Status Based on Payload"]
Response -- No --> Offline["Show 'HA offline'"]
UpdateStatus --> Done["Display Lines or 'Nothing planned'"]
Offline --> Done
```

### Event Handling for Closing the Popup
- Scrim close: Tapping the scrim closes the current popup. For the day detail sub-popup, it only closes the sub-popup; for the main calendar popup, it closes both the calendar and any open day detail.
- Header close: The header includes a close button bound to the same close lambda for consistent behavior.

**Section sources**
- [modal_scrim.yaml:1-17](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/modal_scrim.yaml#L1-L17)
- [calendar_popup.yaml:190-212](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/calendar_popup.yaml#L190-L212)

### Relationship Between Calendar Entities and Displayed Information
- Work hours: Derived from events labeled “Travail” in the primary calendar; displayed as time ranges in the month grid and detailed in the day popup.
- Holidays: Identified from a dedicated holidays calendar using a whitelist of known French holidays; marked in the month grid and shown as a holiday line in the day popup.
- School vacations: Static table for Zone A (Bordeaux) used to mark vacation periods; indicated in the month grid and shown as a vacation line in the day popup.
- Appointments: Events from family and other calendars appear as appointment lines in the day popup and dot indicators in the month grid.
- Birthdays: Events from a dedicated birthdays calendar produce birthday lines and a pink dot indicator in the month grid.

### Template Sensor Configurations for Additional Calendar Data
- Monthly bitmask and hours: Templates aggregate events from multiple calendars to compute per-day flags and work hour ranges.
- Daily detail lines: Templates assemble up to six lines categorized by type (holiday, vacation, work, appointment, birthday, civil holiday), sanitizing special characters to fit the payload contract.
- Whitelists and static tables: Known holidays and school vacation intervals are defined statically to ensure accurate classification without relying solely on calendar titles.

## Dependency Analysis
- UI components depend on LVGL widgets and styles defined elsewhere; the day detail popup relies on shared modal header and scrim components.
- Scripts in Home Assistant depend on multiple calendar entities and static tables to derive calendar data.
- ESPHome services bridge HA outputs to C++ renderers, which update LVGL objects directly.

## Performance Considerations
- Cached monthly data reduces network calls; day details are rendered instantly if available in cache.
- Stale-while-revalidate strategy ensures immediate display even if data is slightly outdated, with background refresh.
- Eviction policy limits cached months to three, balancing memory usage and responsiveness.
- Payload sanitization avoids excessive string processing on the device.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- “Loading...” persists: Verify HA script execution and service delivery; check network connectivity and HA logs for errors.
- “Nothing planned”: Confirm calendar entries and template whitelists; ensure events match expected categories and dates.
- “HA offline”: Check ESPHome API connection and HA server status; review reboot timeout and connection recovery settings.
- Incorrect indicators: Validate bitmask computation and work hour extraction; verify calendar entity names and event summaries.

## Conclusion
The day detail popup provides a clear, layered modal experience with robust dynamic content loading from Home Assistant. Its design balances immediate feedback with reliable data retrieval, offering a comprehensive view of work hours, holidays, appointments, and birthdays. The integration between UI components, scripts, services, and C++ renderers ensures a responsive and informative user experience.

## Introduction
This document explains the monthly calendar grid display system used on the 1280×720 touch screen. It covers:
- The 7×6 grid layout with Monday-first week ordering
- Local date calculation using SNTP time synchronization
- The cal_render_month() function that computes month boundaries and day positioning without requiring Home Assistant connectivity
- Grid cell rendering logic, weekend highlighting, current-day indicators, and navigation controls (previous/next month buttons and Today button)
- Visual styling for work days, holidays, school vacations, appointments, and birthdays
- Performance optimizations including pre-fetching adjacent months and a stale-while-revalidate cache with a 10-minute TTL
- Modal popup architecture integration and responsive design considerations for the 1280×720 display

## Project Structure
The calendar UI is composed of:
- A modal popup defining the 7×6 grid, header navigation, and legend
- Reusable day-cell template instantiated 42 times
- C++ rendering logic that computes dates, highlights weekends/today/holidays, and applies semantic colors
- Scripts that drive navigation, rendering, caching, and background pre-fetching
- Shared modal chrome and scrim components for consistent popups

```mermaid
F --> G["tab5-styles.yaml<br/>color tokens"]
```

## Core Components
- Calendar popup container: defines the modal card, title bar, navigation buttons, weekday headers, and the 7×6 grid of 42 cells.
- Day cell template: reusable cell with number label, optional work-hours subtitle, appointment/birthday dots, and tap handler to open day detail.

## Architecture Overview
The calendar uses a hybrid approach:
- Local computation: cal_render_month() calculates month boundaries, first column offset (Monday-first), and today/past/weekend status purely from local SNTP time. No Home Assistant connection is required to draw a usable grid.
- Enrichment via Home Assistant: when available, HA provides per-day codes and work hours; these are stored in a small in-memory cache and applied during rendering.
- Stale-while-revalidate: if cached data is older than 10 minutes, the UI still shows immediately while a silent refresh is triggered in the background.
- Pre-fetching: adjacent months M−1 and M+1 are fetched in the background to make navigation instant.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant UI as "calendar_popup.yaml"
participant Scripts as "tab5-scripts.yaml"
participant Render as "tab5_custom.cpp"
participant Cache as "In-memory cache"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
User->>UI : Open calendar
UI->>Scripts : Execute tab5_calendar_open
Scripts->>Render : cal_render_month(view_year, view_month, today...)
Render->>Cache : Read CalMonthData (codes/heures/details)
alt Cache missing or stale (>10 min)
Scripts->>HA : script.tab5_calendrier_mois (current month)
HA-->>Scripts : payload
Scripts->>Cache : Store month data + timestamp
end
Scripts->>Scripts : If M-1 missing -> fetch in background
Scripts->>Scripts : If M+1 missing -> fetch in background
Render-->>UI : Update 42 cells (numbers, colors, dots)
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### 7×6 Grid Layout and Monday-First Ordering
- The popup declares 42 day cells arranged in 6 rows and 7 columns. Each cell is positioned at fixed x/y coordinates to form a responsive grid within the modal card.
- Weekday headers are labeled Monday through Sunday, establishing a Monday-first week order.
- The first column offset is computed locally by a weekday algorithm returning 0=Monday…6=Sunday, ensuring correct alignment regardless of locale or timezone.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Start render"]) --> FirstCol["Compute first_col = weekday(1st of month)<br/>0=Mon ... 6=Sun"]
FirstCol --> DaysInMonth["ndays = days_in_month(year, month)"]
DaysInMonth --> LoopCells{"For i in 0..41"}
LoopCells --> |Yes| DayCalc["day = i - first_col + 1"]
DayCalc --> InMonth{"1 <= day <= ndays?"}
InMonth --> |No| ClearCell["Clear number/sub/dots,<br/>transparent bg/border"]
InMonth --> |Yes| ApplyStyles["Apply number color,<br/>work hours, dots, bg/border"]
ClearCell --> Next["Next cell"]
ApplyStyles --> Next
Next --> |Loop| LoopCells
LoopCells --> |No| End(["End render"])
```

### Local Date Calculation Using SNTP Time
- The system reads the current date/time from an SNTP source. If valid, it derives today’s year/month/day and passes them into the renderer.
- The weekday algorithm is implemented locally (no external dependencies), making the calendar fully functional even when Home Assistant is offline.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Scripts as "tab5-scripts.yaml"
participant SNTP as "SNTP time"
participant Render as "tab5_custom.cpp"
Scripts->>SNTP : now()
alt time valid
SNTP-->>Scripts : {year, month, day_of_month}
Scripts->>Render : cal_render_month(..., today_year, today_month, today_day)
else time invalid
SNTP-->>Scripts : invalid
Scripts->>Render : cal_render_month(..., 0, 0, 0) // no today highlight
end
```

### Grid Cell Rendering Logic
Each cell receives:
- Day number
- Optional work hours string
- Appointment dot (gold) and birthday dot (pink)
- Background tint for school vacations
- Border highlight for today
- Color-coded number based on priority: today > past > holiday > weekend > normal

Weekend highlighting:
- Columns 5 and 6 (Saturday/Sunday) use a dimmed text color for the day number.

Current day indicator:
- The cell border becomes fully opaque with the accent color when the cell corresponds to today.

Holiday and vacation styling:
- Holidays set the day number to an error color.
- School vacations apply a translucent violet background to the cell.

Work hours:
- If present, displayed below the day number. Early shifts (start before 9:00) are highlighted in orange. Past days are faded.

Appointment and birthday dots:
- Gold dot appears when there is an appointment.
- Pink dot appears for birthdays.

### Navigation Controls
- Previous month button: decrements month, wraps to December of previous year, closes any open day detail, then re-renders.
- Next month button: increments month, wraps to January of next year, closes day detail, then re-renders.
- Today button: navigates to the current month using SNTP time, closes day detail, then re-renders.

All navigation triggers the same render pipeline, which also performs eviction and background pre-fetching.

## Performance Considerations
- Local rendering: cal_render_month() computes everything needed to draw the grid without network calls, ensuring immediate responsiveness even offline.
- Stale-while-revalidate cache:
  - Stores month payloads with a timestamp.
  - If data is older than 10 minutes, the UI still displays immediately while a silent refresh is triggered in the background.
  - Evicts entries outside the current view window (M−1, M, M+1) to limit memory usage.
- Pre-fetching:
  - On render, if M−1 or M+1 are missing from cache, they are fetched silently to make navigation instant.
  - At boot or Home Assistant reconnect, the current month and adjacent months are pre-fetched in the background.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Open(["Open calendar"]) --> RenderNow["Render grid from cache/local"]
RenderNow --> CheckStale{"Is cache stale (>10 min)?"}
CheckStale --> |Yes| RefreshNow["Background refresh current month"]
CheckStale --> |No| SkipRefresh["Skip refresh"]
RenderNow --> PrefetchPrev{"M-1 missing?"}
PrefetchPrev --> |Yes| FetchPrev["Fetch M-1 in background"]
PrefetchPrev --> |No| SkipPrev["Skip"]
RenderNow --> PrefetchNext{"M+1 missing?"}
PrefetchNext --> |Yes| FetchNext["Fetch M+1 in background"]
PrefetchNext --> |No| SkipNext["Skip"]
RefreshNow --> Evict["Evict distant months"]
FetchPrev --> Evict
FetchNext --> Evict
Evict --> Done(["Ready"])
```

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Calendar not showing today highlight:
  - Ensure SNTP time is valid; otherwise, today cannot be determined and highlights are disabled.
- Missing events or colors:
  - Verify Home Assistant connectivity; payloads are only applied when available.
  - Check if cache is stale; a background refresh will occur automatically after 10 minutes.
- Navigation feels slow:
  - Confirm pre-fetching is enabled; M−1 and M+1 should be fetched in the background during render.
- Day detail not loading:
  - If Home Assistant is offline, the detail popup shows an offline message; otherwise, it loads details from the month payload or falls back to day-specific queries.

**Section sources**
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:732-735](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L732-L735)
- [tab5_custom.cpp:2861-2882](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L2861-L2882)

## Conclusion
The monthly calendar grid delivers a fast, resilient, and visually rich experience by combining local date calculations with optional Home Assistant enrichment. Its design prioritizes immediate usability, smooth navigation through pre-fetching, and consistent visual semantics. The modular architecture—separating UI, rendering, scripting, and styling—makes it straightforward to extend or adapt while maintaining performance and clarity on the 1280×720 display.

## Introduction
This document explains the 320px arc thermostat control used to adjust target temperature between 16°C and 30°C on a circular LVGL arc widget. It covers:
- Smooth, touch-based temperature adjustment via an adjustable arc
- Optimistic UI updates that reflect changes immediately before Home Assistant confirms
- Debounced temperature commands to prevent rapid-fire requests
- Visual feedback through color coding (blue for cooling, red for heating, white/neutral otherwise)
- Mathematical handling of boundaries and interaction flow
- Performance considerations for smooth animations and efficient redraws during user interaction

## Project Structure
The arc thermostat spans UI definitions, C++ helpers, and ESPHome scripts:
- UI layout and widgets are defined in YAML components
- C++ provides helper functions for optimistic UI updates
- Scripts implement debouncing and centralized recoloring logic
- API logic synchronizes authoritative state from Home Assistant back to the UI

```mermaid
graph TB
A["User Interaction<br/>Touch / Buttons"] --> B["LVGL Arc Widget<br/>arc_temp_popup"]
B --> C["Optimistic Update<br/>update_clim_target_ui()"]
C --> D["Debounced Command<br/>tab5_debounce_clim_temp"]
D --> E["Home Assistant Service<br/>climate.set_temperature"]
E --> F["State Sync Back<br/>tab5_maj_clim"]
F --> G["Centralized Recolor<br/>tab5_clim_recolor"]
G --> H["UI Feedback<br/>Target Color & Icons"]
```

## Core Components
- 320x320 LVGL arc widget with min/max values set to 16–30°C and adjustable mode enabled
- Optimistic update function that writes the target value to both labels and the arc
- Debounce script that groups rapid taps into a single climate.set_temperature call
- Centralized recolor script that sets target text color based on HVAC mode (cool=blue, heat=red, off/other=white)
- Compact card buttons that mirror popup behavior with optimistic updates and debouncing

Key behaviors:
- Touch or drag on the arc updates clim_target_temp immediately and triggers debounce
- Minus/Plus buttons adjust by 0.5°C with boundary clamping at 16°C and 30°C
- Target label color reflects current HVAC mode; icons reflect active modes/presets/fan/swing

## Architecture Overview
The system uses an optimistic UI pattern:
- Immediate visual feedback is applied locally without waiting for Home Assistant confirmation
- A short delay groups multiple rapid interactions into one command
- The authoritative state from Home Assistant re-applies colors and values to ensure consistency

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant U as "User"
participant W as "LVGL Arc"
participant C as "C++ Helper"
participant S as "Debounce Script"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant R as "Recolor Script"
U->>W : "Drag/Adjust arc"
W-->>C : "on_value(x)"
C->>C : "update_clim_target_ui(label, arc, x)"
C->>S : "script.execute tab5_debounce_clim_temp"
Note over S : "Groups rapid taps"
S->>HA : "climate.set_temperature(hvac_mode, temperature)"
HA-->>R : "State push via tab5_maj_clim"
R->>R : "Set target color & icon states"
R-->>U : "Updated UI colors & values"
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### 320px Arc Widget Configuration
- Size: 320x320 pixels
- Range: min_value 16, max_value 30
- Adjustable: true (touch/drag supported)
- Indicator width matches track width for consistent visuals
- Initial value set to a default within range

Behavior:
- on_value handler updates clim_target_temp and calls optimistic UI update
- Triggers debounce script to send a single climate.set_temperature after interaction settles

**Section sources**
- [climate_popup.yaml:112-136](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_popup.yaml#L112-L136)

### Optimistic UI Updates
- update_clim_target_ui formats the target temperature string and applies it to the label
- If an arc pointer is provided, lv_arc_set_value updates the indicator immediately
- In the compact card, only the label is updated since there is no arc

Purpose:
- Provides immediate visual feedback to the user
- Reduces perceived latency while awaiting Home Assistant confirmation

**Section sources**
- [tab5_custom.cpp:1627-1629](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L1627-L1629)
- [climate_card.yaml:94-126](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_card.yaml#L94-L126)

### Debounced Temperature Commands
- tab5_debounce_clim_temp waits 250ms then sends climate.set_temperature once per gesture
- Ensures hvac_mode is not off when sending temperature (forces cool if off)
- Groups rapid +/- button presses and arc adjustments into a single command

Benefits:
- Prevents flooding Home Assistant with repeated set_temperature calls
- Improves responsiveness and reduces network overhead

**Section sources**
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:383-397](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L383-L397)
- [climate_popup.yaml:148-184](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_popup.yaml#L148-L184)
- [climate_card.yaml:94-126](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_card.yaml#L94-L126)

### Visual Feedback and Color Coding
- Target label color is set centrally based on HVAC mode:
  - Cool: blue
  - Heat: red
  - Off or other modes: white/neutral
- Icon states for presets, fan, swing, and quiet are also updated centrally

Implementation:
- tab5_clim_recolor reads globals and applies styles to target labels and icons
- Called both on optimistic taps and on authoritative state sync from Home Assistant

**Section sources**
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:399-489](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L399-L489)
- [tab5_custom.h:614-625](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.h#L614-L625)

### Boundary Handling and Step Size
- Minus/Plus buttons adjust by 0.5°C
- Values are clamped to the 16–30°C range
- Arc widget enforces min/max bounds natively

Result:
- Users cannot set temperatures outside the allowed range
- Consistent step size across arc and buttons

**Section sources**
- [climate_popup.yaml:148-184](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_popup.yaml#L148-L184)
- [climate_card.yaml:94-126](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_card.yaml#L94-L126)

### State Synchronization from Home Assistant
- tab5_maj_clim pushes authoritative values back to the UI
- Updates target labels, arc value, room temperature display, and mode globals
- Then executes centralized recolor to ensure consistent visuals

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:171-198](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L171-L198)
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:399-489](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L399-L489)

### Mathematical Notes on Arc Positioning and Touch
- LVGL’s arc widget maps its internal value range to angular positions automatically
- With min_value 16 and max_value 30, each unit corresponds to a fixed angular increment
- Touch angle-to-temperature conversion is handled internally by LVGL; the application receives the resulting value via on_value
- Boundary enforcement is performed both by the widget and by explicit clamping in button handlers

Note:
- No custom angle math is implemented in this codebase; LVGL manages mapping and rendering

## Performance Considerations
- Optimistic updates avoid waiting for network round-trips, improving perceived responsiveness
- Debouncing reduces redundant service calls and minimizes UI flicker caused by frequent updates
- Centralized recolor ensures a single pass to update all relevant elements, reducing redundant style changes
- LVGL handles arc drawing efficiently; keeping updates minimal during interaction helps maintain smooth animations
- Using modal geometry tokens ensures consistent layout without recalculating positions repeatedly

Practical tips:
- Keep debounce delay balanced to group rapid inputs without delaying final confirmation
- Avoid excessive manual redraws; rely on LVGL’s event-driven updates
- Ensure color constants are centralized to prevent inconsistent styling across components

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
Common issues and resolutions:
- Target does not change visually:
  - Verify update_clim_target_ui is called with valid label and arc pointers
  - Check that clim_target_temp is being updated before calling the function
- Multiple set_temperature calls sent rapidly:
  - Confirm debounce script is executing and not interrupted
  - Ensure on_value handlers trigger the debounce script consistently
- Incorrect color for target:
  - Validate HVAC mode global is set correctly before recolor
  - Ensure tab5_clim_recolor runs after state sync or user tap
- Arc appears stuck at boundaries:
  - Confirm min/max values are set to 16 and 30
  - Check button handlers clamp values appropriately

- [tab5_custom.cpp:1627-1629](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5_custom.cpp#L1627-L1629)

- [climate_popup.yaml:112-184](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_popup.yaml#L112-L184)

## Conclusion
The 320px arc thermostat delivers an intuitive, responsive temperature control experience:
- Immediate visual feedback through optimistic updates
- Reliable command delivery via debounced Home Assistant calls
- Clear visual cues using color-coded feedback aligned with HVAC mode
- Robust boundary handling and smooth LVGL-based arc interaction
- Centralized styling and synchronization ensure consistency across UI states

This design balances performance and usability while maintaining a clean separation between UI, logic, and backend synchronization.

## Introduction
This document explains the climate control system that integrates Home Assistant HVAC entities with a compact dashboard card and a near-fullscreen popup. The UI provides three glass cards: Mode (stacked cool/heat/dry/fan/off), Temperature (a 320px arc thermostat with optimistic target updates), and Options (presets eco/boost, quiet fan mode, and airflow controls including swing and Daikin “Brise” windnice). It covers entity mapping, service call patterns, debounced temperature updates, dimmed states when off, real-time temperature display with color coding, and performance considerations for smooth interactions and efficient state synchronization.

## Project Structure
The climate feature is composed of LVGL UI components and ESPHome services/scripts that bridge to Home Assistant:
- Compact dashboard card for quick target adjustments and opening the full popup
- Near-fullscreen popup with three glass cards for comprehensive control
- Reusable button templates for HVAC modes and preset toggles
- Centralized scripts for recoloring icons and debouncing temperature changes
- API logic service to push authoritative state from Home Assistant back to the device
- Entity mapping file that binds the UI to the actual Home Assistant climate entity

```mermaid

Popup --> BtnMode["HVAC Mode Buttons<br/>climate_hvac_mode_btn.yaml"]
Popup --> BtnPreset["Preset Toggle Buttons<br/>climate_preset_toggle_btn.yaml"]
Popup --> ArcTemp["Arc Thermostat<br/>320px"]
Popup --> FanSwing["Fan & Airflow<br/>Quiet / Swing / Windnice"]
UI_Card -.-> Debounce["Debounce Temp<br/>tab5_debounce_clim_temp"]
Popup -.-> Debounce
Debounce --> HA["Home Assistant<br/>climate.set_temperature"]
```

## Core Components
- Compact dashboard card: Shows current room temperatures and a central target value within a glass-styled zone. Tapping the target opens the popup; +/- buttons adjust the target optimistically and trigger a debounced update.
- Near-fullscreen popup: Three glass cards:
  - Mode: stacked buttons for cool, heat, dry, fan_only, and off
  - Temperature: 320px arc thermostat with center target label and +/- buttons
  - Options: presets (eco/away and boost), quiet fan toggle, swing toggle, and windnice toggle
- Button templates: Reusable definitions for HVAC mode buttons and preset toggle buttons
- Scripts:
  - tab5_debounce_clim_temp: Groups rapid taps into a single set_temperature call
  - tab5_clim_recolor: Centralized icon coloring based on current globals
- API service:
  - tab5_maj_clim: Authoritative state push from Home Assistant updating targets, current temp, modes, presets, fan, and swing

## Architecture Overview
The system uses an optimistic UI pattern combined with debounced service calls and authoritative state pushes:
- User interactions immediately update local globals and UI colors without waiting for Home Assistant
- Temperature changes are debounced to avoid flooding Home Assistant with set_temperature calls
- Home Assistant periodically pushes the authoritative state via tab5_maj_clim, which re-applies values and triggers centralized recoloring
- Entity mapping ties UI actions to the correct Home Assistant climate entity

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant U as "User"
participant C as "Climate Card<br/>climate_card.yaml"
participant P as "Popup<br/>climate_popup.yaml"
participant S as "Scripts<br/>tab5-scripts.yaml"
participant A as "API Logic<br/>tab5-api-logic.yaml"
participant H as "Home Assistant"
U->>C : Tap + or -
C->>S : Update clim_target_temp + call debounce
S-->>H : Set temperature (debounced)
Note over S,H : Rapid taps grouped into one call
U->>P : Adjust arc or press mode/preset/fan/swing
P->>S : Update globals + recolor icons
P->>H : Call appropriate climate service
H-->>A : Push state (target/current/mode/preset/fan/swing)
A->>S : Execute recolor script
S-->>C : Update labels/colors
S-->>P : Update labels/colors
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Compact Dashboard Card
- Glass-styled control zone displays the target temperature and +/- buttons
- Tapping the target opens the full-screen popup
- +/- buttons update the global target optimistically and invoke the debounce script to send a single set_temperature after user interaction settles

Key behaviors:
- Optimistic UI: immediate visual feedback before Home Assistant responds
- Debounced updates: prevents rapid-fire commands during fast tapping
- Bounds: clamps target between configured min/max values

**Section sources**
- [climate_card.yaml:56-129](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_card.yaml#L56-L129)

### Near-Fullscreen Popup
Three glass cards provide comprehensive control:

- Mode card: Stacked buttons for cool, heat, dry, fan_only, and off
  - Each button sets the HVAC mode globally, recolors icons immediately, then calls the corresponding Home Assistant service
  - Off uses a dedicated service call path

- Temperature card: 320px arc thermostat
  - Adjustable arc updates the target and invokes the debounce script
  - Center label shows the target; bottom label shows current room temperature pushed by Home Assistant

- Options card: Presets, ventilation, and airflow
  - Presets: eco/away and boost toggles using a template that toggles to none when pressed again
  - Ventilation: quiet fan mode toggle
  - Airflow: swing toggle and windnice toggle (Daikin Onecta-specific)

### Deferencing and Debounce Mechanisms
- Temperature debounce: Groups rapid +/- taps and arc adjustments into a single set_temperature call after a short delay
- Optimistic updates: Globals and UI colors are updated immediately on tap, ensuring responsive UX even if Home Assistant/Daikin cloud responses are delayed
- Authority: Home Assistant pushes authoritative state via tab5_maj_clim, which resets globals and triggers recoloring to reconcile any discrepancies

```mermaid
flowchart TD

UpdateGlobal --> Recolor["Recolor Icons Immediately"]
Recolor --> Debounce{"Debounce Timer?"}
Debounce --> |No| Wait["Wait for Stability"]
Debounce --> |Yes| SendHA["Send Home Assistant Service"]
Wait --> Debounce
SendHA --> End(["UI Synced"])
```

### Entity Mapping Configuration
- The climate entity ID used by the UI is mapped in the user entities file
- All service calls reference this mapped entity ID, decoupling UI from specific device IDs

**Section sources**
- [user_entities.yaml:18-19](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/user_entities.yaml#L18-L19)

### Service Call Patterns
- HVAC mode: climate.set_hvac_mode
- Preset mode: climate.set_preset_mode
- Fan mode: climate.set_fan_mode
- Swing mode: climate.set_swing_mode
- Turn off: climate.turn_off
- Temperature: climate.set_temperature (debounced)

All calls include the mapped entity_id and relevant data fields.

### Error Handling for Disconnected Devices
- The API configuration includes a reboot timeout to recover from prolonged Home Assistant disconnections
- While not specific to climate, this mechanism helps prevent zombie states where the device remains online but cannot communicate with Home Assistant
- For climate-specific unavailability, rely on Home Assistant to push state updates; if no updates arrive, the UI retains last known optimistic state until connectivity resumes

**Section sources**
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:17-37](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L17-L37)

- UI components define interactions and visuals
- Templates standardize repeated controls
- Scripts manage state transitions, debouncing, and styling
- API logic receives authoritative state from Home Assistant
- Entity mapping abstracts device-specific IDs

## Performance Considerations
- Debounced temperature updates reduce network overhead and prevent command storms during rapid interactions
- Optimistic UI updates ensure smooth arc interactions and immediate feedback without waiting for Home Assistant round-trips
- Centralized recoloring minimizes redundant UI updates and keeps styling consistent across components
- Using a single Home Assistant instance avoids duplicate entity issues and simplifies state synchronization
- Glass cards and modal structure keep rendering lightweight while providing rich interactivity

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- If temperature changes do not apply: verify debounced script execution and ensure Home Assistant is reachable; check that the mapped entity ID is correct
- If icons do not reflect state: confirm that tab5_clim_recolor is executed both on user interactions and on authoritative state pushes
- If the device appears stuck offline: review the reboot timeout behavior and network connectivity; the system will attempt recovery after prolonged disconnection
- If Daikin windnice does not respond: ensure swing/windnice toggles are sending the correct values and that Home Assistant reports the expected state

## Conclusion
The climate control system delivers a responsive, visually clear interface for HVAC management through optimistic updates, debounced commands, and authoritative state synchronization. The compact card enables quick adjustments, while the near-fullscreen popup offers comprehensive control over modes, temperature, presets, fan, and airflow—including Daikin windnice. Centralized scripts and API logic ensure consistency and reliability, while entity mapping abstracts device specifics for maintainability.

## Introduction
This document explains the compact climate dashboard card component and its full-screen popup interface. The card provides a minimalist view of current room temperatures, target temperature, and HVAC mode status, with quick access to detailed controls via a modal popup. It integrates with Home Assistant entities, supports optimistic UI updates for responsive touch interactions, and synchronizes real-time state from Home Assistant without blocking the main UI thread.

## Project Structure
The climate feature is composed of:
- A compact dashboard card that shows current temperatures and a glassy control zone for target temperature adjustments.
- A full-screen popup offering detailed HVAC mode selection, temperature arc control, presets, fan mode, and airflow options.
- Shared templates for HVAC mode buttons and preset toggles.
- Scripts and API logic that handle debounced temperature changes, centralized recoloring based on HVAC state, and synchronization with Home Assistant.

```mermaid

end
subgraph "Logic"
API["API Logic<br/>tab5-api-logic.yaml"]

end

CC --> |opens| CP

CP --> |uses| PRESET
CC --> |debounced temp change| SCRIPTS
CP --> |debounced temp change| SCRIPTS
SCRIPTS --> |calls service| HA
HA --> |pushes state| API
API --> |updates UI globals & icons| CP
API --> |updates UI globals & icons| CC
```

## Core Components
- Compact Climate Card: Displays current room temperatures (e.g., living room and greenhouse), a central target temperature label, and a glassy control area with minus and plus buttons to adjust the target. Tapping the target opens the full-screen climate popup.
- Full-Screen Climate Popup: Provides three panels:
  - Mode: Select HVAC modes (cool, heat, dry, fan-only, off).
  - Temperature: An adjustable arc with center target display and ± buttons; also shows current room temperature.
  - Options: Presets (eco/away, boost), quiet fan mode toggle, and airflow options (swing/windnice).
- Templates: Reusable button components for HVAC modes and presets reduce duplication and ensure consistent behavior.
- Scripts and API: Debounce scripts group rapid taps into a single Home Assistant call; a centralized recolor script updates icon colors based on current HVAC state; an API service pushes authoritative state back to the UI.

## Architecture Overview
The climate card acts as a gateway to the full-screen popup. User interactions are handled optimistically to keep the UI responsive, while Home Assistant pushes authoritative state updates through a dedicated API service.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant U as "User"
participant CC as "Climate Card"
participant CP as "Climate Popup"
participant S as "Scripts"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant API as "API Logic"
U->>CC : Tap target or +/-
CC->>CP : Open popup (if tap target)
CC->>S : Debounce temp change (±)
CP->>S : Debounce temp change (arc/±)
S->>HA : climate.set_temperature / set_hvac_mode / set_preset_mode / set_fan_mode / set_swing_mode
HA-->>API : Push state update (target, current, mode, preset, fan, swing)
API-->>CC : Update labels and globals
API-->>CP : Update labels, arc, and icon colors
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Compact Climate Card
- Layout: Transparent container with two top labels showing current temperatures for different zones, and a bottom glassy control zone containing the target temperature label and ± buttons.
- Interactions:
  - Minus/Plus buttons perform optimistic updates to the target temperature and schedule a debounced Home Assistant call to apply the change.
  - Tapping the target label opens the full-screen climate popup.
- Visuals: The control zone uses a glass style to visually separate it from the rest of the card.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["Card Interaction"]) --> Check{"Which element?"}
Check --> |Tap Target| OpenPopup["Open Climate Popup"]
Check --> |Tap Minus| DecTemp["Decrement target by 0.5°C<br/>Update UI immediately"]
Check --> |Tap Plus| IncTemp["Increment target by 0.5°C<br/>Update UI immediately"]
DecTemp --> Debounce["Schedule debounced set_temperature"]
IncTemp --> Debounce
Debounce --> End(["Done"])
OpenPopup --> End
```

### Full-Screen Climate Popup
- Panels:
  - Mode: Buttons for cool, heat, dry, fan-only, and off. Each sets the HVAC mode optimistically and calls the corresponding Home Assistant service.
  - Temperature: Arc-based thermostat with center target label and ± buttons; also displays current room temperature.
  - Options: Preset toggles (eco/away, boost), quiet fan mode toggle, and airflow options (swing/windnice).
- Behavior: All user actions update local globals first, then call Home Assistant services. A centralized recolor script updates icon states immediately for responsiveness.

```mermaid

+toggleSwingMode()
}

+onShortClick()
}
class PresetToggle {
+onShortClick()
}
ClimatePopup --> HVACModeButton : "includes"
ClimatePopup --> PresetToggle : "includes"
```

### State Synchronization and Recoloring
- Home Assistant pushes climate state updates via a dedicated API service, which updates UI labels, arc values, and global variables representing current HVAC settings.
- A centralized recolor script reads these globals and applies appropriate colors to icons and target labels based on HVAC mode, presets, fan mode, and swing mode.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram

participant R as "Recolor Script"
HA->>API : tab5_maj_clim(target, current, mode, preset, fan, swing)
API->>UI : Update labels, arc, and globals
API->>R : Execute recolor
R-->>UI : Apply colors to icons and target
```

## Performance Considerations
- Optimistic UI Updates: Temperature adjustments and mode changes update the UI immediately before calling Home Assistant, improving perceived responsiveness.
- Debouncing: Rapid taps are grouped into a single Home Assistant call to avoid network overload and redundant operations.
- Centralized Recoloring: Icon color updates are centralized to prevent duplicated logic and ensure consistent visuals across components.
- Non-blocking Updates: Home Assistant pushes state updates via an API service, decoupling UI refresh from user actions and preventing main thread blocking.

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Temperature not updating: Ensure the debounced script is triggered and that the Home Assistant entity ID is correctly mapped. Verify that the API service receives the push and updates UI labels.
- Icons not reflecting mode: Confirm that the recolor script executes after state updates and that all referenced icon IDs exist in the UI.
- Popup does not open: Check that the target click handler invokes the popup animation and that the popup object is present and not hidden.

## Conclusion
The compact climate dashboard card offers a streamlined way to monitor and control HVAC systems with immediate visual feedback and seamless integration with Home Assistant. Its design emphasizes responsiveness through optimistic updates and debouncing, while centralized logic ensures consistent state synchronization and styling. Configuration is flexible via external entity mapping, making it adaptable to various deployments.

## Introduction
This document explains the near-fullscreen climate control popup interface on the Tab5 (1280×720). It covers the three-panel glass card layout:
- Mode panel (left): stacked HVAC mode buttons and an Off button
- Temperature panel (center): arc thermostat with target display, ± controls, and room temperature readout
- Options panel (right): presets (Eco/Away, Boost), quiet fan mode, and airflow controls (Oscillation, WindNice/Breeze)

It also documents the modal shell (scrim overlay, header with close button), smooth animation transitions, responsive design for the Tab5 display, touch interaction patterns, keyboard accessibility considerations, popup lifecycle management, state persistence across sessions, integration with the modal shell system, and performance optimizations for smooth scrolling and efficient rendering.

## Project Structure
The popup is composed from reusable UI components and shared tokens:
- The popup container composes a scrim, a modal header, and three glass cards
- Shared geometry tokens define the 1250×690 modal card size and body offsets for the 1280×720 screen
- Reusable templates parameterize repeated buttons (HVAC modes, presets)
- Scripts provide debounced actions and centralized recoloring logic

```mermaid
graph TB

A --> C["modal_header.yaml"]
A --> D["Mode Panel<br/>HVAC buttons + Off"]
A --> E["Temperature Panel<br/>Arc + targets + ±"]
A --> F["Options Panel<br/>Presets + Fan + Airflow"]
D --> G["climate_hvac_mode_btn.yaml"]
F --> H["climate_preset_toggle_btn.yaml"]
A --> I["tab5-ui-tokens.yaml"]
A --> J["tab5-scripts.yaml"]
```

## Core Components
- Scrim overlay: full-screen clickable backdrop that closes the popup when tapped; supports different opacities via a variable
- Modal header: compact title bar with icon, title label, and close button; standardized across all popups
- Three glass cards:
  - Mode panel: four HVAC modes via a template plus an Off button with a distinct service call
  - Temperature panel: adjustable arc (16–30 °C), optimistic target updates, ± buttons with debounced set_temperature calls, and room temperature readout
  - Options panel: preset toggles (Eco/Away, Boost), quiet fan toggle, and airflow toggles (Oscillation, WindNice)
- Shared geometry tokens: modal card width/height and body y-offset tuned for 1280×720
- Scripts: debounce for temperature changes and centralized recoloring of icons based on current state

## Architecture Overview
The popup integrates tightly with the modal shell system and the push-only data flow used by the device:
- Opening: tapping the climate card target triggers an animated open and brings the popup to the foreground
- Display: the popup uses a scrim, a shared header, and three glass cards laid out at fixed positions relative to the modal body
- State synchronization: user interactions update local globals immediately (optimistic UI), then call Home Assistant services; incoming HA pushes re-color and refresh UI via centralized scripts
- Closing: tap the scrim or header close button to animate the popup closed

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant Card as "Climate Card"
participant Popup as "Climate Popup"
participant Shell as "Modal Shell"
participant Scripts as "Scripts"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
User->>Card : Tap target
Card->>Shell : animate_popup_open(clim_options_popup)
Shell-->>Popup : Show scrim + header + cards
User->>Popup : Adjust arc / press ±
Popup->>Popup : Update globals + optimistic UI
Popup->>Scripts : tab5_debounce_clim_temp
Scripts->>HA : climate.set_temperature (debounced)
HA-->>Scripts : State change
Scripts->>Popup : tab5_clim_recolor (icons/target color)
User->>Popup : Tap scrim/close
Popup->>Shell : animate_popup_close()
```

## Detailed Component Analysis

### Modal Shell: Scrim and Header
- Scrim: a full-screen button with configurable opacity; tapping it executes a provided close lambda
- Header: a compact 52 px bar with icon, title, and close button; vertical alignment is handled by LVGL so there is no per-popup drift; the close button executes a provided close lambda

```mermaid
classDiagram
class ModalScrim {
+width : 100%
+height : 100%
+bg_opa : ${scrim_opa}%
+on_short_click(close_lambda)
}
class ModalHeader {
+icon : string
+title : string
+title_id : string
+close_btn_id : string
+close_lambda : string
}
ModalScrim <.. ModalHeader : "used together in popups"
```

### Mode Panel: Stacked HVAC Buttons
- Four HVAC modes are rendered via a single templated button component; each sets the mode globally, triggers recoloring, and calls the appropriate Home Assistant service
- An Off button has its own handler because it invokes a different service (turn off) and requires specific logic

```mermaid
flowchart TD
Start(["HVAC Button Press"]) --> SetGlobal["Set clim_hvac_mode global"]
SetGlobal --> Recolor["Execute tab5_clim_recolor"]
Recolor --> CallHA["Call climate.set_hvac_mode"]
CallHA --> End(["Done"])
```

### Temperature Panel: Arc Thermostat and Controls
- Arc range: 16–30 °C; adjusting the arc updates the target optimistically and schedules a debounced set_temperature call
- ± buttons adjust the target in 0.5 °C steps with clamping and debouncing
- Room temperature is displayed at the bottom and updated by pushes from Home Assistant

```mermaid
flowchart TD
TStart(["Arc or ± Interaction"]) --> UpdateLocal["Update clim_target_temp + UI"]
UpdateLocal --> Debounce["Execute tab5_debounce_clim_temp"]
Debounce --> SetTemp["Call climate.set_temperature (after delay)"]
SetTemp --> WaitPush{"HA push received?"}
WaitPush -- Yes --> Recolor["Recolor target + icons"]
WaitPush -- No --> Idle["Wait for next interaction"]
Recolor --> Idle
```

### Options Panel: Presets and Airflow Controls
- Presets: toggle behavior; if the current preset equals the pressed one, it resets to none; otherwise it sets the selected preset
- Quiet fan mode: toggles between auto and quiet; updates global and calls set_fan_mode
- Airflow: two toggles for swing modes; updates global and calls set_swing_mode

```mermaid
flowchart TD
OStart(["Preset/Fan/Swing Button"]) --> ToggleGlobal["Toggle or set clim_* global"]
ToggleGlobal --> Recolor["Execute tab5_clim_recolor"]
Recolor --> CallService["Call appropriate climate.set_* service"]
CallService --> OEnd(["Done"])
```

### Responsive Design for 1280×720
- Modal card dimensions and body offset are defined in a single token file to ensure consistent sizing and spacing across popups
- The header is compact (52 px) and leaves 20 px breathing space before the body starts at y=72
- All panels use fixed widths and positions within the 1250×690 card to fit the Tab5’s 1280×720 display without clipping

**Section sources**
- [tab5-ui-tokens.yaml:13-24](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ui-tokens.yaml#L13-L24)

### Touch Interaction Patterns
- Opening: tap the climate card target to open the popup and bring it to the foreground
- Scrim: tap anywhere on the dark overlay to close the popup
- Header close: tap the close button in the header to close the popup
- Arc and ±: immediate visual feedback with debounced network calls to avoid spamming Home Assistant
- Buttons: pressed state dimming for tactile feedback; each button performs optimistic UI updates before calling Home Assistant

### Keyboard Accessibility Considerations
- The UI is primarily touch-driven; keyboard navigation is not explicitly implemented in the referenced files
- For keyboard users, consider adding focusable elements and key handlers in future iterations to support arrow keys for arc adjustment and Enter/Space for button activation

[No sources needed since this section provides general guidance]

### Popup Lifecycle Management
- Open: triggered from the climate card; the popup is animated into view and moved to the foreground
- Close: triggered by tapping the scrim or the header close button; the popup animates out
- Animation functions are invoked via lambdas passed to the modal shell components

- [climate_card.yaml:73-83](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_card.yaml#L73-L83)

### State Persistence Across Sessions
- Current state snapshots (including climate-related globals) are maintained in shared globals and refreshed by push updates from Home Assistant
- The device uses a push-only model: Home Assistant detects changes and calls ESPHome API services to update the UI; the firmware parses payloads and applies them atomically

### Integration with the Modal Shell System
- The popup composes the shared scrim and header via includes, ensuring consistent chrome across all popups
- Geometry tokens centralize sizing and offsets, preventing drift and simplifying maintenance
- The decision record enforces a single scrim and compact header for all popups

## Performance Considerations
- Optimistic UI: immediate local updates reduce perceived latency; debounced network calls prevent flooding Home Assistant during rapid interactions
- Centralized recoloring: a single script updates all relevant icons and target colors, minimizing redundant style operations
- Push-only updates: Home Assistant pushes changes atomically, avoiding polling and reducing CPU/network overhead
- Fixed layouts and non-scrollable panels: scrollable disabled ensures predictable rendering and avoids expensive scroll calculations
- Tokenized geometry: changing sizes in one place prevents inconsistent layouts and reduces reflow costs

**Section sources**
- [climate_popup.yaml:112-198](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_popup.yaml#L112-L198)
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:383-479](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L383-L479)
- [architecture.md:191-207](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#L191-L207)

## Troubleshooting Guide
- Popup does not open: verify the climate card target click triggers the open animation and that the popup object is not hidden
- Target not updating: check that the arc value is within 16–30 °C and that debounced set_temperature is called; confirm HA entity responds
- Icons not highlighting: ensure tab5_clim_recolor runs after setting globals; verify globals reflect current state
- Header close not working: confirm close_lambda is correctly passed to modal_header and modal_scrim
- Layout issues: validate modal_card_w/h and modal_body_y tokens; ensure header height and body offsets remain consistent

**Section sources**
- [climate_card.yaml:73-83](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_card.yaml#L73-L83)
- [climate_popup.yaml:112-198](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/ui_components/climate_popup.yaml#L112-L198)
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:383-479](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L383-L479)
- [tab5-ui-tokens.yaml:13-24](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-ui-tokens.yaml#L13-L24)

## Conclusion
The near-fullscreen climate control popup delivers a clear, responsive three-panel experience optimized for the Tab5’s 1280×720 display. By combining a shared modal shell, tokenized geometry, optimistic UI updates, debounced interactions, and centralized recoloring, it achieves smooth performance and consistent behavior. The design adheres to project decisions for modal chrome and factorization, while remaining extensible for future enhancements such as keyboard accessibility and additional airflow options.

## Introduction
This document explains the HVAC mode control system for the Tab5 interface, covering cool, heat, dry, fan_only, and off modes. It details:
- The template-based button system that generates consistent UI elements for each mode with icons, labels, and colors
- The optimistic update pattern where mode changes are immediately reflected before Home Assistant confirmation
- The centralized recoloring script that updates all mode buttons simultaneously
- Error handling considerations for failed service calls
- Entity mapping configuration for climate devices
- Service call patterns for each mode
- State synchronization mechanisms between UI and Home Assistant

## Project Structure
The HVAC controls are implemented as a modal popup with three cards: MODE (left), TEMPERATURE (center), and OPTIONS (right). The MODE card uses a reusable template to generate buttons for each HVAC mode. Temperature adjustments use debounced updates to avoid flooding Home Assistant with rapid requests. A centralized recoloring script ensures consistent visual feedback across all climate-related UI elements.

## Core Components

### Template-Based Button System
The HVAC mode buttons use a single template file that generates four identical button layouts for cool, heat, dry, and fan_only modes. Each button includes:
- Consistent styling with rounded corners and hover effects
- Dynamic icon display based on the mode
- Optimistic UI updates before Home Assistant confirmation
- Centralized recoloring through the tab5_clim_recolor script

### Optimistic Update Pattern
When a user taps an HVAC mode button, the system immediately:
1. Updates the global clim_hvac_mode variable
2. Executes the recoloring script to highlight the active mode
3. Calls the appropriate Home Assistant service
4. Waits for Home Assistant confirmation to correct any discrepancies

### Centralized Recoloring Script
The tab5_clim_recolor script manages all visual state for climate controls:
- Sets active/inactive colors for each mode button
- Updates target temperature display colors (blue for cool, red for heat, white for others)
- Manages preset mode indicators (eco/boost)
- Controls fan mode and swing mode visual states

## Architecture Overview

The HVAC control system follows a client-server architecture where the Tab5 device acts as a sophisticated remote control for Home Assistant climate entities. The system maintains local state for immediate responsiveness while synchronizing with the authoritative Home Assistant state.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant User as "User"
participant UI as "HVAC Button"
participant Local as "Local State"
participant HA as "Home Assistant"
participant Climate as "Climate Entity"
User->>UI : Tap Cool Mode
UI->>Local : Set clim_hvac_mode = "cool"
UI->>UI : Execute tab5_clim_recolor
UI->>HA : Call climate.set_hvac_mode
HA->>Climate : Apply mode change
Climate-->>HA : Confirm state
HA-->>UI : State update via tab5_maj_clim
UI->>UI : Reapply colors from authoritative state
Note over UI,HA : Optimistic update provides immediate feedback<br/>while ensuring eventual consistency
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD

UpdateLocal --> UpdateUI["Update UI displays"]
UpdateUI --> Debounce["Start 250ms debounce timer"]
Debounce --> Timer{"Timer Complete?"}
Timer --> |No| Wait["Wait for more input"]
Wait --> Debounce
Timer --> |Yes| CallHA["Call climate.set_temperature"]
CallHA --> Complete([Complete])
```

### State Synchronization Mechanism
The system maintains two layers of state:
1. **Optimistic Local State**: Immediately updated when user interacts
2. **Authoritative Remote State**: Received from Home Assistant via tab5_maj_clim service

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> Idle
Idle --> Optimistic : "User taps mode"
Optimistic --> Waiting : "Call HA service"
Waiting --> Confirmed : "HA confirms"
Waiting --> Optimistic : "HA rejects"
Confirmed --> Idle : "Sync complete"
Confirmed --> Optimistic : "Sync needed"
```

## Performance Considerations

The HVAC control system is designed for optimal performance:

- **Debouncing**: Temperature changes are debounced to prevent excessive Home Assistant calls during rapid interactions
- **Optimistic Updates**: UI responds immediately without waiting for network round-trips
- **Centralized Recoloring**: Single script handles all visual updates efficiently
- **Efficient State Management**: Global variables minimize memory usage and improve access speed
- **Batched Updates**: Multiple state changes are coordinated to reduce UI refresh overhead

## Troubleshooting Guide

### Common Issues and Solutions

#### Disconnected Devices
**Symptoms**: Mode changes don't take effect, UI shows incorrect state
**Solutions**:
- Check Home Assistant connectivity status
- Verify climate entity is available in Home Assistant
- Restart the climate integration if needed

#### Unsupported Modes
**Symptoms**: Mode button doesn't respond or reverts immediately
**Solutions**:
- Check climate device capabilities in Home Assistant
- Verify supported modes match expected values (cool, heat, dry, fan_only, off)
- Some devices may not support all modes

#### Network Connectivity Problems
**Symptoms**: Delayed response, intermittent failures
**Solutions**:
- Check network connection stability
- Increase timeout settings if possible
- Implement retry logic for critical operations

#### State Synchronization Issues
**Symptoms**: UI shows different state than actual device
**Solutions**:
- Force refresh by closing and reopening the climate popup
- Check tab5_maj_clim service is receiving updates
- Verify global variables are properly synchronized

#### Service Call Failures
**Symptoms**: Buttons appear to work but no actual change occurs
**Solutions**:
- Check Home Assistant logs for service call errors
- Verify entity_id configuration is correct
- Test climate services directly in Home Assistant developer tools

**Section sources**
- [tab5-scripts.yaml:383-398](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-scripts.yaml#L383-L398)
- [tab5-api-logic.yaml:135-199](https://github.com/Axellum/M5-Tab5-ESPHome-LVGL/blob/main/Tab5/tab5-api-logic.yaml#L135-L199)

## Conclusion

The HVAC mode control system provides a robust, responsive interface for managing climate devices through Home Assistant. The combination of template-based UI components, optimistic updates, and centralized state management ensures both immediate user feedback and reliable device control. The system's modular design makes it easy to extend with additional modes or features while maintaining consistent behavior across all climate controls.

Key strengths include:
- **Consistent User Experience**: Template-based buttons provide uniform interaction patterns
- **Responsive Interface**: Optimistic updates eliminate perceived latency
- **Reliable State Management**: Centralized recoloring ensures visual consistency
- **Scalable Architecture**: Easy to add new modes or modify existing behavior
- **Robust Error Handling**: Graceful degradation when external dependencies fail

## Introduction
This document explains the preset and airflow control system for HVAC devices, focusing on:
- Toggle-based presets (eco/boost) that return to none when re-tapped
- Fan mode toggling between quiet and auto states
- Airflow controls for swing stop/oscillation and Daikin windnice integration
- Optimistic UI updates that reflect state changes immediately
- Centralized recoloring to keep all controls visually consistent
- Device-specific adaptations (e.g., Daikin Onecta mapping)
- Service call patterns, error handling considerations, and fallback mechanisms
- Configuration examples and troubleshooting guidance for manufacturer-specific quirks

## Project Structure
The climate UI is composed of a popup with three cards: Mode, Temperature, and Options. The Options card hosts presets, ventilation, and airflow controls. State is managed via globals and updated optimistically before sending Home Assistant service calls. A centralized script handles icon recoloring based on current state.
